/>[[New York Rangers]]<br />[[Avangard Omsk]]<br />[[Philadelphia Flyers]]<br />[[Dallas Stars]]<br />[[Boston Bruins]]<br />[[New Jersey Devils]]<br />[[Florida Panthers]]<br />[[Calgary Flames]]\n| ntl_team = TCH\n| ntl_team_2 = CZE\n| draft = 5th overall\n| draft_year = 1990\n| draft_team = [[Pittsburgh Penguins]]\n| career_start = 1988\n| career_end = \n}}\n'''Jaromír Jágr''' ({{IPA|cs|ˈjaromiːr ˈjaːɡr̩|-|Cs-Jaromir Jagr.ogg}}; born 15 February 1972) is a Czech professional [[ice hockey]] player who is a [[Winger (ice hockey)|right winger]] and owner of [[Rytíři Kladno]] of the [[Czech Extraliga]] (ELH). He previously played in the [[National Hockey League]] (NHL) for the [[Pittsburgh Penguins]], [[Washington Capitals]], [[New York Rangers]], [[Philadelphia Flyers]], [[Dallas Stars]], [[Boston Bruins]], [[New Jersey Devils]], [[Florida Panthers]], and [[Calgary Flames]], serving as captain of the Penguins from 1998 to 2001 and the Rangers between 2006 and 2008.\n\nAfter leaving the Rangers in 2008, he played three seasons in the [[Kontinental Hockey League]] (KHL) with [[Avangard Omsk]]. He returned to the NHL in 2011 with the Flyers and remained in the league for seven more years before being assigned by the Flames in 2018 to HC Kladno. Having played in 37 professional seasons (as of 2024)<ref>{{cite web |title=Jaromir Jagr makes season debut for Kladno Knights at age 51 |url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/story/_/id/39160115/jaromir-jagr-makes-season-debut-kladno-knights-age-51 |access-date=21 December 2023 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press |date=20 December 2023}}</ref> and over 2,000 professional games, Jágr has had the longest playing career in professional ice hockey history. He is the most productive European player who has ever played in the NHL and is widely regarded as one of the greatest players ever.\n\nJágr has the second-most [[Point (ice hockey)|points]] in NHL history, after [[Wayne Gretzky]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Skater Records, Most Career Points|url=https://records.nhl.com/records/skater-records/points/most-points-career|website=NHL.com|access-date=24 December 2024}}</ref> In 1990, at age 18, he was the youngest player in the NHL. Until his transfer, at age 45, he was the oldest player in the NHL and is the oldest player to record a [[hat-trick]].<ref>{{cite news | last= Rosen | first= Dan | url= https://www.nhl.com/gamecenter/phi-vs-njd/2015/01/03/2014020568 | title= Jagr becomes oldest to net hat trick, Devils rout Flyers | publisher= NHL | date= 4 January 2015 | access-date= 22 June 2015}}</ref> In 2017, Jágr was named one of the [[100 Greatest NHL Players]] in history.<ref>{{cite web|title=100 Greatest NHL Players|url=https://www.nhl.com/history/nhl-centennial/nhl-100-greatest-players|website=NHL.com|access-date=27 January 2017|date=27 January 2017}}</ref>\n\nJágr was the fifth overall selection in the [[1990 NHL entry draft]]. He won consecutive [[Stanley Cup]]s in the [[1990–91 NHL season|1991]] and [[1991–92 NHL season|1992 season]]s with the Penguins. Individually, he has won the [[Art Ross Trophy]] as the NHL scoring champion five times (four times in a row), the [[Ted Lindsay Award|Lester B. Pearson Award]] for the NHL's outstanding player as voted by the [[National Hockey League Players' Association|NHL Players' Association]] (NHLPA) three times, and the [[Hart Memorial Trophy]] as the league's most valuable player once, in 1999, while finishing second four times.\n\nJágr is a member of the [[Triple Gold Club]], individuals who have played for teams that have won the [[Stanley Cup]] (1991, 1992), the [[Ice Hockey World Championships]] (2005, 2010) and the [[Ice hockey at the 1998 Winter Olympics|Olympic gold medal in ice hockey]] (1998). Jágr is one of only two Czech players (the other being [[Jiří Šlégr]]) in the club, achieving this feat in 2005.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.iihf.com/iihf-home/history/the-iihf/triple-gold-club.html |title=Triple Gold Club |publisher=Iihf.com |access-date=14 November 2012}}</ref> Jágr was the [[Czech Republic men's national ice hockey team|Czech Republic]]'s flag bearer at the [[2010 Winter Olympics]]. Jágr is also one of only three players from [[1980–81 NHL season|1981]] to [[2000–01 NHL season|2001]] to win the Art Ross Trophy as the leading point-scorer during the regular season; the others are [[Wayne Gretzky]] and [[Mario Lemieux]]. Jágr has won the award more times than any other non-Canadian player. He has been a member of the [[Czech Ice Hockey Hall of Fame]] since 2008 and the [[IIHF Hall of Fame]] since 2024.\n\n==Playing career==\n===Early career===\nJágr began skating at age three, and he immediately showed exceptional abilities. At age 15, he played at the highest level of competition in Czechoslovakia for [[Rytíři Kladno|Poldi SONP Kladno]]. When he was 17, he became the youngest member of the [[Czechoslovakia men's national ice hockey team|Czechoslovakia national team]].<ref name=\"SIKladno\"/>\n\nAs a youth in his native country, he kept a photograph of American president [[Ronald Reagan]] in his school grade book as a protest against the policies of the [[Soviet Union]].<ref name=\"SIKladno\"/>\n\n===Pittsburgh Penguins (1990–2001)===\nJágr was the first Czechoslovak player to be drafted by the NHL without having to defect to the West; his selection in the NHL draft came as the [[Iron Curtain]] fell.<ref name=\"defect\">{{cite news|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/olympics/events/1998/nagano/athletes/122.htm |title=Athlete profile: Jaromir Jagr |access-date=25 August 2007 |publisher=[[CNN]] |date=3 February 1998 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080508030737/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/olympics/events/1998/nagano/athletes/122.htm |archive-date=8 May 2008}}</ref> Because of this, after Jágr was selected by the [[Pittsburgh Penguins]] with the fifth overall pick in the [[1990 NHL entry draft]], he was able to relocate to North America from Czechoslovakia immediately. When he attended the draft in [[Vancouver]], he was the first Czechoslovak player present at the NHL draft with his government's blessings.<ref name=\"SIKladno\"/>\n\nJágr was a supporting player with the powerhouse Penguins that won back-to-back [[Stanley Cup]]s in [[1991 Stanley Cup Final|1991]] and [[1992 Stanley Cup Final|1992]]. He was one of the youngest players in NHL history, at age 20, to score a goal in the [[Stanley Cup Final]].\n\nBefore he had a clear grasp of the [[English language]], Jágr could be heard reading the daily weather forecast on [[Pittsburgh]] radio station [[WDVE]] in his broken, thickly-accented English. He and teammate (and fellow countryman) [[Jiří Hrdina]] were promoted as the \"Czechmates\", a play on the term \"[[checkmate]]\" from [[chess]]. He also played ''[[Scrabble]]'' to increase his English vocabulary. Some Penguins fans realized that the letters in his first name could be scrambled to form the [[anagram]] \"Mario Jr.\", a reference to teammate [[Mario Lemieux]].\n\nIn the [[1994–95 NHL season|1994–95 season]], Jágr won his first [[Art Ross Trophy]] after finishing the regular season with the most points in the NHL; he tied [[Eric Lindros]] with 70 points but won based on his 32 goals to Lindros' 29. Jágr set a record for most points, 149, by a European-born player the following year. His 62 goals and 87 assists from that season still stand as career highs. His [[1995–96 NHL season|1995–96]] totals for assists and points stand as the records for right-wingers in those categories. After the [[1997–98 NHL season|1997–98 season]], Penguins captain [[Ron Francis]] signed with the [[Carolina Hurricanes]], leaving Jágr the Penguins' captaincy. From [[1997–98 NHL season|1997–98]] to [[2000–01 NHL season|2000–01]], Jágr would win four straight NHL scoring titles. In 1999, he would win the [[Hart Memorial Trophy]] as the NHL's [[most valuable player]], as well as the [[Lester B. Pearson Award]]. In 1998, he led the [[Czech Republic men's national ice hockey team|Czech Republic]] to a gold medal at the [[Ice hockey at the 1998 Winter Olympics|1998 Winter Olympics]].\n\nOn 30 December 1999, against the [[New York Islanders]], Jágr scored three goals and four assists for a career-high seven-point night. He would later match this feat on 11 January 2003 by once again scoring three goals and four assists in a game against the [[Florida Panthers]] as a member of the [[Washington Capitals]].\n\nIn [[2000–01 NHL season|2000–01]], Jágr was struggling to find his scoring touch and faced criticisms about his relationship with Penguins head coach [[Ivan Hlinka]].<ref name=\"Struggle\">{{cite news |date=9 December 2000 |title=Super disappointment - Frustrated Jagr struggles to find lost scoring touch |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/hockey/nhl/news/2000/12/09/frustrated_jagr_ap/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010713005827/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/hockey/nhl/news/2000/12/09/frustrated_jagr_ap/ |archive-date=13 July 2001 |access-date=23 March 2025 |work=CNN|agency=Associated Press}}</ref> With the return of Mario Lemieux from retirement, the Penguins had two superstars, but friction developed between the two; Jágr continued to hold the captaincy for the rest of the season even after Lemieux returned, but many fans regarded Lemieux as the [[talisman]] of the team. Additionally, the struggling, medium-market Penguins could, with Lemieux back, no longer hope to afford Jágr's high salary. Thus, on 11 July 2001, the organization traded him, along with [[František Kučera]], to the Washington Capitals in exchange for [[Kris Beech]], [[Michal Sivek]] and [[Ross Lupaschuk]].\n\nIn 806 games with Pittsburgh, Jágr became only the second player (after Lemieux) to score 1,000 points as a Penguin. Jágr sits second behind Lemieux in career goals in franchise history and third in games played, assists, and points, having since been surpassed by [[Sidney Crosby]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kasan |first1=Sam |title=Crosby continues writing his legacy with recent milestones |url=https://www.nhl.com/penguins/news/crosby-continues-writing-his-legacy-with-recent-milestones/c-295881530 |access-date=23 March 2025|website=NHL.com |date=12 February 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180213022254/https://www.nhl.com/penguins/news/crosby-continues-writing-his-legacy-with-recent-milestones/c-295881530 |archive-date=13 February 2018}}</ref> His no. 68 jersey was eventually retired in a pregame ceremony on 18 February 2024, with Jágr becoming just the third Penguins player to receive the honour.<ref>{{cite web |last=Gulitti |first=Tom |title=Jagr's No. 68 retired by Penguins in 'great day' for legend |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/jaromir-jagr-number-68-retired-by-pittsburgh-penguins |website=NHL.com |access-date=19 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240219185257/https://www.nhl.com/news/jaromir-jagr-number-68-retired-by-pittsburgh-penguins |archive-date=19 February 2024 |date=18 February 2024}}</ref>\n\n===Washington Capitals (2001–2004)===\nLater in 2001, the Capitals signed Jágr to the then-largest contract in NHL history at $77&nbsp;million over seven years, an average annual value of $11&nbsp;million, with an option for an eighth year.<ref>{{cite news |date=19 October 2001 |title=Jagr, Capitals Agree to Deal for $88 Million |newspaper=LA Times |agency=Associated Press |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2001-oct-19-sp-59012-story.html |access-date=8 May 2022}}</ref> However, Jágr did not live up to expectations in Washington, as the Capitals failed to defend their division title and missed the [[2002 Stanley Cup playoffs]]. During his tenure with the Capitals, for the first time in his career Jágr failed to finish among the NHL's top scorers, help his team qualify for the [[Stanley Cup playoffs]], or make the [[NHL All-Star team]]. During the summer of 2002, the Capitals reunited Jágr with former teammate [[Robert Lang (ice hockey)|Robert Lang]]. In [[2002–03 NHL season|2002–03]], Washington finished sixth overall in the [[Eastern Conference (NHL)|Eastern Conference]]. Still, it lost to the upstart [[Tampa Bay Lightning]] in the first round of the [[2003 Stanley Cup playoffs|2003 playoffs]] despite winning the series' first two games.<ref>{{cite web |title=2002-2003 NHL Hockey Standings |url=https://www.nhl.com/standings/2002/conference |access-date=8 May 2022 |website=NHL.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=2002-03 Washington Capitals Schedule and Results |url=https://www.hockey-reference.com/teams/WSH/2003_games.html |access-date=8 May 2022 |website=Hockey-Reference.com}}</ref>\n\nThe lack of organizational success prompted the Capitals to [[Fire sale (sports)|unload much of their high-priced talent]] to save money—not just a cost-cutting spree, but also an acknowledgment that their attempt to build a contender with high-priced veteran talent had failed. Disgruntled, Washington ownership spent much of 2003 trying to trade Jágr. Still, a year before a new [[NHL Collective Bargaining Agreement|Collective Bargaining Agreement]] (CBA) was to be signed, few teams were willing to risk $11&nbsp;million on Jágr.\n\nOn 23 January 2004, Jágr was eventually traded to the [[New York Rangers]] in exchange for [[Anson Carter]] and an agreement that Washington would pay approximately $4&nbsp;million per year of Jágr's salary. Jágr also agreed to defer (with interest) $1&nbsp;million per year for the remainder of his contract to allow the trade to go through.<ref name=\"trade\">{{cite web |date=26 January 2004 |title=Capitals get Carter in return |url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/news/story?id=1716156 |access-date=25 August 2007 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}}</ref>\n\n===New York Rangers (2004–2008)===\n[[File:Jaromir Jagr picks stick 2008-05-04.JPG|thumb|Jágr with the Rangers in the [[2008 Stanley Cup playoffs|2008 playoffs.]]]]\nDue to the new CBA signed before the start of the [[2005–06 NHL season|2005–06 season]], Jágr's salary was reduced to $7.8&nbsp;million, the maximum allowed under the terms of the new salary cap.\n\nDuring the [[2004–05 NHL lockout|NHL labor dispute in 2004–05]], he played for HC Kladno in the Czech Republic and, afterward, for [[Avangard Omsk]] in the [[Russian Superleague]] (RSL).\n\nJágr led the Czech Republic to gold at the [[2005 Men's World Ice Hockey Championships|2005 World Hockey Championships]] in Austria and was elected a tournament all-star. He also became a member of hockey's prestigious [[Triple Gold Club]], players who have won a [[Stanley Cup]], a [[Ice Hockey World Championships|World Hockey Championship]] and an [[Olympic Games|Olympic]] gold medal.\n\nBefore the 2005–06 season, the Rangers had missed the playoffs for seven consecutive seasons. Following the [[Fire sale (sports)|fire sale]] of the high-priced, underachieving veterans that made up the team's roster (as well as the retirement of long-time captain [[Mark Messier]]), many experts picked the Rangers to be the worst team in the NHL. Jágr disagreed and promised the team would surprise many people and make the Stanley Cup playoffs. He started strong during the beginning of the 2005 season and the return from the lockout of the NHL. He became only the fourth player in NHL history to score ten or more goals in less than ten games at the start of a season. His return to dominance helped the Rangers return to the Stanley Cup playoffs, but injuries to Jágr and others contributed to a four-game sweep in the first round by the [[New Jersey Devils]].\n\nJágr scored his 1,400th point on a power-play goal against the [[Philadelphia Flyers]] on 2 March 2006, pushing him past [[Jari Kurri]] into second place all-time among European-born players. He later passed [[Stan Mikita]] to become the all-time leader.\n\nOn 18 March 2006, against the [[Toronto Maple Leafs]], Jágr became only the sixth Rangers player in team history to break the 100-point barrier, and became the only Ranger right winger to score 100 points in a season.\n\nOn 27 March 2006, against the [[Buffalo Sabres]], Jágr had a goal and an assist, which tied both the Rangers' single-season goal record of 52 ([[Adam Graves]], [[1993–94 NHL season|1993–94]]) and the Rangers' single-season points record of 109 ([[Jean Ratelle]], [[1971–72 NHL season|1971–72]]). Two nights later, on 29 March, Jágr passed Ratelle when he assisted on [[Petr Průcha]]'s first-period goal against the New York Islanders' [[Rick DiPietro]]. On 8 April, against the [[Boston Bruins]], Jágr scored his NHL-leading 53rd goal of the season, breaking the Rangers' single-season goals record.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2006/04/09/jagrs-53rd-goal-a-rangers-record/|title=Jagr's 53rd goal a Rangers record|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|date=9 April 2006|access-date=15 November 2014}}</ref>\n\n[[File:Jaromirjagr 2006nhlawards.jpg|thumb|left|Jágr at the 2006 NHL Awards Show|alt= Jágr, a caucasian man with short, brown hair, has his head turned down slightly and is wearing a black suit and tie with a white dress shirt.]]\nAfter leading the NHL in points and goals for most of the 2005–06 season, Jágr was surpassed by the [[San Jose Sharks]]' duo of [[Joe Thornton]] (125 points) and [[Jonathan Cheechoo]] (56 goals), losing both the Art Ross and [[Maurice \"Rocket\" Richard Trophy|Maurice Richard]] trophies in the final week of the season. Jágr finished with 123 points, 54 goals, and 24 power-play goals, second in the NHL in all three categories. He also finished third in the NHL in both assists (69) and [[Plus–minus (sports)|plus-minus]] (+34). However, just as in Washington, playoff success was not to be for Jágr, whose Rangers were swept in four games by New Jersey. In the series, he suffered a [[shoulder problems|dislocated shoulder]] in the third period of the first game, which kept him from playing at his top form for the rest of the series. Jágr had surgery on the shoulder after the Rangers were eliminated from the playoffs.<ref name=\"Shoulder\">{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/news/story?id=2437895|title=Rangers' Jagr has shoulder surgery|access-date=26 September 2006|publisher=ESPN |year=2006}}</ref>\n\nDespite being inched out by Joe Thornton for the Art Ross Trophy and Hart Trophy (league MVP), Jágr won his third Lester B. Pearson Award as the NHL's most outstanding player. During his acceptance speech for the Award, Jágr said, \"With this award, you get voted on by players you play against every night, and I think they understand the game better than the media.\"<ref name=\"pearson\">{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/news/story?id=2497134|title=Thornton, Lidstrom, Ovechkin win at NHL awards|access-date=29 July 2022|publisher=ESPN |date=23 June 2006}}</ref> He has been named to seven [[NHL All-Star team|NHL first All-Star teams]].\n\nOn 5 October 2006, before the first game of the [[2006–07 NHL season|2006–07 season]] (against his former team Washington), Jágr was named as the 24th [[Captain (ice hockey)|captain]] in the history of the New York Rangers, replacing Mark Messier, who had retired before the 2005–06 season. Jágr scored a goal on his first shift in the game, just under 30 seconds into the new season.\n\nJágr became the 16th player to score 600 career NHL goals on 19 November 2006 against Tampa Bay goaltender [[Johan Holmqvist]]. Power play linemate [[Brendan Shanahan]] had scored his 600th goal almost three weeks earlier, making them the first teammates in NHL history to score their 600th goal in the same season.\n\nOn 10 February 2007, against Washington, Jágr earned an assist on a goal by [[Michal Rozsíval]] to record his 1,500th career point. He is only the 12th NHLer to reach this mark and the fourth-fastest player to do so after [[Marcel Dionne]], Mario Lemieux, and [[Wayne Gretzky]].\n\nOn 5 April 2007, against the [[Montreal Canadiens]], Jágr scored his 30th goal of the 2006–07 season, tying the NHL record held by [[Mike Gartner]]. Thus, Jágr has now scored 30 or more goals in 15 consecutive seasons.\n\nAfter a regular season slowed by a weak shoulder, Jágr then led the New York Rangers to a sweep of the [[Atlanta Thrashers]] in the [[2007 Stanley Cup playoffs|Eastern Conference quarterfinals]], the Rangers would fall to the [[Buffalo Sabres]] in game six of the conference semifinals.\n\nOn 14 November 2007, against New Jersey, Jágr scored his fourth goal of the [[2007–08 NHL season|2007–08 season]] at the [[Prudential Center]] in [[Newark, New Jersey|Newark]], making him the first player to score a goal in 53 different NHL arenas.\n\n===Avangard Omsk (2008–2011)===\n[[File:Яромир Ягр 68 ХК Авангард Омск.jpg|thumb|Jágr sitting in a [[penalty box]] while playing with Omsk, August 2008]]\nOn 3 July 2008, Jágr, an unrestricted [[free agent]] for the first time in his career, was informed by Rangers general manager [[Glen Sather]] that the club would not offer him a new contract. Sather admitted that the two sides never engaged in detailed negotiations for a new contract and that after many months of speculation, Jágr was \"seriously considering\" going to Russia to finish his career despite offers from other NHL teams.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.newsday.com/sports/hockey/rangers/ny-sprang0704,0,5525930.story|title=Never close to a deal, Rangers say goodbye to Jagr|access-date=3 July 2008|newspaper=[[Newsday]]|year=2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080706225041/http://www.newsday.com/sports/hockey/rangers/ny-sprang0704,0,5525930.story|archive-date=6 July 2008}}</ref> Jágr expressed a desire to possibly finish out his career at his father's club, HC Kladno.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/07/05/sports/hockey/05jagr.html?ref=hockey.story|title=Jagr's New York Exit Becomes N.H.L. Farewell|access-date=5 July 2008|newspaper=New York Times| first=Lynn | last=Zinser | date=5 July 2008}}</ref> On 4 July, Jágr agreed to a two-year contract with [[Avangard Omsk]] of the [[Kontinental Hockey League]] (KHL); the contract was reported to pay Jágr the equivalent of US$5&nbsp;million annually.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tsn.ca/nhl/story/?id=242465 |title=Jagr signs two-year deal with Avangard Omsk |access-date=4 July 2008 |publisher=[[The Sports Network|TSN.ca]] |year=2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140413144619/http://www.tsn.ca/nhl/story/?id=242465 |archive-date=13 April 2014 |url-status=dead}}</ref>\n\nJágr was named Avangard's captain on 30 January 2009. As a member of Avangard, Jágr was sitting next to [[Alexei Cherepanov]], a first-round pick of the New York Rangers, who died during a game against [[Vityaz Chekhov]]. They were discussing the past shift when the 19-year-old Cherepanov collapsed onto Jágr on the bench at the [[Ice Hockey Center 2004]] in [[Chekhov, Moscow Oblast|Chekov]].\n\nIn April 2009, Jágr publicly stated an interest in returning to the NHL, stating that he needed a break from the pressures of an 82-game NHL schedule. Jágr, who claimed to have lost 15 pounds since his last NHL season, and who was \"practicing a lot harder than [he] ever did in [his] life\", stated that he would be interested in joining the [[Edmonton Oilers]] because of the interest they showed in July 2008.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://tsn.ca/nhl/story/?id=277073|title=Jagr Says Oilers Would be His First Choice for Return to NHL|access-date=2 May 2009|publisher=[[The Sports Network|TSN]]|year=2009|archive-date=3 May 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090503222701/http://www.tsn.ca/nhl/story/?id=277073|url-status=dead}}</ref> However, following the expiration of his initial contract with Avangard, Jágr signed a new contract with Avangard for the [[2010–11 KHL season|2010–11 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/news/story?id=5165917|title=Jagr stays with Avangard Omsk|publisher=ESPN (via Associated Press)|date=6 May 2010|access-date=6 May 2010}}</ref>\n\n===Philadelphia Flyers (2011–2012)===\n[[File:Jaromir Jagr Watching 2011-12-29.JPG|upright|thumb|Jágr with the Flyers in 2011]]\nOn 1 July 2011, Jágr returned to the NHL, signing a one-year, $3.3&nbsp;million contract with Pittsburgh's [[Flyers–Penguins rivalry|cross-state rival]], the [[Philadelphia Flyers]].<ref name='2011contract'>{{cite news | title=Jaromir Jagr returns to the NHL, signs one-year deal with new-look Flyers | date=1 July 2011 | url=http://www.startribune.com/sports/124868934.html | agency=Associated Press | access-date=8 January 2013 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130108134311/http://www.startribune.com//sports/124868934.html?refer=y | archive-date=8 January 2013}}</ref> He scored his 1,600th NHL point during his debut game with the Flyers, assisting on a [[Claude Giroux]] goal as the Flyers won their season opener 2–1 over the Boston Bruins on 6 October 2011. Typically playing on the first line with Giroux and [[Scott Hartnell]], Jágr was among the top scorers during the start of the [[2011–12 NHL season|2011–12 season]]. He scored his first and second goals as a Flyer on 24 October against the Toronto Maple Leafs.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nhl.com/gamecenter/tor-vs-phi/2011/10/24/2011020110 |title=Toronto Maple Leafs at Philadelphia Flyers Game Recap – 10/24/2011 |publisher=NHL.com |access-date=14 November 2012}}</ref> On 29 October 2011, against the Carolina Hurricanes, he scored his 650th and 651st NHL goals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nhl.com/gamecenter/car-vs-phi/2011/10/29/2011020145 |title=Carolina Hurricanes at Philadelphia Flyers Game Recap – 10/29/2011 |publisher=NHL.com |date=29 October 2011 |access-date=14 November 2012}}</ref> He scored his only goal of the [[2012 Stanley Cup playoffs|2012 playoffs]] during Philadelphia's series against Pittsburgh. The Flyers were eliminated by the New Jersey Devils, who would ultimately become the 2012 Eastern Conference champions.\n\n===Dallas Stars (2012–2013)===\nOn 3 July 2012, Jágr signed a one-year contract with the [[Dallas Stars]] reportedly worth $4.5&nbsp; million. The signing marked Jágr's first time playing for a club in the [[Western Conference (NHL)|Western Conference]]. Jágr said during a [[conference call]] two days later that the Montreal Canadiens had been his first choice as a free agent. \"I always wanted to play in Canada, and I wanted to go to [[Montreal]] if I had a chance, but Montreal wasn't interested,\" Jágr said. \"All of a sudden, I got a phone call from Stars' general manager [[Joe Nieuwendyk]] that Dallas was interested.\"<ref>{{cite web|url=http://slam.canoe.com/Slam/Hockey/NHL/Dallas/2012/07/05/19956436.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160105114348/http://slam.canoe.com/Slam/Hockey/NHL/Dallas/2012/07/05/19956436.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=5 January 2016 |title=Habs were Jagr's first choice |publisher=canoe.com |date=6 July 2012 |access-date=19 November 2013}}</ref>\n\nDuring the [[2012–13 NHL lockout]], Jágr played for his team, [[HC Kladno|Rytíři Kladno]], in the [[Czech Extraliga]]. During the lockout, he scored 24 goals and 33 assists in 34 games and, before leaving Kladno for the Stars, was in second place on Czech Extraliga's scoring list. After the NHL lockout ended, he made his debut as a Star on 19 January 2013, when he tallied two goals and two assists in a 4–3 victory over the [[Arizona Coyotes|Phoenix Coyotes]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dallasnews.com/sports/dallas-stars/headlines/20130119-jaromir-jagr-2-g-2-a-dazzles-in-dallas-debut-as-stars-outlast-coyotes-4-3.ece |title=The Dallas Morning News &#124; Options |publisher=Dallasnews.com |access-date=19 November 2013}}</ref>\n\nJágr reached the [[List of NHL career assists leaders|1,000-assist mark]] on 29 March 2013 in a game against the [[Minnesota Wild]], becoming just the 12th player to do so and the first non-Canadian NHLer to reach the milestone.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tsn.ca/nhl/story/?id=419437 |title=Jagr reaches assists milestone; Stars end Wild's win streak |publisher=Tsn.ca |date=30 March 2013 |access-date=19 November 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130603205314/http://www.tsn.ca/nhl/story/?id=419437 |archive-date=3 June 2013 |url-status=dead}}</ref>\n\n===Boston Bruins (2013)===\n[[File:Jaromír Jágr 2013-06-07.JPG|thumb|upright|Jágr with the Bruins during the 2013 Eastern Conference finals]]\nOn 2 April 2013, Jágr was traded to the Boston Bruins in exchange for [[Lane MacDermid]], Cody Payne and a conditional [[2013 NHL entry draft|2013]] third-round pick.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tsn.ca/nhl/story/?id=419676 |title=Stars trade Jagr to Bruins for two prospects, draft pick |publisher=Tsn.ca |date=4 February 2013 |access-date=19 November 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130405045838/http://www.tsn.ca/nhl/story/?id=419676 |archive-date=5 April 2013 |url-status=dead}}</ref> He made his Bruins debut on 4 April, scoring the lone goal in Boston's 1–0 win over the New Jersey Devils,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nhl.com/gamecenter/njd-vs-bos/2013/04/04/2012020543|title=New Jersey Devils at Boston Bruins : 04/04/2013 |publisher=[[National Hockey League]] |date=4 April 2013 |access-date=4 December 2015|first1=Matt|last1=Kalman}}</ref> and with his second Bruins goal, the first scored in a 3–0 shutout over the Florida Panthers on 21 April, Jágr tied the record for the most game-winning goals in an NHL career (118), previously set by [[Phil Esposito]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://bruins.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=666949 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130422090330/http://bruins.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=666949 |url-status=dead |archive-date=22 April 2013 |title=Moving in the Right Direction – Jagr Nears Milestone with GWG |last=Switaj |first=Caryn |date=21 April 2013 |publisher=BostonBruins.com |access-date=21 April 2013}}</ref>\n\nWhen Jágr played in the first game of the [[2013 Stanley Cup Final]] on 12 June, he set a new record for the longest gap between Finals appearances at 21 years, surpassing the previous record of 19 years, which was established by [[Gary Roberts (ice hockey)|Gary Roberts]] in [[2008 Stanley Cup Final|2008]];<ref>{{cite web|title=Jagr finally returns to the Finals|url=http://espn.go.com/espn/elias|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090929115634/http://espn.go.com/espn/elias|url-status=dead|archive-date=29 September 2009|work=ESPN – Elias Says|access-date=13 June 2013}}</ref> coincidentally, both instances involved someone with the Penguins at one end of those streaks. Also coincidental was that, as in his previous Stanley Cup appearance, Jágr's opponents were the [[Presidents' Trophy]]-winning [[Chicago Blackhawks]]. He spent the bulk of the Bruins' lengthy playoff run on the top line with [[Brad Marchand]] and [[Patrice Bergeron]]. After the Bruins lost the Final to Chicago in six games, the team announced on 26 June that they did not intend to offer Jágr a new contract.<ref>{{cite news|last=Gretz |first=Adam |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nhl/news/jaromir-jagr-wont-be-back-with-bruins |title=Jaromir Jagr won't be back with Bruins |work=CBSSports.com |access-date=25 January 2021}}</ref>\n\n===New Jersey Devils (2013–2015)===\nOn 22 July 2013, Jágr signed a one-year contract with the New Jersey Devils; the contract included $2&nbsp;million guaranteed and another $2&nbsp;million as an incentive bonus if Jágr was to play in at least 40 games.<ref>{{cite news | last = Mazzeo | first = Mike | title = Report: Jaromir Jagr signs $2 million deal | url = https://www.espn.com/new-york/nhl/story/_/id/9498996/jaromir-jagr-agrees-one-year-deal-new-jersey-devils-source-said | newspaper = ESPN | location = New York | date = 23 July 2013 | access-date = 23 March 2025}}</ref> Jágr, at age 41, hoped to help the Devils overcome the loss of [[Ilya Kovalchuk]], who had previously departed for the KHL. Jágr scored his first goal as a Devil on 7 October, in a 5–4 shootout loss to the Edmonton Oilers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=685897 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141213032449/http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=685897 |url-status=dead |archive-date=13 December 2014 |title=NHL Capsules – NHL.com – News |publisher=NHL.com |access-date=19 November 2013}}</ref> The goal came on the 23rd anniversary of his first NHL goal which, coincidentally, was against the Devils.\n\n[[File:Jaromir Jagr - New Jersey Devils.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Jágr with the Devils in January 2014]]\nOn 21 November, Jágr tied [[Gordie Howe]]'s record of game-winning goals with 121, with his 690th goal, which tied him in ninth place (with former teammate Mario Lemieux) for all-time goal-scoring leaders.<ref>{{cite news|author=Eric Duhatschek |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/sports/hockey/duhatschek-ageless-jagr-reaches-two-more-career-milestones/article15559206/ |title=Ageless Jagr reaches two more career milestones |newspaper=The Globe and Mail |date=22 November 2013 |access-date=20 December 2013}}</ref> On 20 December, he scored his 693rd goal, putting him in eighth place over [[Steve Yzerman]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/careerstats.htm?fetchKey=00002ALLSAHAll&sort=goals&viewName=careerLeadersAllSeasons |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100715160709/http://www.nhl.com/ice/careerstats.htm?fetchKey=00002ALLSAHAll&sort=goals&viewName=careerLeadersAllSeasons |url-status=dead |archive-date=15 July 2010 |title=Regular Season – All Skaters – Career Leaders – All Teams – Career Points – NHL.com – Stats |publisher=NHL.com |access-date=20 December 2013}}</ref> A day later, Jágr tied Mark Messier for seventh place in NHL history for goals scored with 694.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=697112|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131222215946/http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=697112|url-status=dead|archive-date=22 December 2013|title=Jagr ties Messier for seventh place on NHL goals list |publisher=NHL.com |date=21 December 2013 |access-date=21 December 2013}}</ref> Later in the [[2013–14 NHL season|season]], on 14 January 2014, he scored his 695th goal, passing Messier,<ref>{{cite web|author=Rod Perry |url=http://www.cbc.ca/sports/hockey/nhl/jaromir-jagr-scores-695th-career-goal-passes-messier-1.2496846|title=Jaromir Jagr scores 695th career goal, passes Messier|access-date=1 October 2014}}</ref> putting him 14 goals away from passing Mike Gartner. On 1 March, Jágr scored his 700th career NHL goal as the Devils won 6–1 against the New York Islanders at [[Nassau Veterans Memorial Coliseum]].<ref>{{cite news|author=Allan Kreda|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2014/03/02/sports/hockey/jagr-gets-700th-goal-and-devils-rout-the-islanders.html?_r=0|title=Jaromir Jagr Gets 700th Goal, and Devils Rout the Islanders|access-date=1 October 2014|newspaper = The New York Times|date = March 2014}}</ref> On 8 April, near the conclusion of the Devils' season, he was awarded the New Jersey Devils MVP Award at their annual team awards ceremony. He scored two points in his final game of the season (two assists in the third period), surpassing Gordie Howe for eighth place on the NHL's all-time list for career assists and tying Steve Yzerman for sixth on the all-time points list at 1,755.<ref>{{cite web|author=Mike Morreale |url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=714406|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140415072841/http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=714406|url-status=dead|archive-date=15 April 2014|title= Devils' Jagr passes Howe on all-time assists list |publisher=NHL.com|date=13 April 2014 |access-date=13 April 2014}}</ref> Jágr finished the season as the team's leading scorer, with his highest points total in a season since 2007–08. Jágr's play led the Devils to re-sign him to another one-year contract on 30 April.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=720645|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140526041935/http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=720645|url-status=dead|archive-date=26 May 2014|title=Jagr announces retirement from international play|website=NHL.com|access-date=1 October 2014}}</ref> He became the joint sixth-highest scorer in NHL history in November 2014 after scoring his 708th NHL goal for the Devils against Boston.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.radio.cz/en/section/news/jagr-now-joint-sixth-highest-scorer-in-nhl|title=Jágr now joint sixth highest scorer in NHL|work=[[Radio Prague]]|first=Ian|last=Willoughby|date=11 November 2014|access-date=15 November 2014}}</ref> On 8 December, in his 1,500th NHL game, he moved ahead of Marcel Dionne for fifth place on the NHL's all-time points list with 1,772.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=743050|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150510102201/http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=743050|url-status=dead|archive-date=10 May 2015|title=Jagr passes Dionne on all-time points list in 1,500th game|publisher=NHL.com|date=8 December 2014 |access-date=8 December 2014}}</ref> On 3 January 2015, in a game against the Philadelphia Flyers, Jágr became the oldest player in NHL history to score a hat-trick at 42 years and 322 days.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jaromir Jagr's 15th career hat trick propels Devils over Flyers |url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/recap?gameId=400564283 |website=ESPN |access-date=23 March 2025 |date=3 January 2015}}</ref> The record was previously held by [[Detroit Red Wings]] defenceman [[Nicklas Lidström]].\n\n===Florida Panthers (2015–2017)===\nOn 26 February 2015, Jágr was traded to the Florida Panthers in exchange for a [[2015 NHL entry draft|2015]] second-round pick and a [[2016 NHL entry draft|2016]] third-round pick.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jaromir Jagr traded to Florida Panthers by New Jersey Devils|url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=755329|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150227004101/http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=755329|url-status=dead|archive-date=27 February 2015|website=NHL.com|access-date=27 February 2015}}</ref> He made his team debut on 28 February in a 5–3 Panthers win over the Buffalo Sabres and registered his first points with the team in the following game on 1 March, posting a goal and an assist in a 4–3 win over the Tampa Bay Lightning.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jagr helps Panthers edge Lightning|url=https://www.nhl.com/gamecenter/tbl-vs-fla/2015/03/01/2014020934|website=NHL.com|access-date=1 March 2015}}</ref> On 19 March, Jágr scored his 718th career goal against Detroit to move him past Phil Esposito and fifth on the all-time goal-scoring list.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jaromir Jagr scores 718th goal, passes Esposito for fifth all-time|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nhl/news/video-jaromir-jagr-scores-718th-goal-passes-esposito-for-fifth-all-time|website=cbssports.com|date=19 March 2015 |access-date=25 January 2021}}</ref> In a 9 April, 4–2 Panthers victory over the Bruins, Jágr registered two assists to give him 1,800 career points in the NHL and sole possession of fourth place on the all-time points list, surpassing former Penguins teammate Ron Francis.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Gorten|first1=Steve|title=Bruins lose to Panthers, out of playoff position|url=https://www.nhl.com/gamecenter/bos-vs-fla/2015/04/09/2014021207|website=NHL.com|access-date=10 April 2015}}</ref> On 11 April, in the Panthers' season finale, Jágr reached 2,000 NHL points (including playoff games) when he assisted on a [[Jonathan Huberdeau]] goal. He scored his 800th NHL goal (including playoffs) later in the third period.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jaromír Jágr 2014-15 Scoring Log |url=https://www.hockey-reference.com/players/j/jagrja01/scoring/2015/ |website=Hockey-Reference.com |access-date=23 March 2025}}</ref> On 12 April, one day after the end of the 2014–15 regular season, Jágr signed a new one-year, $3.5&nbsp;million contract with Florida for the [[2015–16 NHL season|2015–16 season]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Jagr signs one-year contract with Panthers|url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=762937&|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160105114347/http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=762937&|url-status=dead|archive-date=5 January 2016|website=NHL.com|access-date=12 April 2015}}</ref>\n\n[[File:Jagr Panthers.jpg|thumb|upright|Jágr with the Panthers in 2016]]\nJágr reached multiple milestones as a Panther. On 20 December 2015, he scored his 732nd goal, passing Marcel Dionne for fourth place in NHL history.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gereffi |first1=Paul |title=Jaromir Jagr moves into fourth all-time on NHL scoring list |url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/hockey/2015/12/21/jaromir-jagr-moves-into-fourth-all-time-on-nhl-scoring-list.html |website=Toronto Star |access-date=23 March 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151221145708/https://www.thestar.com/sports/hockey/2015/12/21/jaromir-jagr-moves-into-fourth-all-time-on-nhl-scoring-list.html |archive-date=21 December 2015 |date=21 December 2015}}</ref> On 4 February 2016, Jágr became the sixth player in NHL history to record 1,100 career assists. On 20 February, he scored his 742nd goal, surpassing [[Brett Hull]] for third place in NHL history.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jagr gets No. 742, passes Hull for third|url=https://www.nhl.com/news/jaromir-jagr-scores-goal-742-passes-brett-hull-279023196|website=NHL.com|access-date=20 February 2016}}</ref> In a 7 March, 5–4 overtime loss to the Bruins, an assist on [[Aleksander Barkov]]'s goal put Jágr at 1,851 career points, passing Gordie Howe on the all-time points list and putting him in sole possession of third place overall.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Poupart|first1=Alain|title=Jagr passes Howe on points list|url=https://www.nhl.com/news/jaromir-jagr-gordie-howe-third-nhl-points-list-279439158|website=NHL.com|access-date=8 March 2016}}</ref> With the Panthers qualifying for the [[2016 Stanley Cup playoffs|2016 playoffs]], Jágr played in his first playoff series since the 2013 Stanley Cup Finals. Though he only registered two assists in the Panthers' six-game first-round exit to the Islanders (who would win their first playoff series since 1993), he became the fifth NHL player all-time to record 200 career playoff points.<ref>{{cite news|title=Jagr Becomes 5th Player with 200 Career Playoff Points|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2634608-jagr-becomes-5th-player-with-200-career-playoff-points|access-date=25 April 2016|agency=Bleacher Report|date=22 April 2016}}</ref>\n\nAt age 44, Jágr led the Panthers in scoring with 66 points. In reward for his strong play and leadership abilities, the team announced on 5 May 2016 that they had signed Jágr to a new one-year, $4&nbsp;million contract.<ref>{{cite news|title=Panthers re-sign Jagr to one-year deal|url=https://www.tsn.ca/panthers-re-sign-jagr-to-one-year-deal-1.484322|access-date=5 May 2016|agency=TSN|date=5 May 2016}}</ref>\n\nOn 20 October 2016, Jágr became the third player in NHL history to score 750 goals.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jaromir Jagr scores 750th NHL goal|url=https://www.nhl.com/news/jaromir-jagr-scores-750th-nhl-goal-282885120|website=NHL.com|access-date=21 October 2016|date=20 October 2016}}</ref> On 22 December 2016, he scored his 1,888th career point, surpassing Mark Messier to become second in career points,<ref>{{cite web|last1=Menning|first1=Rick|title=Jaromir Jagr breaks tie for No. 2, Panthers fall to Bruins|url=https://www.apnews.com/4f64fc06e88a4b3b80dfec3f779d5f1c/Jaromir-Jagr-breaks-tie-for-No.-2,-Panthers-fall-to-Bruins|access-date=16 February 2017|website=Associated Press|date=23 December 2016}}</ref> and on 15 February 2017, his 45th birthday, he became the second player to register his 1,900th NHL point.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jaromir Jagr gets 1,900th NHL point|url=https://www.nhl.com/news/panthers-jaromir-jagr-gets-1-900th-nhl-point-286812622|website=NHL.com|access-date=16 February 2017|date=15 February 2017}}</ref>\n\nIn 2017 on Twitter, as a free agent, Jágr tweeted: \"FA 1994 - all GMs called, FA 2017- 0 calls\" accompanied by a trophy emoji and a smiley emoji and pictures taken in 1994 and 2017. In the 1994 picture, a smiling Jágr is on the phone with an unspecified general manager. In the 2017 picture, he looks at his mobile phone with a puzzled expression.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/68Jagr/status/880561778068930560|title=FA 1994- all GMs called, FA 2017- 0 callspic.twitter.com/7uLJm95CAB|last=Jagr|first=Jaromir|date=29 June 2017|website=@68Jagr|access-date=2 July 2017}}</ref> The Panthers organization announced shortly after that they would not offer Jágr a new contract.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jagr won't be back with Panthers |url=https://www.tsn.ca/jagr-likely-won-t-be-back-with-panthers-1.794113 |website=TSN.ca |access-date=23 March 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170701145856/https://www.tsn.ca/jagr-likely-won-t-be-back-with-panthers-1.794113 |archive-date=1 July 2017 |date=1 July 2017}}</ref>\n\n===Calgary Flames (2017–2018)===\nOn 4 October 2017, Jágr signed a one-year contract with the [[Calgary Flames]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Flames Sign Jagr|url=https://www.nhl.com/flames/news/flames-sign-jagr-291572024|website=NHL.com|access-date=5 October 2017|date=4 October 2017}}</ref> Jágr had indicated before that he would like to play professionally until age 50,<ref>{{cite web|title=Jaromír Jágr wants to play until 50|url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/story/_/id/19046492/nhl-qa-ageless-florida-panthers-winger-jaromir-jagr-reveals-why-smiles-much-secret-scoring-how-able-keep-pesky-kids|website=ESPN |access-date=5 May 2017|date=5 April 2017}}</ref> but later said that it would be very likely that he would stop playing after the [[2017–18 NHL season|2017–18 season]], at which point he would be 46.<ref name=999percent>{{cite web|title=Jaromir Jagr says '99.9 per cent' this will be his last season|url=http://www.sportsnet.ca/hockey/nhl/jaromir-jagr-says-99-9-per-cent-will-last-nhl-season/|website=Sportsnet.ca|access-date=4 October 2017|date=4 October 2017}}</ref> He noted the tendency of teams to focus on younger players to the exclusion of older ones like himself, which he considers understandable and in light of which he remarked, \"I was pretty lucky.\"<ref name=999percent/> The Flames were Jágr's ninth NHL team, but his first Canadian team, which prompted him to say, \"I want to get the experience so I can one day say I played for a Canadian team. So I'm here.\"<ref name=999percent/>\n\nOn 9 November 2017 against the Detroit Red Wings, Jágr scored his first goal as a Flame, earning two points in a 6–3 win. However, on 6 January 2018, it was reported that Jágr and the Flames were negotiating the termination of his contract, as injuries had limited Jágr to a career-low seven points (including the one goal above) in 22 games.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Johnston|first1=Mike|title=Calgary Flames, Jaromir Jagr working on an exit|url=http://www.sportsnet.ca/hockey/nhl/flames-jaromir-jagr-working-exit/|website=sportsnet.ca|access-date=6 January 2018|date=6 January 2018}}</ref> On 14 January 2018, Jágr was placed on the injured reserve, retroactive to 31 December 2017, while the Flames called up [[Ryan Lomberg]] from their [[American Hockey League]] (AHL) affiliate, the [[Stockton Heat]], in his place.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jagr placed on injured reserve by Flames|url= https://www.nhl.com/news/calgary-flames-place-jaromir-jagr-on-injured-reserve-294946594|website=NHL.com|date=14 January 2018|access-date=20 January 2018}}</ref> On 28 January, it was reported that Jágr was placed on waivers, signalling the end of his brief tenure with the Flames;<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.sportsnet.ca/hockey/nhl/calgary-flames-waive-jaromir-jagr/|title=Calgary Flames to waive Jaromir Jagr - Sportsnet.ca|work=Sportsnet.ca|access-date=28 January 2018}}</ref> he cleared waivers the following day and was assigned to Rytíři Kladno in the [[1st Czech Republic Hockey League|WSM Liga]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Flames Assign Jaromir Jagr to HC Kladno|url=https://www.nhl.com/flames/news/flames-assign-jaromir-jagr-to-hc-kladno-295413028|website=NHL.com|access-date=30 January 2018|date=29 January 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Návrat krále: Rytíři Jaromíru Jágrovi vyřizují transfer kartu z Calgary|url=http://www.hc-kladno.cz/cz/navrat-krale-rytiri-jagrovi-vyrizuji-transfer-kartu-z-calgary|website=www.hc-kladno.cz|access-date=30 January 2018|language=cs-CZ|date=29 January 2018|archive-date=30 January 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180130092954/http://www.hc-kladno.cz/cz/navrat-krale-rytiri-jagrovi-vyrizuji-transfer-kartu-z-calgary|url-status=dead}}</ref>\n\n===Return to Kladno (2018–present)===\nOn 3 February 2018, Jágr played his first game for his hometown team, and his first game since 31 December 2017, playing nearly 20 minutes and recording three assists.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Johnston|first1=Mike|title=Jaromir Jagr lights up scoresheet in first game with Kladno|url=http://www.sportsnet.ca/hockey/nhl/jaromir-jagr-lights-score-sheet-first-game-kladno/|website=sportsnet.ca|access-date=3 February 2018|date=3 February 2018}}</ref> In his fifth game for Kladno, he was injured and remained sidelined for the rest of the season with a knee injury. He played a few seconds in ten playoff games to be eligible for participation in the playoff finals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.idnes.cz/hokej/hokejova-1-liga/jaromir-jagr-kladno-semifinale-prvni-hokejove-ligy.A180312_150440_hok_1liga_par|title=Jágr bude i v semifinále první ligy jenom sbírat starty kvůli baráži|date=12 March 2018|website=iDNES.cz|access-date=29 April 2019}}</ref> On 14 May, Jágr announced his plans to remain with Kladno for his 30th professional season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jágr vybral nové trenéry pro Rytíře! Sám bude za Kladno hrát|url=https://www.sport.cz/hokej/1liga/clanek/989285-jagr-vybral-nove-trenery-pro-rytire-sam-bude-za-kladno-hrat.html|website=sport.cz|access-date=23 May 2018|language=cs-CZ|date=14 May 2018}}</ref> On 19 April, Jágr scored four goals in one game as Kladno was promoted to the top-flight Czech Extraliga.<ref name=\"spor_Jaro\">{{cite web |last=He |first=Eric |date=19 April 2019 |title=Jaromir Jagr casually scores four goals in game to promote club to top Czech league |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/jaromir-jagr-casually-scores-four-goals-in-game-to-promote-club-to-top-czech-league-230231709.html |access-date=21 April 2019 |website=Yahoo! Sports}}</ref>\n\nIn 2022, at the age of 50 and spending most of his games in the dressing room, Jágr admitted he was considering retirement, being too busy with the team administration and lacking the motivation for the physically demanding game, saying that at most he will \"have to force myself to go play\" in the alumni game of the [[2023 NHL Winter Classic]] featuring the Penguins.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jágr připustil konec hráčské kariéry: Postrádám chuť, čas a motivaci...|url=https://isport.blesk.cz/clanek/hokej-tipsport-extraliga/420815/jagr-pripustil-konec-hracske-kariery-postradam-chut-cas-a-motivaci.html|website=isport.cz|author=Horák, Miroslav|access-date=2 October 2022|language=cs-CZ|date=13 October 2022}}</ref> The 2023–24 season marked Jágr's 36th consecutive season of professional ice hockey, and in February 2023 he scored his 1,100th professional goal. Jágr has said that the biggest fear regarding retirement is the potential loss of sponsors for Kladno, thereby jeopardizing Kladno's viability as a team.<ref name=\"nyt\" />\n\nOn 20 December 2023, at 51, Jágr played his first game of his 36th professional season, recording an assist in a 4–3 loss.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jagr starts 36th season, has an assist in Kladno loss |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/jaromir-jagr-begins-36th-professional-hockey-season |website=NHL.com |access-date=21 December 2023 |date=20 December 2023}}</ref>\n\nOn 18 April 2024, at 52 years and 63 days, Jágr scored against [[VHK Vsetín]] to become the oldest player ever to score a goal in a professional competition. He thus broke the record of [[Gordie Howe]], who scored the last goal of his career at 52 years and six days.<ref>{{cite news |last=O'Brien |first=Derek |title=Jágr records 2 points in first game in 2 months; eclipses Howe's age record |url=https://thehockeynews.com/international/latest-news/jagr-records-2-points-in-first-game-in-2-months-eclipses-howes-age-record-record |access-date=24 April 2024 |website=The Hockey News |date=18 April 2024}}</ref>\n\nDuring the 2024 off-season, Jágr hinted on multiple occasions that he would retire from professional ice hockey at the conclusion of the 2024–25 season.<ref>{{cite news |last=O'Brien |first=Derek |title=This will be Jaromír Jágr's last season ... \"in Kladno for sure\" |url=https://thehockeynews.com/international/players/this-will-be-jaromir-jagrs-last-season-in-kladno-for-sure |access-date=5 March 2025 |website=The Hockey News |date=5 June 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Rossi |first=Rob |title=Jaromir Jagr, 52, says he intends to retire from professional hockey after this season |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5780014/2024/09/19/jaromir-jagr-retirement/ |access-date=19 September 2024 |work=The New York Times |issn=0362-4331 |date=19 September 2024}}</ref> However, following Kladno's final game of the season, Jágr avoided answering questions on the topic of retirement, leading to speculation that he would return for a 38th professional season.<ref>{{cite news |last=O'Brien |first=Derek |title=Did Jaromír Jágr Play His Last Career Game On Sunday? Maybe Not, Some Say |url=https://thehockeynews.com/international/latest-news/did-jaromr-jgr-play-his-last-career-game-on-sunday-maybe-not-some-say |access-date=5 March 2025 |website=The Hockey News |date=3 March 2025}}</ref>\n\nOn 28 July 2025, Jágr skated with the Kladno team on the opening day of training camp, further fuelling speculation that he would continue playing.<ref>{{cite web |last1=O'Brien |first1=Derek |title=Jaromír Jágr On The Ice As Kladno's Training Camp Opens – Pro Season No. 38 Coming Up? |url=https://thehockeynews.com/international/latest-news/jaromir-jagr-on-the-ice-as-kladno-s-training-camp-opens-pro-season-no-38-coming-up |website=The Hockey News |access-date=20 September 2025 |date=29 July 2025}}</ref> Jágr made his season debut for Kladno on 17 October, in a 3–1 victory over [[HC Vítkovice Ridera]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Jaromir Jagr is back: At 53, the former NHL great starts his 38th professional season |url=https://apnews.com/article/jaromir-jagr-53-38th-season-kladno-nhl-3d46cccd98f0c001680daa64f0b0b0e3 |access-date=22 October 2025 |website=Associated Press |date=17 October 2025}}</ref>\n\n==International play==\n{{MedalTableTop|Jaromir Jagr Russia vs. Czech Republic.jpg|150px|Jágr during the [[Ice hockey at the 2010 Winter Olympics – Men's tournament|2010 Winter Olympics]] in [[Vancouver]]|name=no|medals=\n{{Medal|Sport | Men's [[ice hockey]]}}\n{{Medal|Country|{{ih|CZE}}}}\n{{Medal|Comp|[[Ice hockey at the Winter Olympics|Winter Olympic]]}}\n{{Medal|Gold|[[1998 Winter Olympics|1998 Nagano]]|}}\n{{Medal|Bronze|[[2006 Winter Olympics|2006 Turin]]|}}\n{{Medal|Competition|[[World Cup of Hockey|World Cup]]}}\n{{Medal|Bronze|[[2004 Championships|1990 Bern]]|}}\n{{Medal|Competition|[[IIHF European Junior Championships|European Junior Championship]]}}\n{{Medal|Silver|[[1989 IIHF European U18 Championship|1989 Kiev]]|}}\n{{Medal|Competition|[[World Junior Ice Hockey Championship|World Junior Championship]]}}\n{{Medal|Bronze|[[1990 World Junior Ice Hockey Championships|1990 Finland]]|}}\n}}\nJágr has represented his country many times. In 1994, he and Pittsburgh Penguins teammate [[Martin Straka]] arrived in the middle of the [[1994 IIHF World Championship|1994 World Championships]] after Pittsburgh's elimination from the Stanley Cup playoffs. Czech fans' expectations were high as Jágr was an NHL star, but before the team could integrate him, the Czechs lost their quarterfinal game and were eliminated. Jágr was also hurt in numerous other games.\n\nThe [[1996 World Cup of Hockey]] also did not see Jágr at his best. The flu hampered his performance and it only underscored the poor play of the whole team — after losing 7–3 to [[Finland men's national ice hockey team|Finland]], 3–0 to [[Sweden men's national ice hockey team|Sweden]] and even 7–1 to a relatively weak [[Germany men's national ice hockey team|Germany]], the team did not qualify for the tournament's playoffs.\n\nThe team's recent failures, however, were mitigated in 1998 when the Czech Republic won the men's gold medal in the [[Ice hockey at the 1998 Winter Olympics|1998 Winter Olympics]] in [[Nagano (city)|Nagano]], [[Japan]]. It was only the third gold medal for Czech or Czechoslovak athletes from the Winter Olympics and is still fondly remembered.\n\nJágr did not play in the [[1996 IIHF World Championship|1996]], [[1999 IIHF World Championship|1999]], [[2000 IIHF World Championship|2000]] nor [[2001 IIHF World Championship|2001 World Championships]] in which the Czech Republic won the gold medals. He was, however, a team member at the [[2004 IIHF World Championship|2004 World Championship]] in Prague, where the expectations were high. However, after the team won all the games in the group, they lost in the quarterfinal game, stumbling out of the tournament.\n\nThe [[2005 IIHF World Championship|2005 edition]] of the tournament finally brought a gold medal to Jágr. Although he broke his finger in an early game against Germany, he played with it bandaged during the tournament, leading his team to victory.\n\nMore injuries struck Jágr in the [[Ice hockey at the 2006 Winter Olympics – Men's tournament|2006 Winter Olympics]] in [[Turin]]. He was injured after a hit from Finland's [[Jarkko Ruutu]], requiring stitches to his eyebrow. However, the injury was not as severe as first anticipated, and Jágr could play in the following games, though he could not finish the bronze medal game due to muscle injury. Despite the trouble, Jágr won his second career Olympic medal. In 2010, Jágr was his nation's flag bearer at the [[2010 Winter Olympics]]. Still, in the [[Ice hockey at the 2010 Winter Olympics – Men's tournament|men's ice hockey tournament]], the Czechs finished a disappointing seventh after defeating Finland in the quarterfinals. Jágr again represented his country at the [[Ice hockey at the 2014 Winter Olympics – Men's tournament|2014 Winter Olympics]] in [[Sochi]], scoring two goals and one assist in five games as the Czech Republic again lost in the quarterfinals.\n\nAfter losing to Sweden in a battle for a bronze medal on [[2014 IIHF World Championship|2014 World Championship]], Jágr announced the end of his career in international play with the Czech national team, focusing his efforts on returning to the NHL playoffs after New Jersey failed to qualify in [[2014 Stanley Cup playoffs|2014]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Yerdon |first=Joe |date=25 May 2014 |title=Jaromir Jagr announces retirement... from Czech National team |url=https://nhl.nbcsports.com/2014/05/25/jaromir-jagr-announces-retirement-from-czech-national-team/ |access-date=16 July 2021 |website=ProHockeyTalk |publisher=NBC Sports}}</ref> However, Jágr stepped back from his decision<ref>{{cite news |date=24 April 2015 |title=Jagr returns from retirement to play for Czechs at worlds |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/jagr-returns-retirement-play-czechs-worlds-193504475--nhl.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150623071715/http://sports.yahoo.com/news/jagr-returns-retirement-play-czechs-worlds-193504475--nhl.html |archive-date=23 June 2015 |access-date=3 May 2015 |work=Yahoo! Sports|agency=Associated Press}}</ref> after being called up to the Czech team for the [[2015 IIHF World Championship|2015 World Championship]] in Prague and [[Ostrava]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=765088 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150426115106/http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=765088 |url-status=dead |archive-date=26 April 2015 |title=Jagr named to Czech Republic roster for 2015 Worlds |publisher=NHL.com |access-date=3 May 2015}}</ref> making the team's roster.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.iihfworlds2015.com/en/teams/#CZE |title=Czech Republic roster, 2015 IIHF World Ice Hockey Championship |publisher=IIHF.com |access-date=3 May 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150518035947/http://www.iihfworlds2015.com/en/teams#CZE |archive-date=18 May 2015 |url-status=usurped}}</ref> On 1 May, he scored a goal in the Czechs' 6–5 loss to Sweden, his 50th for the national team, to become the oldest player to score at the World Championship.<ref>{{cite web | last=Gold-Smith | first=Josh | title=Jagr becomes oldest player ever to score at World Hockey Championship | website=theScore.com | date=1 May 2015 | url=https://www.thescore.com/nhl/news/756804 | access-date=10 June 2025}}</ref>\n\nIn the Czech Republic's quarterfinal game against Finland, Jágr scored one assist and two goals, including the game-winning goal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.iihfworlds2015.com/en/news/fin-cze/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150516093235/http://www.iihfworlds2015.com/en/news/fin-cze/ |url-status=usurped |archive-date=16 May 2015 |title=Jagr mania as Czechs advance |publisher=IIHF |access-date=19 May 2015}}</ref> At the end of the tournament, despite the Czechs' loss in the bronze medal game, Jágr was named the tournament's most valuable player.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.iihfworlds2015.com/en/news/awards/ |title=Jagr wins MVP |publisher=IIHF |access-date=19 May 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150519225052/http://www.iihfworlds2015.com/en/news/awards/ |archive-date=19 May 2015 |url-status=usurped}}</ref>\n\n==Personal life==\nJágr resides in the Czech Republic during the off-season. His father, also named {{ill|Jaromír Jágr, Sr.|lt=Jaromír Jágr|cs|Jaromír Jágr starší}} (1940–2022), owned a chain of hotels and served as president of HC Kladno.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hc-kladno.cz/index.asp?staly=10|title=Jágr's father, HC Kladno president|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100303001203/http://www.hc-kladno.cz/index.asp?staly=10|archive-date=3 March 2010}}</ref> Jágr credited his physical strength and penchant for exercise to growing up on a farm and working all year long.<ref name=\"nyt\">{{cite web |last1=Waldstein |first1=David |title=The 51-Year-Old Hockey Star Who Won't Quit |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/02/28/sports/hockey/jaromir-jagr-czech-extraliga.html |website=The New York Times |access-date=9 August 2023 |date=28 February 2023}}</ref>\n\nJágr wears the number 68, which he has worn through his entire career, in honour of the [[Prague Spring]] that occurred in Czechoslovakia in 1968 and his grandfather, who died while in prison that same year and had earlier been imprisoned for opposing the collectivization of his farm in the post-war Communist takeover of Czechoslovakia.<ref name=\"SIKladno\">{{cite magazine|last1=Swift|first1=E.M.|title=The KID From Kladno: By achieving NHL stardom, the Penguins' Jaromir Jagr has realized the dream he had as a youth in Czechoslovakia|url=https://www.si.com/vault/1992/10/12/127318/the-kid-from-kladno-by-achieving-nhl-stardom-the-penguins-jaromir-jagr-has-realized-the-dream-he-had-as-a-youth-in-czecholovakia|access-date=23 December 2016|magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=12 October 1992}}</ref> In any interviews when asked about his number, Jágr explains that he wears it not due to bad relations with Russian people, but rather due to disaffection with Communism. During his time with the New Jersey Devils, Jágr was granted special exception to keep wearing number 68, as then-general manager [[Lou Lamoriello]] had a policy in place which generally forbade players from wearing any number higher than 35.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Stromberg |first1=Mike |title=After Lou Lamoriello's Exit, It Appears Many of His Quirks Will Leave With Him |url=https://www.allaboutthejersey.com/2015/8/5/9094865/as-lou-lamoriello-departs-so-do-many-of-his-quirks |publisher=Allaboutthejersey.com |access-date=9 March 2019 |date=5 August 2015}}</ref> Jágr names former United States President [[Ronald Reagan]] as his hero for his work towards ending communism in Europe.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Avery |first1=Martin |title=Why Rangers and Penguins Didn't Ask Jaromir Jagr To Defect from KHL |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/129254-why-the-rangers-and-penguins-didnt-ask-jaromir-jagr-to-defect-from-the-khl |publisher=[[Bleacher Report]] |access-date=15 September 2020 |date=25 February 2009}}</ref>\n\nJágr has been a long-time supporter of the [[liberal conservatism|liberal conservative]] [[Civic Democratic Party (Czech Republic)|Civic Democratic Party]] (ODS), stating in 2004 that he \"had always\" voted for the party. In the previous election, he appeared on the party's billboards and was among its sponsors.<ref>{{cite news |language=cs-CZ |title=Jaromír Jágr v závěru volební kampaně podpoří ODS |url=http://www.ceskenoviny.cz/domov/volby/zpravy/jaromir-jagr-v-zaveru-volebni-kampane-podpori-ods/482333|publisher=České noviny |date=26 May 2010 |access-date=30 May 2010}}</ref> On 26 May 2010, Jágr announced that he was backing the Civic Democrats and its leader [[Petr Nečas]]. At the press conference, he said, \"I realize that there will be elections in two to three days. I would like their outcome to be good.\"<ref name=\"Jagr ODS\"/> He also urged the party not to forget about sports when distributing money. \"We all know what would happen if the young did not practice any sport. If children practice some sport, they do not have time for other things such as alcohol.\"<ref name=\"Jagr ODS\">{{cite news |title=Jaromír Jágr podpořil ODS. Nechci abychom dopadli jako Řecko! |url=http://www.ods.cz/volby2010/aktuality-Jaromir-Jagr-podporil-ODS--Nechci-abychom-dopadli-jako-ecko-1524.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100530115902/http://www.ods.cz/volby2010/aktuality-Jaromir-Jagr-podporil-ODS--Nechci-abychom-dopadli-jako-ecko-1524.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=30 May 2010 |publisher=[[Civic Democratic Party (Czech Republic)|ODS]] |language=cs-CZ |date=26 May 2010 |access-date=30 May 2010}}</ref>\n\nJágr is an [[Czech and Slovak Orthodox Church|Orthodox Christian]]; he was baptized in 2001 by [[Prague]]'s [[Metropolitan bishop|metropolitan]].<ref name=\"Jagr Ortodox\">{{cite news |title=Jsem pravoslavný křesťan, přiznal Jágr |url=http://hokej.idnes.cz/nhl.asp?r=nhl&c=A030604_085313_nhl_ot |language=cs-CZ |date=4 June 2010 |website=hokej.idnes.cz |access-date=4 June 2010}}</ref> He began to speak more publicly about his faith during his three-year stint in Russia, a historically Orthodox nation.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Seravalli |first1=Frank |title=Jagr sticks with his faith |url=https://www.inquirer.com/philly/sports/flyers/20120503_Jagr_sticks_with_his_faith.html |website=Inquirer.com |access-date=23 March 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200929181448/https://www.inquirer.com/philly/sports/flyers/20120503_Jagr_sticks_with_his_faith.html |archive-date=29 September 2020 |date=3 May 2012}}</ref>\n\nAlthough he has repeatedly denied that he has a [[Problem gambling|gambling problem]], Jágr admitted in 2003 that he settled debts totaling $950,000 with two internet gambling sites between 1998 and 2002.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Everson |first1=Mark |title=JAGR HAS BATTLED WAGERING WOES IN PAST |url=https://nypost.com/2006/02/08/jagr-has-battled-wagering-woes-in-past/ |access-date=30 May 2018 |newspaper=New York Post |date=8 February 2006}}</ref> The first of these incidents centered on [[Belize]]-based website CaribSports and its owner, William Caesar, to which Jágr owed $500,000. ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' reported that Jágr agreed to make monthly payments to Caesar to settle the debt, and Caesar leaked the story to the press when Jágr stopped making payments.<ref name=\"Lein\">{{cite magazine|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/si_online/news/2003/03/12/scorecard/ |title=Capital Losses |access-date=26 September 2006 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |year=2003 |first1=Michael |last1=Farber |first2=Don |last2=Yaeger |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060529204838/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/si_online/news/2003/03/12/scorecard/ |archive-date=29 May 2006}}</ref> In 2003, the [[Internal Revenue Service]] (IRS) filed a $3.27&nbsp;million [[lien]] against him for unpaid taxes for the 2001 tax year. Only a few months before, Jágr had settled a $350,000 claim for taxes dating to 1999.<ref name=\"Lein\" /> In the summer of 2006, Jágr sued his former accountant over a tax form that was supposed to have been filed in 2003, claiming that the form would have saved him $6&nbsp;million had it been timely filed.<ref name=\"Sue\">{{cite news|url=http://www.pittsburghlive.com/x/pittsburghtrib/sports/penguins/s_465310.html|title=Jagr sues former accountant|access-date=26 September 2006|newspaper=Pittsburgh Tribune-Review|year=2006|author=David Conti|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071114070732/http://www.pittsburghlive.com/x/pittsburghtrib/sports/penguins/s_465310.html|archive-date=14 November 2007}}</ref>\n\nIn 2015, an 18-year-old model attempted to extort $2,000 from Jágr, threatening to post a photo of them in bed; Jágr responded, \"I don’t care,\" leading to the picture being published online.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Blackburn |first1=Pete |title=Must Watch Video A Model Tried To Blackmail Hockey Legend Jaromir Jagr, But Failed Miserably |date=21 September 2015 |url=https://uproxx.com/sports/jaromir-jagr-model-blackmail-selfie/ |publisher=Uproxx |access-date=19 September 2024}}</ref>\n\nJágr's longevity in the NHL spawned a fan club known as \"The Traveling Jagrs\", a group of hockey fans from the [[Alberta]] cities of [[Calgary]] and [[Camrose, Alberta|Camrose]] who share interest in the player. The group dressed in the sweater, hockey socks and pant shells of 11 of Jágr's teams (his nine NHL teams, the NHL All-Star team and the Czech national team) plus long black wigs in reference to Jágr's traditional hair-style. Typically, the club travelled once or twice a year to see him play in person, but after Jágr signed with the Flames, they announced that they would be a more regular fixture at games.<ref>{{cite web |last=Pickens |first=Pat |title=Traveling Jagrs recruiting new member after hero signs with Flames |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/traveling-jagrs-happy-with-jaromir-jagr-s-new-home-291613386 |access-date=23 March 2025 |website=NHL.com |date=5 October 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Pickens |first=Pat |title=Traveling Jagrs cheer on their hero in New York |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/jaromir-jagr-fan-club-takes-trip-to-new-york-287846730 |access-date=23 March 2025 |website=NHL.com |date=18 March 2017}}</ref> When Jagr's number 68 was retired by the Pittsburgh Penguins in 2024, the Traveling Jagrs made the trip one last time to watch their namesake player skate during warm-ups, and see his banner raised to the rafters.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.stalbertgazette.com/local-news/st-albert-travelling-jagr-dusts-off-mullet-for-no-68s-jersey-retirement-8332564|title=St. Albert 'Travelling Jagr' dusts off mullet for No. 68's jersey retirement 'Travelling Jagr' Ryan Sellers joined the troupe and thousands of fans in Pittsburgh to wave goodbye to hockey great Jaromir Jagr's NHL jersey\n|author=Tjosvold, Riley |date=February 21, 2024|accessdate=March 21, 2025}}</ref>\n\nIn October 2025, Jágr published an autobiography named ''JÁ68'' that was released by the newspaper ''Sport''. The book presented insight into his life, career, faith, and values, and also included previously unpublished photographs and reflections on the meaning of sport and life.<ref>{{Cite web |title=JÁ68. Jágr a Sport spouští předprodej unikátní biografie, můžete ji exkluzivně získat i s podpisem! |url=https://isport.blesk.cz/clanek/hokej/467139/ja68-jagr-a-sport-spousti-predprodej-unikatni-biografie-muzete-ji-exkluzivne-ziskat-i-s-podpisem.html |access-date=26 October 2025 |website=[[Blesk|iSport.cz]] |language=cs |date=6 October 2025|publisher=[[Czech News Center]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Muzika |first=Rudolf |title=Já68 je pokřtěna.
