Esposito","revisions":[{"slots":{"main":{"contentmodel":"wikitext","contentformat":"text/x-wiki","content":"{{Short description|Canadian ice hockey player and executive (born 1942)}}\n{{Use dmy dates|date=September 2023}}\n{{Use Canadian English|date=August 2017}}\n{{Infobox ice hockey player\n| name = Phil Esposito<br />{{post-nominals|Canada|OC}}\n| birth_date = {{birth date and age|mf=yes|1942|2|20}}\n| birth_place = [[Sault Ste. Marie, Ontario]], Canada\n| image = Philip Esposito, February 2012 (cropped).jpeg\n| caption = Esposito in 2012\n| position = [[Centre (ice hockey)|Centre]]\n| played_for = [[Chicago Blackhawks|Chicago Black Hawks]]<br />[[Boston Bruins]]<br />[[New York Rangers]]\n| shoots = Left\n| height_ft = 6\n| height_in = 1\n| weight_lb = 205\n| ntl_team = CAN\n| career_start = 1963\n| career_end = 1981\n| hall_of_fame = 1984\n| medal_templates = {{MedalCountry | {{flag|Canada}} }}\n{{MedalSport | Men's [[ice hockey]]}}\n{{MedalCompetition|[[Canada Cup]]}}\n{{MedalGold | [[1976 Canada Cup|1976 Canada]] |Ice hockey}}\n}}\n\n<!-- *** DO NOT CHANGE THE SPELLING OF \"BLACK HAWKS\" IN THIS ARTICLE *** \"BLACK HAWKS\" IS HOW THE NICKNAME OF THE CHICAGO TEAM WAS SPELLED BEFORE 1986. -->\n'''Philip Anthony Esposito''' {{post-nominals|post-noms=[[Order of Canada|OC]]}} ({{IPAc-en|ˌ|ɛ|s|p|ə|ˈ|z|iː|t|oʊ}} {{respell|ESP|ə|ZEE|toh}},<ref>{{Cite encyclopedia |url=http://www.lexico.com/en/definition/Esposito,+Phil |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220826192111/https://www.dictionary.com/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=2022-08-26 |title=Esposito, Phil |dictionary=[[Lexico]] US English Dictionary |publisher=[[Oxford University Press]]}}</ref> {{IPA|it|eˈspɔːzito|lang}}; born February 20, 1942) is a Canadian former professional [[ice hockey]] player, coach and executive, and current broadcaster for the [[Tampa Bay Lightning]].  A member of the [[Hockey Hall of Fame]], he played 18 seasons in the [[National Hockey League]] (NHL) for the [[Chicago Blackhawks|Chicago Black Hawks]], [[Boston Bruins]], and [[New York Rangers]], winning two [[Stanley Cup]]s with Boston.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Augustyn |first=Adam |date=January 8, 2026 |title=Phil Esposito: Canadian ice hockey player |url=https://www.britannica.com/biography/Phil-Esposito |access-date=January 9, 2026 |website=Britannica}}</ref>\n\nHe is considered one of the greatest players of all time, and is the older brother of Hall-of-Fame goaltender [[Tony Esposito]]. He became the first player to score more than 100 points in a season, with 126 in [[1968–69 NHL season|1968–69]], a feat he achieved a further five times. In [[1970–71 NHL season|1970–71]] Esposito also became the first player to score 50 goals in five consecutive seasons, including the then records of 76 goals and 152 points the same year. Altogether, he won the [[Art Ross Trophy]] as the leading point scorer five times, led the league in goals six times, was voted the [[Hart Trophy]] for MVP twice, and was named as a [[NHL All-Star team|first team All-Star]] centre six times.\n\nAfter retiring as a player, Esposito served as head coach and general manager for the Rangers for two seasons. In 1991, he and brother Tony co-founded the Tampa Bay Lightning, the first NHL team in Florida. Phil Esposito served as the franchise's first president and general manager until 1998; he now serves as the Lightning's radio [[colour commentator]].\n\nEsposito was named one of the '[[100 Greatest NHL Players]]' in history in 2017, and the ninth-best player of all time by ''[[The Athletic]]'' in 2023.<ref name=\":0\">{{cite web|title=100 Greatest NHL Players|url=https://www.nhl.com/history/nhl-centennial/nhl-100-greatest-players|publisher=National Hockey League|access-date=January 27, 2017|date=January 27, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=NHL99: Phil Esposito's boldness followed him from the ice to NHL front offices |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4061679/2023/01/27/nhl99-phil-esposito/ |author=Eric Duhatschek}}</ref> His #7 jersey was [[List of National Hockey League retired numbers|retired]] by the Bruins on December 3, 1987, and there is a [[Phil Esposito Statue|statue in his likeness]] at Tampa Bay's [[Benchmark International Arena]].\n\n== Early life ==\nPhil Esposito was born on February 20, 1942, in [[Sault Ste. Marie, Ontario]], Canada, to his parents Pat and Frances, who were both of Italian descent. His father's parents immigrated to Canada at the beginning of 20th century. His father quit school as a teenager to work in Sault Ste. Marie's steel mills, and later worked as a labourer and a welder, and married Frances in 1941. He built the family's first house for $3,000 and paid it off six years later.<ref name=\":7\">{{Cite web |date=2017-03-05 |title=Phil Esposito, Tony Esposito share stories, laughs {{!}} NHL.com |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/phil-esposito-tony-esposito-share-stories-in-sunday-long-read-287373038 |access-date=2025-12-10 |website=www.nhl.com |language=en}}</ref> Esposito grew up with his sisters Mary and Janice and his brother [[Tony Esposito|Tony]].<ref name=\":7\" /> The Esposito brothers started playing hockey together at an early age on frozen ponds, outdoor rinks, and local community leagues.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-11-18 |title=Esposito brothers began road to Hockey Hall of Fame playing in great outdoors {{!}} NHL.com |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/esposito-brothers-began-road-to-hockey-hall-of-fame-playing-in-great-outdoors |access-date=2025-12-10 |website=www.nhl.com |language=en}}</ref>\n\n==Playing career==\n\n===Minor league===\n{{BLP unreferenced section|date=December 2025}}\nEsposito signed with the [[Chicago Blackhawks|Chicago Black Hawks]] as a teenager and was assigned to the Sarnia Legionnaires Jr. 'B' hockey team for the 1960–61 season. In just 32 games with the Legionnaires, he scored 47 goals and 61 assists, for 108 points - a scoring pace of 3.3 points per game. He scored 12 points in one playoff game as the Legionnaires advanced to the Western Ontario final before being eliminated.\nAfter a sparkling junior season with the [[St. Catharines Teepees]] of the [[Ontario Hockey Association]] in [[1961–62 OHA season|1961–62]], Esposito spent two seasons with Chicago's minor league affiliate, the [[St. Louis Braves]], scoring 90 points in his first season and 80 points in only 46 games in his second. He was then named to the OHA-Jr. Second All-Star Team.\n\n===Chicago Black Hawks (1963-1967)===\nMidway through the [[1963–64 NHL season]], Esposito was called up to the parent Black Hawks to make his NHL debut. He appeared in 27 games and scored his first NHL goal on January 25, 1964 versus the Detroit Red Wings. Centreing for [[Bobby Hull]] beginning in the [[1964–65 NHL season|1964–65 season]], he proved himself a quality playmaker, twice finishing amongst the league-leading scorers over the next three seasons. In 1964–65 he appeared in 70 games scoring 20+ goals for the first time, along with 32 assists for 55 total points.<ref name=\":11\" /> Esposito appeared in 13 playoff games scoring 3 goals and 3 assists as the Black Hawks reached the [[1965 Stanley Cup Final]], in which they were defeated 4–3 by Montreal.<ref name=\":13\">{{Cite web |title=Chicago Blackhawks vs. Montréal Canadiens {{!}} Stanley Cup Final, 1965 Stanley Cup Playoffs |url=https://www.nhl.com/schedule/playoffs/1965/series-i/chicagoblackhawks-vs-montr%C3%A9alcanadiens |access-date=2025-12-31 |website=www.nhl.com |language=en}}{{dead link|date=July 2026|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> Esposito produced similar numbers the following season scoring 27 goals and 26 assists in 69 games, as the Black Hawks were eliminated in the first round of the playoffs.<ref name=\":13\" /> His final season with the Black Hawks came in [[1966–67 NHL season|1966-67]] during which he scored 21 goals and 41 assists in 69 games, as the Black Hawks again lost in the first round.<ref name=\":13\" />\n\n===Boston Bruins (1967-1975)===\n[[File:Phil Esposito action shot.jpg|thumb|Esposito with the [[Boston Bruins]] in 1969.]]In [[1967–68 NHL season|1967]], Esposito was dealt with [[Ken Hodge]] and [[Fred Stanfield]] to the [[Boston Bruins]] in a blockbuster trade. While Hodge and Stanfield rose to become stars in Boston, Esposito blossomed into the greatest scorer of his day.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Archives |first=THW |date=2025-02-20 |title=Esposito: The Trade That Shaped the Boston Bruins - The Hockey Writers Hockey History Latest News, Analysis & More |url=https://thehockeywriters.com/a-trade-that-shaped-a-franchise/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250424025937/https://thehockeywriters.com/a-trade-that-shaped-a-franchise/ |archive-date=24 April 2025 |access-date=2025-12-30 |work=The Hockey Writers |language=en-US |url-status=live }}</ref> In his first year with the club, Esposito's play improved greatly; he appeared in 74 games and had his first 30+ goal season, scoring 35 goals along with 49 assists. As a result he led the Bruins in all 3 categories of goals, assists and points. This resulted in him being named to the [[NHL All-Star team|NHL second All-Star team]] for the first time in his career.<ref name=\":11\">{{Cite web |title=Phil Esposito (b.1942) Hockey Stats and Profile at hockeydb.com |url=https://www.hockeydb.com/ihdb/stats/pdisplay.php?pid=1588 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240524163208/https://www.hockeydb.com/ihdb/stats/pdisplay.php?pid=1588 |archive-date=24 May 2024 |access-date=2025-12-30 |website=www.hockeydb.com |language=en |url-status=live }}</ref> In addition he helped the Bruins break their 8 year playoff drought. However they were swept by the Montreal Canadiens in the first round.<ref>{{Cite web |title={{!}} NHL Records |url=https://records.nhl.com/history/yearly-playoff-results?year=19671968 |access-date=2025-12-30 |website=records.nhl.com}}</ref>\n\nA 6-foot-1, 215-pound, strong man who seldom hid his emotions, Esposito was nearly unstoppable when he maneuvered in the slot. He'd find or fight for some free ice against the frustrated defenders trying to stop him, and figure out a way to get the puck on his stick. As soon as it was there, he sent it goalward.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Phil Esposito Stats and News {{!}} NHL.com |url=https://www.nhl.com/player/phil-esposito-8446722 |access-date=2025-08-12 |website=www.nhl.com |language=en}}</ref> One of his best attributes was his shot. During his time with the Bruins he benefitted from his point-blank positioning, especially on the power play. Being a big player for his day, and even as he withstood a flogging from penalty-killing stick swingers, he would still get his shots in, with 249 going in, which made him one of the greatest power-play scorers in league history.<ref name=\":2\">{{Cite web |title=ESPN.com: NHL - Esposito on record: 'I had no clue' |url=https://a.espncdn.com/nhl/columns/parent_rob/1453650.html |access-date=2025-08-12 |website=a.espncdn.com}}</ref> Esposito play style has led to him being described as hockey's version of [[Willie Sutton]], the prolific American bank robber. Asked why he robbed banks, Sutton said, \"Because that's where the money is.\" As for Esposito he parked his hulking frame in front of the opponent's net because that's where his goals were scored.<ref name=\":2\" />\n\nThe following year, [[1968–69 NHL season|1968–69]] season, Esposito had both a breakout and historic year; in 74 games Esposito scored 49 goals and 77 assists for 126 total points, making him the first player in NHL history to score 100 points in a season.<ref name=\":9\">{{Cite web |title=ESPN.com: NHL - Esposito on record: 'I had no clue' |url=https://a.espncdn.com/nhl/columns/parent_rob/1453650.html |access-date=2025-12-30 |website=a.espncdn.com}}</ref> Esposito scored the historic 100th point in a game against the [[Pittsburgh Penguins]] on March 2, 1969 when he scored 2 goals in a 4-0 Bruins victory.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.nhl.com/video/memories-esposito-s-100th-point-6342897604112 |title=Memories: Esposito's 100th point {{!}} NHL.com |date=2017-06-08 |language=en |access-date=2025-08-11 |via=www.nhl.com}}</ref> For this feat, Esposito ended up playing in his first NHL [[22nd National Hockey League All-Star Game|all star game]] and was named to the [[NHL All-Star team|NHL first All-Star team]] for the first time as well. In addition, Esposito took home the [[Art Ross Trophy]] as the league's top scorer, and also won the [[Hart Memorial Trophy]] as the league's [[most valuable player]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=100-Point Seasons - Milestones {{!}} NHL Records |url=https://records.nhl.com/records/milestones/100-point-season |access-date=2025-08-02 |website=records.nhl.com}}</ref> The Bruins defeated The Rangers in the first round, but despite Esposito’s 18 point postseason, the Bruins once again lost to Montreal 4-2 in the semifinals.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1968-69 Playoff Results {{!}} NHL Records |url=https://records.nhl.com/playoff-summary/series-results?season=19681969 |access-date=2025-12-30 |website=records.nhl.com}}</ref>\n\nDuring his prime, Esposito centered one of the most renowned forward lines in history, featuring Ken Hodge on his right wing and [[Wayne Cashman]] on his left. Esposito continued to put up sensational numbers alongside fellow superstar [[Bobby Orr]]. During the [[1969–70 NHL season|1969–70 season]] Esposito appeared in 76 games and finished just one point shy of a second consecutive 100 point campaign, scoring 43 goals and 56 assists.<ref name=\":9\" /> For his efforts, he was once again selected to the NHL first All-Star team. The Bruins once again made the postseason and Esposito led the way during the postseason, scoring a career high 13 playoff goals along with 14 assists in 14 games.<ref name=\":9\" /> The Bruins defeated both New York and [[Chicago Blackhawks|Chicago]] to reach the [[1970 Stanley Cup Final]] where they defeated the [[St. Louis Blues|St Louis Blues]] to secure Boston's first cup in 29 years.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-05-09 |title=Orr's Cup-Winning Goal Played Out to Perfection {{!}} Boston Bruins |url=https://www.nhl.com/bruins/news/bobby-orr-s-cup-winning-goal-in-1970-played-out-to-perfection-316886220 |access-date=2025-12-30 |website=www.nhl.com |language=en}}</ref>\n\nDuring [[1970–71 NHL season|1970–71]], Esposito shattered the record for most goals in a season: in 78 games he averaged nearly a goal a game, scoring 76 goals. This mark stood until [[1981–82 NHL season|1982]], when [[Wayne Gretzky]] scored his 77th, 78th and 79th goals against the [[Buffalo Sabres]] on February 24, 1982, at the Buffalo Memorial Auditorium. Esposito was on hand to present the game puck to Gretzky. Esposito also set the single-season point-scoring record in 1971, as along with his 76 goals, he tallied 76 assists for 152 total points,<ref name=\":9\" /> a mark later superseded by Gretzky's 215 points in 1985-86. Only four others have reached the 150 point plateau — [[Mario Lemieux]] (four times), [[Steve Yzerman]], [[Bernie Nicholls]] and [[Connor McDavid]] — and only Gretzky, Lemieux, [[Brett Hull]], [[Teemu Selänne]] and [[Alexander Mogilny]] have matched or bettered Esposito's 76 goals in a season.\n\nThe 1970 season also saw Esposito shatter the single-season mark for shots on goal, tallying 550. Only one other player has come within 100 shots of this record, [[Alexander Ovechkin]] in 2008–09, in a season that was four games longer than when it was set. With Esposito scoring 152 points, his fellow teammates also put up incredible numbers: Bobby Orr (with 139), [[Johnny Bucyk]] (116) and Ken Hodge (105). The group finished 1–2–3–4 in league scoring, the first time in NHL history the season's top four scorers all played for one team. Once again, Esposito received numerous accolades for his performance, earning his second Art Ross Trophy, a third NHL first All-Star team selection, and his first [[Lester B. Pearson Award]] as the  league's most outstanding player in the regular season. Despite the tremendous regular season, Esposito and the Bruins were upset by the Canadians in the first round of the playoffs 4-3.<ref>{{Cite web |title={{!}} NHL Records |url=https://records.nhl.com/history/yearly-playoff-results?year=19701971 |access-date=2025-12-30 |website=records.nhl.com}}</ref> \n\nOn August 31, 1971, Esposito signed a lucrative four-year contract extension with the Bruins, making him one of the highest-paid players in the NHL at over $100,000 per season following a record-breaking 76-goal season.<ref>{{Cite news |date=1971-09-08 |title=Esposito Scores Again—In Contract |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1971/09/08/archives/esposito-scores-againin-contract.html |access-date=2026-08-11 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>\n\nThe next year, during the [[1971–72 NHL season|1971–72 season]], Esposito continued his tremendous scoring average; in 76 games, Esposito scored 66 goals and 67 assists for 133 total points. This resulted in Esposito, along with teammate Bobby Orr, becoming the first players in league history to have back to back 100+ point seasons.<ref name=\":10\">{{Cite web |title=100-Point Seasons - Milestones {{!}} NHL Records |url=https://records.nhl.com/records/milestones/100-point-season |access-date=2025-12-30 |website=records.nhl.com}}</ref> Esposito earned his third Art Ross Trophy and his fourth first All-Star team selection. The Bruins finished that season with the league's best record, and once again Esposito put up big numbers during their postseason run, scoring 9 goals and a postseason-best 15 assists in 15 games, as the Bruins reached the 1972 Stanley Cup Final vs. New York.<ref name=\":10\" /> After the Rangers staved off elimination in game five, Esposito said famously, \"If the Rangers think they're going to beat us in the next two games, they're full of 'Park' spelled backwards,\" referring to Rangers star defensemen [[Brad Park]]. Sure enough, the Bruins put them away in game six at Madison Square Garden, winning their second Stanley cup in three years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1971-72 Playoff Results {{!}} NHL Records |url=https://records.nhl.com/playoff-summary/series-results?season=19711972 |access-date=2025-12-31 |website=records.nhl.com}}</ref>\n\nDuring the [[1972–73 NHL season|1972-73]] season, Esposito had a third consecutive 100+ point season. In 78 games, he scored 55 goals and 75 assists for 130 total points.<ref name=\":10\" /> This resulted in a fifth All Star game appearance, fifth first All-Star team selection and his fourth Art Ross Trophy. However, Esposito only appeared in 2 postseason games, as the Bruins were defeated by New York in the first round.\n\nDuring the [[1973–74 NHL season|1973–74]] season, Esposito scored his 1000th career point on February 15, 1974 vs the Detroit Red wings.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Hockey News Archive |url=https://archive.thehockeynews.com/issue/596182/16 |access-date=2025-08-12 |website=archive.thehockeynews.com}}</ref> He would go on to have another explosive year: in 77 games Esposito would score 66 goals and tally 76 assists for 145 total points.<ref name=\":11\" /> Esposito's 145 points, combined with teammate Orr's 122 points, Hodge's 105 points, and Cashman's 89 points, meant the Bruins again finished 1–2–3–4 in league scoring, the only other time in NHL history the season's top four scorers all played for one team. Esposito would win his fifth and final [[Art Ross Trophy]], along with the Hart Memorial Trophy as the league's MVP for a second time.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-04-18 |title=NHL Art Ross Trophy Winners {{!}} NHL.com |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/nhl-art-ross-trophy-winners-complete-list-287899824 |access-date=2025-12-31 |website=www.nhl.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-06-12 |title=NHL Hart Memorial Trophy Winners {{!}} NHL.com |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/nhl-hart-memorial-trophy-winners-complete-list-287743272 |access-date=2025-12-31 |website=www.nhl.com |language=en}}</ref> The Bruins once again finished with the league's best record, and during the postseason, Esposito scored 14 points (9 goals and 5 assists) in 16 games, as the Bruins reached the 1974 Stanley Cup finals. However, they were defeated by Philadelphia 4-2.<ref>{{Cite web |title={{!}} NHL Records |url=https://records.nhl.com/history/yearly-playoff-results?year=19731974 |access-date=2025-12-31 |website=records.nhl.com}}</ref>\n\nThe following year in [[1974–75 NHL season|1974-75]], Esposito became just the 6th player in NHL history to score his 500th career goal. The goal came in a 5-4 win over the Detroit Red Wings on December 22, 1974.<ref>{{Cite web |title=500th Goals - Milestones {{!}} NHL Records |url=https://records.nhl.com/records/milestones/500-goal-career |access-date=2025-12-31 |website=records.nhl.com}}</ref> Three days prior on December 19, Esposito tied the Bruins record for most points in a game (3 goals, 4 assists) in a 11-3 win over the New York Rangers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Skater Records - Most Points, Game {{!}} BOS Records |url=https://records.nhl.com/bos/records/skater-records/points/most-points-one-game |access-date=2026-08-11 |website=records.nhl.com}}</ref> Esposito would go on to his fifth consecutive (and final) 100+ point season, as in 79 games he scored 61 goals and 66 assists for 127 total points.<ref name=\":11\" /> He also finished as the league leader in goal scoring for a fifth and final time.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NHL & WHA Yearly Leaders and Records for Goals |url=https://www.hockey-reference.com/leaders/goals_yearly.html |access-date=2025-12-31 |website=Hockey-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> However, the Bruins were eliminated in the first round of the playoffs.\n\nEsposito was named to the NHL's first All-Star team six consecutive times (from 1969 to 1974), and won the Hart Memorial Trophy as the NHL's most valuable player in 1969 and 1974. His Boston fans, celebrating his scoring touch during his heyday, displayed bumper stickers that read, \"Jesus saves, Espo scores on the rebound.\" Esposito, while not a fast or graceful skater, was best known for his unmovable presence in front of the opposition net from which he could score from all angles. Esposito has said, \"Scoring is easy. You simply stand in the slot, take your beating and shoot the puck into the net.\"<ref>McDonell, Chris. ''Hockey's Greatest Stars'', page 15.</ref>  He also possessed a combination of skating and stickhandling ability, strength, and long reach that enabled him to \"rag the puck,\" holding onto it for long periods of time in the face of opponents' checks and thus enabling his team to kill off penalties. Along the way, he captured the [[Art Ross Trophy]] as the top regular-season scorer in 1969 and 1971 to 1974, and led the League in goals six straight seasons between 1969–70 and 1974–75.\n\nAs of May 2024, Esposito ranked second in all-time regular-season goals for Boston with 459 (behind only Johnny Bucyk's 545).  As of 2024, Esposito was fourth behind [[Brad Marchand]], [[Cam Neely]] and [[Patrice Bergeron]] in all-time Bruins playoff goals with 46. Esposito holds the Boston record for most playoff hat-tricks with four, one of which was a four-goal game versus Toronto in 1969.  Often used to kill penalties, Esposito scored 20 shorthanded goals for Boston over his career. His last full season with Boston was [[1975–76 NHL season|1975–76]], in which he scored 61 goals and 127 points. During his time with Boston, Esposito played in the All-Star Game seven straight years from [[1969 NHL All-Star Game|1969]]-[[1975 NHL All-Star Game|1975]], was selected as a first team all star six straight years from [[1968–69 NHL season|1969]]-[[1973–74 NHL season|1974]], and was named to the NHL second all star team twice in [[1968–69 NHL season|1969]] and [[1974–75 NHL season|1975]].\n\n===New York Rangers (1975-1981)===\nIn [[1975–76 NHL season|1975–76]], Esposito was traded because he did not want to relinquish his playing time, even with his age.<ref name=\"greatesthockeylegends1\">{{cite web|last=Pelletier |first=Joe |url=http://www.greatesthockeylegends.com/2008/11/brad-park-hated-bruins-then-he-became.html |title=Brad Park Hated The Bruins, Then He Became One |publisher=Greatest Hockey Legends.com |date=2008-11-15 |access-date=2013-06-23}}</ref> He and [[Carol Vadnais]] were traded to the [[New York Rangers]] on November 7<ref name=\"nyr 1st\">{{cite web |title=Esposito Gets 2 Goals, But Rangers Lose, 7-5 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1975/11/08/archives/esposito-gets-2-goals-but-rangers-lose-75-esposito-nets-pair-to-no.html |work=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=27 January 2019 |date=8 November 1975}}</ref> in exchange for [[Brad Park]], [[Joe Zanussi]] and [[Jean Ratelle]]. This trade was monumental, as Esposito was still a great scorer, but Ratelle was a skilled centre and Park was arguably the second best defenceman in the NHL, behind Bobby Orr.<ref name=\"greatesthockeylegends1\"/> Esposito was upset to be traded from Boston as he became thoroughly connected with Boston and its fan base. When [[Don Cherry]] went to  Esposito’s hotel room to tell him he was going to be traded Esposito stated \"Please don’t say it’s New York, please, because if you do I am going to jump out the window.\"<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kreiser |first=John |date=2021-01-09 |title=Phil Esposito Grew to Love Rangers Fans, Playing in New York - The Hockey Writers Rangers History Latest News, Analysis & More |url=https://thehockeywriters.com/phil-esposito-rangers-tenure-retirement/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250421020757/https://thehockeywriters.com/phil-esposito-rangers-tenure-retirement/ |archive-date=21 April 2025 |access-date=2025-12-31 |work=The Hockey Writers |language=en-US |url-status=live }}</ref> However one of his best singular performances would later come against the Bruins in a four-goal game on March 15, 1979.'''''<ref name=\":1\">{{Cite web |date=2023-12-11 |title=Centennial Stories: Seven to Seventy-Seven {{!}} Boston Bruins |url=https://www.nhl.com/bruins/news/centennial-stories-seven-to-seventy-seven |access-date=2025-08-02 |website=www.nhl.com |language=en}}</ref>''''' He finished the 1975–76 season appearing in 62 games for the Rangers, scoring 29 goals and 38 assists. His overall totals for the season were 35 goals and 48 assists in 74 games.<ref name=\":11\" />\n\nWhile not as strong an offensive force as in his glory days, as captain of the Rangers Esposito still led the team in points each of his full seasons with the club and remained an effective scorer until his final season. During the [[1976–77 NHL season|1976-77]] season Esposito appeared in all 80 games and was a point per game scorer finishing with exactly 80 points (36 goals and 46 assists).<ref name=\":11\" /> He had similar production in [[1977–78 NHL season|1977–78]] scoring 81 points (38 goals and 43 assists) in 79 games.<ref name=\":11\" /> On November 4, 1977, Esposito scored his 600th NHL goal, against the [[Vancouver Canucks]], becoming the first player to reach that milestone in a Rangers uniform and the third player in NHL history.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New York Times Archive Rangers Win, 5‐1; 600th for Esposito |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1977/11/05/archives/rangers-win-51-600th-for-esposito.html}}</ref> However the Rangers were defeated in the first round of the playoffs.\n\nThe highlight of his years in New York came during the [[1978–79 NHL season|1978-79 season]], in which he played every regular season game scoring 78 points,<ref name=\":11\" /> and led the Rangers all the way to the [[1979 Stanley Cup Final]] where, at 37 years of age, he finished third in postseason scoring with 20 points.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://rangers.nhl.com/team/app?service=page&page=HistoricalPlayerDetail&pkey=8451916 |title=New York Rangers - All Time Roster |website=rangers.nhl.com |access-date=3 February 2022 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20070808042627/http://rangers.nhl.com/team/app?service=page&page=HistoricalPlayerDetail&pkey=8451916 |archive-date=8 August 2007 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://rangers.nhl.com/team/app?service=page&page=NHLPage&bcid=tra_photomemory_1979 |title=NewYork Rangers - Photo Memory - New York Rangers - All Time Roster |website=rangers.nhl.com |access-date=3 February 2022 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20101228035828/http://rangers.nhl.com/team/app?service=page&page=NHLPage&bcid=tra_photomemory_1979 |archive-date=28 December 2010 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Esposito had a nearly identical season in [[1979–80 NHL season|1979–80]] as he once again appeared in all 80 games scoring 78 points (34 goals 44 assists).<ref name=\":11\" /> The Rangers advanced to the second round of the playoffs where they were defeated by the Flyers.\n\nEsposito's final season came in [[1980–81 NHL season|1980-81]] when he only played in 41 games before retiring, scoring 7 goals and 13 assists.<ref name=\":12\" /> Near the end of 1980 he could see the writing on the wall, with Rangers general manager and coach Craig Patrick having replaced the fired [[Fred Shero]] that November and leaning heavily on younger players. On Christmas Eve of that year Esposito told his wife he planned to retire.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-01-09 |title=Phil Esposito remembers final NHL game {{!}} NHL.com |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/phil-esposito-remembers-final-nhl-game-with-rangers-285405878 |access-date=2025-12-31 |website=www.nhl.com |language=en}}</ref> Esposito then played his final game on January 9, 1981 vs the [[Buffalo Sabres]]. Prior to the game both teams lined up along the blue lines, Esposito was introduced to a sellout crowd at Madison Square Garden and skated out to center ice. He then tossed his gloves back to the bench while the crowd cheered, 'Espo, Espo' for close to four minutes. [[Gordie Howe]] was also present to show his respects to Esposito.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Phil Esposito, about to play the final game of... - UPI Archives |url=https://www.upi.com/Archives/1981/01/09/Phil-Esposito-about-to-play-the-final-game-of/4769347864400/ |access-date=2025-12-31 |website=UPI |language=en}}</ref>\n\nHe then retired at the end of the season putting an end to his 18 year long career, finishing behind only Gordie Howe in career goals with 717 and total points 1,590, and third in assists 873 to Howe and [[Stan Mikita]]. During his time with the Rangers he played in the All star game three times, in [[1977 NHL All-Star Game|1977]], [[1978 NHL All-Star Game|1978]], [[1980 NHL All-Star Game|1980]]. From 1979 until his retirement in 1981 Esposito served as the [[National Hockey League Players' Association|NHLPA President]].\n\n== International play ==\nIn 1972 Esposito took part in the [[Summit Series]], in which he was the captain and inspirational leader for [[Canada men's national ice hockey team|Team Canada]] and its leading scorer in the series, Esposito won the 1972 [[Lou Marsh Trophy]] as Canada's outstanding male athlete of the year and was made an Officer of the [[Order of Canada]]. He also scored the first goal of the series and he scored or assisted four times in the deciding game. During that series, his scolding of Canadian fans, who booed the national team after a 5–3 loss to the [[Soviet Union men's national ice hockey team|Soviet Union]] in Game Four, was credited with firing up his teammates:<ref>{{cite news |title=Home fans boo, Espo lets them have it |url=http://archives.cbc.ca/IDC-1-41-318-1646/sports/summit_series/clip3 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040302040239/http://archives.cbc.ca/IDC-1-41-318-1646/sports/summit_series/clip3 |archive-date=2 Mar 2004 |publisher=CBC News}}</ref><blockquote>\"If the Russian fans boo their players in Moscow like you people are booing us, I'll come back and apologize personally to every one of you, but I really don't think that will happen. We gave it and are doing our best. All of us guys are really disheartened. . . We came out here because we love Canada. They're a good hockey team, and we don't know what we could do better, but I promise we will figure it out. But it's totally ridiculous – I don't think it is fair that we should be booed.\"<ref>McDonell, Chris. ''Hockey's Greatest Stars'', page 24.</ref></blockquote>Esposito also played for Canada in the inaugural [[Canada Cup]] in 1976, on a line with Hall-of-Famers [[Bobby Hull]] and [[Marcel Dionne]]. During the event he scored 7 points in 7 games helping team Canada secure their first gold medal in the tournament. The following year, he represented Canada once more in the [[1977 Ice Hockey World Championships]] in Vienna.\n\nFor his time with Team Canada and his overall career he was later inducted into the [[Canada's Sports Hall of Fame]] in 1989, and again in 2005 alongside all the other members of the 1972 Summit Series team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hall of Famers {{!}} Canada's Sports Hall of Fame {{!}} Home: Mobile |url=https://halloffamers.sportshall.ca/mobile.html#phil_esposito |access-date=2025-08-02 |website=halloffamers.sportshall.ca}}</ref>\n\n==Post-playing career==\n===New York Rangers===\n[[File:Rustam Minnikhanov and Phil Esposito (2015-02-04) 05.jpg|thumb|350x350px|Esposito with [[Rustam Minnikhanov]] in 2015]]\nEsposito served as general manager and head coach of the Rangers from 1986 to 1989, during which he earned the nickname \"Trader Phil\" for the numerous transactions he made.<ref name=\"NHL99\">{{cite web |last1=Duhatschek |first1=Eric |title=NHL99: Phil Esposito's boldness followed him from the ice to NHL front offices |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4061679/2023/01/27/nhl99-phil-esposito/ |website=The Athletic |access-date=28 October 2023 |language=en |date=27 January 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Finn |first=Robin |date=1986-07-15 |title=ESPOSITO IS REPLACING PATRICK AS GENERAL MANAGER |language=en |work=[[New York Times]] |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1986/07/15/sports/esposito-is-replacing-patrick-as-general-manager.html |access-date=2023-08-21}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Finn |first=Robin |date=1986-07-16 |title=Esposito Relishes Top Post|language=en |work=[[New York Times]] |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1986/07/16/sports/esposito-relishes-top-post.html |access-date=2023-08-21}}</ref> During his tenure as GM, he made more trades than the Vancouver Canucks had made in the entire 1980s.<ref>Remembering Phil Esposito, Craig McInnis, Editor, {{ISBN|978-1-55192-639-1}}.</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Castro |first=Tom |date=2021-01-18 |title=Rangers' Esposito Era: 5 Best and Worst Trades of 'Trader Phil' |url=https://thehockeywriters.com/rangers-phil-esposito-best-worst-trades/ |access-date=2023-08-21 |website=The Hockey Writers |language=en-us}}</ref> While serving as GM, two of his most famous moves were the trade for the legendary [[Marcel Dionne]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cart |first=Julie |author-link=Julie Cart |date=1987-03-11 |title=Dionne Asks for a Trade, Goes to Rangers |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1987-03-11-sp-9930-story.html |access-date=2023-08-21 |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |language=en-US}}</ref> and one in which he sent a first-round pick to the [[Quebec Nordiques]] as compensation for signing [[Michel Bergeron (hockey coach)|Michel Bergeron]] to be the Rangers' head coach.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Eskenazi |first=Gerald |date=1987-06-19 |title=Rangers Pull a Surprise: Bergeron Becomes Coach (Published 1987) |language=en |work=[[New York Times]] |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1987/06/19/sports/rangers-pull-a-surprise-bergeron-becomes-coach.html |access-date=2023-08-21}}</ref>\n\n===Tampa Bay Lightning===\n====Founder and Manager====\nWhen the NHL announced its expansion plans in the late 1980s, Phil Esposito, along with his brother Tony, and [[Mel Lowell]], sought to place a franchise in [[Tampa Bay]], Florida. They faced competition from the [[Compuware|Compuware Group]], which wanted to place a team in nearby [[St. Petersburg, Florida]]. It was proposed to Esposito that he merge his bid with the Compuware Group, which he refused.<ref>Thunder and Lightning: a No-B.S. Hockey Memoir, Phil Esposito and Peter Golenbock, {{ISBN|978-0-7710-3086-4}}.</ref> His reputation and force of personality was widely credited with winning the expansion bid for Tampa Bay on December 6, 1990. The [[Tampa Bay Lightning]] commenced play in the [[1992–93 NHL season]], with the elder Esposito as the team's first president and general manager.<ref>{{cite web |title=A franchise is born 25 years ago |url=https://www.nhl.com/lightning/news/a-franchise-is-born-25-years-ago/c-791248 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190525035237/https://www.nhl.com/lightning/news/a-franchise-is-born-25-years-ago/c-791248 |url-status=dead |archive-date=25 May 2019 |website=NHL.com |access-date=May 27, 2019 |date=December 6, 2015}}</ref>\n\nFor the Lightning's inaugural season, Esposito hired many of his former teammates from the Bruins, including Cashman as an assistant coach and former Bruins trainer John \"Frosty\" Forristal as trainer. He also made hockey history by signing [[Manon Rhéaume]], making her the first woman to sign with and play for an NHL team.\n\nHowever, one of the Esposito group's key backers, the [[Pritzker family]], had backed out a few months before the bid, to be replaced by a Japanese consortium headed by Kokusai Green, a golf course and resort operator.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Power Plays: An Inside Look at the Big Business of the National Hockey League|last=Stein|first=Gil|year=1997|pages=86–92}}</ref> Though Kokusai Green had helped the Espositos secure the initial bid, the team languished under their ownership; financed almost entirely by loans, the Lightning were constantly short of cash, hampering Esposito's ability to function as GM.<ref name=\"Sandomir\">{{Cite news|first=Richard |last=Sandomir |title=A Soap Opera on Ice |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1998/04/06/sports/hockey-a-soap-opera-on-ice.html |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=April 6, 1998|access-date=January 27, 2008 }}</ref> Kokusai Green's owner, Takashi Okubo, never met with the Espositos (or with any other NHL officials), and it was rumored that the consortium was a criminal front for the [[yakuza]].<ref name=\"HC\">{{Cite book |last=Duhatschek |first=Eric |title=Hockey Chronicles |year=2001 |publisher=Checkmark Books |location=New York City |isbn=0-8160-4697-2 |display-authors=etal |url-access=registration |url=https://archive.org/details/hockeychronicles00tren }}</ref> The Lightning quickly fell to the bottom of the league and Esposito fired head coach [[Terry Crisp]] in [[1997–98 NHL season|1997]]. Even with interim coach [[Jacques Demers]], who had enjoyed successful tenures with the Red Wings and Canadiens, the Lightning lost 55 games for a franchise-worst .268 winning percentage.\n\nKokusai Green sold the Lightning to insurance tycoon [[Arthur L. Williams, Jr.|Art Williams]] in 1998. Shortly after taking control, Williams fired both Esposito brothers two games into the [[1998-99 NHL season|1998–99 season]].\n\nEsposito now serves as vice president of corporate relations for the Lightning.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Official Tampa Bay Lightning Website {{!}} Tampa Bay Lightning |url=https://www.nhl.com/lightning/team/front-office |access-date=2025-08-03 |website=www.nhl.com |language=en}}</ref>\n\n====Broadcaster====\nAfter he retired with the Rangers in 1981, he joined [[MSG Network]]/[[WWOR-TV]] for the [[1981–82 NHL season|1981–82 season]] as a TV color commentator replacing [[Bill Chadwick]]. He called games alongside first with [[Jim Gordon (sportscaster)|Jim Gordon]] and later [[Sam Rosen (sportscaster)|Sam Rosen]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=1983-09-20 |title=SPORTS PEOPLE; Comings and Goings |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1983/09/20/sports/sports-people-comings-and-goings.html |access-date=2024-03-28 |work=[[The New York Times]] |page=B14 |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Eskenazi |first=Gerald |date=1985-03-12 |title=TV SPORTS; IT'S PRIME TIME FOR HOCKEY ANNOUNCERS |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1985/03/12/sports/tv-sports-it-s-prime-time-for-hockey-announcers.html |access-date=2024-03-28 |work=[[The New York Times]] |page=B8 |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> In 1988, the pair called [[Wales Conference]] playoff games for [[NHL on ESPN|ESPN]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Chad |first=Norman |date=April 22, 1988 |title=ESPN, HOME TEAM SPORTS COOL ON ICE |newspaper=[[Washington Post]] |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/sports/1988/04/22/espn-home-team-sports-cool-on-ice/f34eebf5-d1ee-4d8e-88b2-cbf907d10acb/ |accessdate=April 17, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=1988-04-21 |title=SPORTS PEOPLE; Esposito's Blessings |language=en-US |page=B16 |work=[[The New York Times]] |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1988/04/21/sports/sports-people-esposito-s-blessings.html |access-date=2023-10-10 |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>\n\nAfter his firing, Esposito returned to the Lightning organization for the [[1999–2000 NHL season|1999–2000 season]] as a radio colour commentator.<ref>{{Cite web |author=Staff Writer |title=Esposito's presence will be clearly felt |url=https://www.southcoasttoday.com/story/sports/1999/08/14/esposito-s-presence-will-be/50512680007/ |access-date=2024-10-01 |website=New Bedford Standard-Times |language=en-US}}</ref> He still calls home games on [[WHPT]] (and previously, on [[WFLA (AM)|WFLA]]), along with play-by-play commentator [[Dave Mishkin]], with [[Bobby Taylor (ice hockey)|Bobby Taylor]] replacing him for away games.<ref name=\":8\">{{Cite web|title=Esposito still enjoying every moment of Lightning hockey {{!}} Tampa Bay Lightning|url=https://www.nhl.com/lightning/news/esposito-still-enjoying-every-moment-of-lightning-hockey|website=www.nhl.com|date=2025-02-20|access-date=2025-11-27|language=en}}</ref> Esposito also co-hosts a daily call-in show on [[SiriusXM]]'s ''[[SiriusXM NHL Network Radio]]'' channel. Esposito is known for his passionate and candid nature, often delivering unfiltered opinions while on commentary.<ref name=\":8\" />\n\n=== Boston Bruins ===\n[[File:Banners at the Garden.jpg|thumb|Photo of retired numbers at the [[TD Garden]] Esposito’s number was retired in 1987.]]\nOn December 3, 1987 Esposito returned to the [[TD Garden|Boston Garden]] to watch his number 7 get retired to the rafters. However [[Ray Bourque]] at the time wore no. 7. Team president [[Harry Sinden]] told Esposito that Bourque would continue to wear the number, and that when Bourque retired his name would be placed to Esposito's, which Esposito supported. During the ceremony, however, Bourque skated over to Esposito to shake his hand and then took off his no. 7 jersey, revealing his newly minted 77 jersey, officially retiring Esposito's jersey with only his name going to the rafters.<ref name=\":1\" />\n\nIn 2005 Esposito returned to Boston and was honored by the sports museums tradition event at the [[TD Garden]] as a member of that year's class, and received the hockey legacy award. In 2016 Esposito returned to the event to present Wayne Cashman with the same award.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-11-30 |title=Cashman Honored at Sports Museum's Annual Tradition {{!}} Boston Bruins |url=https://www.nhl.com/bruins/news/former-bruins-captain-wayne-cashman-honored-at-sports-museum-s-15th-an-284222166 |access-date=2025-08-02 |website=www.nhl.com |language=en}}</ref>\n\n== Personal life ==\nEsposito was married during his playing career to his first wife Linda, and they had three children together Carrie, Laurie, and Cherise.<ref>{{Cite web |title=OFF THE ICE |url=https://www.tampabay.com/archive/1993/10/05/off-the-ice/ |access-date=2025-12-10 |website=Tampa Bay Times |language=en}}</ref> He is now married to his second wife, Bridget, and the couple live in Tampa.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Opening his home to late daughter's 19-year-old son a mind-bending life change for Phil Esposito |url=https://www.tampabay.com/sports/hockey/lightning/opening-his-home-to-late-daughters-19-year-old-son-a-mind-bending-life/1249168/ |access-date=2025-07-11 |website=Tampa Bay Times |language=en}}</ref> His daughter Carrie was married to former NHL player [[Alexander Selivanov]]. In 2012 Carrie died of an [[aneurysm]], and in 2016 Esposito along with the Tampa Bay Lighting established the Carrie Esposito Memorial Fund in her honour, which provides financial assistance for children to participate in youth ice hockey programs throughout Tampa Bay.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-07-20 |title=Esposito Memorial Fund - Tampa Bay Lightning Community & Hockey Development |url=https://lightninghockeydevelopment.com/financial-support/esposito-memorial-fund/,%20https://lightninghockeydevelopment.com/financial-support/esposito-memorial-fund/ |access-date=2025-12-10 |language=en-US }}{{Dead link|date=February 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>\n\nEsposito's younger brother [[Tony Esposito|Tony]] is also an honoured member of the Hockey Hall of Fame.\n\nAfter retirement, Esposito established the Phil Esposito Foundation, to help promote the game of hockey and provide crisis financial assistance to former NHL players, many of whom were retired before the league established pension benefits.<ref name=\":3\">{{Cite web |title=Hockey Hall of Famer Phil Esposito, who made a... - UPI Archives |url=https://www.upi.com/Archives/1984/10/04/Hockey-Hall-of-Famer-Phil-Esposito-who-made-a/5942465710400/ |access-date=2025-08-03 |website=UPI |language=en}}</ref> Esposito also performs charity work in Florida, participating in charity golf events and hockey games. In 2011 Esposito hosted his own celebrity charity golf tournament to raise funds for the [[Johns Hopkins All Children's Hospital|All Children's Hospital]] of St. Petersburg and surrounding communities.<ref>{{Cite web |last=ESPO |first=The |title=NHL Hall-of-Famer Phil Esposito Hosts Celebrity Golf Invitational |url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/nhl-hall-of-famer-phil-esposito-hosts-celebrity-golf-invitational-119337329.html |access-date=2025-08-03 |website=www.prnewswire.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-09-29 |title=NHL legend Phil Esposito plays charity game at MAC |url=https://theeyeopener.com/2016/09/nhl-legend-phil-esposito-plays-charity-game-at-mac/ |access-date=2025-08-03 |website=The Eyeopener |language=en-US}}</ref>\n\nEsposito is an avid golfer, competing in the 2002 World Golf League tournament, and in 2004 he became an official spokesman of the organization.<ref>{{cite press release |author= <!-- not stated --> |date= March 17, 2004 |title= Hockey Great Phil Esposito Joins The World Golf League Team |url= https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2004/03/17/307766/2873/en/Hockey-Great-Phil-Esposito-Joins-The-World-Golf-League-Team.html |location= ORLANDO, Fla. |publisher= World Golf League, Inc. |agency= EQUITILINK LLC |access-date = 2025-08-03 }}</ref>\n\nIn 2006 Esposito partnered with Paragon Financial Corp to help introduce the company to builders and real estate developers in need of a preferred mortgage provider.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Relying on famous power plays|url=https://www.tampabay.com/archive/2006/02/11/relying-on-famous-power-plays/|website=Tampa Bay Times|access-date=2025-11-27|language=en|first=Louis|last=Hau}}</ref>\n\nIn 2017 he became a member of the advisory board for [[Kunlun Red Star]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Phil Esposito Linkedin |url=https://www.linkedin.com/in/philespo7}}</ref>\n\n=== Publications ===\nIn 1971 Esposito and his brother Tony co-wrote a book about their life and careers called ''The Brothers Esposito''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=OpenLibrary.org |title=Phil Esposito |url=https://openlibrary.org/authors/OL1910175A/Phil_Esposito |access-date=2025-12-10 |website=Open Library |language=en}}</ref> The following year Esposito released his first book ''Hockey Is My Life'', which was co-written with Gerald Eskenazi, covering his experience in the Summit Series and his time with the Boston Bruins.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Thunder and Lightning: A No-BS Hockey Memoir · Canadian Book Review Annual Online |url=https://cbra.library.utoronto.ca/items/show/17376 |access-date=2025-11-27 |website=cbra.library.utoronto.ca}}</ref> In 2003 Esposito released his autobiography, ''Thunder and Lightning'', covering his entire playing career along with his post retirement activities up to that point.<ref name=\":12\">{{Cite web |title=Phil Esposito |url=https://www.blueskyse.com/talent/phil-esposito |access-date=2025-08-03 |website=Blue Sky Sports & Entertainment |language=en-US}}</ref>\n\n==Honours==\n[[File:Phil Esposito Statue.jpg|thumb|Esposito’s statue outside of the Tampa Bay Lightning's arena]]\nDuring his playing days in 1972 Esposito received the [[Academy of Achievement|American Academy of Achievement]] award, which is given out to high achievers in public service, business, science and exploration, sports, and the arts.<ref name=\":4\" /> That same year he was also awarded the [[Lou Marsh Trophy]] as the top Canadian athlete of the year.\n\nPhil Esposito [[park]] located in [[Sault Ste. Marie, Ontario]] was dedicated in his honor in 1981.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |last2= |date=2024-07-14 |title=Historic plaque at Phil Esposito park among those no longer on display |url=https://www.sootoday.com/local-news/historic-plaque-at-phil-esposito-park-among-those-no-longer-on-display-9217394 |access-date=2026-08-11 |website=SooToday.com |language=en}}</ref>\n\nIn 1984 Esposito was given the Guinness Stout 'Big 'G' Award' for extraordinary accomplishments beyond the game of hockey. They held a special New York Hockey Night event, with all three New York area sports team present to celebrate Esposito. He was also inducted into the New York hockey Hall of Fame during the festivities.<ref name=\":3\" />\n\nEsposito was elected to the [[Hockey Hall of Fame]] in 1984. On December 3, 1987, his No. 7 jersey was retired by the Boston Bruins in an emotional ceremony where the then-current wearer, superstar defenceman [[Ray Bourque]], pulled off his No. 7 jersey to reveal his new number, 77—dramatically \"surrendering\" his old number in Esposito's favour (coincidentally, Esposito wore 77 with the New York Rangers, because 7 was already being worn by [[Rod Gilbert]]). Esposito was \"visibly moved\" when Bourque showed the [[Boston Garden]] crowd his new number, which he used for the rest of his career.<ref>McDonell, Chris. ''Hockey's Greatest Stars'', page 104.</ref> Esposito was also on hand in Boston to hand Bourque his retired number after the latter retired. In 2017, Esposito was named one of the [[100 Greatest NHL Players]].<ref name=\":0\" /> In 2023 Esposito was named to the [[List of Boston Bruins award winners|Boston Bruins All-Centennial Team]].<ref name=\":5\" />\n\nIn 2007, alongside his brother [[Tony Esposito|Tony]], Esposito received a star on the [[Sault Ste. Marie Walk of Fame]]. In 2009 Esposito was part of the first group of people to receive a star on the [[Italian Walk of Fame]] in Toronto.<ref name=\":6\" />\n\nOn December 31, 2011 the [[Tampa Bay Lightning]] unveiled a statue in his honour in front of their home arena, the [[Tampa Bay Times Forum]]. He was also inducted as an inaugural member of the Lighting Hall of Fame in 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-05-09 |title=Tampa Bay Lightning Hall of Fame Weekend |url=https://www.mymagic949.com/fp/tampa-bay-lightning-hall-fame-weekend/ |access-date=2025-08-17 |website=My Magic 94.9 |language=en}}</ref>\n\n==Awards and achievements==\n* [[NHL All-Star team|NHL second All-Star team]] ([[1967–68 NHL season|1968]], [[1974–75 NHL season|1975]])\n* [[List of Boston Bruins award winners|Elizabeth C.
