World Junior Ice Hockey Championships|1985 Helsinki/Turku]]|}}\n}}\n'''Dominik Hašek''' ({{IPA|cs|ˈdomɪnɪk ˈɦaʃɛk|lang}}, {{Audio|Dominik Hašek.ogg|audio}}; born 29 January 1965) is a Czech former professional [[ice hockey]] player who was a [[goaltender]] for 16 seasons in the [[National Hockey League]] (NHL), mostly for the [[Buffalo Sabres]]. Widely considered to be among the greatest goaltenders in history, Hašek also played for the [[Chicago Blackhawks]], [[Detroit Red Wings]], and [[Ottawa Senators]] in his NHL career before finishing his career in Europe. While in Buffalo, he became one of the league's finest goaltenders, earning him the nickname \"'''the Dominator'''\". His strong play has been credited with establishing European goaltenders in a league previously dominated by North Americans.<ref name=\"return\">{{cite news|last = Samuelson|first = Karl|title = The return of the dominator: after taking a year off to charge his batteries, Dominik Hasek is back in goal for Detroit and ready to win another Stanley Cup|publisher = Hockey Digest|date = 1 November 2003}}</ref> He is a two-time [[Stanley Cup]] champion, both with the Red Wings, winning his first as the starting goaltender in his first season with the team in [[2002 Stanley Cup Final|2002]], and his second in [[2008 Stanley Cup Final|2008]] as the team's backup in his last NHL season.\n\nHašek was one of the league's most successful goaltenders of the 1990s and early 2000s. From [[1992–93 NHL season|1993]] to [[2000–01 NHL season|2001]], he won six [[Vezina Trophy|Vezina Trophies]], the most under the award's current system of voting for the best individual goaltender. In [[1997–98 NHL season|1998]] he won his second consecutive [[Hart Memorial Trophy]], the only goaltender to win that award more than once. During the [[Ice hockey at the 1998 Winter Olympics|1998 Winter Olympics]] in [[Nagano, Nagano|Nagano]], Japan, he led the [[Czech national ice hockey team]] to its first and only [[Olympic gold medal]]. The feat made him a popular figure in his home country and prompted hockey legend [[Wayne Gretzky]] to call him \"the best player in the game\".<ref name=\"Popularity\">{{cite news|title=Q&A: Czech hockey goalie Dominik Hasek |publisher=[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation]] |date=3 February 2006 |url=http://www.cbc.ca/olympics/stories/indepth.shtml?/story/olympics/national/2006/02/01/Sports/hasek-qa060201.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060514122115/http://www.cbc.ca/olympics/stories/indepth.shtml?%2Fstory%2Folympics%2Fnational%2F2006%2F02%2F01%2FSports%2Fhasek-qa060201.html |archive-date=14 May 2006 |access-date=7 August 2006 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=\"passion\">{{cite magazine| last = Wigge| first = Larry| title = Passionate or passionless? It's a harbinger of spring – whether certain key players are playing with the passion and intensity needed for success in the Stanley Cup playoffs| url = https://business.highbeam.com/62653/article-1G1-20425448/passionate-passionless-harbinger-spring| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20161129082607/https://business.highbeam.com/62653/article-1G1-20425448/passionate-passionless-harbinger-spring| url-status = usurped| archive-date = 29 November 2016| date = 23 March 1998| magazine = [[The Sporting News]]| via = [[HighBeam Research]]| url-access = subscription| access-date = 4 April 2007}}</ref> While with the Red Wings in [[2001–02 NHL season|2002]], Hašek became the first European-trained starting goaltender to win the Stanley Cup.<ref>{{cite web| title = Lidstrom becomes first European to win Conn Smythe Trophy| url = http://www.iihf.com/news/iihfpr3402.htm| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20070930011136/http://www.iihf.com/news/iihfpr3402.htm| archive-date = 30 September 2007| publisher = IIHF| date = 14 June 2002| access-date = 26 April 2007}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Charlie Gardiner Stats |url=https://www.nhl.com/player/charlie-gardiner-8449966 |website=NHL.com |access-date=29 September 2026}}</ref> In the process, he set a record for [[Shutout (ice hockey)|shutouts]] in a postseason year.\n\nHašek was considered an unorthodox goaltender, with a distinct style that led to his being labeled as a \"flopper\".<ref name=\"MainBio\">{{cite web|url=http://hockeygoalies.org/bio/hasek.html|title=Dominik Hasek (1990–present)|publisher=hockeygoalies.org|access-date=24 April 2007|year=2007}}</ref> He was best known for his concentration, foot speed, flexibility, and unconventional saves, such as covering the puck with his [[Blocker (ice hockey)|blocker]] rather than his [[trapper (ice hockey)|trapper]].<ref name=\"MainBio\" /> Hašek holds the record for highest NHL career [[save percentage]] (0.9223) and is seventh (first in the modern era) in [[goals against average]] (2.202). He also has the third-highest NHL single-season save percentage (0.9366 in [[1998–99 NHL season|1998–99]]), behind [[Tim Thomas (ice hockey, born 1974)|Tim Thomas]] in 2010–11 and [[Brian Elliott]]'s 0.940 in 2011–12.<ref>{{cite web|last=Yerdon|first=Joe|title=Tim Thomas sets new single-season NHL record for save percentage|date=9 April 2011|url=http://prohockeytalk.nbcsports.com/2011/04/09/tim-thomas-sets-new-single-season-nhl-record-for-save-percentage/|publisher=NBC Sports}}</ref><!-- Yes, it's save /percentage/ but expressed as 0.###(#), typically rounded to three digits --><ref>{{cite web |title=Best Save Percentage in One Season by NHL Goalies|url=http://www.quanthockey.com/nhl/records/best-save-percentage-in-one-season-by-nhl-goalies.html|publisher=QuantHockey.com}}</ref> Hašek is the only goalie to face the most [[shots per 60 minutes]] and have the highest save percentage in the same season, which he achieved twice (1996 and 1998) playing for the Sabres.\n\nAt the time of his retirement, he was the oldest active goaltender in the NHL at 43, and the second-oldest active player in the league after Red Wings teammate [[Chris Chelios]], who was 46. Hašek announced his retirement on 9 June 2008,<ref>{{cite news | url = https://www.cbc.ca/sports/hockey/dominik-hasek-announces-retirement-1.735218 | title = Dominik Hasek announces retirement | date = 9 June 2008 | access-date = 21 November 2008 | publisher = CBC Sports}}</ref> but on 21 April 2009, he announced a comeback to professional ice hockey and signed a contract with [[HC Dynamo Pardubice|HC Pardubice]] of the [[Czech Extraliga]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tsn.ca/nhl/story/?id=275860 |title=44-year-old Hasek unretiring to play for Czech club |publisher=[[The Sports Network]] |access-date=23 September 2015 |date=21 April 2009 |agency=The Canadian Press |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090423024741/http://www.tsn.ca/nhl/story/?id=275860 |archive-date=23 April 2009 |url-status=dead}}</ref> On 7 June 2010, he signed with [[HC Spartak Moscow|Spartak Moscow]] of the [[Kontinental Hockey League]] (KHL) and played the last season of his career with this team.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://nhl.fanhouse.com/2010/06/07/dominik-hasek-signs-one-year-deal-with-khls-spartak-moskow/ |title=Dominik Hasek Signs One-Year Deal With KHL's Spartak Moskow |publisher=[[Fanhouse]] |access-date=13 June 2010 |date=7 June 2010 |author=Hal Spivack |archive-date=9 June 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100609082403/http://nhl.fanhouse.com/2010/06/07/dominik-hasek-signs-one-year-deal-with-khls-spartak-moskow/ |url-status=dead}}</ref> Hašek announced his second retirement on 9 October 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://redwings.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=643118 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141129042429/http://redwings.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=643118 |url-status=dead |archive-date=29 November 2014 |title=Six-time Vezina winner Hasek retires – Detroit Red Wings |publisher=National Hockey League |date=10 September 2012 |access-date=19 November 2013}}</ref> Hašek was inducted into the [[Hockey Hall of Fame]] on 17 November 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://redwings.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=723528 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141129042431/http://redwings.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=723528 |url-status=dead |archive-date=29 November 2014 |title=Hasek, Modano in Hall's Class of 2014|publisher=National Hockey League |date=23 June 2014 |access-date=23 June 2014}}</ref> He is also a member of the [[Czech Ice Hockey Hall of Fame]] and the [[IIHF Hall of Fame]]. His number was retired by the Buffalo Sabres (2015) and [[HC Dynamo Pardubice|HC Pardubice]] (2013).<ref>{{cite web |last1=Škvor |first1=Jan |title=Pocta Haškovi! Pardubice v neděli vyvěsí jeho dres a číslo devět vyřadí z používání |url=https://www.sport.cz/clanek/hokej-extraliga-pocta-haskovi-pardubice-v-nedeli-vyvesi-jeho-dres-a-cislo-devet-vyradi-z-pouzivani-528062 |website=sport.cz |access-date=12 November 2023 |language=cs-CZ |date=27 November 2013}}</ref> In 2017, he was named one of the '[[100 Greatest NHL Players]]' in history.\n\n==Early life==\nHašek was born Dominik Kaštánek to Alois and Marie. When he was two his parents divorced, and Marie later married Jan Hašek, who adopted Hašek.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stars24.cz/celebrity/tajemstvi-z-detstvi-dominika-haska-byl-tak-trochu-jiny.m645fqpd|title=Tajemství z dětství Dominika Haška: Byl tak trochu jiný!|trans-title=Dominik Hašek's childhood secret: He was a little different!|last=Krejčí|first=Pavel|date=31 January 2025|publisher=Stars24.cz|access-date=12 October 2025|language=Czech}}</ref> Hašek started playing hockey at the age of six in his native [[Czechoslovak Socialist Republic|Czechoslovakia]]. As he explains:\n\n{{Blockquote|They held a tryout for 5-year-old boys and my father took me there. I didn't even have real skates. I had those blades that you screwed onto the soles of your shoes, but I was tall, and the 9-year-olds didn't have a goalie, so they put me in with them and that's where I fell in love with the game of hockey.<ref name=\"flex\">{{cite magazine\n| last = Wigge\n| first = Larry\n| title = The Dominator\n| magazine = The Sporting News\n| date = November 6, 1995\n| pages = 26–27}}</ref>|sign=|source=}}\n\nIn 1980, Hašek joined the top hockey league in the country, the [[Czechoslovak First Ice Hockey League]], with his hometown team, [[HC Dynamo Pardubice|HC Pardubice]]. He became the youngest hockey player in history to play at the professional level at age 16. He helped to win two league titles in 1987 and 1989. The next year, he was conscripted in the Czechoslovak Army and played for an army team [[HC Dukla Jihlava|Dukla Jihlava]]. After making his mark and eventually playing for the Czechoslovak national team, Hašek entered the NHL draft and was drafted by the [[Chicago Blackhawks]] in [[1983 NHL entry draft|1983]]. At the time, NHL teams were wary of drafting players from behind the [[Iron Curtain]] who were often barred from playing in NHL by their countries. Consequently, Hašek was picked in the 10th round (199th overall) and was the 17th goaltender selected. Hašek did not even know he had been drafted until several months later.<ref name=\"draft\">{{cite web|url=http://www.legendsofhockey.net/LegendsOfHockey/jsp/SearchPlayer.jsp?player=18282|title=Dominik Hasek|publisher=legendsofhockey.net|access-date=5 August 2006}}</ref>\n\nHašek played on the Czechoslovakia team in the [[Ice hockey at the 1988 Winter Olympics|1988 Winter Olympics]], featuring in games against [[Finland men's national ice hockey team|Finland]] and [[Canada men's national ice hockey team|Canada]] as the team finished sixth overall.<ref>{{cite news|date=29 February 1988|title=Na nejvyšším stupínku SSSR|page=8|url=https://archiv.ucl.cas.cz/index.php?path=RudePravo/1988/2/29/8.png|work=Rudé právo|location=Prague|language=cs|access-date=8 November 2024}}</ref>\n\nUntil 1990, Hašek played in his native Czechoslovakia for HC Pardubice and [[HC Dukla Jihlava|Dukla Jihlava]]. He won the [[Golden Hockey Stick (Czechoslovakia)|Golden Hockey Stick]], given to the most valuable player in the Czechoslovak top league, in 1987, 1989 and 1990. He was named the league's Goaltender of the Year for five consecutive years from 1986 through 1990.<ref name=\"TSNprofile\">{{cite web|url=http://tsn.ca/nhl/teams/players/bio/?id=126&hubname=nhl-red_wings |title=TSN.ca player profile |publisher=[[The Sports Network]] |access-date=14 May 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070513190046/http://www.tsn.ca/nhl/teams/players/bio/?id=126&hubname=nhl-red_wings |archive-date=13 May 2007}}</ref> His American career began with the [[Indianapolis Ice]] of the [[International Hockey League (1945–2001)|International Hockey League]] (IHL), where he played parts of two seasons. His NHL debut with the Blackhawks finally came in the [[1990–91 NHL season|1990–91 season]], seven years after the 1983 NHL entry draft.<ref name=\"hr\">{{cite web|title=Dominik Hasek|publisher=Hockey-Reference|url=https://www.hockey-reference.com/players/h/hasekdo01.html|access-date=20 April 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Dominik Hasek 1991 Game Log|publisher=Hockey-Reference|url=https://www.hockey-reference.com/players/h/hasekdo01/gamelog/1991/|access-date=20 April 2016}}</ref>\n\n==NHL career==\n\n===Chicago Blackhawks (1990–1992)===\nIn Chicago, Hašek spent time as the backup to [[Ed Belfour]]. Belfour was a 25-year-old rookie but he would shine immediately, winning the Vezina Trophy, Jennings Trophy, and [[Calder Trophy]] after the conclusion of the 1990–91 season, Hašek played only 25 games over two seasons with the Blackhawks, splitting time between the Blackhawks and the Indianapolis Ice of the IHL. On 6 November 1990, wearing the number 34 (31 was worn by backup goaltender [[Jacques Cloutier]] that year), Hašek made his first NHL start in a 1–1 tie against the [[Hartford Whalers]].<ref name=\"detroit page\">{{cite web\n| title = Dominik Hasek player profile\n| url = http://www.detroitredwings.com/wings/bio.jsp?id=4535\n| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20070516073753/http://www.detroitredwings.com/wings/bio.jsp?id=4535\n| archive-date = 16 May 2007\n| publisher = detroitredwings.com\n| access-date = 15 May 2007}}</ref>\nHis first victory came on 8 March 1991, by a score of 5–3 over the Buffalo Sabres, and on 9 January 1992, he recorded his first shutout in a 2–0 win against the [[Toronto Maple Leafs]].<ref name=\"detroit page\" />\n\nDuring his time in Chicago, the Blackhawks goaltending coach was [[Vladislav Tretiak]],<ref>{{cite news|last=Feschuk|first=Dave|title=The puck stopped with Dominik Hasek: Feschuk|work=Toronto Star|date=16 November 2014|url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/hockey/2014/11/16/the_puck_stopped_with_dominik_hasek_feschuk.html|access-date=21 April 2016}}</ref> who was selected in the 1983 entry draft but was barred from playing in the NHL by the Soviet government.<ref>{{cite book|last=Denault|first=Todd|title=The Greatest Game: The Montreal Canadiens, the Red Army, and the Night that Saved Hockey|publisher=McClelland & Stewart|year=2011|page=289|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7hefvDqLrEAC&pg=RA2-PA4|isbn=9780771026355}}</ref>\n\nHašek made his first NHL playoff appearance, which was in game four of the [[1992 Stanley Cup Final]] against [[Mario Lemieux]]'s [[Pittsburgh Penguins]], after Belfour allowed two goals on four shots in the opening 6:33. Hašek played well with 21 saves despite the loss.<ref>{{cite web|title=Pittsburgh Penguins at Chicago Blackhawks Box Score: June 1, 1992|publisher=Hockey-Reference|url=https://www.hockey-reference.com/boxscores/199206010CHI.html|access-date=2 June 2016}}</ref> Although the Penguins won and clinched the Stanley Cup, Hašek's performance attracted the attention of the Sabres, who had considered trading for him earlier that season.<ref>{{cite news|last=Kelley|first=Jim|title=Stanley Cup Performance Rekindles Hasek Interest|work=The Buffalo News|date=7 June 1992|page=C2}}</ref>\n\n===Buffalo Sabres (1992–2001)===\nAfter the Stanley Cup Final appearance, Chicago decided to stay with Belfour and [[Jimmy Waite]],<ref>{{cite news|last=Jacobs|first=Jeff|title=Awkward Or Not, Belfour Effective|work=Hartford Courant|date=24 January 1993|url=https://www.courant.com/1993/01/24/awkward-or-not-belfour-effective/|access-date=6 July 2016}}</ref> and traded Hašek to the Buffalo Sabres on August 7, 1992, for goaltender [[Stéphane Beauregard]] and future considerations, which later materialized into a draft pick used to obtain [[Éric Dazé]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Blackhawks, Sabres swap goalies|work=United Press International|date=7 August 1992|url=http://www.upi.com/Archives/1992/08/07/Blackhawks-Sabres-swap-goalies/2188713160000/|access-date=27 July 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Fans Top Five: Trades|publisher=Buffalo Sabres|date=7 July 2009|url=http://sabres.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=438566|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170116173112/https://www.nhl.com/sabres/news/fans-top-five-trades/c-438566|url-status=dead|archive-date=16 January 2017|access-date=27 July 2016}}</ref> In Buffalo, wearing number 39,<ref>{{cite web|title=Sabres honor Dominik Hasek|publisher=ESPN|agency=Associated Press|date=13 January 2015|url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/story/_/id/12164178/buffalo-sabres-honor-former-star-goalie-dominik-hasek|access-date=8 August 2016}}</ref> he was initially the backup goaltender, playing behind [[Grant Fuhr]]. When Fuhr was injured partway through the [[1993–94 NHL season|1993–94 season]], Hašek was elevated to starter and soon developed into a top-tier goaltender.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Fischler|first1=Stan|last2=Fischler|first2=Shirley|title=Who's Who in Hockey|publisher=Andrews McMeel Publishing|year=2003|pages=164–166|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=wpbLnSHBNHgC&pg=PT184|isbn=9780740719042}}</ref> In 1994, he won his first [[Vezina Trophy]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Vezina Trophy winners|publisher=ESPN|date=24 June 2015|url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/news/story?page=nhlvezina|access-date=12 August 2016}}</ref> was runner-up for the [[Hart Memorial Trophy]] and shared the [[William M. Jennings Trophy]] with Fuhr.<ref>{{cite web|title=1993–94 NHL Awards Voting|publisher=Hockey-Reference|url=https://www.hockey-reference.com/awards/voting-1994.html#all-hart-stats|access-date=23 August 2016}}</ref> Hašek played 58 games with a league-best 1.95 [[goals against average]] (GAA), seven shutouts, and a .930 [[save percentage]]. He followed this feat by again winning the Vezina Trophy and again placing as a Hart finalist in [[1994–95 NHL season|1994–95]].<ref name=\"hr\" />\n\nHašek's success in the [[1996–97 NHL season|1996–97 season]] was overshadowed by a conflict with then-head coach [[Ted Nolan]]. The conflict created a tense, clique-like atmosphere in the Sabres' clubhouse.<ref name=\"rattling\">{{cite magazine\n| last = Wigge\n| first = Larry\n| title = Sabres are rattling over Hasek's Nolan comments – Buffalo goalie Dominik Hasek, former coach Ted Nolan – NHL Report – Column\n| url = https://business.highbeam.com/62653/article-1G1-19757655/sabres-rattling-over-hasek-nolan-comments\n| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20161129082847/https://business.highbeam.com/62653/article-1G1-19757655/sabres-rattling-over-hasek-nolan-comments\n| url-status = usurped\n| archive-date = 29 November 2016\n| magazine = The Sporting News\n| date = 15 September 1997\n| via = HighBeam Research\n| url-access = subscription\n| access-date = 4 April 2007}}</ref>\nIn game three of the Sabres' best-of-seven first-round playoff series against the [[Ottawa Senators]], Hašek removed himself in the second period and was replaced by [[Steve Shields (ice hockey)|Steve Shields]].<ref name=\"KneeInjury\">{{cite news\n| url = https://www.usatoday.com/sports/scores97/97111/97111374.htm\n| title = Sabres vs. Senators – April 21, 1997\n| work=USA Today\n| date = 21 April 1997\n| access-date = 21 May 2007}}</ref> Hašek suffered a mild sprain of his right [[Medial collateral ligament|MCL]], and the team doctor pronounced him day-to-day. However, the media and some teammates speculated Hašek was using his injury to bail out on the team.<ref name=\"rattling\" /> One such individual was ''[[Buffalo News]]'' columnist [[Jim Kelley]], who wrote a column detailing Hašek's injury and his conflict with Nolan, and questioning the goaltender's mental toughness.<ref name=\"kelley\">{{cite news\n| last = Don\n| first = Brennan\n| title = Dominator feels the love\n| url = http://slam.canoe.com/Slam/Columnists/Brennan/2006/02/05/1427127-sun.html\n| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160408095537/http://slam.canoe.com/Slam/Columnists/Brennan/2006/02/05/1427127-sun.html\n| url-status = dead\n| archive-date = 8 April 2016\n| publisher = Slam! Sports\n| year = 2006\n| access-date = 4 April 2007}}</ref> When Kelley approached Hašek for an interview after a loss in game five, Hašek physically attacked the journalist<ref name=\"kelley\" /> and received a three-game suspension and a $10,000 (US) fine as a result of the incident.<ref name=\"luck\">{{cite news|last=Bowen|first=Les|title=Dom Luck: Hasek Suspended For First 3 Games Vs. Flyers|work=Philadelphia Daily News|date=2 May 1997|url=http://articles.philly.com/1997-05-02/sports/25564100_1_buffalo-sabres-goaltender-flyers-sabres-steve-shields|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160102224508/http://articles.philly.com/1997-05-02/sports/25564100_1_buffalo-sabres-goaltender-flyers-sabres-steve-shields|url-status=dead|archive-date=2 January 2016|access-date=13 October 2016}}</ref> With Shields in goal, the Sabres fought back against the Senators and took the series in seven games.<ref name=\"luck\" /> However, Hašek did not play in the following series against the [[Philadelphia Flyers]], which Buffalo lost in five games.<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Farber|first=Michael|title=Private Parts|magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=7 June 1999|url=https://www.si.com/vault/1999/06/07/261743/private-parts-dominik-hasek-came-back-from-a-highly-scrutinized-groin-injury-to-lead-the-sabres-past-the-maple-leafs-and-into-the-stanley-cup-finals|access-date=19 October 2016}}</ref>\n\nThough general manager [[John Muckler]] was named Executive of the Year, he was fired for his constant feuding with Nolan. Hašek, who sided with Muckler, stated in an interview during the 1997 NHL Awards ceremony that the team would benefit from replacing Nolan.<ref>{{cite news\n| last = Smith\n| first = Jim\n| title = Buffalo in love with 'Dominator': Sabres fans hope to ride Hasek to Stanley Cup\n| work = [[The Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]]\n| date = 24 May 1998\n| page = 10}}</ref>\nAlthough Nolan won the [[Jack Adams Award]] as the league's top coach and was popular with Sabres fans, new general manager [[Darcy Regier]] only offered him a one-year contract extension. Nolan rejected the offer on the grounds that it was too short and parted ways with the franchise. This upset many fans, who blamed Nolan's departure on Hašek's alleged attempt to get rid of him.<ref>{{cite news\n |last = Crouse\n |first = Karen\n |title = Solving Hasek not an easy task: Goalie keeps opponents, teammates off balance\n |work = The Milwaukee Journal Sentinel\n |date = 10 January 1998\n |page = 6\n}}</ref>\nFor the first six weeks of the next season he was booed so vigorously that arena workers would play tapes of a crowd cheering to help balance it out.<ref>{{cite news\n| last = Gleason\n| first = Bucky\n| title = Hasek awakens from dream run: Olympic star settles back into life as an NHL goalie\n| work = The Milwaukee Journal Sentinel\n| date = 8 March 1998\n| page=1}}</ref>\nAs the season progressed, the booing of Hašek ceased, as he posted a league-record seven shutouts in December and continued to play at an elite level.<ref>{{cite news|last=Willes|first=Ed|title=Hockey: Hockey's Improvising Gold Glove; Hasek Has Redefined The Way to Play Goalie, But Don't Tell Him That|work=The New York Times|date=2 March 1998|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1998/03/02/sports/hockey-hockey-s-improvising-gold-glove-hasek-has-redefined-way-play-goalie-but.html|access-date=26 October 2016}}</ref> He won the Vezina Trophy again, as well as the [[Ted Lindsay Award|Lester B. Pearson Award]] and the Hart Trophy as league MVP.<ref name=\"hr\" /> He became one of the few goaltenders in NHL history to win the Hart, alongside [[Connor Hellebuyck]], [[Jacques Plante]], [[Carey Price]], [[Chuck Rayner]], [[Al Rollins]], [[José Théodore]] and [[Roy Worters]].<ref>{{cite web|title=NHL Hart Memorial Trophy Winners|publisher=Hockey-Reference|url=https://www.hockey-reference.com/awards/hart.html|access-date=19 November 2016}}</ref>\n\nHašek played a career-high 72 games in the [[1997–98 NHL season|1997–98 season]], and set a team record with 13 shutouts. Six of these shutouts came in December, which tied the all-time NHL record for most in one month.<ref name=\"HockeydCentral\">{{cite web|url=http://www.hockeydraftcentral.com/1983/83199.html|title=Dominik Hasek Bio at HockeyDraftCentral|publisher=hockeydraftcentral.com|access-date=24 April 2007|year=2007}}</ref> He again won the Lester B. Pearson Award, the Hart Trophy, and the Vezina Trophy, becoming the first goaltender in NHL history to win the Hart twice. He donated the $10,000 prize money after winning the Pearson Award in 1998 to the ''Variety Club of Buffalo''.<ref name=\"HockeydCentral\" /> In the off-season he signed a three-year, $26&nbsp;million deal, securing the highest goaltender salary contract at that time.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dominik 'The Dominator' Hasek|url=http://hockeygoalies.org/bio/hasek.html|website=The Goaltender}}</ref>\n\nIn [[1998–99 NHL season|1998–99]], Hašek averaged a career-best 1.87 GAA and .937 save percentage, capturing him his third consecutive Vezina, and fifth overall. He was also a finalist for the Hart and Pearson trophies, which were won by fellow Czech [[Jaromír Jágr]]. Though the Sabres did not have a stellar regular season and finished with the seventh seed in the [[Eastern Conference (NHL)|Eastern Conference]], they defeated the Ottawa Senators, [[Boston Bruins]] and Toronto Maple Leafs in the playoffs en route to a best-of-seven [[1999 Stanley Cup Final]] against the [[Presidents' Trophy]]-winning [[Dallas Stars]]. The Sabres eventually lost the series four games to two, with the decisive sixth game being one of the longest Stanley Cup playoff games in NHL history. Hašek and the Stars' Ed Belfour (Hašek's former teammate in Chicago) made 50 and 53 saves, respectively, in a sudden-death [[overtime (ice hockey)|triple-overtime]] duel that only ended when Stars forward [[Brett Hull]] (who would later be his teammate in [[Detroit Red Wings|Detroit]], winning the Stanley Cup together in [[2002 Stanley Cup Final|2002]]) scored a controversial Cup-winning goal with his skate in the [[Crease (hockey)|goal crease]].<ref name=\"HullGoal\">{{cite news\n | url = https://www.usatoday.com/sports/scores99/99170/99170437.htm\n | title = Stars vs. Sabres, June 19, 1999\n | work=USA Today\n | date = 19 June 1999\n | access-date = 21 May 2007\n}}</ref> The goal was not reviewed immediately, so officials did not notice Hull's skate in the crease until minutes later. After video reviews showed Hull's position, the goal was still upheld, leaving the Sabres infuriated. Hašek commented, \"Maybe [the video goal judge] was in the bathroom. Maybe he was sleeping. Maybe he doesn't know the rule.\"<ref name=\"Hull goal\">{{cite news\n| title = 37: Brett Hull's controversial Stanley Cup goal\n| url = https://www.tsn.ca/20/news_story/?ID=104962&hubname=\n| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20070929125615/http://www.tsn.ca/20/news_story/?ID=104962&hubname=\n| archive-date = 29 September 2007\n| publisher = The Sports Network\n| date = 17 November 2004\n| access-date = 22 January 2007}}</ref> The following season, NHL commissioner [[Gary Bettman]] announced that video replays would no longer be used to judge if players are in the crease or not, and that it would be a judgment call by the officiating crew. After the season ended, Hašek contemplated retirement because of a combination of injuries and a desire to become more involved in his family life.<ref name=\"wp retire\">{{cite news\n| last = La Canfora\n| first = Jason\n| title = The Dominator Down to One Season and Out\n| url = https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-srv/sports/nhl/longterm/1999/preview/articles/hasek1.htm\n| newspaper = The Washington Post\n| date = 1 October 1999\n| access-date = 6 November 2006}}\n</ref> The announcement stunned many of his teammates, particularly [[Michael Peca]] and [[Jason Woolley]].<ref name=\"wp retire\" />\n\nIn the [[1999–2000 NHL season|1999–2000 season]], Hašek was hampered by a nagging groin injury.<ref name=\"9900injury\">{{cite news\n | url = http://connection.ebscohost.com/c/articles/3806091/end-dominance\n | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150716034714/http://connection.ebscohost.com/c/articles/3806091/end-dominance\n | url-status = dead\n | archive-date = 16 July 2015\n | title = The End of the Dominance? – Buffalo Sabres goalie Dominik Hasek\n | journal = Hockey Digest\n | date = January 2001\n | volume = 29\n | issue = 3\n | page = 24\n | last = O'Shei\n | first = Tim\n}}</ref> He missed forty games and failed to win a major NHL award for the first time in several years. Though he healed in time for the playoffs, the Sabres were eliminated in the first round in five games by the Flyers.\n\nIn [[2000–01 NHL season|2000–01]], his final season with Buffalo, Hašek set a modern era record by being awarded his sixth Vezina Trophy, and also won his second William M. Jennings Trophy. The Sabres played Philadelphia in the first round of the playoffs again, where Hašek outplayed his 1998 Olympic back-up [[Roman Čechmánek]]. In the first period of game one, Hašek saved [[Mark Recchi]]'s penalty shot attempt.<ref name=\"01playoffs\">{{cite news|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/hockey/nhl/recaps/2001/04/21/buf_phi/ |title=NHL Hockey Scoreboard: Recap. Buffalo 8, Philadelphia 0 |publisher=CNN SI |date=21 April 2001 |access-date=21 May 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060616050115/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/hockey/nhl/recaps/2001/04/21/buf_phi/ |archive-date=16 June 2006}}</ref> In the clinching sixth game, Hašek recorded a shutout against the Flyers in an 8–0 rout.<ref name=\"01playoffs\" /> In the second round, the Sabres played a seven-game series against the Penguins featuring [[Jaromír Jágr]] and [[Mario Lemieux]] (the latter who came back from retirement), which culminated with the Penguins winning the final game in overtime.<ref>{{cite news|last=Molinari|first=Dave|title=Penguins best Sabres in OT win, advance to face Devils|work=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette|date=11 May 2001|url=http://old.post-gazette.com/penguins/20010511penspens2.asp|access-date=13 December 2016|archive-date=20 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220185542/http://old.post-gazette.com/penguins/20010511penspens2.asp|url-status=dead}}</ref>\n\n===First tenure with the Detroit Red Wings (2001–2002; 2003–2004)===\nBefore the start of [[2001–02 NHL season|the next season]], Hašek was traded to the Detroit Red Wings on 30 June 2001, in an attempt to lower the Sabres' payroll and to send Hašek to a more competitive team. The Red Wings traded for him after the team decided to move on from starting goaltender (and future teammate) [[Chris Osgood]], who was left unprotected in the [[2001 NHL waiver draft|NHL waiver draft]] and selected by the [[New York Islanders]] before the season began to make room for Hašek as the starter, as the team wanted to upgrade their goaltending after two consecutive losses in the second round of the playoffs in [[1999 Stanley Cup playoffs|1999]] and [[2000 Stanley Cup playoffs|2000]] against their archrivals, the [[Colorado Avalanche]], and a first round upset loss in [[2001 Stanley Cup playoffs|2001]] against the [[Los Angeles Kings]].<ref name=\"return\" /> He was dealt for [[Vyacheslav Kozlov]], a first-round selection in the [[2002 NHL entry draft]] and future considerations, which eventually became the draft pick of [[Jim Slater (ice hockey)|Jim Slater]]. During his [[2001–02 Detroit Red Wings season|first season with Detroit]], Hašek posted a career-high 41 wins with just 15 losses,<ref name=\"Stats\">{{cite web\n| url = http://sports.espn.go.com/nhl/players/stats?playerId=348\n| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20070812151054/http://sports.espn.go.com/nhl/players/stats?playerId=348\n| url-status = dead\n| archive-date = 12 August 2007\n| title = #39 Dominik Hasek – Career Stats\n| publisher = ESPN\n| access-date = 21 May 2007}}</ref> helping the Red Wings earn the President's Trophy with the league's best record. In the playoffs, he led the Wings past the [[Vancouver Canucks]] in six games, the [[St. Louis Blues]] in five (where he was pulled for the only time in the playoffs in game three), and the defending Stanley Cup champions Colorado Avalanche in the Western Conference final, and eventually the [[Carolina Hurricanes]] in five games in the finals to win the Stanley Cup, his first of his two championships. During the conference finals against Colorado, he became the first goaltender to be awarded an assist on an overtime game-winning goal in the postseason after passing the puck to Wings captain [[Steve Yzerman]], who then assisted [[Fredrik Olausson]] in scoring the final goal of the third game of that series.<ref name=\"OTassist\">{{cite news\n| url = http://content.usatoday.com/sports/scores102/102142/20020522NHL--COLORADO--0.htm\n| title = Detroit vs. Colorado – May 22, 2002\n| work = USA Today\n| date = 22 May 2002\n| access-date = 20 June 2013}}</ref> He also set a record for most shutouts in a postseason with six,<ref name=\"draft\" /> broken the year after by [[Martin Brodeur]] with seven.<ref>{{cite web|title=NHL Playoff Shutouts|publisher=Hockey Hall of Fame|url=https://www.hhof.com/htmlFaceOff/r%26rPSO.shtml|access-date=4 March 2017|archive-date=5 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170305114049/https://www.hhof.com/htmlFaceOff/r%26rPSO.shtml|url-status=dead}}</ref>\n\nThat summer, Hašek officially announced his retirement on 25 June 2002, so that he could spend time with his family and other hobbies.<ref name=\"comeback\">\n{{cite news\n| title = Hasek contemplates NHL comeback\n| url = https://www.cbc.ca/sports/hockey/hasek-contemplates-nhl-comeback-1.358081\n| publisher = [[CBC Sports]]\n| access-date = 24 January 2007\n| date=24 June 2003}}</ref>\nHowever, after Detroit's first-round loss to the [[Mighty Ducks of Anaheim]] in the [[2002–03 NHL season|following season]], he expressed his desire to play again. The Red Wings picked up the option on his contract on 1 July 2003, and this created an awkward and difficult situation for the Red Wings, who had two years left on [[Curtis Joseph]]'s three-year $24&nbsp;million contract, who left the Toronto Maple Leafs in the 2002 off-season as a [[Unrestricted free agent|UFA]] to replace Hašek as the teams starting goaltender, and who also had a no-trade clause. Detroit was also under pressure knowing that the rival Avalanche would be looking for a goaltender of at least more or of equal talent to replace [[Patrick Roy]] after his retirement on 28 May 2003.<ref name=\"comeback\" /> With [[Manny Legace]] also on the Wings' roster, Detroit now had three potential starting goaltenders.<ref>{{cite news|last=Allen|first=Kevin|title=Red Wings' Joseph up, down, up, down, up|work=USA Today|date=21 April 2004|url=http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/hockey/cup/2004-04-21-cujo-allen_x.htm|access-date=8 March 2017}}</ref>\n\nIn the [[2003–04 Detroit Red Wings season|2003–04 season]] Hašek injured his groin after playing just 14 games. On 9 January, he and the team agreed he should rest his injury for two to four weeks. Hašek privately told general manager [[Ken Holland]] that he would not accept any pay while he was injured. On 10 February, he announced that he was not going to continue to play that season, surprising the Red Wings management.<ref>\n{{cite news\n| last = Allen\n| first = Kevin\n| title = Hasek's decision to sit out season ruffles Red Wings\n| url = https://www.usatoday.com/sports/hockey/nhl/wings/2004-02-10-hasek-out_x.htm\n| work=[[USA Today]]\n| date = 10 February 2004\n| access-date = 24 January 2007}}</ref> He eventually revealed that he refused about $3&nbsp;million of his $6&nbsp;million salary.<ref>{{cite news\n| last = Householder\n| first = Mike\n| title = Hasek refuses about $3 million of salary while out with injury\n| url = https://www.usatoday.com/sports/hockey/nhl/wings/2004-03-12-hasek-salary_x.htm\n| work=USA Today\n| date = 12 March 2004\n| access-date = 22 January 2007}}</ref> In April 2004, he underwent groin surgery in [[Prague]], and returned to his hometown of Pardubice to recuperate.<ref>{{cite news|title=Hasek recovering from groin operation|work=USA Today|agency=Associated Press|date=20 April 2004|url=http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/hockey/nhl/wings/2004-04-20-hasek-surgery_x.htm|access-date=10 March 2017}}</ref>\n\n===Ottawa Senators (2005–2006)===\nAfter his contract with the Red Wings expired,<ref>{{cite news|title=Senators scheduled to sign Dominik Hasek today|work=Orillia Packet and Times|date=6 July 2004|page=B2}}</ref> Hašek announced his intention to play for a Stanley Cup contender, and specifically named the Ottawa Senators as a possibility.<ref>{{cite news|title=Goaltender Dominik Hasek expects to join a new NHL club in a few weeks|work=Whitehorse Star|date=17 June 2004|page=18}}</ref> On 6 July 2004, after trading starting goaltender [[Patrick Lalime]] to the St. Louis Blues, the Senators signed Hašek to a one-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dominik Hasek joins Senators|publisher=[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation]]|date=6 July 2004|url=http://www.cbc.ca/sports/hockey/dominik-hasek-joins-senators-1.495892|access-date=20 January 2017}}</ref>\n\nDuring the [[2004–05 NHL lockout]], Hašek toured with the Primus Worldstars. Similar to the [[Ninety Nine All Stars Tour|tour]] Wayne Gretzky and [[IMG (business)|IMG]] formed during the [[1994–95 NHL lockout]], the Primus Worldstars Tour ran 7–23 December, playing in seven different countries (Riga, Latvia; Moscow and St Petersburg, Russia; Bratislava, Slovakia; Bern, Switzerland; Karlstad, Jönköping and Linköping, Sweden; Oslo, Norway; Katowice, Poland) in ten scheduled games. The tour competed against all-star teams or club teams of each country.<ref name=\"Worldstars\">{{cite web|url=http://www.imgworld.com/press_room/fullstory.sps?iType=13708&iNewsid=126891&iCategoryID=12543|title=IMG Announces Primus Worldstars Tour Brought to you by Reebok Hockey|access-date=18 March 2012|work=Press Release|publisher=IMGWorld.com|year=2004|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070927074043/http://www.imgworld.com/press_room/fullstory.sps?iType=13708&iNewsid=126891&iCategoryID=12543|archive-date=27 September 2007}}</ref>\n\nHašek played increasingly well for the Senators up until the [[2006 Winter Olympics]] in [[Turin]]. During the season, he reached [[List of NHL goaltenders with 300 wins|300 career wins]], and his GAA and save percentage were the second-best in the league. Upon departure to Turin, Hašek's equipment was accidentally left behind in [[Ottawa]]. This caused Hašek to miss a number of practices with the [[Czech Republic men's national ice hockey team|Czech national team]]. At the Winter Olympics, he injured his right [[adductor muscles of the hip|adductor muscle]] while making a save in the first qualifying match against [[Germany at the 2006 Winter Olympics#Ice hockey|Germany]], forcing him to leave the game after only 9 minutes and 25 seconds.<ref name=\"Hasek sidelined by groin injury\">{{cite news\n| title = Hasek sidelined by groin injury\n| url = https://www.tsn.ca/nhl/news_story/?ID=155130&hubname=\n| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20070102185458/http://www.tsn.ca/nhl/news_story/?ID=155130&hubname=\n| archive-date = 2 January 2007\n| publisher = The Sports Network\n| date = 16 February 2006\n| access-date = 24 January 2007}}</ref>\nHašek's injury caused him to miss the rest of the regular season and postseason, despite several rumours that he would return in time for [[2006 Stanley Cup playoffs|the playoffs]], which he did not. He said that if he were to be re-signed, he would play for a base salary of $500,000 with bonuses.<ref>{{cite news\n| last = Garrioch\n| first = Bruce\n| title = Hasek willing to play for a base salary of $500,000\n| url = http://slam.canoe.com/Slam/Hockey/NHL/Draft/2006/06/24/1651041-sun.html\n| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160310040022/http://slam.canoe.com/Slam/Hockey/NHL/Draft/2006/06/24/1651041-sun.html\n| url-status = dead\n| archive-date = 10 March 2016\n| newspaper = [[Ottawa Sun]]\n| date = 24 June 2006\n| access-date = 24 January 2007}}</ref>\n\nAfter the Senators were eliminated in the second round, they opted not to re-sign Hašek.<ref>{{cite news|last=Garrioch|first=Bruce|title=Ottawa not Hasek's finest hour|work=Ottawa Sun|date=17 November 2014|url=http://www.ottawasun.com/2014/11/17/ottawa-not-haseks-finest-hour|access-date=11 March 2017}}</ref>\n\n===Return to and second tenure with the Red Wings (2006–2008)===\n[[File:Dominator39.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Hašek with the Red Wings in October 2006]]\nOn 31 July 2006, at the age of 41, Hašek joined the Red Wings for the second time. He signed a one-year $750,000 US\ncontract, with added bonuses if the team succeeded in the playoffs. He posted 38 wins and a 2.05 GAA while leading the Red Wings to\nthe number one seed in the [[Western Conference (NHL)|Western Conference]]. He also broke his own personal record by going 181 minutes and 17 seconds without allowing a goal.<ref>{{cite news|title=Hasek sets career-best NHL shutout streak |url=http://www.iht.com/articles/ap/2006/11/15/sports/NA_SPT_HKY_NHL_Red_Wings_Hasek.php |date=15 November 2006 |agency=Associated Press |access-date=15 November 2006 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120111112722/http://www.iht.com/articles/ap/2006/11/15/sports/NA_SPT_HKY_NHL_Red_Wings_Hasek.php |archive-date=11 January 2012}}\n</ref>\nMidway through the regular season, the team announced that to avoid injury and preserve Hašek for the playoffs, he would not play on consecutive nights.<ref>{{cite news\n |last=Sharp\n |first=Drew\n |title=THE REJUVENATOR: Hasek plays like his old self\n |url=http://www.freep.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=/20070422/COL08/704220597/1081\n |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070926162841/http://www.freep.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=%2F20070422%2FCOL08%2F704220597%2F1081\n |archive-date=26 September 2007 |newspaper=[[Detroit Free Press]]\n |date=22 April 2007 |access-date=22 April 2007 |url-status=dead\n}}</ref> He played his first consecutive nights of the season on 21 and 22 April against the [[Calgary Flames]] in games five and six of the Western Conference quarterfinals. Hašek won both games,<ref name=\"200607log\">{{cite web|title=Dominik Hasek 2006–07 Game Log|publisher=Hockey-Reference|url=https://www.hockey-reference.com/players/h/hasekdo01/gamelog/2007|access-date=29 March 2017}}</ref> clinching the series for Detroit.<ref>{{cite web|title=Franzen's double-OT goal earns Red Wings spot in next round|publisher=ESPN|agency=Associated Press|date=23 April 2007|url=http://scores.espn.com/nhl/recap?gameId=270422003|access-date=30 March 2017|archive-date=31 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170331114102/http://scores.espn.com/nhl/recap?gameId=270422003|url-status=dead}}</ref> In the next round against the [[San Jose Sharks]], the Red Wings were on the road and down two games to one,<ref>{{cite web|title=Red Wings rally to force OT, win it on Schneider's goal|publisher=ESPN|agency=Associated Press|date=3 May 2007|url=http://www.espn.com/nhl/recap?gameId=270502018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170414081201/http://www.espn.com/nhl/recap?gameId=270502018|url-status=dead|archive-date=14 April 2017|access-date=13 April 2017}}</ref> but Hašek held the Sharks to three goals in the next three games.<ref name=\"200607log\" /> His 28-save shutout in game six was his 13th in postseason play and sent the Red Wings to the Western Conference finals against the [[Anaheim Ducks]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Red Wings Top Sharks to Advance in NHL|newspaper=The Washington Post|agency=Associated Press|date=8 May 2007|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2007/05/08/AR2007050800439_pf.html|access-date=7 May 2017}}</ref> However, Hašek and the Red Wings lost in six games to the Ducks, who eventually defeated his former team, the Ottawa Senators, for the [[2007 Stanley Cup Final|Stanley Cup]].<ref name=\"200607log\" /><ref>{{cite web|title=2007 NHL Stanley Cup Playoffs Summary|publisher=Hockey-Reference|url=https://www.hockey-reference.com/playoffs/NHL_2007.html|access-date=13 May 2017}}</ref>\n\nHašek contemplated retirement in the 2007 off-season, but on 5 July 2007, he signed a one-year contract with Detroit worth $2&nbsp;million with up to $2&nbsp;million in bonuses,<ref>{{cite news\n| title = Hasek agrees to one-year deal with Wings\n| url = http://tsn.ca/nhl/news_story/?ID=212899&hubname=nhl\n| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20070708103849/http://tsn.ca/nhl/news_story/?ID=212899&hubname=nhl\n| archive-date = 8 July 2007\n| agency=The Canadian Press\n| date = 5 July 2007\n| access-date = 6 July 2007}}</ref>\nreportedly turning down $5&nbsp;million for salary cap room for the rest of the Red Wings' roster.<ref name=\"Hasek 5 Million\">{{cite web|url=http://www.hockeyjournal.com/Article.php?ArtID=196198|title=The Fischler Report: Grab a Mic|access-date=13 July 2007|publisher=HockeyJournal.com|year=2007|author=Fischler, Stan| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20070928090204/http://www.hockeyjournal.com/Article.php?ArtID=196198| archive-date = 28 September 2007}}</ref>\n\nDuring the [[2007–08 NHL season|2007–08 season]], Hašek was replaced by backup Chris Osgood, who he had replaced in 2002 as the teams starting goaltender. When Hašek recovered and got back into his stride, Detroit chose to alternate goaltenders in tandem instead of designating either as the backup. Detroit head coach [[Mike Babcock]] announced that Hašek was to start in the [[2008 Stanley Cup playoffs|2008 playoffs]]. Through the first two games against the [[Nashville Predators]], the Red Wings were victorious, but after a lackluster performance in the next two, Osgood was in goal for the remainder of the playoffs.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Perez |first1=A.J. |title=Red Wings' Osgood perseverance pays off with another Cup |url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/hockey/nhl/wings/2008-06-04-osgood_N.htm |website=USA Today |access-date=29 September 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080605175911/https://www.usatoday.com/sports/hockey/nhl/wings/2008-06-04-osgood_N.htm |archive-date=5 June 2008 |date=4 June 2008}}</ref> Despite expressing disappointment at losing his starting position, Hašek maintained his professionalism in practice and continued to support his teammates, with [[Darren McCarty]] citing a close relationship between Hašek and Osgood.<ref name=\"CP HHOF\">{{cite web|url=https://thehockeynews.com/news/news/future-hall-of-famer-dominik-hasek-handles-not-playing-like-a-pro|title=Future Hall of Famer Dominik Hasek handles not playing like a pro|agency=[[The Canadian Press]]|date=31 May 2008|access-date=13 February 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120318162527/http://www.thehockeynews.com/articles/16365-Future-Hall-of-Famer-Dominik-Hasek-handles-not-playing-like-a-pro.html|archive-date=18 March 2012|url-status=live}}</ref> Eventually the Red Wings beat the Pittsburgh Penguins in six games for the Stanley Cup, winning his second and last championship as the backup goaltender for the team in his final NHL season.<ref>{{cite news|last=Dellapina|first=John|title=Red Wings beat Penguins in game six, win fourth Stanley Cup since 1997|work=Daily News|location=New York|date=4 June 2008|url=http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/hockey/red-wings-beat-penguins-game-6-win-fourth-stanley-cup-1997-article-1.295080|access-date=22 May 2017}}</ref>\n\nOn 9 June 2008, Hašek announced his retirement from the NHL, only five days after winning his second Stanley Cup with the Red Wings, saying he lacked the motivation for another year in the NHL. With Osgood, the two were awarded the William M. Jennings Trophy for fewest goals against on a team in the season.<ref name=\"CP HHOF\" />\n\n==Final years in Europe and retirement==\nIn April 2009, Hašek once again came out of retirement and signed a one-year contract with [[HC Dynamo Pardubice|HC Pardubice]], the club where he started his long career.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/news/story?id=4085480|title=Hasek returning to former club team|access-date=8 January 2012|date=21 April 2009|publisher=[[ESPN]]}}</ref> In the 2009–10 season he led his team to win the Czech league title. Hašek had three shutouts in the playoffs, one in the finals, while his Pardubice lost just one game in the playoffs before claiming 12 consecutive wins.<ref>{{cite news | title =Hasek becomes Czech champion at 45 | url = https://www.usatoday.com/sports/olympics/2010-04-22-50389377_x.htm | work=USA Today | date = 23 April 2010 | access-date = 23 April 2010 | first=Karel | last=Janicek}}</ref> For the 2010–11 hockey season, Hašek signed a one-year contract with [[HC Spartak Moscow|Spartak Moscow]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wkbw.com/sports/national/43384882.html|title=Dominik Hasek comes out of retirement|access-date=30 September 2014|date=8 July 2010|publisher=[[WKBW-TV|WKBW]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120310095457/http://www.wkbw.com/sports/national/43384882.html|archive-date=10 March 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref>\n\nOn 15 May 2012, Czech website hokej.cz reported that Hašek had discussed playing for [[Piráti Chomutov]] after their promotion to the [[Czech Extraliga]].<ref>{{cite news | title = Legendary hockey and Hasek Chomutov? It is possible | url = http://hokej.idnes.cz/legendarni-hasek-a-hokejovy-chomutov-dst-/hokej.aspx?c=A120515_113410_hokej_mah | work = Mladá fronta DNES | date = 15 May 2012 | access-date = 17 May 2012 | language = cs | first=Petr | last=Bilek}}</ref> On 25 May 2012, Czech sport website Deniksport reported that Hašek was considering a return to the NHL, possibly with the Red Wings or Tampa Bay Lightning.<ref>{{cite news|title=Hasek eyes NHL return|work=Kingston Whig-Standard|agency=QMI Agency|date=28 May 2012|url=http://www.thewhig.com/2012/05/28/hasek-eyes-nhl-return|access-date=22 May 2017}}</ref> However, the start of the [[2012–13 NHL season]] was delayed due to the [[2012–13 NHL lockout]] and Hašek announced his retirement on 9 October 2012.<ref>{{cite news|last=Simmons|first=Steve|title=Dominik Hasek, 'the best ever', retires from hockey|newspaper=Toronto Sun|date=9 October 2012|url=http://www.torontosun.com/2012/10/09/dominik-hasek-the-best-ever|access-date=5 June 2017}}</ref>\n\nThe Sabres [[Buffalo Sabres#Retired numbers|retired]] Hašek's No. 39 jersey prior to a 13 January 2015 game against the Red Wings, making Hašek's number the seventh to be retired in Sabres history.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://sabres.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=735396 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20141021052905/http://sabres.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=735396 | url-status = dead | archive-date = 21 October 2014 | title = Hasek Jersey Retirement Ceremony on January 13 | publisher = [[Buffalo Sabres]] | date = 20 October 2014 | access-date = 20 October 2014}}</ref> In a ceremony held on 27 January 2017, during the All-Star Weekend in Los Angeles, Hašek was named one of the '[[100 Greatest NHL Players]]' in history.<ref>{{cite web|title=100 Greatest NHL Players|url=https://www.nhl.com/history/nhl-centennial/nhl-100-greatest-players|publisher=National Hockey League|access-date=27 January 2017|date=27 January 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Beacham|first=Greg|title=NHL reveals top 100|work=Toronto Star|agency=Associated Press|date=27 January 2017|url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/hockey/2017/01/27/nhl-reveals-top-100.html|access-date=29 November 2017}}</ref>\n\n==International play==\n\n===1998 Winter Olympics===\n[[File:Nagano 1998-Russia vs Czech Republic.jpg|thumb|left|Hašek in goal for the Czech Republic during the gold medal game of the [[1998 Winter Olympics]]]]\nHašek's most memorable international performance came in the [[Ice hockey at the 1998 Winter Olympics|1998 Winter Olympics]], the first edition that the NHL took a break to allow their players to participate, where he led the Czech national team to the gold medal. He allowed six goals in total, with only two of them coming in the knockout round. In the quarterfinals versus the [[United States men's national ice hockey team|United States]], Hašek conceded only a goal to [[Mike Modano]] in a decisive 4–1 win. Against [[Canada men's national ice hockey team|Canada]] in the semifinals, seen as a goaltending duel against [[Patrick Roy]], Hašek allowed only a rebound by [[Trevor Linden]] with 67 seconds left in the third period which tied the game at 1-1, sending it to overtime. In a dramatic shootout win, Hašek stopped all five Canadians ([[Theoren Fleury]], [[Ray Bourque]], [[Joe Nieuwendyk]], [[Eric Lindros]] and [[Brendan Shanahan]]), while Roy allowed only [[Robert Reichel]] to score and stopped the next four Czechs. As a result of Hašek's heroics, [[Wayne Gretzky]] dubbed him \"the best player in the game\"; once the NHL resumed Hašek continued his strong performances with the Buffalo Sabres and would go on to win his second consecutive Hart Trophy as MVP.<ref name=\"Popularity\" /><ref name=\"passion\" />\n\nIn the gold medal match, Hašek then shut out the [[Russia men's national ice hockey team|Russian team]] 1–0 in the final game, stopping 20 shots. He was later announced as the best goaltender in the Olympics. After he won the gold, he was quoted as saying:<ref name=\"OlympicQuote\">\n{{cite news\n| last = Alexander\n| first = Rachel\n| title = For Cap's Gonchar, a Silver Lining\n| newspaper = The Washington Post\n| date = 22 February 1998\n| url = https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-srv/sports/longterm/olympics1998/sport/hockey/articles/gonchar23.htm\n| access-date = 5 August 2006}}</ref>\n\n{{Blockquote|When the game ended, I just threw my stick. I was so happy. When I saw the flag go up, I saw my whole career flash before my eyes from the first time my parents took me to a game until now.}}\n\nHašek's performance in the 1998 Olympics made him one of the most popular figures in the Czech Republic, so much so that residents chanted \"Hašek to the castle!\" in the streets, referring to the [[Prague Castle]], the seat of the [[President of the Czech Republic]]. In response to this, Hašek called the president [[Václav Havel]] and jokingly told him that his job was not in jeopardy.<ref>\n{{cite news\n |title=Q&A: Czech hockey goalie Dominik Hasek\n |publisher=[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation]]\n |date=3 February 2006 |url=http://www.cbc.ca/olympics/stories/indepth.shtml?/story/olympics/national/2006/02/01/Sports/hasek-qa060201.html\n |access-date=7 August 2006 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060514122115/http://www.cbc.ca/olympics/stories/indepth.shtml?%2Fstory%2Folympics%2Fnational%2F2006%2F02%2F01%2FSports%2Fhasek-qa060201.html\n |archive-date=14 May 2006 |url-status=dead\n}}</ref>\nHe also helped to inspire an opera (titled ''Nagano'') about the Czech team's gold medal victory,<ref>\n{{cite web\n| last = Asiedu\n| first = Dita\n| title = \"Nagano\" Opera premieres at Prague's Estates Theatre\n| url = http://www.radio.cz/en/article/52625\n| publisher = Radio Prague\n| date = 4 September 2004\n| access-date = 14 August 2006}}</ref>\nand in 2003, [[Petr Pravec]] and [[Lenka Šarounová]] named an [[asteroid]] ([[8217 Dominikhašek]]) in his honour.<ref>\n{{cite web\n| title = JPL Small-Body Database Browser\n| url = http://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/sbdb.cgi?sstr=8217\n| date = 23 September 2003\n| access-date = 2 September 2006}}</ref>\n\n===2006 Winter Olympics===\nFor the 2006 Winter Olympics in [[Turin]], Italy, upon departure from Ottawa, Hašek's equipment was accidentally left behind. This caused Hašek to miss a number of practices with the [[Czech Republic men's national ice hockey team|Czech national team]].\n\nIn the opening match of the Olympics, he injured his right [[adductor muscles of the hip|adductor muscle]] while making a save in the first qualifying match against [[Germany at the 2006 Winter Olympics#Ice hockey|Germany]], forcing him to leave the game after only 9 minutes and 25 seconds.<ref name=\"Hasek sidelined by groin injury\" /> Despite his absence, the Czechs managed to earn the bronze medal with backup goaltender [[Tomáš Vokoun]],<ref>{{cite web|title=2006 Olympics: Czech Republic Takes Bronze|publisher=National Hockey League|date=24 February 2006|url=https://www.nhl.com/avalanche/news/2006-olympics-czech-republic-takes-bronze/c-426452|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170812021642/https://www.nhl.com/avalanche/news/2006-olympics-czech-republic-takes-bronze/c-426452|url-status=dead|archive-date=12 August 2017|access-date=7 July 2017}}</ref> which Hašek received as well.<ref>{{cite web|last=Zaccardi|first=Nick|title=Dominik Hasek's favorite Buffalo memory—Olympic homecoming|publisher=NBC Sports|date=13 January 2015|url=http://olympics.nbcsports.com/2015/01/13/dominik-hasek-buffalo-sabres-olympics-nagano-1998-hockey-czech-republic/|access-date=11 August 2017}}</ref>\n\nHašek's injury from the Olympics caused him to miss the rest of the NHL regular season and postseason with the Ottawa Senators, despite several rumours that he would return in time for [[2006 Stanley Cup playoffs|the playoffs]], which he did not.\n\n==Style of play==\n[[File:Dominik Hasek stretching.jpg|thumb|right|Hašek displaying his flexibility in warm-ups before a 2006 game. Hašek's flexibility is credited as one of his strengths.]]\nHašek had an unorthodox [[Stand-up style|goaltending style]].<ref name=\"MainBio\" /><ref>{{cite magazine|title=In The Crease |last=Maguire |first=Pierre |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |volume=88 |issue=21 |page=92 |year=1998 |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/features/1998/weekly/980525/nhl0525/d.html |access-date=5 August 2006 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081010214622/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/features/1998/weekly/980525/nhl0525/d.html |archive-date=10 October 2008}}\n</ref>\nHe was extraordinarily flexible and was jokingly described in a [[MasterCard]] commercial as having \"a [[Slinky]] for a spine\".<ref name=\"mastercard\">{{cite news\n| last = Hartley\n| first = Tom\n| title = MasterCard banks on Hasek\n| url = http://buffalo.bizjournals.com/buffalo/stories/1999/03/08/story2.html\n| date = 5 March 1999\n| publisher = Buffalo Business First\n| access-date = 1 March 2007}}</ref>\nIn order to cover the bottom of the net, where most goals are scored, Hašek dropped down on almost every [[shot (ice hockey)|shot]]. His \"flopping\" style saw him flailing in the crease, using every part of his body, including his head, to stop the puck. Hašek occasionally dropped his stick and covered the puck with his stick hand, whereas most goaltenders would use the glove hand instead.<ref name=\"MainBio\" />\nIn response to the speculation he received from his style, Hašek explained:\n\n{{Blockquote|They say I am unorthodox, I flop around the ice like some kind of fish. I say, who cares as long as I stop the puck?<ref name=\"flex\" />}}\n\nHašek's unique style attracted fans to games.<ref name=\"entertainment\">{{cite news\n| last = O'Donnell\n| first = Chuck\n| title = That's entertainment: from Hull to Hasek, these are the 10 most exciting players in the history of the NHL – Bobby Hull; Dominik Hasek\n| publisher = Hockey Digest\n| date = 1 December 2003}}</ref>\nBecause of his flexibility, Hašek could make difficult saves that other goaltenders could not<ref name=\"flex\" />—an opposing coach once referred to them as \"miracle saves\".<ref name=\"entertainment\" /> These types of saves include toe-stops and a maneuver known as the \"Hašek roll\".<ref name=\"flex\" /><ref>{{cite news|last=Teaford|first=Elliott|title=Hebert, Hasek Duel to Standoff|work=Los Angeles Times|date=7 December 1996|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1996-12-07-sp-6588-story.html|access-date=15 January 2017}}</ref><ref name=\"HasekRoll\">{{cite web|url=https://www.nhl.com/news/unmasked-more-than-luck-in-haseks-barrel-roll/c-738929 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171031053911/https://www.nhl.com/news/unmasked-more-than-luck-in-haseks-barrel-roll/c-738929 |url-status=dead |archive-date=31 October 2017 |title=Unmasked: More than luck in Hasek's barrel roll |publisher=National Hockey League |access-date=15 January 2017 |date=13 November 2014}}</ref> Hašek was also known for his strict regimen of [[Physical exercise|conditioning]].<ref>{{cite news\n| last = Loria\n| first = Keith\n| title = The plot thickens: these 10 story lines are sure to keep NHL fans on the edge of their seats this season\n| publisher = Hockey Digest\n| date = 1 December 2003}}</ref> During the off-season between May and September 2006, he lost a considerable amount of weight to increase his flexibility.\n\nHašek was one of the last goaltenders to wear a helmet-and-cage combo rather than a contemporary hybrid [[goaltender mask]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1999/06/09/sports/stanley-cup-playoffs-sabres-stun-the-stars-on-a-goal-by-wooley.html|title=Stanley Cup Playoffs; Sabres Stun the Stars On a Goal by Wooley|access-date=8 January 2012|date=9 June 1999|work=[[The New York Times]]|author=Lapointe, Joe}}</ref> The last few included his former teammate Chris Osgood, who left the NHL three years after Hašek;<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/773334-saying-goodbye-to-the-wizard-of-oz-chris-osgood-calls-it-a-career|title=Chris Osgood Retires: Saying Goodbye to the \"Wizard of Oz\"|access-date=8 January 2012|date=20 July 2011|work=[[Bleacher Report]]|author=Slivka, Steven}}</ref> [[Rick DiPietro]] borrowed one of Osgood's helmets for a short time while he recovered from a facial injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ingoalmag.com/news/islanders-dipietro-dons-osgoods-old-mask-to-protect-shattered-face/|title=Islanders Dipietro dons Osgood's old mask to protect shattered face &#124; InGoal Magazine|access-date=1 September 2020|archive-date=22 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200922073421/https://ingoalmag.com/news/islanders-dipietro-dons-osgoods-old-mask-to-protect-shattered-face|url-status=dead}}</ref>\n\n==Personal life==\nHašek and his former wife Alena have a son named Michael (born 1990) and a daughter named [[Dominika Hašková|Dominika]] (born 1995). Dominika is the lead singer of the electro-pop band [[We Are Domi]], which represented the Czech Republic in the [[Eurovision Song Contest 2022]], finishing in 22nd place. In November 2012 Hašek announced his divorce after 23 years of marriage.<ref>{{cite news\n| last = Herrmannová\n| first = Nela\n| title = Dominik Hašek se rozvádí, s manželkou už nežije půl roku\n| url = http://revue.idnes.cz/dominik-hasek-a-jeho-manzelka-alena-oznamili-rozvod-fxo-/sex.aspx?c=A121116_100018_sex_nh\n| publisher = idnes.cz (in Czech)\n| date = 16 November 2012\n| access-date = 20 September 2015}}</ref>\nHe divides much of his free time playing [[squash (sport)|squash]] and [[inline hockey]], where he plays defence. When he was younger, Hašek played competitive football as a [[midfielder]], and was a junior tennis champion in Eastern [[Bohemia]].<ref>{{cite news\n| last = Wigge\n| first = Larry\n| title = For Hasek hunger burns for another Cup\n| url = https://www.nhl.com/redwings/news/for-hasek-hunger-burns-for-another-cup/c-467068\n| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20161129023800/https://www.nhl.com/redwings/news/for-hasek-hunger-burns-for-another-cup/c-467068\n| url-status = dead\n| archive-date = 29 November 2016\n| publisher = National Hockey League\n| date = 11 April 2007\n| access-date = 21 April 2007}}</ref>\nHis brother [[Martin Hašek (footballer, born 1969)|Martin]] is also a competitive athlete and played for the Czech Republic football team [[AC Sparta Prague]] before retiring and eventually deciding to coach. Hobby-wise, Hašek claims that he has been a fan of professional wrestling since his Buffalo days, and says that he mostly follows his favorite wrestlers, [[Stone Cold Steve Austin]] and [[Don Muraco|Don \"The Rock\" Muraco]].<ref>{{cite news\n| last = Kulfan\n| first = Ted\n| title = Hasek has WrestleMania fever, and that's no foolin': Goalie is taking his son and son's friends to WWE's annual event April 1 at Ford Field\n| work = The Detroit News\n| date = 14 March 2007\n| page = D3}}</ref>\n\nBecause of his formal education, Hašek stands out among Czech sportsmen. He earned a [[Academic degree|university degree]] after studying history and the [[Czech language]] in the Faculty of Education at the [[University of Hradec Králové]], which qualified him to be a teacher, and led him to teach high school classes.<ref name=\"education\">{{cite news\n| last = Horakova\n| first = Pavla\n| title = Dominik 'The Dominator' Hasek\n| url = http://www.radio.cz/en/article/30316\n| publisher = Radio Prague\n| date = 17 July 2002\n| access-date = 3 April 2007}}</ref> Hašek also had a brand of sportswear named ''Dominator Clothing'', which was launched shortly after the Nagano Olympics in 1998. It also had two locations in [[Michigan]] for a short time.<ref>\n {{cite web\n | title = Hasek opens first North American Dominator Clothing stores in Michigan!\n | publisher = Dominator Clothing\n | year = 2004\n | url = http://www.dominatorclothing.com/domclothing/assets/images/mag/aug_04/dom_news_08_04.htm\n | access-date = 10 May 2007\n | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20041214041232/http://www.dominatorclothing.com/domclothing/assets/images/mag/aug_04/dom_news_08_04.htm\n | archive-date = 14 December 2004\n | url-status=usurped}}</ref> However, sales were low, and the Dominator brand was forced out of business in 2008.<ref>{{cite news\n| title = Hasek's cuts 'Dominator' clothing line in Czech Republic\n| url = http://blog.mlive.com/snapshots/2008/08/haseks_cuts_dominator_clothing.html\n| work = The Prague Post\n| date = 7 August 2008\n| access-date = 20 September 2015\n}}</ref>\nIn May 2001, Hašek founded the ''Dominik Hašek Youth Hockey League''/''Hašek's Heroes'', and donated over $1&nbsp;million to help underprivileged children in Buffalo play hockey.<ref>\n{{cite news\n|author = James Fink\n|title = Hasek group makes save for rink\n|url = http://www.bizjournals.com/buffalo/stories/2005/08/08/story5.html\n|publisher = Buffalo Business First\n|date = 5 August 2005\n|access-date = 5 August 2006\n}}</ref>\nHe organized a charity hockey game in Prague in 1998, and donated the profits to hospitals in the Czech Republic.<ref>{{cite web|last=Norris |first=Doug |title=hockeygoalies.org news |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070501123437/http://www.hockeygoalies.org/news/oldnews.html |archive-date=1 May 2007}}</ref>\n\nHašek was known to appreciate humor to keep team spirits up, and often jokes about his resemblance to [[Cosmo Kramer]] of ''[[Seinfeld]]''.<ref>{{cite magazine|title=Hasek, Sabres hope laughter is best medicine for bitter defeats |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/hockey/nhl/events/1998/playoffs/news/1998/05/31/hasek_31 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |date=31 May 1998 |access-date=21 April 2007 |url-status=dead he was featured in a [[MasterCard]] commercial that praised his flexibility.<ref name=\"mastercard\" /> On 26 November 2006, [[Mark Parisi]]'s [[comic panel]] ''[[Off the Mark (comic strip)|off the syndicate=[[United Feature Syndicate]]}}</ref>\n\nThroughout his long career, Hašek was represented by agent [[Ritch Winter]].<ref name=\"HockeydCentral\" />\n\n===Politics===\nHašek developed an interest in politics following his retirement from hockey, including possibly running for [[president of the Czech Republic]] in 2023 and 2028.<ref>{{cite news|last=Willoughby|first=Ian|url=https://english.radio.cz/drahos-and-ex-hockey-star-hasek-show-early-interest-running-presidency-8124741|title=Drahoš and ex-hockey star Hašek show early interest in prezidentem|work=Parlamentní listy|date=12 March 2020|access-date=20 June 2023|language=cs-CZ}}</ref> He closely followed Czech politics throughout the 2010s before publicly speaking at the [[Je to na nás!]] rally in 2019 against Prime Minister [[Andrej Babiš]]. When Babiš visited [[Ivan Hlinka Stadion]] in [[Litvínov]] to discuss renovations to the arena, Hašek wrote on his Twitter account that he did \"not want the Czech national sport to be stained by your name.\"<ref>{{cite news|last=Vrablik|first=Lukas|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1697135/2020/03/26/hasek-to-the-castle-dominik-haseks-foray-into-politics-and-where-it-may-lead/|title='Hasek to the Castle!': Dominik Hasek's foray into politics and where it may lead|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|date=26 March 2020|access-date=26 November 2024|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Šeliga|first=Vojtěch|url=https://www.echo24.cz/a/Sbdnj/babis-jezdi-po-stadionech-a-slibuje-k-hokeji-se-nepriblizuj-stbaku-vraci-mu-hasek|title=Babiš jezdí po stadionech a slibuje. \"K hokeji se nepřibližuj, StBáku,\" vrací mu Hašek|publisher=Echo24|date=9 February 2020|access-date=26 November 2024|language=cs-CZ}}</ref> He supported [[Petr Pavel]] in the [[2023 Czech presidential election]]; in 2024, Hašek opined that Pavel is \"doing an excellent job\" and praised him for his [[pro-Western]] views and domestic policy.<ref>{{cite news|last=Bartoníček|first=Radek|url=https://zpravy.aktualne.cz/domaci/jak-se-potkal-prezident-s-dominikem-haskem/r~1ab761c4e1db11eebeca0cc47ab5f122/|title=\"Co vy tady děláte?\" Dominik Hašek po rozhovoru překvapil prezidenta Pavla|publisher=Aktuálně.cz|date=14 March 2024|access-date=26 November 2024|language=cs-CZ}}</ref>\n\nHe was [[TOP 09]]'s nominee for the [[2024 Czech Senate election]], running for the 41st district in [[Benešov]]. He received 20.28 percent of the vote in the first round, the third most of the six candidates but missing the second round by less than six percent.<ref>{{cite news|last=Kellner|first=Zdeněk|url=https://benesovsky.denik.cz/zpravy_region/do-finale-hry-o-senat-postoupili-zdenek-hraba-a-helena-valkova-20240921.html|title=Do finále hry o Senát postoupili Hraba a Válková. Dominik Hašek pod čarou|website=Benešovský deník|date=21 November 2024|access-date=26 November 2024|language=cs-CZ}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.volbyhned.cz/se2024/se_41_en.html|title=Election into the Senate of the Czech Republic held on 20 – 21 September 2024|website=Volbyhned.cz|publisher=[[Czech Statistical Office]]|access-date=26 November 2024}}</ref>\n\nIn August 2025, he spoke at a rally organized by [[Milion chvilek pro demokracii]] to protest [[political polarization]] and warn of foreign interference with the [[2025 Czech parliamentary election]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://milionchvilek.cz/clanek/stovky-lidi-se-postavily-proti-nasili-a-nenavisti-ve-verejnem-prostoru|title=Stovky lidí se postavily proti násilí a nenávisti ve veřejném prostoru|website=[[Milion chvilek pro demokracii]]|date=5 August 2025|access-date=14 August 2025|language=cs-CZ}}</ref> Hašek pointed to rhetoric made domestically from those like far-right Czech politician [[Filip Turek (racing driver)|Filip Turek]] and abroad such as Trump for inflaming political tensions within the country, urging to \"not let hatred and violence dictate our politics.\"<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.expats.cz/czech-news/article/hundreds-protest-in-prague-for-return-to-decency-in-world-politics|title=Hundreds protest in Prague for return to 'decency' in world politics|website=Expats.cz|date=5 August 2025|access-date=14 August 2025}}</ref>\n\nHašek has also commented on American politics. He is a critic of American President [[Donald Trump]], whom he called \"unpredictable\" and linked to \"dictatorship, evil, and endless lies.\"<ref>{{cite news|last=Sobotka|first=Michal|url=https://www.sport.cz/clanek/podcasty-priklep-priklep-trump-je-nepredvidatelny-musime-byt-pripraveni-na-ledasco-rika-hasek-5039664|title=PŘÍKLEP: Trump je nepředvídatelný. Harris|publisher=[[Fox News]]|date=24 October 2024|access-date=26 November 2024}}</ref> In 2020, after Trump suggested a [[Buffalo police shoving incident|Buffalo man injured by police]] could be an \"[[Antifa (United States)|ANTIFA]] provocateur\" for the [[George Floyd protests]], Hašek called his words \"disgusting\" and accused [[Republican Party (United States)|Republicans]] save for Senator [[Mitt Romney]] of \"hiding like rats.\"<ref>{{cite administration's friendlier stance towards Russia]] amidst the [[Russo-Ukrainian War]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://english.nv.ua/nation/hasek-slams-rubio-for-praising-putin-s-people-50521927.html|title=Hockey legend slams Rubio for greeting Russians on Russia Day|newspaper=[[The New Voice of Ukraine]]|date=13 June 2025|access-date=14 August 2025}}</ref> In 2026, he denounced [[Speaker of the United States House of Representatives|United States House of Representatives Speaker]] [[Mike Johnson]] as a \"complete scumbag\" for ridiculing Congressional attempts to release the [[Epstein files]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Connor|first=Trevor|url=https://www.hockeyfeed.com/nhl-news/dominik-hasek-rips-into-us-speaker-of-the-house-mike-johnson|title=Dominik Hasek rips into US Speaker of the House Mike Johnson|publisher=HockeyFeed|date=7 September 2026|access-date=18 September 2026}}</ref>\n\n====Russian invasion of Ukraine====\nFollowing the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]], Hašek advocated for the NHL and Olympics to ban Russians from playing except for those who speak out against it.<ref>{{cite news|last=Ostly|first=Ayrton|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nhl/2024/08/02/paris-olympics-dominik-hasek-ban-russian-players-hockey-war-ukraine/74653209007/|title=Hockey Hall of Famer Hašek says NHL owners should ban Russian athletes|newspaper=[[USA Today]]|date=2 August 2024|access-date=26 November 2024}}</ref> When the Sabres visited Prague to play in the [[NHL Global Series|2024 NHL Global Series]], Hašek did not attend the games to protest the league's inaction. He told ''[[The Athletic]]'' afterward that he wrote messages to discuss the matter but received \"only a brief response\" whereas the league \"made no effort to have a dialogue\". As a result, he decreased his involvement with the NHL.<ref>{{cite news|last=Fairburn|first=Matthew|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5821944/2024/10/10/dominik-hasek-nhl-russia-ukraine/|title=Dominik Hašek vs. the NHL: Why a legendary goalie shunned the Global Series spotlight|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|date=10 October 2024|access-date=26 November 2024|url-access=subscription}}</ref> His sentiment extended to other sports as well, such as criticizing the [[Stade Roland Garros]] for allowing Russian tennis players.<ref>{{cite news|last=Shostal|first=Oleksandr|url=https://112.ua/en/gasek-rozkritikuvav-wta-atp-ta-franciu-cerez-ucast-rosian-u-rolan-garros-66019|title=Hasek criticized WTA, ATP and France for the participation of Russians in the Roland Garros.|publisher=112.ua|date=12 June 2025|access-date=14 August 2025}}</ref>\n\nHašek has visited Ukrainian cities following their liberation from Russian occupation like [[Irpin]] and [[Bucha, Ukraine|Bucha]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Janicek|first=Karel|url=https://apnews.com/article/hasek-paris-olympics-russian-athletes-war-ukraine-2a7ba93cd185043abe9019f333e658d0|title=NHL great Hašek demands Russians openly condemn war against Ukraine or be banned from Paris Olympics|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|date=7 July 2023|access-date=26 November 2024}}</ref> He is an \"honorary Fella\" of [[NAFO (group)|NAFO]], a pro-Ukrainian social media movement.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://nafobase.cz/en/history-and-achievements-of-nafo/|title=History and achievements of NAFO|website=CZ/SK NAFO|access-date=26 November 2024|quote=Among the notable personalities who have been included among the honorary Fellas and who support and recognize the work of NAFO are, for example [...] Among the Czech personalities stand out [[Dana Drábová]] and Dominik Hašek.}}</ref>\n\nHis vocal stances on the war have caused tension with other hockey players and former teammates. He urged fellow Czech [[Libor Šulák]] against playing in the KHL and criticized their country's lawmakers for not passing legislation that would prohibit Czech citizens from working in Russia.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.idnes.cz/hokej/reprezentace/dominik-hasek-libor-sulak-rusko-khl-ukrajina-reakce-kalousek.A230808_091233_reprezentace_huda|title=Hašek oponuje Šulákovi: Ohrožujete mou rodinu. Reagoval také Kalousek|website=iDNES.cz|date=8 August 2023|access-date=26 November 2024|language=cs-CZ}}</ref> Ex-Red Wings teammate and Russian politician [[Viacheslav Fetisov]] demanded Hašek return the money he received while playing for Spartak Moscow, to which Hašek responded that Fetisov \"gave the green light\" to [[War crimes in the Russian invasion of Ukraine|Russian war crimes in Ukraine]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://athletistic.com/hockey/314028.html|title=Fetisov responded to Hasek's criticism of Russian athletes|website=Athletistic|date=4 July 2023|access-date=26 November 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Chekanov|first=Oleksandr|url=https://eng.obozrevatel.com/section-sport/news-for-the-deaths-of-ukrainians-legendary-hockey-player-put-the-olympic-champion-from-russia-in-his-place-25-07-2023.html|title=\"For the deaths of Ukrainians\": legendary hockey player put the Olympic champion from Russia in his place|publisher=[[Obozrevatel]]|date=25 July 2023|access-date=26 November 2024}}</ref> In 2024, he questioned the induction of Russian and former Red Wings teammate [[Pavel Datsyuk]] into the Hockey Hall of Fame, feeling the timing is inappropriate due to the war unless Datsyuk condemned it.<ref>{{cite news|last=Allen|first=Kevin|url=https://detroithockeynow.com/2024/07/13/domini-hasek-pavel-hasek-former-detroit-red-wings-hockey-hall-fame/|title=The Daily: Hasek Consistent in His Views: Sabres Grades|publisher=Detroit Hockey Now|date=13 July 2024|access-date=26 November 2024}}</ref>\n\n{{quote box\n| quote  = \"An NHL that showcases a Putin supporter is an advertisement for Russia's imperialist war. The NHL becomes complicit. Through its stance, the NHL bears a share of responsibility for the people killed and maimed in Russia's war in Ukraine.\"\n| source = Hašek, in a 2026 [[op-ed]] for ''[[The Washington Post]]''<ref>{{cite news|last=Hašek|first=Dominik|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/opinions/2026/09/30/when-ovechkin-takes-ice-putins-war-gets-boost/|title=When Ovechkin takes the ice, Putin's war Capitals]] captain and Russian player [[Alexander Ovechkin]], a supporter of President [[Vladimir Putin]], set the record for the most career goals in NHL history in 2025, Hašek branded him a \"huge advertisement for the aggressive Russian war and other Russian crimes.\"<ref>{{cite news|last=Penfold|first=Chuck|url=https://www.dw.com/en/ovechkin-breaks-nhl-goal-record-but-putin-link-casts-shadow/a-72046269|title=Ovechkin breaks NHL goal record but Putin link casts
