player and executive (born 1969)}}\n{{Use Canadian English|date=January 2020}}\n{{Use mdy dates|date=July 2024}}\n{{Infobox ice hockey player\n| name = Joe Sakic\n| hall_of_fame = 2012\n| image = Joe sakic.jpg\n| caption = Sakic with the [[Colorado Avalanche]] in 1997\n| birth_date = {{birth date and age|1969|7|7}}\n| birth_place = [[Burnaby]], British Columbia, Canada\n| height_ft = 5\n| height_in = 11\n| weight_lb = 195\n| position = [[Centre (ice hockey)|Centre]]\n| shoots = Left\n| played_for = [[Quebec Nordiques]]<br />[[Colorado Avalanche]]\n| ntl_team = CAN\n| draft = 15th overall\n| draft_year = 1987\n| draft_team = [[Quebec Nordiques]]\n| career_start = 1988\n| career_end = 2009\n}}\n\n'''Joseph Steven Sakic''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|s|æ|k|ᵻ|k}};<ref>{{cite web|last=Emrick |first=Mike |title=NHL Pronunciation Guide 19th annual edition 2002–03 season |publisher=National Hockey League |year=2002 |url=http://www.nhl.com/intheslot/read/impact/november/PronGuideTeam.pdf |page=11 |access-date=December 2, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120904003244/http://www.nhl.com/intheslot/read/impact/november/PronGuideTeam.pdf |archive-date=September 4, 2012}}</ref> ({{IPA|hr|ʃakitɕ}}<ref>{{cite web |author=Dražen Brajdić |date=June 8, 2006 |title=Bilo kuda, Hrvati svuda |url=http://www.vecernji.hr/newsroom/sports/more/496937/index.do?show=all |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071017151942/http://vecernji.hr/newsroom/sports/more/496937/index.do?show=all |archive-date=October 17, 2007 |access-date=September 20, 2007 |publisher=[[Večernji List]] |language=hr}}</ref>) born July 7, 1969) is a Canadian professional [[ice hockey]] executive and former player who currently serves as president of hockey operations and [[General manager#Sports teams|general manager]] of the [[Colorado Avalanche]] of the [[National Hockey League]] (NHL). He spent his entire 21-year NHL career, which lasted from 1988 to 2009, with the [[Quebec Nordiques]]/Colorado Avalanche franchise. Named [[captain (ice hockey)|captain]] of the team in [[1992–93 NHL season|1992]] (after serving as a co-captain in [[1990–91 NHL season|1990–91]]).\n\nSakic is regarded as one of the greatest team leaders in league history<ref name=\"Rocky Mountain News\"/> and was able to consistently motivate his team to play at a winning level.<ref name=\"Canadian Gold\">{{cite book|last=Podnieks|first=Andrew|title=Canadian Gold 2002: Making Hockey History|url=https://archive.org/details/canadiangold200200podn|url-access=registration|year=2002|publisher=Fenn Publishing Company Ltd.|location=Bolton, Ontario|page=[https://archive.org/details/canadiangold200200podn/page/144 144]|isbn=9781551682686}}</ref> Nicknamed \"'''Burnaby Joe'''\", Sakic was named to 13 [[NHL All-Star Game]]s and selected to the NHL First All-Star Team at [[Centre (ice hockey)|centre]] three times. Sakic led the Avalanche to two [[Presidents' Trophy|first-place regular season finishes]] in 1997 and 2001, and two [[Stanley Cup]] titles in 1996 and 2001, earning the [[Conn Smythe Trophy|most valuable player (MVP)]] in the [[1996 Stanley Cup playoffs|1996 playoffs]]. In 2001, Sakic earned both the [[Hart Memorial Trophy]] and [[Lester B. Pearson Award]] as MVP of the NHL.<ref name=\"Recordbook\"/> He is one of six players to participate in the first two of the team's Stanley Cup victories. He won the Stanley Cup a third time with the Avalanche in [[2022 Stanley Cup Final|2022]] while serving as the team's general manager. Sakic became the fourth person, after [[Milt Schmidt]], [[Serge Savard]] and [[Lester Patrick]] to win the Stanley Cup with the same franchise as a player and general manager.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://records.nhl.com/playoff-summary/stanley-cup-winner?season=19271928 |title=1978-28 New York Rangers\n|date=August 5, 2026 |first=Colin |last=Newby |website=records.nhl.com}}</ref>\n\nOver his career, Sakic was one of the most productive forwards in the game, scoring 50 goals twice and earning at least 100 points in six different seasons. Sakic's [[wrist shot (ice hockey)|wrist shot]], considered one of the best in the NHL, was the source of much of his production as goalies around the league feared his rapid snap-shot release.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.thehockeynews.com/articles/27171-Top-Shelf-Its-all-in-the-wrist-not-mouth-for-Sakic.html|title=Top Shelf: It's all in the wrist – not mouth – for Sakic|last=Dixon|first=Ryan|date=July 8, 2009|work=The Hockey News|access-date=July 26, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090712142541/http://www.thehockeynews.com/articles/27171-Top-Shelf-Its-all-in-the-wrist-not-mouth-for-Sakic.html|archive-date=July 12, 2009|url-status=dead}}</ref> At the conclusion of the [[2008–09 NHL season]], Sakic was the eighth [[List of NHL statistical leaders|all-time points leader]] in the NHL, as well as 14th in all-time goals<ref name=\"500 goals\">{{cite news|url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=417887|title=NHL 500-Goal Scorers |access-date=November 21, 2007|publisher=NHL.com|year=2007|agency=Associated Press}}{{dead link|date=July 2026|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> and 11th in all-time assists.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/careerstats.htm?fetchKey=00002ALLAAHAll&sort=assists&viewName=careerLeadersAllSeasons|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090116223803/http://nhl.com/ice/careerstats.htm?fetchKey=00002ALLAAHAll&sort=assists&viewName=careerLeadersAllSeasons|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 16, 2009|title=NHL Career Assists Leaders|publisher=NHL.com|access-date=December 28, 2009}}</ref> During the [[2002 Winter Olympics]], Sakic helped lead [[Canada men's national ice hockey team|Team Canada]] to its first ice hockey gold medal in 50 years and was voted as the tournament's MVP.<ref name=\"Canadian Gold\"/> Sakic represented Team Canada in six other international competitions, including the [[Canada at the 1998 Winter Olympics|1998]] and [[Canada at the 2006 Winter Olympics|2006]] Winter Olympics.\n\nSakic retired from the NHL in 2009 and had his jersey number 19 retired prior to the Avalanche's [[2009–10 NHL season|2009–10 season]] opener.<ref name=\"Retired Jersey\"/> In 2012, Sakic was inducted into the [[Hockey Hall of Fame]]. In 2013, Sakic was inducted into the [[Canada's Sports Hall of Fame]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Sakic, Costello named to Canada Sports Hall of Fame|publisher=NHL.com|date=April 11, 2013|url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=665293|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150206041145/http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=665293|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 6, 2015|access-date=December 4, 2013}}</ref> In 2017, Sakic was named one of the [[100 Greatest NHL Players]] in history.<ref>{{cite web|title=100 Greatest NHL Players|url=https://www.nhl.com/history/nhl-centennial/nhl-100-greatest-players| website = NHL.com|access-date=January 27, 2017|date=January 27, 2017}}</ref> He was also inducted into the [[IIHF Hall of Fame]] in 2017.\n\nTwo years after retiring as a player, Sakic returned to the Avalanche organization in a management capacity, first serving as executive advisor and alternate governor from 2011 to 2013. Sakic was promoted to executive vice president of hockey operations on May 10, 2013, and named general manager the following year. After overseeing a team rebuild, culminating in the franchise's third first-place regular season finish in 2021, and a Stanley Cup victory in 2022, Sakic won the [[Jim Gregory General Manager of the Year Award]]. The team announced shortly thereafter that Sakic was being promoted to president of hockey operations.<ref name=THN220711>{{cite web|last=Ellis|first=Steven|title=Chris MacFarland becomes Avalanche GM, Sakic moves to Hockey Ops|website=[[The Hockey News]]|url=https://thehockeynews.com/news/news/chris-macfarland-to-become-avalanche-gm-sakic-moves-to-hockey-ops|date=July 11, 2022|access-date=July 11, 2022}}</ref> Following the departure of his successor [[Chris MacFarland]] in 2026, Sakic re-assumed the role of general manager. Sakic has spent all but three years of his adult life with the Nordiques/Avalanche as a player or executive, being a member of all three Stanley Cups and four [[Presidents' Trophy|Presidents' Trophies]] in franchise history.\n\n==Early life==\nSakic was born in [[Burnaby]], British Columbia, to Marijan and Slavica Šakić<ref name=\"Encyclopedia\">{{cite book|editor-last=Francis|editor-first=Daniel |title=Encyclopedia of British Columbia|year=2000|publisher=Harbour Publishing|location=Madeira Park, BC|isbn=1-55017-200-X|page=806}}</ref> ({{IPA|hr|ʃakitɕ}}<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.vecernji.hr/newsroom/sports/more/496937/index.do?show=all|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071017151942/http://vecernji.hr/newsroom/sports/more/496937/index.do?show=all|archive-date=October 17, 2007|title=Bilo kuda, Hrvati svuda|publisher=[[Večernji List]]|date=June 8, 2006|author=Dražen Brajdić|access-date=September 20, 2007|language=hr}}</ref>), immigrants from [[Croatia]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Merk|first=Martin|title=NHL history for Croatia|publisher=International Ice Hockey Federation|date=December 10, 2014|url=http://www.iihf.com/home-of-hockey/news/news-singleview/?tx_ttnews%5Btt_news%5D=9242&cHash=2f3123bf391669da167f53cc516b5b92|access-date=December 24, 2016}}</ref> Growing up in Burnaby,<ref>{{cite news|last=Pap|first=Elliott|title='Burnaby Joe' Sakic returns home for Giants honour|work=The Vancouver Sun|date=January 30, 2013|url=https://vancouversun.com/sports/canucks%20-%20hockey/burnaby-joe-sakic-returns-home-for-giants-honour|access-date=February 16, 2023}}</ref> Sakic did not learn to speak English until [[kindergarten]], having been raised with [[Croatian language|Croatian]] as his [[mother tongue]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Frei|first=Terry|title=Do you speak hockey?|work=The Denver Post|date=October 8, 2000|url=http://extras.denverpost.com/hockey/focus1008.htm|access-date=December 24, 2016}}</ref> At the age of four, Sakic attended his first NHL game, a match between the [[Vancouver Canucks]] and [[Atlanta Flames]]. After watching the game, Sakic decided that he wanted to become a hockey player. As a smaller player, Sakic was forced to use skill rather than size to excel and modelled himself after his idol, [[Wayne Gretzky]].<ref name=\"No Average Joe\"/> After showing exceptional promise as a young hockey player, Sakic was referred to as a new Wayne Gretzky in the making.<ref name=\"Encyclopedia\"/> Sakic scored 83 goals and 156 points in 80 games for Burnaby BC Selects<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 4, 2024 |title=Joe Sakic - Stats, Contract, Salary & More |url=https://www.eliteprospects.com/player/8862/joe-sakic |access-date=May 4, 2024 |website=Elite Prospects}}</ref> while attending school at [[Burnaby North Secondary]]. Soon after, he was added to the [[Lethbridge Broncos]] of the [[Western Hockey League]] (WHL) for the last part of the [[1985–86 WHL season|1985–86 season]].<ref name=\"Sudden Death 113\">{{cite book|last1=Culp|first1=Leesa|last2=Drinnan|first2=Gregg|last3=Wilkie|first3=Bob|title=Sudden Death: The Incredible Saga of the 1986 Swift Current Broncos|year=2012|publisher=Dundurn|location=Toronto|isbn=978-1459705449|page=113}}</ref>\n\nDuring the [[1986–87 WHL season|1986–87 season]], the Broncos relocated to [[Swift Current, Saskatchewan]], becoming the [[Swift Current Broncos]]. Sakic, playing in his first full season, scored 60 goals and 73 assists for 133 points.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Culp|last2=Drinnan|last3=Wilkie|title=Sudden Death: The Incredible Saga of the 1986 Swift Current Broncos|pages=112–113}}</ref> These totals saw him named Rookie of the Year of the WHL.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Culp|last2=Drinnan|last3=Wilkie|title=Sudden Death: The Incredible Saga of the 1986 Swift Current Broncos|page=188}}</ref> But while Sakic enjoyed success on the ice, he and his team faced a tragedy on the night of December 30, 1986. The Broncos were driving to a game against the [[Regina Pats]] and due to bad weather conditions, the bus [[Swift Current Broncos bus crash|crashed after the driver lost control]] on a patch of black ice outside of Swift Current. While Sakic was unharmed, four of his teammates (Trent Kresse, Scott Kruger, Chris Mantyka, and Brent Ruff) were killed. This incident had a lasting impact on the young Sakic,<ref name=\"No Average Joe\">{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=287938|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121013161448/http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=287938|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 13, 2012|title=No average Joe – Sakic quietly moving among NHL all-time greats men|access-date=January 28, 2007|publisher=[[NHL|NHL.com]]|year=2007|agency=Associated Press}}</ref> who declined to talk about the crash throughout his career.<ref name=\"Denial of Death\">{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/espn/eticket/story?lid=tab1pos1&lpos=spotlight&page=swiftcurrent&redirected=true|title=Denial of Death|access-date=April 9, 2007|publisher=ESPN|year=2007|author=Joyce, Gare}}</ref> The next year, in [[1987–88 WHL season|1987–88]], Sakic was named the [[Four Broncos Memorial Trophy|WHL Most Valuable Player]] and [[CHL Player of the Year|Canadian Major Junior Player of the Year]]. He scored 160 points (78 goals, 82 assists), tying him with [[Theoren Fleury]] of the [[Moose Jaw Warriors]] for the WHL scoring title.<ref name=\"Sudden Death 113\"/><ref name=\"Canadian Gold\"/><ref>{{cite web |title=Player of the Year – Four Broncos Memorial Trophy|url=http://whl.ca/records/awards.php?id=50|archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20071017172353/http://whl.ca/records/awards.php?id=50|archive-date=October 17, 2007|publisher=[[Western Hockey League|WHL]]|access-date =September 18, 2007}}</ref>\n\n==NHL career==\n\n===Quebec Nordiques===\nSakic was drafted 15th overall by the [[Quebec Nordiques]] in the [[1987 NHL entry draft]], a pick the Nordiques received when they traded away [[Dale Hunter]] and [[Clint Malarchuk]] to the [[Washington Capitals]].<ref name=\"Recordbook\"/> Rather than make the immediate jump into the NHL, Sakic told Nordiques management he would prefer to spend the 1987–88 season in Swift Current to prepare for the NHL.<ref name=\"Legends of Hockey\">{{cite web|url=http://www.legendsofhockey.net/LegendsOfHockey/jsp/SearchPlayer.jsp?player=11437 |title=Joe Sakic Page |access-date=April 9, 2007 |publisher=Legends of Hockey |year=2007 |author=Legends of Hockey |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070929154056/http://www.legendsofhockey.net/LegendsOfHockey/jsp/SearchPlayer.jsp?player=11437 |archive-date=September 29, 2007}}</ref> Sakic made his professional debut on October 6, 1988, against the [[Hartford Whalers]] and registered an assist. His first NHL goal came two days later against goaltender [[Sean Burke]] of the [[New Jersey Devils]].<ref name = \"NHLPA Bio\"/> During the season, Sakic wore number 88, because his preferred number 19 was already taken by a teammate, [[Alain Côté (ice hockey, born 1957)|Alain Côté]].<ref name=\"Numbers\">{{cite book | last = Morrison | first = Scott | author-link = Scott Morrison (journalist) | title = Hockey Night in Canada By the Numbers: From 00 to 99 | publisher = Key Porter Books Ltd. | year = 2007 | location = Toronto | page = [https://archive.org/details/bynumbersfrom00t0000morr/page/232 232] | isbn = 978-1-55263-984-9 | url = https://archive.org/details/bynumbersfrom00t0000morr/page/232}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title =1988–89 Quebec Nordiques|url =http://www.hockeydb.com/ihdb/stats/leagues/seasons/teams/0000471989.html|publisher =The Internet Hockey Database|access-date =July 16, 2007}}</ref> While considered a front-runner for [[Calder Memorial Trophy|rookie of the year]] due to his rapid scoring pace, an ankle injury forced Sakic to miss 10 games in December. The resulting scoring slump helped quash any hopes of winning the award.<ref name=\"Globe and Mail\">{{cite news |last= Beamish |first= Mike|title= Nords' rookie Sakic hits first slump|work= Vancouver Sun|location= Vancouver|page= E. 1|date= February 16, 1989}}</ref> Sakic would finish his rookie season with 62 points in 70 games, finishing eighth in voting for the Calder. Defenceman [[Brian Leetch]] won the rookie scoring race with 28 goals and 48 assists, receiving forty-two first-place votes, while Sakic only received two third-place votes.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nhl.com/stats/player?reportType=season&seasonFrom=19881989&seasonTo=19881989&gameType=2&experience=1&filter=gamesPlayed,gte,1&sort=points,goals,assists|title=NHL.com - Stats|website=www.nhl.com|access-date=October 2, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hockey-reference.com/awards/voting-1989.html|title=1988-89 NHL Awards Voting {{!}} Hockey-Reference.com|website=Hockey-Reference.com|access-date=October 2, 2018}}</ref>\n\nIn [[1989–90 NHL season|1989–90]], his second NHL season, Sakic was able to switch back to his familiar number 19 (Alain Côté had retired over the summer) and scored 102 points, which was ninth overall in the league, becoming the first player in NHL history to score 100 points on a last place team. At the start of the next season, [[1990–91 NHL season|1990–91]], Sakic was named [[captain (hockey)|co-captain]] of the Nordiques along with [[Steven Finn (ice hockey)|Steven Finn]] (Sakic was captain for home games, Finn for away games).<ref name=\"Steven Finn\">{{cite web|url=http://www.hockeydraftcentral.com/1984/84057.html|title=1984 NHL Entry Draft: Steven Finn|access-date=November 21, 2007|publisher=HockeyDraftCentral.com|year=2005|author=Hockey Draft Central}}</ref> Sakic again passed the 100 point mark, improving to 109 points and sixth overall in the league but would slip during the [[1991–92 NHL season|1991–92 season]] to 94 points after missing 11 games.<ref>{{cite web|title=Joe Sakic|publisher=Hockey-Reference|url=https://www.hockey-reference.com/players/s/sakicjo01.html|access-date=December 26, 2016}}</ref> In [[1991–92 NHL season|1991–92]], [[Mike Hough]] became captain of the Nordiques, while Sakic and Finn became alternate captains. Sakic began to display the leadership for which he would become known, standing firm during the tumultuous [[Eric Lindros trade|Eric Lindros holdout]].<ref name=\"speaks\">{{cite news|title=Sakic speaks out ... Nords' star says players want Page to deal Lindros|work=The Hamilton Spectator|agency=Canadian Press|date=October 30, 1991|page=E2}}</ref><ref name=\"leaders\">{{cite web|last=Eichel|first=Matt|title=Joe Sakic: NHL's All-Time Greatest Leaders Part I|website=Bleacher Report|date=May 25, 2008|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/25392-joe-sakic-nhls-all-time-great-leaders-part-i|access-date=December 26, 2016}}</ref><ref name=\"C\">{{cite web|last=Marin|first=Christian|title=NHL captains who were stripped of the \"C\"|publisher=The Sports Network|date=August 22, 2014|url=http://www2.tsn.ca/bardown/Story.aspx?NHL+captains+who+were+stripped+of+the+%E2%80%9CC%E2%80%9D&id=460003|access-date=December 26, 2016|archive-date=December 27, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161227061044/http://www2.tsn.ca/bardown/Story.aspx?NHL+captains+who+were+stripped+of+the+%E2%80%9CC%E2%80%9D&id=460003|url-status=dead}}</ref> With Lindros refusing to play for the Nordiques, one of the worst teams in league, Sakic commented, \"We only want players here who have the passion to play the game. I'm tired of hearing that name. He's not here and there are a lot of others in this locker room who really care about the game.\"<ref>{{cite news|last=Hochberg|first=Len|title=Lindros Trade Fills Avalanche's Cup|newspaper=The Washington Post|date=June 8, 1996|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/sports/1996/06/08/lindros-trade-fills-avalanches-cup/087d10b3-32fe-4a23-a42b-ba54063ccad6/|access-date=December 26, 2016}}</ref><ref name=\"exec\">{{cite web|last=Wharnsby|first=Tim|title=Joe Sakic thriving in role as Avalanche exec|publisher=[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation]]|date=October 17, 2013|url=http://www.cbc.ca/sports-content/hockey/opinion/2013/10/joe-sakic-thriving-in-new-role-with-avalanche.html|access-date=December 26, 2016}}</ref> Lindros was traded a year later, ending the situation and bringing in a number of quality players who vastly improved the Nordiques.<ref name=\"Lindros\">{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/intheslot/read/impact/2003_04/march/lindros.html |title=Quantity and quality: Avalanche still reap reward from Lindros trade |access-date=July 11, 2013 |publisher=NHL.com |date=March 2004 |author=Coffey, Phil |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140318193733/http://www.nhl.com/intheslot/read/impact/2003_04/march/lindros.html |archive-date=March 18, 2014}}</ref> During their first four seasons with Joe Sakic, the Nordiques finished last place in the [[Adams Division]] and last in the league for three straight years, from 1989 to 1991.<ref name=\"Recordbook\"/>\n\nStarting with the [[1992–93 NHL season|1992–93 season]], Sakic became the sole captain of the franchise.<ref name=\"Recordbook\"/> Under his leadership, the Nordiques made the playoffs for the first time in six years and set a franchise record for wins and points in the process (since broken by the [[2021–22 NHL season|2021–22]] Colorado Avalanche team).<ref name=\"Recordbook\"/> Sakic reached the 100-point plateau, the third time in five years, scoring 48 goals and 105 points in the regular season while adding another six points in the playoffs. After the shortened [[1994–95 NHL season|1994–95]] following the [[1994–95 NHL lock-out]], Sakic finished eight points behind [[Jaromír Jágr]] for the scoring title, finishing fourth place overall, and helped the Nordiques win the division title, their first since the 1985–86 season.<ref name=\"Recordbook\"/>\n\n===Colorado Avalanche===\nIn May 1995, the Nordiques announced that the team had been sold and were relocating from Quebec. The franchise then moved to [[Denver|Denver, Colorado]], and were renamed the [[Colorado Avalanche]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1995/05/26/sports/1995-nhl-playoffs-nordiques-off-to-denver-after-75-million-deal.html|title=1995 N.H.L. Playoffs; Nordiques Off to Denver After $75 Million Deal|access-date=August 18, 2018|newspaper=The New York Times|author=Richard Sandomir|date=May 26, 1995}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.upi.com/Archives/1995/08/10/Colorados-NHL-team-to-be-Avalanche/3476808027200/|title=Colorado's NHL team to be Avalanche|access-date=August 18, 2018|publisher=United Press International|date=August 10, 1995}}</ref> Sakic led the team to a [[1996 Stanley Cup Final|Stanley Cup]] championship in its first year, scoring 120 points in 82 regular season games and 34 points in 22 playoff games. Sakic was awarded the Conn Smythe Trophy as the most valuable player of the 1996 NHL playoffs. During the run for the Cup, Sakic again proved himself to be an effective team leader. Although his Nordiques had missed the playoffs in five of his first seven years in the NHL, he scored 18 goals, including six game-winners, and 34 points. Sakic was one goal away from the record for goals in a playoff year, and his game-winning goals established a new record.<ref name=\"1997 NHL Yearbook\">{{cite book | last = National Hockey League | title = 1997 NHL Yearbook | year = 1996 | publisher = Worldsport Properties | location = Toronto | page = 232}}</ref>\n\n[[File:Joe Sakic 1997.jpg|thumb|upright|Sakic playing with the Avalanche in 1997]]\nIn the [[1996–97 NHL season|1996–97]] season, Sakic played in only 65 games due to a lacerated calf<ref name=\"Rocky Mountain News\">{{cite news|url=http://www.rockymountainnews.com/drmn/nhl/article/0,2777,DRMN_23920_5301508,00.html |title=Sakic lets game, NHL do talking |access-date=April 10, 2007 |newspaper=Rocky Mountain News |year=2007 |author=Sadowski, Rick |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070930223252/http://www.rockymountainnews.com/drmn/nhl/article/0%2C2777%2CDRMN_23920_5301508%2C00.html |archive-date=September 30, 2007 |url-status=dead}}</ref> yet still managed to score 74 points as the Avalanche earned their first [[Presidents' Trophy]] and third straight division title.<ref name=\"NHLPA Bio\">{{cite web|url=http://www.nhlpa.com/WebStats/PlayerBiography.asp?ID=4934|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061115141123/http://www.nhlpa.com/WebStats/PlayerBiography.asp?ID=4934|archive-date=November 15, 2006|title=NHLPA Player Bio|access-date=April 10, 2007|publisher=NHLPA|year=2007|author=National Hockey League Players' Association|author-link=National Hockey League Players' Association}}</ref> Sakic had another great playoff season with eight goals and 17 assists and took the Avalanche all the way to the conference finals, where they eventually lost to the [[Detroit Red Wings]] in six games. As a free agent during the summer of 1997, Sakic signed a three-year, $21 million [[offer sheet]] with the [[New York Rangers]] as a restricted free agent. Under the [[collective bargaining agreement]] at the time, the Avalanche had one week to match the Rangers' offer or let go of Sakic in exchange for five first-round draft picks as compensation. While it seemed as if the Avalanche could not afford to keep Sakic, as they had already committed large amounts of salary to [[Peter Forsberg]] and [[Patrick Roy]], an unlikely lifeline would appear in the form of the summer blockbuster movie ''[[Air Force One (film)|Air Force One]]'', produced by Avalanche owners [[COMSAT]]. Its profits enabled the Avalanche to match the offer,<ref name=\"Legends of Hockey\"/> which instigated a salary raise for many NHL players.<ref name=\"TSN about the CBA\">{{cite news|url=https://www.tsn.ca/nhl/news_story/?ID=99378&hubname=nhl|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070519022104/http://www.tsn.ca/nhl/news_story/?ID=99378&hubname=nhl|archive-date=May 19, 2007|title=Three key contracts helped kill the CBA|access-date=April 9, 2007|publisher=TSN.ca|year=2004|agency=Associated Press}}</ref>\n\nInjuries would again limit Sakic's playing time during the [[1997–98 NHL season|1997–98]] season. While playing in his first Olympics with Team Canada, Sakic hurt his knee and was forced to miss 18 games with the Avalanche.<ref name=\"Avalanche Website\">{{cite web|url=https://www.nhl.com/player/joe-sakic-8451101|title=Colorado Avalanche Team Bio|access-date=April 10, 2007|publisher=Colorado Avalanche|year=2006|author=Colorado Avalanche|author-link=Colorado Avalanche}}</ref> In the 64 games in which he did play, Sakic still scored 63 points, enough to earn him his seventh all-star appearance.<ref name=\"NHLPA Bio\"/> Sakic finally rebounded from his injuries in the [[1998–99 NHL season|1998–99]] season, finishing fifth in the league in scoring with 41 goals and 96 points in only 73 games. Sakic led the Avalanche to within one game of the Stanley Cup Final, where they lost to the eventual champion [[Dallas Stars]]. After the season ended, Sakic ranked number 94 on ''[[The Hockey News]]''' list of the 100 greatest hockey players.<ref name=\"100 Greatest Players\">{{cite book | last = Dryden | first = Steve | title = The Top 100 NHL Players Of All Time | year = 1997 | publisher = McClelland & Stewart Inc. | location = Toronto | page = 160 | isbn= 0-7710-4176-4}}</ref>\n\nDuring the [[1999–2000 NHL season|1999–2000]] season, Sakic reached several career milestones. Injuries limited him to only 60 games, but he still managed to lead the team in scoring with 81 points. On December 27, 1999, against the [[St. Louis Blues]], Sakic earned an assist to become the 56th player in NHL history to reach 1,000 career points.<ref name=\"2001 NHL Yearbook\"/> Later in the season, on March 23, 2000, he scored a [[hat-trick]] against the [[Arizona Coyotes|Phoenix Coyotes]] and became the 59th player to score 400 career goals.<ref name=\"2001 NHL Yearbook\"/> It also gave Sakic 1,049 points with the franchise, passing [[Peter Šťastný]] as the all-time leader on the team.<ref name=\"NHLPA Bio\"/><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/sakics-hat-tricks-coyotes/|title=Sakic's Hat Tricks Coyotes|access-date=August 18, 2018|publisher=CBS News|date=March 24, 2000}}</ref>\n\nSakic eclipsed the 100 point mark again in [[2000–01 NHL season|2000–01]], finishing with 118 points along with a career-best 54 goals, both second-best in the league. Sakic won the Hart Memorial Trophy, the [[Lady Byng Memorial Trophy]] and the Lester B. Pearson Award (the latter presented to him by former Nordiques mentor Peter Šťastný<ref>{{cite news|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/hockey/nhl/news/2001/06/14/sakic_pearson_ap/|title=Sakic wins Pearson|access-date=August 19, 2018|publisher=CNN/Sports Illustrated|date=June 14, 2001|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140318194315/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/hockey/nhl/news/2001/06/14/sakic_pearson_ap/|archive-date=March 18, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>) while also being a finalist for the [[Frank J. Selke Trophy]]. Sakic led the Avalanche to their second Stanley Cup championship, defeating the defending title holding [[New Jersey Devils]] in seven games. Memorably, after receiving the [[Stanley Cup]] from [[NHL Commissioner]] [[Gary Bettman]], Sakic broke with tradition. Instead of hoisting it first as most captains do, Sakic passed the cup straight to [[Ray Bourque]], a player who had waited a record-breaking 22 seasons to win the Stanley Cup.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.denverpost.com/2012/11/11/frei-joe-sakic-was-defined-by-passing-the-cup-to-ray-bourque/|title=Frei: Joe Sakic was defined by passing the Cup to Ray Bourque|access-date=August 18, 2018|newspaper=The Denver Post|author=Terry Frei|date=November 11, 2012}}</ref><ref name=\"Pass\">{{cite web|url=http://www.hockeyforum.com/nhl-forum/7602-hockey-tradition-comes-nfl.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110712213418/http://www.hockeyforum.com/nhl-forum/7602-hockey-tradition-comes-nfl.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 12, 2011|title=A hockey tradition comes to the NFL|access-date=January 28, 2007|publisher=NHL.com|year=2007|author=Weiner, Evan}}</ref>\n\nSakic led the Avalanche in scoring again in the [[2001–02 NHL season|2001–02 season]], finishing sixth in the league with 79 points. On March 9, 2002, Sakic played in his 1,000th career game. The Avalanche once again reached the Western Conference Finals but lost to the eventual cup-winning [[Detroit Red Wings]]. The following year, Sakic appeared in only 58 games and finished with just 58 points.<ref name=\"NHLPA Bio\"/> Sakic rebounded the following year, finishing third in the league with 87 points. It also marked the first time since the [[1993–94 NHL season|1993–94]] season that the franchise did not win the division title, which was won by the [[Vancouver Canucks]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2006/05/12/AR2006051201751_2.html|title=Avalanche's Lacroix Steps Down As GM|access-date=August 18, 2018|newspaper=The Washington Post|author=Arnie Stapleton|date=May 12, 2006}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nucksmisconduct.com/2013/1/5/3829158/top-10-canucks-seasons-of-all-time-5-2003-04|title=Top 10 Canucks Seasons of All-time - #5: 2003-04|access-date=August 18, 2018|publisher=Nucks Misconduct|date=January 5, 2013|archive-date=August 18, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180818182143/https://www.nucksmisconduct.com/2013/1/5/3829158/top-10-canucks-seasons-of-all-time-5-2003-04|url-status=dead}}</ref>\n\n[[File:SakicWarmup2'.jpg|left|thumb|upright|Sakic warming up before a game in 2007]]\n\nFollowing the [[2004–05 NHL lock-out]], the Avalanche were forced to lose many of their key players in order to stay below the salary cap.<ref name=\"Lockout\">{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/news/story?id=2116068|title=Sakic, Blake to stay; Forsberg, Foote up in air|access-date=April 10, 2007|work=ESPN.com|year=2005|agency=Associated Press}}</ref> Even with the loss of teammates [[Peter Forsberg]] and [[Adam Foote]], Sakic still helped the Avalanche get into the playoffs, where they eventually lost to the [[Anaheim Ducks]] in the conference semi-finals.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/ducks/news/ducks-sweep-avalanche/c-468707 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180829073725/https://www.nhl.com/ducks/news/ducks-sweep-avalanche/c-468707 |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 29, 2018 |title=DUCKS SWEEP AVALANCHE! |date=May 11, 2006 |publisher=NHL.com |access-date=August 29, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/avalanche/news/avs-end-season-with-4-1-loss-to-ducks/c-426516 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180829072652/https://www.nhl.com/avalanche/news/avs-end-season-with-4-1-loss-to-ducks/c-426516 |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 29, 2018 |title=Avs End Season With 4-1 Loss To Ducks |date=May 11, 2006 |publisher=NHL.com |access-date=August 29, 2018}}</ref> In June 2006, Sakic signed a one-year, $5.75 million deal to keep him with the Avalanche for the [[2006–07 NHL season|2006–07 season]].<ref name=\"Contract\">{{cite news|url=http://www.denverpost.com/avalanche/ci_3961182|title=Sakic stays with Avs|access-date=September 19, 2006|publisher=DenverPost.com|year=2006|author=Dater, Adrian}}</ref> Upon the retirement of [[Steve Yzerman]] a month later, on July 3, 2006, Sakic became the league leader for most career points among active players.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/news/story?id=2508103|title=Longtime Red Wings captain Yzerman retires|access-date=August 18, 2018|publisher=ESPN|date=July 4, 2006}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.eliteprospects.com/league/nhl/stats/all-time?sort=tp&from=1918-1919&to=2006-2007|title=NHL - All-time totals|access-date=August 18, 2018|publisher=eliteprospects.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180818110421/https://www.eliteprospects.com/league/nhl/stats/all-time?sort=tp&from=1918-1919&to=2006-2007|archive-date=August 18, 2018}}</ref>\n\nSakic had another strong season in the [[2006–07 NHL season|2006–07]]. He scored his 600th career goal on February 15, 2007, against the [[Calgary Flames]], becoming the 17th player in history to reach the milestone and third that year.<ref name=\"600 Goals\">{{cite news|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nhl/recap?gameId=270215003|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120111120644/http://sports.espn.go.com/nhl/recap?gameId=270215003|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 11, 2012|title=Sakic scores empty-netter for No. 600 in Avs' win|access-date=April 10, 2007|work=ESPN.com|year=2007|agency=Associated Press}}</ref> On the final day of the regular season, Sakic scored his 100th point, reaching the milestone for the sixth time in his career. At the same time, Sakic became the second-oldest NHL player to score 100 points in a season at age 37, alongside hockey legend [[Gordie Howe]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nhl/recap?gid=2007040817 |title=Avalanche 6, Flames 3 |access-date=April 10, 2007 |publisher=Yahoo! Sports! |year=2007 |agency=Associated Press |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070416092803/http://sports.yahoo.com/nhl/recap?gid=2007040817 |archive-date=April 16, 2007}}</ref> Despite his efforts, as well as a late-season charge, Sakic and the Avalanche missed the playoffs for the first time in 11 years, finishing one point behind the eighth placed Calgary Flames.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nhl.com/news/predators-4-avalanche-2/c-106480|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180820172505/https://www.nhl.com/news/predators-4-avalanche-2/c-106480|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 20, 2018|title=Predators 4, Avalanche 2|publisher=NHL.com|date=April 8, 2007|access-date=August 20, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/standings/_/season/2007/group/conference|title=NHL Standings - 2006-07|publisher=ESPN|access-date=August 20, 2018}}</ref> On May 1, the NHL announced that Sakic was named as one of the three finalists for the Lady Byng Trophy,<ref name=\"Byng Finalist\">{{cite news|url=http://www.denverpost.com/sports/ci_5796168|title=Sakic one of three Lady Byng finalists|access-date=May 13, 2007|newspaper=The Denver Post|author=Dater, Adrian|date=May 2, 2007}}</ref> but it was eventually awarded to [[Pavel Datsyuk]] of the Detroit Red Wings.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/news/story?id=2855100|title=2007 NHL Awards: Finalists and winners|access-date=August 18, 2018|publisher=ESPN|date=June 15, 2007}}</ref>\n\nIn April 2007, Sakic signed to a 19th NHL season with the Avalanche on a one-year deal for the [[2007–08 NHL season|2007–08 season]].<ref name=\"Sakic signs one-year deal with Avalanche\">{{cite web|url=https://www.tsn.ca/nhl/news_story/?ID=203493&hubname=|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070929123113/http://www.tsn.ca/nhl/news_story/?ID=203493&hubname=|archive-date=September 29, 2007|title=Sakic signs one-year deal with Avalanche|access-date=April 9, 2007|publisher=TSN.ca|year=2007|agency=Canadian Press}}</ref> Sakic commented on the deal, saying, \"at this stage in my career, I prefer to do one-year deals as I evaluate my play year-to-year.\"<ref name=\"Sakic signs one-year deal with Avalanche\"/> Upon signing Sakic to the deal, Avalanche General Manager [[François Giguère]] said, \"Joe is the heart of this organization and his leadership and value to this team and especially our young players is unquestioned.\"<ref name=\"Sakic resigned\">{{cite news|title=Joe Sakic signs one-year deal |work=Cranbrook Daily Townsman |date=April 10, 2007 |agency=Canadian Press |page=7}}</ref> On October 7, 2007, he scored a goal and had an assist against the [[San Jose Sharks]], moving past [[Phil Esposito]] into eighth place on the NHL career points list with 1,591 points.<ref>{{cite news|title=Stastny lifts Avs to 6-2 win over San Jose with goal and 4 assists |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nhl/recap?gid=2007100717 |agency=Associated Press |publisher=Yahoo! Sports! |date=October 7, 2007 |access-date=October 27, 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071011021544/http://sports.yahoo.com/nhl/recap?gid=2007100717 |archive-date=October 11, 2007}}</ref> Nineteen days later, Sakic scored a goal and assisted [[Ryan Smyth]] for an overtime game-winning goal against the Calgary Flames, reaching his 1,600th point in the NHL.<ref>{{cite news|title=Smyth scores OT goal to give Avalanche 3-2 victory over Flames |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nhl/recap?gid=2007102603 |agency=Associated Press |publisher=Yahoo! Sports! |date=October 26, 2007 |access-date=October 27, 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071029041028/http://sports.yahoo.com/nhl/recap?gid=2007102603 |archive-date=October 29, 2007}}</ref> On December 27, 2007, it was announced that Sakic underwent [[Hernia repair|hernia surgery]] to accelerate the recovery of an injury that had forced him to miss the previous 12 games after a 232 consecutive games-played streak. The operation caused him to miss a career-high 38 games. He was activated off injured reserve on February 24 and played that night, recording an assist.<ref name=\"Sakic returns\">{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/news/story?id=3263018|title=Sakic back after career-high 38-game absence; has assist, shot on goal |access-date=March 6, 2008|publisher=ESPN|year=2008|agency=Associated Press}}</ref> On March 22, 2008, Sakic recorded his 1,000th career assist against the [[Edmonton Oilers]], becoming the 11th player in NHL history to reach the milestone.<ref name=\"1000 assists\">{{cite news |title=Sakic hits major milestone with assist No. 1,000|url=http://www.denverpost.com/avalanche/ci_8665090|author=Frei, Terry|work=[[Denver Post]]|date=March 22, 2008|access-date=March 27, 2008}}</ref>\n\nIn June 2008, Sakic spoke with Colorado General Manager François Giguère and said he was uncertain with his future with the Avalanche.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.denverpost.com/2008/06/02/avs-gm-anxious-but-not-pushy/|title=Avs GM anxious but not pushy|access-date=August 18, 2018|newspaper=The Denver Post|date=June 2, 2008}}</ref> However, it was announced on August 27, 2008, that Sakic would sign a one-year contract with the team.<ref name=\"Sakic Signs 1-Year Deal\">{{cite web|url=http://avalanche.nhl.com/team/app/?service=page&page=NewsPage&articleid=380558 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080829200623/http://avalanche.nhl.com/team/app/?service=page&page=NewsPage&articleid=380558 |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 29, 2008 |title=Sakic Signs 1-Year Contract |access-date=August 27, 2008 |publisher=Colorado Avalanche |year=2008 |author=Colorado Avalanche}}</ref> Injuries limited Sakic's playing time in [[2008–09 NHL season|2008–09]]. After 15 games, in which he scored 12 points, a herniated disk forced Sakic to stop playing in early November.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nhl.com/news/avalanche-captain-sakic-sidelined-at-least-six-weeks-with-herniated-disc/c-395913|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180818185411/https://www.nhl.com/news/avalanche-captain-sakic-sidelined-at-least-six-weeks-with-herniated-disc/c-395913|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 18, 2018|title=Avalanche captain Sakic sidelined at least six weeks with herniated disc|access-date=August 18, 2018|publisher=NHL.com|date=December 3, 2008}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.denverpost.com/2008/11/16/no-go-for-joe-on-road-trip/|title=No-go for Joe on road trip|access-date=August 18, 2018|newspaper=The Denver Post|author=Adrian Dater|date=November 16, 2008}}</ref> While at home letting his back heal, Sakic broke three fingers in a snow-blower accident.<ref name=\"2008–09 season\">{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=397221|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110521204133/http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=397221|url-status=dead|archive-date=May 21, 2011|title=Sakic injures hand in snow blower accident |access-date=December 10, 2008|publisher=NHL.com|year=2008|author=Coffey, Phil}}</ref>\n\nSakic announced his retirement on July 9, 2009<ref name=\"Retirement\">{{cite news|url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=436687|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100210030730/http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=436687|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 10, 2010|title=Sakic steps away from the NHL after 20 year of hockey|access-date=July 9, 2009|publisher=NHL.com|year=2009|agency=Associated Press}}</ref> The Avalanche [[List of NHL retired numbers|retired]] his jersey number 19 prior to their [[2009–10 NHL season|2009–10 season]] opener on October 1, 2009, with a \"C\" on the banner to represent his lengthy service as team captain (having been the only captain of the Avalanche until he retired).<ref name=\"Retired Jersey\">{{cite web|url=http://avalanche.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=500710 |title=Avalanche Announces Alumni Association |access-date=October 3, 2009 |publisher=ColoradoAvalanche.com |date=October 2, 2009 |author=Colorado Avalanche |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091129031057/http://avalanche.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=500710 |archive-date=November 29, 2009}}</ref> The Avalanche also named Sakic the inaugural member of the Avalanche Alumni Association.<ref name=\"Alumni\">{{cite web|url=http://avalanche.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=498994|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100713183713/http://avalanche.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=498994|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 13, 2010|title=Avalanche Announces Alumni Association|access-date=October 1, 2009|publisher=ColoradoAvalanche.com|date=September 18, 2009|author=Colorado Avalanche}}</ref>\n\n===All-Star Games===\nSakic was voted into the [[NHL All-Star Game]] 13 times and played in 12 of them, serving as a captain for two, the last in [[55th National Hockey League All-Star Game|2007]]. He had at least one point in 11 of them.<ref>{{cite news |title =Sakic Named To 13th NHL All-Star Game |url =http://avalanche.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=426703|archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20131203093553/http://avalanche.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=426703|url-status =dead|archive-date =December 3, 2013|publisher =[[Colorado Avalanche]]|date =January 9, 2007|access-date =December 2, 2013}}</ref> The only one Sakic missed was the [[47th National Hockey League All-Star Game|1997 All-Star Game]] due to injury. Sakic won the MVP award in the [[54th National Hockey League All-Star Game|2004 All-Star Game]] after scoring a hat trick, despite the Western Conference losing the game. He is the all-time assist leader in All-Star Games with 16 assists<ref name=\"AllStarAssists\">{{cite web|url=https://www.nhl.com/avalanche/news/sakic-leads-western-all-stars-to-victory/c-426728|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161225213848/https://www.nhl.com/avalanche/news/sakic-leads-western-all-stars-to-victory/c-426728|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 25, 2016|title=Sakic Leads Western All-Stars To Victory|access-date=December 24, 2016|publisher=NHL.com|date=January 23, 2007|agency=Associated Press}}</ref> and is third place in all-time all-star scoring with 22 points, behind [[Mario Lemieux]] (23 points) and [[Wayne Gretzky]] (25 points).<ref name=\"AllStarAssists\"/> His best record in an All-Star Game was in 2007, when he scored four assists for the winning team; however, the MVP award was given to [[Daniel Brière]], who had a goal and four assists.<ref name=\"AllStarAssists\"/>\n\n==International play==\n{{MedalTableTop| name = |Joe Sakic Team Canada.jpg|200px|Sakic (no. 91) at the 2006 Olympics}}\n{{MedalCountry | {{flagicon|Canada}} Canada}}\n{{MedalCompetition | [[Ice hockey at the Olympics|Olympics]]}}\n{{MedalGold | [[2002 Winter Olympics|2002 Salt Lake City]] | }}\n{{MedalCompetition|[[Ice Hockey World Championships|World Championships]]}}\n{{MedalGold | [[1994 Men's Ice Hockey World Championships|1994 Italy]] | }}\n{{MedalSilver | [[1991 Men's Ice Hockey World Championships|1991 Finland]] |}}\n{{MedalCompetition|[[World Cup of Hockey|World Cup]]}}\n{{MedalGold | [[2004 World Cup of Hockey|2004 World Cup]] | }}\n{{MedalSilver | [[1996 World Cup of Hockey|1996 World Cup]] | }}\n{{MedalCompetition|[[IIHF World Junior Championship|World Junior Championships]]}}\n{{MedalGold | [[1988 World Junior Ice Hockey Championships|1988 Soviet Union]] | }}\n{{MedalBottom}}\nSakic had an extensive international hockey career, representing Canada in seven international competitions.<ref name=\"Canadian Gold\"/> After being drafted by the Nordiques in 1987, Sakic went on to help the [[Canada men's national junior ice hockey team|Canadian junior team]] win the [[1988 World Junior Ice Hockey Championships|1988 World Junior Championship]].<ref name=\"Legends of Hockey\"/> Sakic's next tournament was the [[1991 Men's Ice Hockey World Championships|1991 World Championships]], in which Team Canada won the silver medal and Sakic contributed eleven points in ten games.<ref name=\"Legends of Hockey\"/> Sakic tried out for the [[1991 Canada Cup]] Canadian team but was the first player to be cut, being cited for his weak leg strength.<ref name=\"Legends of Hockey\"/> Sakic was bitter about the experience, feeling he was not given a good enough chance to prove himself, and called the whole experience \"a complete waste of time.\"<ref name=\"Second Chance\">{{cite news |title=Sakic's Second Chance|author=Strachan, Al|newspaper=[[Toronto Sun]]|date=August 15, 1996}}</ref>\n\nSakic's first successful professional tournament was the [[1994 Men's Ice Hockey World Championships|1994 World Championships]], in which Canada won its first gold medal in the tournament since 1961. Sakic's seven points in eight games were a crucial part of the team's success.<ref name=\"Legends of Hockey\"/> During the [[1996 World Cup of Hockey]], Sakic played only a minor role in Canada's second-place finish as he scored one goal and two assists in six games.<ref name=\"1996WCH\">{{cite web|url=http://slam.canoe.com/HockeyWorldCup/stats.html|title=1996 World Cup of Hockey Statistics|access-date=April 9, 2007|publisher=Canoe – Slam Sports!|year=1996|agency=Canadian Press}}{{dead link|date=April 2026|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> However, the tournament allowed Sakic to showcase that he was indeed a dominant player who had simply been overlooked.<ref name=\"HockeyWinner\">{{cite web|url=http://slam.canoe.com/HockeyWorldCup/sep16_wctucker.html|title=HOCKEY THE BIG WINNER|access-date=April 9, 2007|publisher=Canoe – Slam Sports!|year=1996|author=Tucker, Larry}}{{dead link|date=April 2026|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>\n\nSakic's first Olympic appearance came in [[1998 Winter Olympics|1998]] at [[Nagano (city)|Nagano]], Japan, the first tournament in which NHL players participated. Bothered by a knee injury, Sakic scored only three points in four games<ref name=\"Avalanche Website\"/> as the Canadian squad failed to meet expectations and finished fourth. Sakic's second Olympic appearance came in [[2002 Winter Olympics|2002]] in [[Salt Lake City]]; led by his strong play, the Canadian team reached the gold medal match against [[USA Hockey|Team USA]], in which Sakic scored four points and helped Canada to its first gold medal in 50 years. Sakic was later named MVP of the tournament with a cumulative tally of four goals and six assists and became one of the first Canadian members of the [[Triple Gold Club]].<ref name=\"TGC\"/> Sakic also played a part in Canada's triumph in the [[2004 World Cup of Hockey]], where he scored six points in six games.<ref name=\"Legends of Hockey\"/>\n\nOn December 21, 2005, Sakic was named captain of Canada for the [[2006 Winter Olympics]] in [[Turin]], Italy.<ref name=\"USA Today\">{{cite news |title=Canada's deep Olympic roster is minus Crosby|url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/olympics/torino/hockey/2005-12-21-canada-roster_x.htm|author=Brehm, Mike|work=[[USA Today]]|date=December 21, 2005|access-date=November 19, 2007}}</ref> Once again, Canada was heavily favoured to win and given high expectations, but they failed to medal, finishing seventh overall.<ref name=\"New York Times\">{{cite news |title=2006 Olympic Winter Games—Hockey: Men; Canada Is Left With Questions and Speculation|url=https://query.nytimes.com/gst/fullpage.html?res=9C01E2DF1F3EF937A15751C0A9609C8B63|author=Westhead, Rick|newspaper=New York Times|date=February 24, 2006|access-date=November 19, 2007}}</ref> Sakic finished the tournament with three points.\n\n==Executive career==\nAfter he retired, Sakic decided to take time off from hockey and spent time with his family. In 2011, two years after his retirement, Sakic returned to the Avalanche to work in their front office. Sakic was named an executive advisor and alternate governor of the team, effective at the end of the [[2010–11 NHL season|2010–11 season]]. In his role as an advisor, Sakic advised the team in hockey-related matters. As an alternate governor, Sakic represented the team at [[National Hockey League#Board of Governors|Board of Governors meetings]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=557255|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110326210247/http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=557255|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 26, 2011|title=Joe Sakic joins Av's front office|author=NHL.com|date=March 25, 2011|publisher=NHL.com|access-date=March 25, 2011}}</ref>\n\nOn June 26, 2012, Sakic was selected to the [[Hockey Hall of Fame]] in his first year of eligibility. He was inducted into the [[Hockey Hall of Fame]] on November 12, 2012, along with [[Mats Sundin]], [[Pavel Bure]], and [[Adam Oates]]. Sakic was the only member of his class who won the [[Stanley Cup]] during his career.\n\nOn May 10, 2013, the Avalanche promoted Sakic to executive vice president of hockey operations. In this expanded role, Sakic had the final say on all matters regarding hockey personnel.<ref>{{cite web|last=Kimelman|first=Adam|title=Sakic will have final say in new Avalanche role|publisher=NHL.com|date=May 10, 2013|url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=670167&navid=nhl:topheads|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130608041115/http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=670167&navid=nhl:topheads|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 8, 2013|access-date=December 4, 2013}}</ref> During [[Patrick Roy]]'s tenure as head coach, they shared most of the duties normally held by a general manager. General Manager [[Greg Sherman]] remained in his post but served mainly in an advisory role to Roy and Sakic. This de facto arrangement was formalized the following season, when Sakic was formally named general manager and Sherman was demoted to assistant general manager.<ref name=TheAthletic220627>{{cite web|last=LeBrun|first=Pierre|title=How Joe Sakic built a Cup champion: NHL GMs marvel at Avalanche's patient, methodical rise|website=[[The Athletic]]|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3385198/2022/06/27/joe-sakic-avalanche-stanley-cup-champion/|date=June 27, 2022|access-date=July 11, 2022}}</ref>\n\nSakic's tenure as general manager faced early adversity, notably in the [[2016-17 NHL season|2016–17 season]], in which the team finished in last place and managed only 48 points in the standings. Sakic later admitted that at points he was to be relieved by team ownership in midst of the poor results. Despite finishing last, the team did not win any of the top three lottery picks in the [[2017 NHL entry draft]], dropping to fourth. This seeming misfortune would later prove beneficial, as it led to the Avalanche selecting future [[James Norris Memorial Trophy|Norris Trophy]]-winning defenceman [[Cale Makar]] at fourth overall. The poor season also perpetuated a trade request from star player [[Matt Duchene]], which Sakic would ultimately translate into several assets, including defencemen [[Sam Girard]] and [[Bowen Byram]]. In later years, Sakic would make additional trades for [[Nazem Kadri]], [[Devon Toews]], and [[Artturi Lehkonen]], and sign [[Valeri Nichushkin]] as a free agent. The Avalanche won the [[Presidents' Trophy]] for the [[2020-21 NHL season|2020–21 season]] but faltered in the second round of the playoffs for the third consecutive season. The Avalanche finished second in the regular season [[2021-22 NHL season|the following year]] but [[2022 Stanley Cup playoffs|won the Stanley Cup]].<ref name=TheAthletic220627/> Sakic became only the third person, after Milt Schmidt and Serge Savard, to win a Stanley Cup with the same franchise as a player and general manager.<ref>{{cite web|last=Newby|first=Colin|title=What Joe Sakic Means to the Avalanche|website=The Hockey Writers|url=https://thehockeywriters.com/colorado-avalanche-sakic-importance/|date=July 7, 2022|access-date=July 15, 2022}}</ref> In recognition of his work for the 2021–22 season, Sakic received the Jim Gregory General Manager of the Year Award.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.prohockeyrumors.com/2022/07/joe-sakic-wins-gm-of-the-year.html |title=Joe Sakic Wins GM Of The Year|date=July 7, 2022}}</ref>\n\nOn July 11, 2022, the Avalanche announced that Sakic would be ceding the general manager title to longtime assistant [[Chris MacFarland]] and assuming a new role as president of hockey operations.<ref name=THN220711/> Following MacFarland's departure to the [[Nashville Predators]] on June 2, 2026, Sakic re-assumed the role of general manager.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/avalanche/news/statement-on-chris-macfarland-s-departure |title=Statement On Chris MacFarland's Departure |website=NHL.com |date=June 2, 2026 |access-date=June 2, 2026}}</ref>\n\n==Personal life==\nSakic and his wife Debbie have three children: son Mitchell, born 1996,<ref>{{cite web|title=Joe Sakic Answers Your Questions|publisher=Colorado Avalanche|date=December 11, 2007|url=http://avalanche.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=427157|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120119203145/http://avalanche.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=427157|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 19, 2012|access-date=December 4, 2013}}</ref> and fraternal twins, son Chase and daughter Kamryn, born October 2000.<ref name=\"Avalanche Website\"/><ref>{{cite news|work=The Gazette |first=John |last=Branch |title=An Avalanche of newborns/ Seven have been born since August |date=February 14, 2001 }}</ref> Sakic and his wife met at a local high school while he was playing in Swift Current, and they frequently return to the town during the off-season.<ref name=\"Denial of Death\"/> Sakic is an avid [[golf]]er and competed in the celebrity [[Pro–am|pro am]] golf tournament in [[Lake Tahoe]] in the summer of 2006. Each summer during his playing career, Sakic also hosted his own charity golf tournament, which benefited the Food Bank of the Rockies.<ref name=\"Save Avs\">{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/columns/story?columnist=frei_terry&id=3556791|title=Can Captain Joe save the day for the Avalanche?|access-date=August 27, 2008|publisher=ESPN|year=2008|author=Frei, Terry}}</ref> Sakic's charity work is estimated to have provided more than seven million meals to poor children and families and earned him an NHL Foundation Player Award in 2007.<ref>{{cite news |title =Sakic receives NHL Foundation Player Award for outstanding community service|url =http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=373076|archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20100310034727/http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=373076|url-status =dead|archive-date =March 10, 2010|publisher =[[National Hockey League|NHL]]|date =October 15, 2007|access-date =October 19, 2007}}</ref>\n\nSakic is a fan favourite in his hometown of Burnaby, where a street has been named Joe Sakic Way in his honour.<ref name=\"No Average Joe\"/> Throughout [[British Columbia]], Sakic is known as \"Burnaby Joe\".<ref name=\"ESPN Page 2\">{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/page2/s/bermanfiles/sakicresponses.html|title=Case No. 4, Joe Sakic\n|access-date=November 7, 2007|publisher=ESPN|year=2001|author=ESPN Staff}}</ref> In [[Colorado]], Sakic is known as \"Super Joe.\" His younger brother [[Brian Sakic|Brian]] joined the [[Swift Current Broncos]] during Joe's final season with the team and later played for the [[Flint Generals]] of the [[United Hockey League]].<ref name=\"Avalanche Website\"/>\n\n==Career statistics==\n\n===Regular season and playoffs===\n{| border=\"0\" cellpadding=\"1\" cellspacing=\"0\" style=\"text-align:center; width:60em\"\n|- bgcolor=\"#e0e0e0\"\n! colspan=3 | All-Star totals\n! 6 !! 16 !! 22\n|}\n\n==Legacy==\n\n===Milestones===\nSakic recorded his 1,000th career point on December 27, 1999, against the [[St. Louis Blues]].<ref name=\"2001 NHL Yearbook\">{{cite book | last = National Hockey League | title = 2001 NHL Yearbook | year = 2000 | publisher = Worldsport Properties | location = Toronto | page = 272}}</ref> Sakic became the 11th player to reach 1,500 points, doing so on October 25, 2006, with an assist against the [[Washington Capitals]], and the sixth to do so with one franchise.<ref name=\"1500 Points\">{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/news/story?id=2638889|title=Sakic scores 1,500th point|access-date=May 13, 2007|publisher=ESPN|year=2006|agency=Associated Press}}</ref> [[Gordie Howe]], [[Wayne Gretzky]], [[Mario Lemieux]], [[Ray Bourque]], and [[Steve Yzerman]] are the others who achieved this feat.<ref name=\"No Average Joe\"/>\n\nSakic played his 1,000th career game on March 9, 2002, against the [[Los Angeles Kings]].<ref name=\"Recordbook\">{{cite book | last = National Hockey League | author-link = National Hockey League | title = National Hockey League Official Guide & Record Book 2007 | publisher = Dan Diamond & Associates, Inc. | year = 2006 | location = Toronto | page = [https://archive.org/details/nationalhockeyle0000unse_a8h9/page/656 656] | isbn = 978-1-894801-02-7 | url = https://archive.org/details/nationalhockeyle0000unse_a8h9/page/656}}</ref> Sakic's 500th career goal came against the [[Vancouver Canucks]] on December 11, 2002.<ref name=\"500 Goals\">{{cite news|url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/hockey/canucks-spoil-sakic-s-500th-goal-1.339282|title=Canucks spoil Sakic's 500th goal|access-date=February 16, 2023|publisher=CBC|author=CBC Sports | date=December 15, 2002}}</ref> In a February 15, 2007, game against the [[Calgary Flames]], Sakic scored his 600th career goal. He also earned his 900th assist, the 16th player to do so, against the Flames in a game on March 12, 2006.<ref name=\"Avalanche Bio\">{{cite web|title=Joe Sakic: Bio|publisher=Colorado Avalanche|url=https://www.nhl.com/player/joe-sakic-8451101|access-date=July 26, 2013}}</ref>\n\nDuring the final game of the [[2006–07 NHL season|2006–07 season]], Sakic scored his 100th point of the year. This made him, at age 37, the second oldest player in NHL history, after Gordie Howe, to record 100 points in a regular season.<ref name=\"Forbes Article\">{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2007/04/08/AR2007040801332.html|title=Sakic Reaches 100 Points As Avs Win|access-date=December 24, 2016|newspaper=The Washington Post|agency=Associated Press|date=April 9, 2007|author=Stapleton, Arnie}}</ref> Sakic became the longest active tenured captain in the league, with fifteen seasons leading the Nordiques/Avalanche franchise, after the retirement of Steve Yzerman at the conclusion of the 2005–06 regular season.<ref name=\"Avalanche Bio\"/> On March 22, 2008, against the [[Edmonton Oilers]], Sakic recorded the 1,000th assist of his career, the 11th player to do so.<ref name=\"1000 assists\"/> The gloves he wore in the game were later sent to the [[Hockey Hall of Fame]].<ref name=\"1000 Assists HHOF\">{{cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/hockey/2008-03-25-58530803_x.htm|title=Theodore's Shutout Gives Avs Crucial Win|access-date=March 27, 2008|agency=Associated Press|work=USA Today|date=March 25, 2008|author=Stapleton, Arnie}}</ref>\n\nAlongside [[Bobby Clarke]], Wayne Gretzky, and [[Mark Messier]], Sakic is one of four players to captain his team to a Stanley Cup championship and win the Hart Memorial Trophy in the same year.<ref name=\"Trophy Winner\">{{cite web|url=http://slam.canoe.com/NHLAwards/010615_awards1-sun.html|title=Sakic is no ordinary Joe|access-date=May 14, 2007|publisher=NBCSports.com|year=2001|author=Zeisberger, Mike}}{{dead link|date=April 2026|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> Sakic is also a member of the [[Triple Gold Club]], a term used in hockey to describe players who have won an Olympic gold medal, a World Championship gold medal and the Stanley Cup.<ref name=\"TGC\">{{cite web|url=https://www.iihf.com/en/static/5315/triple-gold-club|title=Hockey's exclusive company–Triple Gold Club|access-date=February 16, 2023|publisher=[[International Ice Hockey Federation]]|year=2008}}</ref>\n\n===Records===\nSakic retired holding almost every scoring record in Nordiques/Avalanche franchise history, including most all-time goals (625), assists (1,016) and points (1,641). He also holds the franchise record for most games played (1,363).<ref name=\"Recordbook 2009\">{{cite book | last = National Hockey League | author-link = National Hockey League | title = National Hockey League Official Guide & Record Book 2009 |publisher = Dan Diamond & Associates, Inc. | year = 2008 | location = Toronto | page = 656 |isbn = 978-1-894801-14-0}}</ref> Sakic also holds several notable NHL records, including most All-Star game assists (16) and most playoff overtime goals (8).<ref name=\"April 9, 2008\">{{cite news|url=http://scores.espn.go.com/nhl/recap?gameId=280409030|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080412144718/http://scores.espn.go.com/nhl/recap?gameId=280409030|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 12, 2008|title=Sakic, Avs drop Wild in OT to take 1-0 series lead|access-date=April 9, 2008|work=ESPN.com|year=2008|agency=Associated Press}}</ref>\n\n===Leadership===\n[[File:Stastnysakic.jpg|thumb|200px|right|Sakic with [[Paul Šťastný]]. When Sakic entered the NHL, he was mentored by [[Peter Šťastný]], Paul's father.]]\n\nThroughout his career, Sakic was one of the top scorers in the league; but in his early years, he was criticized for not leading his team to playoff success.<ref name=\"100 Greatest Players\"/> While in Quebec, the Nordiques were one of the worst teams in the league, finishing last in their division five out of the seven years Sakic was with the team, including three straight years of being last overall in the league.<ref name=\"Recordbook\"/> After leading the Avalanche to the Stanley Cup in 1996 with his 34 playoff points,<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Wigge|first=Larry|title=Joe Sakic, center, Avalanche|magazine=The Sporting News|date=September 29, 1997|pages=S6–S7}}</ref> Sakic began to be seen as capable of leading a team to success, and he was seen as one of the league's premier players.<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Murphy|first=Austin|title=Two Much|magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=December 9, 1996|url=https://www.si.com/vault/1996/12/09/220196/two-much-peter-forsberg-and-joe-sakic-of-colorado-are-the-nhls-best-center-pairing-since-gretzky-and-messier|access-date=December 27, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Beacon|first=Bill|title=Sakic finally gets his due: Recognized as one of hockey's top centres|work=The Montreal Gazette|date=September 6, 1996|page=D3}}</ref>\n\nThough Sakic was a quiet individual, he was able to motivate his team to play at higher levels, which earned him the respect of his peers and executives.<ref name=\"Captain\">{{cite news|url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/hockey/captains-sakic-stevens-are-consummate-hockey-leaders-1.281008|title=Captains Sakic, Stevens are consummate hockey leaders|access-date=February 16, 2023|publisher=CBC|author=Stevens, Neil | date=June 9, 2001}}</ref> The first signs of Sakic's leadership began to show while still a member of the Swift Current Broncos of the WHL. After the bus crash that killed four of his teammates, Sakic was seen as the leader of the team, acknowledging that the experience changed his outlook on life.<ref name=\"No Average Joe\"/><ref>{{cite news|last=MacGregor|first=Roy|title=Lessons from Swift Current: Twenty-one years ago, Joe Sakic lost four teammates in a bus crash. Today, he breaks his silence to Roy MacGregor in hopes of helping those in Bathurst heal|work=The Globe and Mail|date=March 13, 2009|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/national/lessons-from-swift-current-twenty-one-years-ago-joe-sakic-lost-four-teammates-in-a-bus-crash-today-he-breaks-his-silence-to-roy-macgregor-in-hopes-of-helping-those-in-bathurst-heal/article17979486/?page=all|access-date=December 26, 2016}}</ref> Early in his career with the Nordiques (when [[Mike Hough]] was still captain),<ref name=\"C\"/><ref name=\"exec\"/> with the team hoping to rebuild around their top draft pick [[Eric Lindros]] and holding onto Lindros' rights for the season when he refused to sign, Sakic suggested that the team could progress without Lindros. Lindros was traded a year later, bringing in a number of quality players, which vastly improved the Nordiques.<ref name=\"Lindros\"/> Sakic's leadership qualities led him to be courted by other teams, such as in the summer of 1997, when the [[New York Rangers]] offered him a large contract in order to replace departed captain [[Mark Messier]], though the Avalanche ultimately matched the offer and retained Sakic.<ref name=\"TSN about the CBA\"/>\n\nOne of the most defining actions of Sakic's career was at the conclusion of the 2001 playoffs. Defying the NHL tradition of the captain being the first to skate around with the Stanley Cup, Sakic passed it off to teammate [[Ray Bourque]].<ref name=\"Bourque\">{{cite news |title =Avalanche beat Devils to capture Stanley Cup|url =https://www.usatoday.com/sports/hockey/cup01/games/2001-06-09-njcol.htm|author =Allen, Kevin|work=[[USA Today]]|date =June 10, 2001|access-date =November 26, 2007}}</ref> Bourque, one of the best defensemen to ever play, had been traded to the Avalanche the year before after spending 21 years with the [[Boston Bruins]] and setting the record for most games played without winning the Cup.<ref>{{cite news|last=Brehm|first=Mike|title=Commentary: Bourque's story tugs us again|work=USA Today|date=June 26, 2001|url=http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/hockey/col/2001-06-26-brehm-bourque.htm|access-date=December 2, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Ray, meet Stanley|publisher=CNN Sports Illustrated. Associated Press|date=June 10, 2001|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/hockey/nhl/2001/playoffs/news/2001/06/09/bourque_cup_ap/|access-date=December 2, 2013|archive-date=June 4, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110604140001/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/hockey/nhl/2001/playoffs/news/2001/06/09/bourque_cup_ap/|url-status=dead}}</ref>\n\nWhen an eye injury forced [[Steve Yzerman]] (who normally wore number 19 for Canada) to miss the [[2004 World Cup of Hockey]], Sakic and [[Joe Thornton]] both refused the number out of respect for their injured countryman, even though both players each wore the number 19 for their respective NHL clubs and were now eligible to wear it for [[Canada men's national ice hockey team|Team Canada]] in Yzerman's absence.\n\nSakic's leadership qualities and abilities helped carry the Avalanche in the years after their 2001 Stanley Cup,<ref name=\"leaders\"/><ref>{{cite news|last=Dater|first=Adrian|title=\"Super Joe\" carrying Avs on his back again|work=The Denver Post|date=November 19, 2006|url=http://www.denverpost.com/2006/11/19/super-joe-carrying-avs-on-his-back-again/|access-date=December 26, 2016}}</ref> which saw the team lose key players to retirement and free agency, especially after the 2004–05 lock-out.<ref>{{cite web|title=20 In 20: The 20 Best Avalanche Players In 20 Years of Franchise History Part 2|publisher=KCNC-TV|date=October 20, 2015|url=http://denver.cbslocal.com/2015/10/20/20-in-20-the-20-best-avalanche-players-in-20-years-of-franchise-history-part-2/|access-date=December 26, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Scanlan|first=Wayne|title=Shed no tears for Sakic|work=Ottawa Citizen|date=October 20, 2006|page=B1}}</ref>\n\n==Awards==\n\n===WHL and CHL===\n{| class=\"wikitable\"\n|-\n!
