Rangers announced that they would retire number 30 in his honor during the [[2021–22 NHL season|2021–22 season]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Lundqvist to have No. 30 retired by Rangers this season |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/henrik-lundqvist-no-30-to-be-retired-by-new-york-after-announcing-reti-326001628 |website=NHL.com |access-date=21 August 2021 |date=20 August 2021}}</ref> which was retired on 28 January 2022.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rangers Buy Out Contract of Henrik Lundqvist |url=https://www.nhl.com/rangers/news/rangers-buy-out-contract-of-henrik-lundqvist/c-319243646 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200930201401/https://www.nhl.com/rangers/news/rangers-buy-out-contract-of-henrik-lundqvist/c-319243646 |url-status=dead |archive-date=30 September 2020 |website=NHL.com |access-date=29 January 2022 |date=30 September 2020}}</ref>\n\n==International play==\n{{MedalTableTop|HenrikLundqvist2010WinterOlympics cropped.jpg|220px|Lundqvist with the [[Sweden men's national ice hockey team]].|name=no}}\n{{MedalSport|Men's [[ice hockey]]}}\n{{MedalCountry|{{ih|SWE}}}}\n{{MedalCompetition|[[Ice hockey at the Olympic Games|Winter Olympics]]}}\n{{MedalGold|[[2006 Winter Olympics|2006 Turin]]|}}\n{{MedalSilver|[[2014 Winter Olympics|2014 Sochi]]|}}\n{{MedalCompetition|[[Ice Hockey World Championships|World Championships]]}}\n{{MedalGold|[[2017 Men's Ice Hockey World Championships|2017 Cologne/Paris]]|}}\n{{MedalSilver|[[2003 Men's Ice Hockey World Championships|2003 Helsinki]]|}}\n{{MedalSilver|[[2004 Men's Ice Hockey World Championships|2004 Prague]]|}}\n{{MedalSport|[[Inline hockey]]}}\n{{MedalCompetition|[[IIHF Inline Hockey World Championship|World Championships]]}}\n{{MedalGold|[[2002 IIHF InLine Hockey World Championship|2002 Nuremberg]]|}}\n{{MedalBottom}}\nLundqvist is the all-time leader among goaltenders, and 11th overall of all players, in games played for the Swedish national junior's ice hockey team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.swehockey.se/t3b.asp?p=69309%20&x=1&a=1117682 |title=De är historiska |access-date=26 February 2008 |last=Feltenmark |first=Anders |date=4 January 2008 |website=[[Swedish Ice Hockey Association]] |language=sv |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090301073259/http://www.swehockey.se/t3b.asp?p=69309%20&x=1&a=1117682 |archive-date=1 March 2009 |url-status=dead}}</ref>\n\nAt the [[2001 World Junior Ice Hockey Championships|2001 World U20 Championship]], Lundqvist led [[Sweden men's national junior ice hockey team|Sweden]] to a fourth-place finish in the tournament. After an upset 3–2 win over the hosting nation [[Russia men's national junior ice hockey team|Russia]] in the quarterfinals, Sweden lost 1–0 against the [[Czech Republic men's national junior ice hockey team|Czech Republic]] in the semifinals, and 2–1 in overtime against [[Canada men's national junior ice hockey team|Canada]] in the bronze medal game.\n\nLundqvist debuted for the [[Sweden men's national ice hockey team|senior Swedish team]] on 10 November 2002 in the 2002 [[Karjala Tournament]] in [[Helsinki]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.swehockey.se/files/%7B6A834FA2-E7DA-4EC7-9A39-9A98DF894BAD%7D.pdf |title=Debutanter i Tre Kronor sedan 1937 |access-date=26 February 2008 |date=13 December 2007 |website=[[Swedish Ice Hockey Association]] |page=22 |language=sv |quote=679 Henrik Lundqvist Västra Frölunda HC 10/11 2002 Karjala Tournament, Helsingfors, Finland, Finland-Sverige |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080227194758/http://www.swehockey.se/files/%7B6A834FA2-E7DA-4EC7-9A39-9A98DF894BAD%7D.pdf |archive-date=27 February 2008 |url-status=dead}}</ref>\n\nLundqvist was selected to the [[2003 IIHF World Championship|2003 World Championship]] but was third string goaltender behind [[Tommy Salo]] and [[Mikael Tellqvist]]. The following year, at the [[2004 IIHF World Championship|2004 World Championship]], Lundqvist was the starting goaltender and he was selected to the tournament all-star team.\n\nLundqvist and [[Jörgen Jönsson]] were the only two Elitserien players selected to play for Sweden at the [[2004 World Cup of Hockey]]. Lacking experience on the smaller ice surface, Lundqvist was again third string behind Salo and Tellqvist.\n\nIn the [[2004–05 Euro Hockey Tour]], Lundqvist was named best goaltender in Karjala Tournament and [[LG Hockey Games|Sweden Hockey Games]] by the directorate, as well as to the media all-star team in both tournaments. At the [[2005 IIHF World Championship|2005 World Championship]] in [[Vienna]] and [[Innsbruck]], Austria, Lundqvist played in all nine games during the tournament, where Sweden eventually lost the bronze medal game against [[Russia men's national ice hockey team|Russia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.swehockey.se/files/%7B447620C3-CCC9-4D0E-BDF5-7D40C6C652AF%7D.pdf |title=GOALKEEPERS IN TRE KRONOR 2004/2005 |access-date=26 February 2008 |date=16 May 2005 |website=[[Swedish Ice Hockey Association]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071117004748/http://www.swehockey.se/files/%7B447620C3-CCC9-4D0E-BDF5-7D40C6C652AF%7D.pdf |archive-date=17 November 2007 |url-status=dead}}</ref>\n\nLundqvist's most memorable international performance came at the [[Ice hockey at the 2006 Winter Olympics – Men's tournament|2006 Winter Olympics]] in [[Turin]], where he led Sweden to the gold medal over their archrivals [[Finland men's national ice hockey team|Finland]]. In six Olympic starts, Lundqvist went 5–1, allowing only 12 goals with a .907 save percentage. He holds the career record for most shutouts in best-on-best hockey, with four.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://tlh.evcco.com/players.html |title=Top Level Hockey World Rankings – Players|publisher=EVCco |date=21 March 2010 |access-date=24 February 2014}}</ref>\n\nIn the [[2017 IIHF World Championship|2017 World Championship]], Lundqvist joined the Swedish team in the group stage and stayed in net for all five remaining games, including the final against [[Canada men's national ice hockey team|Canada]]. Lundqvist had an excellent tournament and recorded a 1.31 GAA, and a .946 save percentage. The final against Canada went into a shootout and Lundqvist stopped all four Canadian chances to lead his country to its tenth World Championship title, on a national team captained by his identical twin brother Joel Lundqvist.\n\nLundqvist joined Sweden again in the [[2019 IIHF World Championship|2019 World Championship]] right after the NHL season ended. Sweden finished the tournament in fifth place after a 5–4 overtime loss to Finland in the quarterfinals, marking the only time Lundqvist lost to the Finnish team.{{citation needed|date=May 2019}}\n\n===Inline hockey===\nLundqvist led team Sweden with spectacular goaltending to their first ever medal in [[inline hockey]] when they won gold at the [[2002 IIHF InLine Hockey World Championship|2002 InLine Hockey World Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://imanager.ip-finland.com/iihf/magazine/1-2003/10.php|title=Sweden Strikes Gold in 2002|access-date=26 February 2008|year=2003|work=In-Line Hockey Magazine|publisher=[[International Ice Hockey Federation]]|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090228082707/http://imanager.ip-finland.com/iihf/magazine/1-2003/10.php|archive-date=28 February 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.swehockey.se/files/%7B31BABAF2-5346-4905-91C6-7832BA62F79D%7D.pdf |title=2002 IIHF WORLD INLINE CHAMPIONSHIP |access-date=26 February 2008 |date=31 July 2002 |website=[[Swedish Ice Hockey Association]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080227194756/http://www.swehockey.se/files/%7B31BABAF2-5346-4905-91C6-7832BA62F79D%7D.pdf |archive-date=27 February 2008 |url-status=dead}}</ref>\n\n==Personal life==\n\n===Family===\nLundqvist has an identical twin brother, [[Joel Lundqvist|Joel]], who, like Henrik, is also a former professional ice hockey player.{{citation needed|date=November 2025}}\n\nLundqvist and his wife have two daughters.<ref>{{cite web|last=Nyström|first=Magnus|title=Henrik Lundqvist friade i ett hav av blommor|url=http://www.expressen.se/noje/extra/1.2278611/henrik-lundqvist-friade-i-ett-hav-av-blommor|work=Expressen|access-date=15 March 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Orfanides |first1=Effie 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Kreda |first1=Allan |title=Henrik Lundqvist Loses Practice Time but Gains a Daughter 2015}}</ref>\n\n===Charity work===\n[[File:Henrik & Joel Lundqvist 2009-11-19 001.jpg|thumb|Henrik (left) with his identical twin brother, [[Joel Lundqvist|Joel]], during an ad campaign for clothing retailer Brothers]]\nIn 2009, Lundqvist became the Rangers spokesman for the Garden of Dreams Foundation, which works mostly with Madison Square Garden and its tenants to host charitable events and grant wishes to sick children, similar to the [[Make-A-Wish Foundation]]. In this role, Lundqvist hosts events and records public service messages.<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://rangers.nhl.com/team/app?articleid=403873&page=NewsPage&service=page |title=Lundqvist new Garden of Dreams spokesman |publisher=[[New York Rangers]] |date=13 January 2009 |access-date=22 January 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090116125924/http://rangers.nhl.com/team/app/?service=page&page=NewsPage&articleid=403873 |archive-date=16 January 2009}}</ref> In order to benefit the charity, Lundqvist launched a clothing line, called the Crown Collection, on 19 January 2012. The items of the Crown Collection were available exclusively at retail outlets within the confines of Madison Square Garden.{{citation needed|date=August 2021}}\n\nIn 2014, Lundqvist and his wife founded the Henrik Lundqvist Foundation a non-profit organization with a focus on health and education for children and families.<ref>{{cite web |title=Henrik Lundqvist Foundation |url=http://www.hlundqvistfoundation.com/ |website=Henrik Lundqvist Foundation |access-date=12 April 2019}}</ref> HLF is an international grantmaking organization, with community partners in New York City, Sweden and the Dominican Republic. The Henrik Lundqvist Foundation hosted its inaugural fundraising event on 14 September 2014, at Refinery Rooftop. The evening included a silent auction, a Q&A session hosted by NHL Network's Kevin Weekes & an acoustic performance by Henrik Lundqvist and bandmate John McEnroe.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://doublegsports.com/henrik-lundqvist-foundation-hosts-inaugural-fundraising-event-nyc-rooftop/ |title=Henrik Lundqvist Foundation Hosts Inaugural Fundraising Event on NYC Rooftop |publisher=Double G Sports |first=Jackie |last=Daly |date=16 September 2014 |access-date=6 February 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150204020219/http://doublegsports.com/henrik-lundqvist-foundation-hosts-inaugural-fundraising-event-nyc-rooftop/ |archive-date=4 February 2015}}</ref> Lundqvist was named a finalist for the 2014–15 NHL Foundation Player Award for his exemplary work with the Henrik Lundqvist Foundation as well as the Garden of Dreams Foundation.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=766094|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150505184836/http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=766094|url-status=dead|archive-date=5 May 2015|title=NHL Foundation finalists: Burns, Giordano, Lundqvist|website=National Hockey League}}</ref> On 29 June 2015, Lundqvist was selected as an athlete finalist for the first ever ESPN Humanitarian of the Year Awards for his commitment to \"using the power of sports to transform lives and uplift communities.\"<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/espn/story/_/id/13169828|title=Four up for inaugural sports humanitarian honor|date=29 June 2015|website=ESPN.com}}</ref>\n\n===Hobbies and other ventures===\nIn 2004, Lundqvist was awarded \"Best Dressed\" in Sweden.<ref>{{cite web | last=Gormley | first=Chuck | website=National Hockey League | url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=369671 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130618010629/http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=369671 | url-status=dead | archive-date=18 June 2013 | title=Atlantic: Lundqvist front and center for Rangers' revival | date=5 November 2007 | access-date=24 February 2012}}</ref> In April 2006, he was named one of ''[[People (magazine)|People]]'''s World's 100 Most Beautiful People.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=etonline.com |url=http://et.tv.yahoo.com/celebrities/14550/ |title=People's World's Most Beautiful (NHL). Nicknamed \"'''Geno'''\", Malkin began his career with his hometown club [[Metallurg Magnitogorsk]], playing for their junior and senior teams. He was then selected second overall in the [[2004 NHL entry draft]] by the Pittsburgh Penguins, though an international transfer dispute delayed the start of his NHL career until 2006. Malkin is widely regarded as one of the greatest players of the modern NHL era and a quintessential piece of the Pittsburgh Penguins' salary cap era success.<ref>{{Cite web |date=9 May 2025 |title=Sidney Crosby and Evgeni Malkin Named to NHL's Quarter-Century Team {{!}} Pittsburgh Penguins |url=https://www.nhl.com/penguins/news/sidney-crosby-and-evgeni-malkin-named-to-nhl-s-quarter-century-team |access-date=11 March 2026 |website=www.nhl.com |language=en}}</ref>\n\nAfter his first season with the Penguins, Malkin was awarded the [[Calder Memorial Trophy]] as the NHL's best [[rookie]]. In his second season, he helped lead Pittsburgh to the [[2008 Stanley Cup Final]] and was a runner-up for the [[Hart Memorial Trophy]], awarded to the NHL's most valuable player during the regular season. The [[2008–09 NHL season|following season]] saw Malkin win the [[Art Ross Trophy]], awarded to the points leader in the NHL and again placed second for the Hart Trophy. He and the Penguins again reached the [[2009 Stanley Cup Final|Stanley Cup Final]], winning the [[Stanley Cup]] championship this time around. Malkin was awarded the [[Conn Smythe Trophy]] as most valuable player of the playoffs. In [[2011–12 NHL season|2012]], Malkin was awarded the Hart Trophy and [[Ted Lindsay Award]], awarded to the best player as voted on by the players, after winning the Art Ross Trophy for the second time; his 12-point lead was the largest margin of victory since [[1998–99 NHL season|1999]].\n\nInternationally, Malkin has competed for [[Russia men's national ice hockey team|Russia]] in two [[IIHF World U18 Championship]]s and three [[IIHF World Junior Championship|World Junior Championships]], capturing one gold, two silvers and one bronze medal as a junior. In [[2006 World Junior Ice Hockey Championships|2006]], he was named tournament MVP. As a senior, he has played in four [[IIHF World Championships]], winning gold twice and being named the tournament MVP for the 2012 event. Malkin has played for Russia in three [[Winter Olympic Games]]: [[2006 Winter Olympics|Turin]] in 2006, [[2010 Winter Olympics|Vancouver]] in 2010 and [[2014 Winter Olympics|Sochi]] in 2014, respectively. In 2020, he was named to the [[IIHF All-Time Teams|IIHF All-Time Russia Team]].\n\n==Early life==\nMalkin was born on 31 July 1986, in [[Magnitogorsk]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.malkin-71.net/biography.html |title=Evgeni Malkin biography |website=Malkin-71.net |access-date=2 February 2014 |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140219000259/http://www.malkin-71.net/biography.html |archive-date=19 February 2014 }}</ref> to Vladimir and Natalia Malkin.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 6, 2024 |title=Malkin parents tear up after Penguins forward scores 2 goals against Lightning {{!}} NHL.com |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/evgeni-malkin-parents-tear-up-penguins-star-two-goals |website=www.nhl.com |language=en}}</ref> Vladimir worked for [[Magnitogorsk Iron and Steel Works]], the largest iron and [[steel]] works in Russia and the city's dominant industry, and played in the [[Metallurg Magnitogorsk]] youth and club hockey system. Malkin has one brother, Denis, who is older by one year.<ref name=\"PPG2014\">{{Cite news |last=McCollough |first=J. Brady |date=February 8, 2014 |title=Evgeni Malkin: A Russian tale with roots founded in ice and iron |url=https://www.post-gazette.com/sports/olympicfeatures/2014/02/09/Evgeni-Malkin-A-Russian-tale-with-roots-founded-in-ice-and-iron/stories/201402090133 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140806035551/http://www.post-gazette.com/sports/olympicfeatures/2014/02/09/Evgeni-Malkin-A-Russian-tale-with-roots-founded-in-ice-and-iron/stories/201402090133 |archive-date=2014-08-06 |url-status=live |work=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette}}</ref> Malkin began skating at age three, and joined his first organized hockey league two years later,<ref name=\"PPG2014\"/> as he showed an aptitude for the sport at an early age.<ref name=\"auto\">{{Cite web |title=Malkin conjuring visions of a young Lemieux - Pittsburgh Tribune-Review |url=http://www.pittsburghlive.com/x/pittsburghtrib/sports/penguins/s_551876.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080213164416/http://www.pittsburghlive.com/x/pittsburghtrib/sports/penguins/s_551876.html |archive-date=2008-02-13 |website=www.pittsburghlive.com}}</ref>\n\n==Playing career==\n\n===Early career===\nMalkin is a product of the [[Metallurg Magnitogorsk]] hockey program. Prior to being drafted, he made his [[Russian Superleague]] debut in the [[2003–04 Russian Superleague season|2003–04 season]] as a 17-year-old.<ref name=\"PPG2014\"/>  He also made his international debut for Russia during the [[2003 IIHF World U18 Championships|2003 U-18 World Championships]], where he skated on the top line with [[Alexander Ovechkin]]. The team went on to claim the bronze medal.{{cn|date=May 2026}}\n\n====Transfer dispute====\nAfter his first professional season in Russia, Malkin was drafted second overall (behind national teammate Alexander Ovechkin) in the [[2004 NHL entry draft]] by the [[Pittsburgh Penguins]].<ref name=draft>{{cite web|title=NHL Entry Draft Year by Year Results|url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/draftsearch.htm?year=2004&team=PIT&position=&round=|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160113094705/http://www.nhl.com/ice/draftsearch.htm?year=2004&team=PIT&position=&round=|url-status=dead|archive-date=13 January 2016|publisher=National Hockey League}}</ref> However, a transfer dispute between the NHL and the [[International Ice Hockey Federation]] (IIHF) delayed his Pittsburgh debut;<ref name=\"PPG2014\"/> though he would have stayed in Russia for what would have been his rookie season with the Penguins in any event due to the [[2004–05 NHL lockout]]. On 7 August 2006, it appeared the 20-year-old Malkin had come to a compromise with Metallurg and signed a deal that would have kept him in Russia until May 2007. However, Malkin stated he signed the one-year contract not as a compromise, but because of the immense \"psychological pressure\" his former club exerted on him.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=The New New Kid |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1105756/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131211164428/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1105756/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=11 December 2013 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=2 October 2006 |access-date=15 July 2013|last=Swift|first=E. M.}}</ref> Desiring to play in the NHL, he left Metallurg Magnitogorsk's training camp in [[Helsinki]] before it began on 12 August.<ref name=\"PPG2014\"/> It would later appear the team had taken Malkin's passport away to prevent him from leaving, but it was eventually given back to him, and Malkin was allowed to pass through Finnish customs. Meeting with his agent, J. P. Barry, the two quickly departed and waited for Malkin's visa clearance from the U.S. Embassy.\n\nIn order to legally leave the team, on 15 August, Malkin invoked via fax a law allowing him to cancel his one-year contract by giving his employer two weeks' notice.<ref>{{cite web |title=Malkin sits down for interview with TSN |url=https://www.tsn.ca/nhl/news_story/?ID=174657&hubname=nhl |work=[[The Sports Network]] |date=19 August 2006 |access-date=22 April 2009 |archive-date=29 September 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070929162353/http://www.tsn.ca/nhl/news_story/?ID=174657&hubname=nhl}}</ref> Having untied himself of obligations in Russia, he was able to sign an entry-level contract with the Penguins on 5 September 2006.<ref>{{cite web |first=Kevin |last=Allen |title=Russian phenom finally signs with Penguins |url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/hockey/nhl/penguins/2006-09-04-malkin-update_x.htm |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130208221249/http://www.usatoday.com/sports/hockey/nhl/penguins/2006-09-04-malkin-update_x.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=8 February 2013 |work=[[USA Today]] |date=6 September 2006 |access-date=22 April 2009}}</ref>\n\nFollowing his first NHL game with Pittsburgh, on 19 October 2006, Malkin's former Russian hockey club filed an [[antitrust]] lawsuit against the NHL and the Penguins in the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York.<ref>{{cite news |title=Russian club seeks to stop Malkin from playing in NHL. |url=http://www.sportsline.com/nhl/story/9740727 |work=[[CBS SportsLine]] |location=[[New York City]] |date=19 October 2006 |access-date=22 April 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120910044707/http://www.sportsline.com/nhl/story/9740727 |archive-date=10 September 2012 }}</ref> The lawsuit claimed Malkin should not be permitted to play in the NHL because he is still under contract in Russia. The claim also sought unspecified [[damages]] as well. The motion for an [[injunction]] was denied on 15 November 2006, ensuring Malkin would continue to play in the NHL that season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Legal Challenge Against Malkin Fails |url=https://www.tsn.ca/nhl/news_story/?ID=184456&hubname=nhl |work=[[The Sports Network]] |date=15 November 2006 |access-date=22 April 2009 |archive-date=29 September 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070929155250/http://www.tsn.ca/nhl/news_story/?ID=184456&hubname=nhl}}</ref> The lawsuit was ultimately dismissed on its [[Merit (law)|merits]] by the District Court on 1 February 2007.<ref>{{cite news |first=Eric |last=Duhatschek |title=Penguins get to keep Malkin |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/servlet/story/RTGAM.20061115.wsportstickers/TPStory/Sports/columnists |work=[[The Globe and Mail]] |date=15 November 2006 |access-date=22 April 2009}}{{dead link|date=January 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes}}</ref>\n\n===Pittsburgh Penguins (2006–present)===\n\n====Calder Trophy, first Stanley Cup title and Conn Smythe Trophy (2006–2009)====\n[[File:Evgeni Malkin.jpg|thumb|left|Malkin smiling during a practice with the Penguins in [[2006–07 NHL season|September 2006]].]]\nIn his first pre-season game with the Penguins, on 20 September 2006, Malkin collided with teammate [[John LeClair]] and dislocated his own shoulder, which forced him to miss the start of the season. Subsequently, his NHL debut would be delayed until 18 October, against the [[New Jersey Devils]], in which he scored his first goal against [[Martin Brodeur]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nhl.com/gamecenter/njd-vs-pit/2006/10/18/2006020087|title=New Jersey Devils - Pittsburgh Penguins - Oct 18, 2006|date=18 October 2006|publisher=NHL.com|access-date=7 March 2024}}</ref> Malkin set a modern NHL record when he scored a goal in each of his first six games. No player had achieved this feat since the NHL's inaugural [[1917–18 NHL season|1917–18]] season, when [[Montreal Canadiens]] forward [[Joe Malone]] scored at least one goal in 14 consecutive games to start his NHL career (Malone, however, had played in the [[National Hockey Association]], the predecessor league to the NHL).<ref name=\"cbc-rookie-honours\">{{cite news |title=Malkin earns rookie honours |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/hockey/malkin-earns-rookie-honours-1.577859 |work=[[CBC Sports]] |date=2 November 2006 |access-date=22 April 2009}}</ref> Malkin's streak was eventually stopped on 4 November in his seventh game by the [[San Jose Sharks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nhl.com/gamecenter/pit-vs-sjs/2006/11/04/2006020203|title=Pittsburgh Penguins - San Jose Sharks - Nov 4, 2006|date=4 November 2006|publisher=NHL.com|access-date=7 March 2024}}</ref> Playing on a team with another highly touted prospect, sophomore forward and generational talent [[Sidney Crosby]], Malkin finished his rookie season with 33 goals, 52 assists and 85 points in 78 games played, leading all first-year players and capturing the [[Calder Memorial Trophy]] as the NHL's top rookie, the second Penguin to win the award after [[Mario Lemieux]] in 1985. Malkin was named alternate captain for the Penguins shortly after. When Malkin arrived in the United States, he spoke little English, but with the help of fellow Russian teammate [[Sergei Gonchar]], he eventually started to give short, simple interviews in the language.<ref>{{cite news |first=Shelly |last=Anderson |title=Hockey easier than English for Malkin |url=http://www.post-gazette.com/pg/07334/838014-61.stm |work=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]] |date=30 November 2007 |access-date=22 April 2009 |archive-date=10 June 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080610210445/http://www.post-gazette.com/pg/07334/838014-61.stm |url-status=dead }}</ref>\n\nHalfway into the 2007–08 season, his sophomore season in the NHL, Malkin recorded his first NHL [[hat-trick]], against the [[Toronto Maple Leafs]], on 3 January 2008. He earned another three-goal performance several games later, on 14 January, against the [[New York Rangers]]. Midway through the season, when more heralded teammate and captain Sidney Crosby went down with an ankle injury, Malkin seized the opportunity to lead the Penguins, scoring 44 points in the 28 games Crosby was absent.<ref>{{cite news |title=Senators-Penguins Preview |url=https://www.espn.com/espn/wire?section=nhl&id=3337897 |work=[[ESPN.com]] |agency=[[Associated Press|AP]] |date=9 April 2008 |access-date=22 April 2009}}</ref> In total, Malkin completed the season second in NHL scoring with 106 points, six points behind [[Alexander Ovechkin]] of the [[Washington Capitals]] for the [[Art Ross Trophy]]. Malkin continued to dominate into the [[Stanley Cup playoffs]] as the Penguins made it to the [[2008 Stanley Cup Final]]. He scored three points against the [[Presidents' Trophy]]-winning [[Detroit Red Wings]] in the finals, totalling 22 points overall (10 goals, 12 assists) in all 20 games, but the Penguins were defeated by Detroit in six games. Malkin's sophomore season culminated in a [[Hart Memorial Trophy]] nomination as NHL MVP—the award was given to Ovechkin—and [[NHL All-Star team|First team All-Star]] honours.\n\n[[File:EvgeniMalkin-Trophy2009Parade.jpg|thumb|Malkin, along with his parents (left), during the Penguins' victory parade for their 2009 Stanley Cup victory.]]\nOn 2 July 2008, with one year left in his entry-level contract, he signed a five-year, $43.5 million contract extension with Pittsburgh.<ref>{{cite news |title=Penguins lock up Evgeni Malkin, Brooks Orpik |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/hockey/penguins-lock-up-evgeni-malkin-brooks-orpik-1.762822 |work=[[CBC Sports]] |date=3 June 2008 |access-date=22 April 2009}}</ref> Malkin began the [[2008–09 NHL season|2008–09 season]] by scoring his 200th NHL point with an assist to Sidney Crosby on 18 October 2008, in just the sixth game of the season against the Toronto Maple Leafs. The goal was also Crosby's 100th career goal and 300th career point. Crosby had a team trainer cut the puck in half so both players could commemorate the moment.<ref>{{cite news |first=Rob |last=Rossi |title=Crosby not worried about puck |url=http://www.pittsburghlive.com/x/pittsburghtrib/s_594125.html |work=[[Pittsburgh Tribune-Review]] |date=20 October 2008 |access-date=28 October 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090620224625/http://www.pittsburghlive.com/x/pittsburghtrib/s_594125.html |archive-date=20 June 2009 }}</ref> Voted as a starter to the [[2009 NHL All-Star Game]] later in the season, Malkin won the shooting accuracy segment of the Skills Competition, initially shooting four-for-four before beating [[Dany Heatley]] three-for-four in a tie-breaker. After having finished runner-up to Alexander Ovechkin the previous season for the Art Ross Trophy, Malkin captured the scoring championship with 113 points. He became the second Russian-born player to win it, after Ovechkin, and the fourth Penguin, after Mario Lemieux, [[Jaromír Jágr]] and Crosby. However, he would once again be runner-up to Ovechkin for the Hart Trophy, although this time garnering a few more first-place votes. In 2008, he had just one first-place vote (out of 134 votes) and 659 points to Ovechkin's 128 first-place votes and 1,313 points.<ref>{{cite news|title=Full voting results for the 2008 NHL Awards|url=https://thehockeynews.com/news/news/full-voting-results-for-the-2008-nhl-awards|access-date=25 June 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140711105503/http://www.thehockeynews.com/articles/16631-Full-voting-results-for-the-2008-NHL-Awards.html|archive-date=11 July 2014|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2009, Malkin had 12 first-place votes (out of 133 votes) and 787 points to Ovechkin's 115 first-place votes and 1,264 points.<ref>{{cite news|title= NHL Award and All-star Voting|url= http://hfboards.com/showthread.php?t=145895&page=10|access-date= 1 May 2010|archive-date= 11 July 2011|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20110711164713/http://hfboards.com/showthread.php?t=145895&page=10|url-status= dead}}</ref> On 12 June 2009, the Penguins won the [[Stanley Cup]] after defeating the Detroit Red Wings 2–1 in game seven of the [[2009 Stanley Cup Final|Final]]. Malkin tallied 36 points (14 goals and 22 assists) to become the first player to lead both the regular season and playoffs in scoring since Mario Lemieux accomplished the feat in 1992. His 36 points were the highest playoff total of any player since [[Wayne Gretzky]] amassed 40 points in 1993. Malkin received the [[Conn Smythe Trophy]] as playoff MVP, becoming the first Russian-born player to do so. He is also just the second player in franchise history to win both the Art Ross and Conn Smythe trophies in the same year. The other Penguin to accomplish this feat was [[Hockey Hall of Fame]]r and team co-owner/president Mario Lemieux (1992).\n\n====Hart Trophy, playoff shortcomings (2009–2015)====\nOn 28 October 2009, Malkin suffered a strained shoulder in a 6–1 win over the [[Montreal Canadiens]], resulting in him missing the next seven games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.patriotledger.com/story/sports/pro/2009/11/15/penguins-snap-four-game-skid/40239947007/ |title=Penguins snap four-game skid, beat Bruins in OT |website=patriotledger.com |publisher=Patriot Ledger |author=The Patriot Ledger |date=14 November 2009 |access-date=6 July 2025}}</ref> On 21 March 2010, Malkin would suffer a bruised foot as a result of a fall he took near the boards in a 3–2 overtime loss to the [[Carolina Hurricanes]], sidelining him for seven more games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://penguinpoop.com/2010/gameday-poop-penguins-vs-flyers-evgeni-malkin-is-out/ |title=Gameday Poop: Penguins vs Flyers – Evgeni Malkin is Out |website=penguinpoop.com |publisher=Penguin Poop |author=Phil Krundle |date=27 March 2010 |access-date=6 July 2025}}</ref> Malkin played 67 games in the [[2009–10 NHL season|2009–10 season]] and recorded 28 goals, 49 assists and 77 points. Malkin and the Penguins came into the [[2010 Stanley Cup playoffs|2010 playoffs]] as the defending Stanley Cup champions and fourth seed in the Eastern Conference and defeated the fifth-seeded [[Ottawa Senators]] in six games in the first round but then were upset by the eighth-seeded Montreal Canadiens in seven games in the second round, squandering a 3–2 series lead along the way.<ref>{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=aFpuDwAAQBAJ&dq=evgeni+malkin+2009-10+season&pg=PT279 |title=The Rise of the Pittsburgh Penguins |first=Rick |last=Buker |date=19 March 2019 |publisher=Simon and Schuster |isbn=9781683582717 |access-date=6 July 2023}}</ref>\n\n[[File:2011-10-13 Capitals vs Penguins Lokomotiv Yaroslavl Game.JPG|thumb|left|Malkin (foreground) and [[Alexander Ovechkin]] participating in a ceremonial puck drop with [[Mario Lemieux]] before an October 2011 game, to honour the victims of the [[2011 Lokomotiv Yaroslavl plane crash]].]]\nOn 4 February 2011, after missing five games due to a left knee injury and sinus infection, Malkin returned to play against the [[Buffalo Sabres]]. At the start of the second period, Sabres defenceman [[Tyler Myers]] collided with Malkin against the end boards, injuring his right knee. He was helped off the ice and went straight to the dressing room, unable to return to the game as he suffered both a torn [[anterior cruciate ligament]] (ACL) and [[medial collateral ligament]] (MCL). On 9 February, it was announced that Malkin would undergo knee surgery. The Penguins estimated his recovery period as six months, sidelining him for the remainder of the [[2010–11 NHL season|2010–11 season]] and playoffs, but stated he should be ready for training camp in mid-September.<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://penguins.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=552119|title=Malkin To Undergo Knee Surgery Thursday; Rehab Period Will Be Six Months|publisher=[[Pittsburgh Penguins]]|date=9 February 2011|access-date=9 February 2011|archive-date=10 February 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110210025555/http://penguins.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=552119|url-status=dead}}</ref> According to then Penguins' general manager [[Ray Shero]], Malkin sent him a text message after the incident occurred stating, \"I'm sorry.\" In Shero's words, \"I told him he had nothing to apologize for.\"<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/nhl/post/_/id/4362/with-evgeni-malkin-out-what-now-for-pens|title=With Evgeni Malkin out, what now for Pens?|publisher=[[ESPN]]|first=Pierre |last=LeBrun|date=5 February 2011}}</ref> In Malkin's absence, the Penguins as a team would end the season as the fourth seed in the Eastern Conference for the third straight season but their fortunes would change in the opening round of the [[2011 Stanley Cup playoffs|2011 playoffs]] against the [[Tampa Bay Lightning]] as the Penguins would lose in seven games to the fifth-seeded Lightning, despite initially having a 3–1 series lead earlier in the series.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Myers |first=Alison |title=2011 NHL Playoffs: Did the Pittsburgh Penguins Really Choke? |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/681509-2011-nhl-playoffs-did-the-pittsburgh-penguins-really-choke |access-date=18 February 2024 |website=Bleacher Report}}</ref>\n\n[[File:Evgeni Malkin - Metallurg Magnitogorsk.jpeg|thumb|right|Malkin in October 2012. He played with [[Metallurg Magnitogorsk]] of the [[Kontinental Hockey League]] (KHL) during the [[2012–13 NHL lockout]].]]\nMalkin had a bounce-back season in [[2011–12 NHL season|2011–12]]. With [[post-concussion syndrome]] limiting team captain [[Sidney Crosby]] to 22 games, Malkin led the Penguins on a line with newly acquired winger [[James Neal (ice hockey)|James Neal]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1028830-pittsburgh-penguins-evgeni-malkin-james-neal-displaying-franchise-line-promise|work=[[Bleacher Report]]|title=Pittsburgh Penguins: Evgeni Malkin, James Neal Displaying Franchise-Line Promise|access-date=7 April 2012|first=James|last=Conley}}</ref> Despite missing seven games due to lingering effects of his knee surgery the previous season, Malkin scored 50 goals for the first time in his career, including three hat-tricks, 59 assists and won his second scoring title with 109 points in the 75 games he did play to collect his second career [[Art Ross Trophy]]. He was the only player in the NHL during the 2011–12 season to score at least 100 points.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=626475|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120408231258/http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=626475|url-status=dead|archive-date=8 April 2012|title=Malkin joins 50-goal club vs. Flyers|publisher=National Hockey League|access-date=7 April 2012}}</ref> Malkin would go on to win the Hart Trophy as the NHL's MVP for his performance in the season beating out Tampa Bay Lightning forward [[Steven Stamkos]] and [[New York Rangers]] goaltender [[Henrik Lundqvist]], respectively.<ref name=\"2012Hart\">{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/lightning/news/hart-finalists-have-nothing-but-respect-for-one-another/c-635222 |title=Hart finalists have nothing but respect for one another |website=NHL.com |publisher=Tampa Bay Lightning |first=Dan |last=Rosen |date=20 June 2012 |access-date=24 July 2023 |archive-date=25 July 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230725012952/https://www.nhl.com/lightning/news/hart-finalists-have-nothing-but-respect-for-one-another/c-635222 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He also went on to win the [[Ted Lindsay Award]] for the most outstanding player judged by the [[NHL Players' Association]], beating out finalists Stamkos and Lundqvist for this award as well.<ref>{{cite web |title=NHLPA members select Evgeni Malkin as the 2011-12 Ted Lindsay Award recipient|url=https://www.nhlpa.com/news/1-13166/nhlpa-members-select-evgeni-malkin-as-the-2011-12-ted-lindsay-award-recipient |website=nhlpa.com |access-date=25 March 2024 |date=20 June 2012}}</ref> He also became the first player in the past ten NHL seasons to win two scoring titles, putting an end to a streak of nine different players over nine seasons leading the NHL in points. Malkin's 50 goals also resulted in him being the runner-up to the [[Maurice \"Rocket\" Richard Trophy|Rocket Richard Trophy]], only behind the 60 goals scored by Steven Stamkos. Despite Malkin's impressive season and the Penguins clinching the fourth-seed in the East for the fourth straight season, the Penguins were eliminated in the first round of the [[2012 Stanley Cup playoffs|2012 playoffs]] by the in-state rival and fifth-seeded [[Philadelphia Flyers]] in six games. Malkin scored eight points (three goals, five assists) in all six games. Following the Penguins' early playoff exit, it was announced Malkin would again represent Russia at the [[2012 Men's World Ice Hockey Championships|2012 World Championships]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Malkin and Datsyuk confirmed for Russia at Worlds |url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=629772 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120427214333/http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=629772 |url-status=dead |archive-date=27 April 2012 |work=National Hockey League |date=6 April 2012 |access-date=4 May 2012}}</ref>\n\nWith the start of the [[2012–13 NHL season]] delayed due to the [[2012–13 NHL lockout|lockout]], Malkin went to Russia and played for Magnitogorsk, his former team, who had joined the [[Kontinental Hockey League]] (KHL) since he last played there.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/sports/hockey/globe-on-hockey/malkin-ovechkin-make-khl-debuts/article4557191/|title=Malkin, Ovechkin make KHL debuts|last=Duhatschek|first=Eric|work=[[The Globe and Mail]]|location=[[Toronto]]|date=20 September 2012|access-date=28 January 2014}}</ref> By the time the lockout ended in early-January 2013, Malkin was second in KHL scoring with 23 goals and 42 assists for 65 points in 37 games.<ref name=\"PPG2014\"/><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.post-gazette.com/sports/penguins/2013/01/16/Malkin-on-the-lookout-for-a-new-winger-and-a-Stanley-Cup-for-Penguins/stories/201301160244|title=Malkin on the lookout for a new winger and a Stanley Cup for Penguins|last=Molinari|first=Dave|work=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette|location=Pittsburgh|date=16 January 2013|access-date=28 January 2014}}</ref> Though he missed the final part of the [[2012–13 KHL season|KHL season]], he still finished third overall in scoring.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.post-gazette.com/penguins/2013/05/01/Penguins-Notebook-Malkin-is-excited-by-arrival-of-playoffs/stories/201305010191|title=Penguins Notebook: Malkin is excited by arrival of playoffs|last=Anderson|first=Shelly|work=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette|location=Pittsburgh|date=1 May 2013|access-date=28 January 2014}}</ref> A concussion suffered on 22 February 2013, in a 3–1 win over the [[Florida Panthers]] after getting hit by Panthers defenceman [[Erik Gudbranson]] and a shoulder injury on 10 March in a 5–4 shootout win over the [[Toronto Maple Leafs]] caused by a hit by opposing forward [[James van Riemsdyk]] limited Malkin to 31 games during the season, rather than the 48 scheduled, in which he scored 33 points (nine goals, 24 assists). In the [[2013 Stanley Cup playoffs|2013 playoffs]], Malkin and the Penguins faced the eighth-seeded [[New York Islanders]] in the first round, eliminating them in six games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hockey-reference.com/playoffs/NHL_2013.html|title=2013 NHL Stanley Cup Playoffs Summary - Hockey-Reference.com|website=Hockey-Reference.com}}</ref> Malkin had an excellent series, recording two goals, nine assists and 11 points in the six games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hockey-reference.com/playoffs/2013-new-york-islanders-vs-pittsburgh-penguins-eastern-conference-quarter-finals.html|title=2013 NHL Stanley Cup Eastern Conference Quarter-Finals: NYI vs. PIT - Hockey-Reference.com|website=Hockey-Reference.com}}</ref> In the next round, the Penguins defeated the seventh-seeded Ottawa Senators in five games, with Malkin scoring two more goals and five points to clinch a third round appearance for the first time since the Penguins [[2009 Stanley Cup playoffs|2009]] Stanley Cup run.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hockey-reference.com/playoffs/2013-ottawa-senators-vs-pittsburgh-penguins-eastern-conference-semi-finals.html|title=2013 NHL Stanley Cup Eastern Conference Semi-Finals: OTT vs. PIT - Hockey-Reference.com|website=Hockey-Reference.com}}</ref> The Penguins were then swept in the Eastern Conference Finals against the fourth-seeded [[Boston Bruins]]. The entire Penguins team was kept to two goals in the four-game series against the Bruins, with Malkin held off the scoresheet and posting a −5 [[Plus–minus (sports)|plus-minus]] rating.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hockey-reference.com/playoffs/2013-boston-bruins-vs-pittsburgh-penguins-eastern-conference-finals.html|title=2013 NHL Stanley Cup Eastern Conference Finals: BOS vs. PIT - Hockey-Reference.com|website=Hockey-Reference.com}}</ref>\n\nIn the [[2013–14 NHL season|2013–14 season]], Malkin was held out of 22 games, missing two games with a lower body injury against the [[San Jose Sharks]] on 5 December 2013, nine games with another lower-body injury against the [[Detroit Red Wings]] on 14 December, and then 11 games with a foot injury against the [[Phoenix Coyotes]] on 25 March 2014. In the 60 games he was healthy, Malkin scored 23 goals, 49 assists and 72 points, second on the Penguins behind only Sidney Crosby. In his second-to-last game of the season three days earlier, against the Tampa Bay Lightning, Malkin had two goals and two assists for four points.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nhl.com/penguins/player/evgeni-malkin-8471215?stats=gamelogs-r-nhl&season=20132014|title=Evgeni Malkin Stats and News|website=NHL.com}}</ref> In the [[2014 Stanley Cup playoffs|2014 playoffs]], the Penguins met the [[Columbus Blue Jackets]] in the first round, eliminating them in six games. Malkin was unable to score for Pittsburgh in the first five games and only managed four assists in that time, causing Penguins fans to worry, especially since Crosby was being held off the scoresheet as well. But Malkin broke through with a hat-trick in game six, propelling his team to Round 2.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nhl.com/penguins/player/evgeni-malkin-8471215?stats=gamelogs-p-nhl&season=20132014|title=Evgeni Malkin Stats and News|website=NHL.com}}</ref> In Round 2 against the fifth-seeded New York Rangers, Malkin and the Penguins were eliminated in seven games, despite initially holding a 3–1 lead in the series. The Penguins only managed three goals in the last three games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hockey-reference.com/playoffs/2014-new-york-rangers-vs-pittsburgh-penguins-eastern-second-round.html|title=2014 NHL Stanley Cup Eastern Second Round: NYR vs. PIT - Hockey-Reference.com|website=Hockey-Reference.com}}</ref> Malkin had a solid series, scoring three goals and seven points in seven games, leading the Penguins.\n\nOn 30 October 2014, Malkin recorded his 400th assist on a [[Chris Kunitz]] goal in a 3–0 victory over the [[Los Angeles Kings]] to become the fifth player in franchise history to reach the mark.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/recap/_/gameId/400564464 |title=Marc-Andre Fleury makes 35 saves, helps Penguins topple Kings |website=[[ESPN]] |publisher=ESPN |agency=Associated Press |date=31 October 2014 |access-date=12 April 2024}}</ref> On 22 April 2015, in the fourth game in the first round of the [[2015 Stanley Cup playoffs|2015 playoffs]] against the [[Presidents' Trophy]]-winning New York Rangers, Malkin played his 100th career playoff game becoming the fifth player in Penguins history to do so.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/recap/_/gameId/400790518 |title=Kevin Hayes scores in OT as Rangers take 3-1 series lead over Penguins |agency=Associated Press |website=[[ESPN]] |publisher=ESPN |date=23 April 2015 |access-date=12 April 2024}}</ref> The Penguins would eventually fall to the Rangers in five games.\n\n====Back-to-back Stanley Cup championships, continued success (2015–2024)====\nMalkin had an injury-depleted [[2015–16 NHL season|2015–16]] campaign. On 4 February 2016, Malkin sustained an undisclosed lower-body injury in a 6–5 win against the [[Ottawa Senators]], resulting in him missing the next 10 games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.in/nhl/story/_/id/14747710/evgeni-malkin-pittsburgh-penguins-miss-rest-week-lower-body-injury |title=Malkin to miss rest of week with lower-body injury |website=espn.com |publisher=ESPN |author=ESPN |date=10 February 2016 |access-date=29 September 2024}}</ref> On 11 March, in a 3–2 win over the [[Columbus Blue Jackets]], Malkin suffered what was believed to be an undisclosed upper-body injury after colliding with Columbus’ defenceman [[Dalton Prout]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/nhl-puck-daddy/evgeni-malkin-out-6-8-weeks-with-upper-body-injury-215944141.html |title=Evgeni Malkin out 6-8 weeks with upper-body injury |website=yahoosports.com |publisher=Yahoo Sports |author=Josh Cooper |date=12 March 2016 |access-date=29 September 2016}}</ref> This injury resulted in Malkin missing the remainder of the season and the first game in the first round of the [[2016 Stanley Cup playoffs|2016 playoffs]] against the [[New York Rangers]]. He finished the season playing in 57 games with 27 goals and 31 assists for 58 points. After playing against the Rangers in the opening round for a second consecutive year and third consecutive year altogether and this time defeating them in five games, the Penguins would defeat the [[Presidents' Trophy]]-winning [[Washington Capitals]] in six games in the second round and the [[Tampa Bay Lightning]] in the third round in seven games before defeating the [[San Jose Sharks]] in six games in the [[2016 Stanley Cup Final]], as the Penguins clinched the Stanley Cup for the first time since [[2009 Stanley Cup Final|2009]]. He ended the run with six goals and 12 assists for 18 points in 23 games.<ref name = \"third championship\">{{cite web|last1=Campbell|first1=Tim|title=Evgeni Malkin, Sidney Crosby win third championship with Penguins|url=https://www.nhl.com/news/pittsburgh-s-evgeni-malkin-sidney-crosby-combine-for-another-title-289889724|website=NHL.com|access-date=12 March 2018|date=12 June 2017}}</ref>\n\n[[File:Evgeni Malkin 2017-06-11 1.jpg|thumb|left|Malkin with the [[Stanley Cup]] following game six of the [[2017 Stanley Cup Final]] in [[Nashville]]. It was the second consecutive championship and third overall of Malkin's career.]]\nOn 29 October 2016, Malkin recorded his 300th career NHL goal in a 5–4 win over the [[Philadelphia Flyers]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Sidney Crosby, Evgeni Malkin help Penguins top Flyers |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/pittsburgh-penguins-philadelphia-flyers-game-recap-october-29-283232686 |website=NHL.com |access-date=27 October 2025}}</ref> On 17 February 2017, Malkin recorded his 500th career assist on a goal by [[Ian Cole]] in a 2–1 overtime loss to the Columbus Blue Jackets. He ended the [[2016–17 NHL season|2016–17 season]] with 33 goals and 39 assists for 72 points in 62 games. He became the 29th player in the history of the NHL to record 150 points in the playoffs after recording three assists in a 7–0 win in game five of the Eastern Conference Finals against the [[Ottawa Senators]] on goals by [[Sidney Crosby]], [[Phil Kessel]] and [[Trevor Daley]], respectively.<ref name = \"third championship\"/> He ended the [[2017 Stanley Cup playoffs|2017 playoffs]] by leading the team and league with 28 points (10 goals, 18 assists) in all 25 playoff games as the Penguins would repeat as Stanley Cup champions.<ref name=\"third championship\"/>\n\nMalkin enjoyed a healthy and productive [[2017–18 NHL season|2017–18 season]] as he would finish the season with 98 points (42 goals, 56 assists) in 78 games. On 15 April 2018, in game three of the opening round of the [[2018 Stanley Cup playoffs|2018 playoffs]], Malkin recorded his 100th career playoff assist on a [[Justin Schultz]] goal in a 5–1 win over the in-state rival Philadelphia Flyers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/recap/_/gameId/401029178 |title=Crosby scores goal, leads Penguins to 5-1 Game 3 over Flyers |website=espn.com |publisher=ESPN |agency=Associated Press |date=15 April 2018 |access-date=25 July 2024}}</ref> After eventually defeating the Flyers in six games, the Penguins would face the Washington Capitals in the second round for the third consecutive year where Malkin and the Penguins would fall in six games to the eventual Stanley Cup champion and second-seeded Capitals.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.sbnation.com/nhl/2018/5/7/17326270/penguins-capitals-game-6-score-results|title=Capitals finally vanquish the Penguins with this OT winner|last=Kirshner|first=Alex|date=7 May 2018|work=SBNation.com|access-date=27 October 2018|archive-date=27 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181027232010/https://www.sbnation.com/nhl/2018/5/7/17326270/penguins-capitals-game-6-score-results|url-status=live}}</ref>\n\nOn 30 January 2019, Malkin suffered a suspected hand injury in a 4–2 win over the Tampa Bay Lightning after he was hit by Lightning’ defenceman [[Daniel Girardi]].<ref name=\"Dan Kingerski\">{{cite web|url=https://pittsburghhockeynow.com/evgeni-malkin-suffered-injury-before-the-fight-with-stamkos/ |title=Evgeni Malkin Suffered Injury Before the Fight with Stamkos |author=Dan Kingerski |website=pittsburghhockeynow.com |publisher=Pittsburgh Hockey Now |date=8 February 2019 |access-date=8 February 2019}}</ref> Despite this, he was able to finish the game recording two assists on goals by Phil Kessel and [[Kris Letang]] while also getting into a [[Fighting in hockey|fight]] with Lightning forward and captain [[Steven Stamkos]], which was later believed to have aggravated the injury.<ref name=\"Dan Kingerski\"/><ref>{{Cite news |last=Mackey |first=Jason |date=8 February 2019 |title=Even while injured, Evgeni Malkin delivers a message to Penguins |url=https://www.post-gazette.com/sports/penguins/2019/02/08/Penguins-Evgeni-Malkin-injury-winning-Stanley-Cup-Murray-Schultz-Lightning/stories/201902080145 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190722202054/https://www.post-gazette.com/sports/penguins/2019/02/08/Penguins-Evgeni-Malkin-injury-winning-Stanley-Cup-Murray-Schultz-Lightning/stories/201902080145 |archive-date=22 July 2019 |work=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette |language=en}}</ref> After missing the next four games and returning to the lineup on 11 February, in a 4–1 win over the Philadelphia Flyers, Malkin was the subject of a high-sticking call after swinging his stick into the face of Flyers’ forward [[Michael Raffl]], resulting in a one game suspension.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nhl/2019/02/11/evgeni-malkin-stick-swing-penguins-flyers-michael-raffl/2844012002/ |title=Penguins star Evgeni Malkin suspended one game for swinging point on a Phil Kessel goal against the Washington Capitals, becoming the [[List of NHL players with 1,000 points|88th player in league history]] to reach the mark.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Crosby |first1=Wes |title=Malkin gets 1,000th NHL point for Penguins against Capitals |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/washington-capitals-pittsburgh-penguins-game-recap-305706972 |website=NHL.com |access-date=25 March 2024 |date=12 March 2019}}</ref> Malkin would finish the [[2018–19 NHL season|2018–19 season]] with 21 goals and 51 assists for 72 points in 68 games as the Penguins as a team finished as the fifth seed in the East. In the [[2019 Stanley Cup playoffs|2019 playoffs]], Malkin recorded a goal and two assists for three points in all four games against the [[New York Islanders]] as the Penguins would get swept in the first round by the fourth-seeded Islanders.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/recap/_/gameId/401126377 |title=Islanders finish off Penguins 3-1 for stunning playoff sweep |author=AP |website=espn.com |publisher=ESPN |date=16 April 2019 |access-date=11 August 2024}}</ref>\n\nOn 16 March 2021, Malkin suffered a minor knee injury in a 2–1 loss over the [[Boston Bruins]] after he collided with Bruins' defenceman [[Jarred Tinordi]], resulting in him missing the next 23 games until recovering to play the final four games of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://apnews.com/penguins-c-malkin-out-week-to-week-with-lower-body-injury-a1f278a7aa2a31627e37511f4ffba976 |title=Penguins C Malkin out \"week to week\" with lower-body injury |author=AP |website=apnews.com |publisher=AP News |date=19 March 2021 |access-date=7 September 2024}}</ref> He would end the [[COVID-19 pandemic|pandemic]]-shortened [[2020–21 NHL season|2020–21 season]] with eight goals and 20 assists for 28 points in 33 games. He re-aggravated the injury in the season finale on 8 May in the Penguins 1–0 win over the [[Buffalo Sabres]], causing him to miss the first two games in the opening round of the [[2021 Stanley Cup playoffs|2021 playoffs]] against the New York Islanders.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2928500-penguins-evgeni-malkin-out-vs-islanders-for-game-1-of-2021-nhl-playoffs |title=Penguins' Evgeni Malkin Out vs. Islanders for Game 1 of 2021 NHL Playoffs |author=Paul Kasabian |website=bleacherreport.com |publisher=Bleacher Report |date=16 May 2021 |access-date=7 September 2021}}</ref> Malkin returned to the lineup for game three but the Penguins would eventually get defeated by the Islanders in six games, marking the second time in three seasons where the Islanders defeated Malkin and the Penguins in the first round of the playoffs. Malkin finished the playoffs with a goal and four assists for five points in four games.\n\nMalkin underwent knee surgery in the 2021 off-season, resulting in him missing the first 32 games of the [[2021–22 NHL season|2021–22 season]] before making his season debut on 11 January 2022, in a 4–1 win against the [[Anaheim Ducks]] and recording two goals along with an assist on a [[Jeff Carter]] goal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcwashington.com/news/sports/nbcsports/penguins-c-evgeni-malkin-to-miss-at-least-first-two-months-of-2021-22-season/2811725/ |title=\nPenguins C Evgeni Malkin to Miss at Least First Two Months of 2021-22 Season |author=Bijan Todd |website=nbcsportswashington.com |publisher=NBC Washington |date=23 September 2021 |access-date=7 September 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nhl.com/news/pittsburgh-penguins-anaheim-ducks-game-recap-329656596 |title=Malkin scores twice, in return, helps Penguins defeat Ducks |author=Dan Arritt |website=nhl.com |publisher=National Hockey League |date=12 January 2022 |access-date=7 September 2024}}</ref> On 11 April, Malkin was handed a four game suspension after he cross-checked [[Nashville Predators]] defenceman [[Mark Borowiecki]] the previous day and bloodying him.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.espn.com/nhl/story/_/id/33721064/pittsburgh-penguins-evgeni-malkin-suspended-4-games-cross-check-face-nashville-predators-mark-borowiecki |title=Pittsburgh Penguins' Evgeni Malkin suspended 4 games for cross-check to face of Nashville Predators' Mark Borowiecki |website=espn.com |publisher=ESPN |author=AP |date=11 April 2022 |access-date=29 September 2024}}</ref> He would go on to finish the season with 20 goals and 22 assists for 42 points in 41 games played while the Penguins as a team finished as the sixth seed in the East. Malkin followed up in the [[2022 Stanley Cup playoffs|2022 playoffs]] with three goals and three assists for six points in all seven games as the Penguins would lose in round one once more as they were defeated in seven games by the New York Rangers and surrendering a 3–1 series lead in the series against the third-seeded Rangers in the process.\n\nOn 12 July 2022, after initial reports that he would be heading to free agency, Malkin signed a four-year, $24.4 million contract extension to stay with the Penguins.<ref>{{cite web |title=Malkin signs four-year, $24.4 million contract extension with Penguins |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nhl/article/malkin-signs-four-year-24-4-million-contract-extension-with-penguins/ |website=[[Sportsnet]] |access-date=13 July 2022 |date=12 July 2022}}</ref> He played his [[List of NHL players with 1,000 games played|1,000th NHL game]] on 23 November against the [[Chicago Blackhawks]], joining Sidney Crosby as the only players to play all 1,000 games with the Penguins.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Crosby |first=Wes |date=23 November 2022 |title=Penguins honor Malkin for 1,000 games with pregame ceremony |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/pittsburgh-penguins-honor-evgeni-malkin-for-1-000-games-with-pregame-c-337964024 |access-date=30 November 2022 |website=NHL.com}}</ref> Malkin finished the [[2022–23 NHL season|2022–23 season]] playing in all 82 games with 83 points recorded (27 goals, 56 assists) and the Penguins missed the [[2023 Stanley Cup playoffs|playoffs]] for the first time since 2006 and it would be the first time in Malkin's career that he missed the playoffs.<ref>{{cite web |title=Penguins eliminated from NHL playoffs, ending the longest postseason streak of the four major sports leagues |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nhl/news/penguins-eliminated-from-nhl-playoffs-ending-the-longest-postseason-streak-of-the-four-major-sports-leagues/ |website=cbssports.com |author=Bryan DeArdo |date=12 April 2023 |access-date=25 March 2024}}</ref>\n\nMalkin recorded 27 goals, 40 assists and 67 points in all 82 contests played in the [[2023–24 NHL season|2023–24 season]] as the Penguins missed the playoffs for the second consecutive season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nhl.com/news/why-2023-24-pittsburgh-penguins-are-eliminated |title=Penguins eliminated after issues with power play, goaltending |website=nhl.com |publisher=NHL |author=Tom Gulitti |date=17 April 2024 |access-date=17 April 2024}}</ref>\n\n====Recent years (2024–present)====\nThe beginning of the [[2024–25 NHL season|2024–25 season]] was filled with milestones for Malkin. On 10 October 2024, Malkin recorded his 800th career assist on a goal by [[Erik Karlsson]] in a 6–3 win over the [[Detroit Red Wings]], becoming the 34th player in league history to reach the mark.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Rossi |first1=Rob |title=Penguins' Evgeni Malkin records 800th assist, becomes 34th player in NHL history to reach feat 2024}}</ref> Two days later, in a 4–2 loss to the [[Toronto Maple Leafs]], Malkin recorded his 1,300th NHL point with an assist on a goal by [[Rickard Rakell]], becoming the 37th player in league history to reach the mark.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Damp |first1=Patrick |title=Evgeni Malkin hits career milestone in second straight game, records 1,300th career point In the Penguins first round exit in six games in the [[2026 Stanley Cup playoffs|2026 playoffs]] against the [[Philadelphia Flyers]], Malkin scored two goals and an assist in six games.<ref>{{Cite web Championships|2003 Russia]]|\n}}\n{{MedalBottom}}{{BLP sources section|date=April 2026}}\nMalkin made his first international appearance with Russia at the [[2003 IIHF World U18 Championships]] in [[Yaroslavl]]. He helped Russia to a bronze medal, scoring nine points in six games.<ref name=\"EliteProspects\">{{cite web |title=Yevgeni Malkin |url=https://www.eliteprospects.com/player/4231/yevgeni-malkin |website=EliteProspects.com |access-date=27 October 2025}}</ref> He was named Russia's U18 captain for the [[2004 IIHF World U18 Championships]]{{citation needed|date=May 2025}} the following year and scored eight points as Russia improved to a gold medal in the tournament.<ref name=\"EliteProspects\" />\n\nSeveral months prior to his second and final U18 tournament, Malkin debuted at the under-20 level with Russia at the [[2004 World Junior Ice Hockey Championships|2004 World Junior Championships]]. In his first of three tournament appearances, he contributed five points in six games but could not help Russia reach the podium.<ref name=\"EliteProspects\" /> The following year, Malkin finished second in team scoring at the [[2005 World Junior Ice Hockey Championships|2005 World Junior Championships]] to Alexander Ovechkin with ten points.{{citation needed|date=May 2025}} Led by the duo of Malkin and Ovechkin (the two had also played together the previous year), Russia won the silver, losing to [[Canada men's national junior ice hockey team|Canada]] in the gold medal game.{{citation needed|date=May 2025}} Later in 2005, Malkin made his debut with the [[Russia men's national ice hockey team|Russian men's team]] at the [[2005 Men's World Ice Hockey Championships|2005 World Championships]].{{citation needed|date=May 2025}} Despite failing to score a goal in the tournament, Malkin contributed four assists to help Russia to a bronze medal in [[Vienna]].{{citation needed|date=May 2025}}\n\nIn 2006, Malkin did triple duty for Russia, competing in his third [[IIHF World Junior Championship|World Junior Championships]], his first [[Ice hockey at the Winter Olympics|Winter Olympics]] and his second [[World Ice Hockey Championships|World Championships]].{{citation needed|date=May 2025}} He was named the top forward and MVP of the [[2006 World Junior Ice Hockey Championships|2006 World Junior Championships]] in January, captaining Russia to a second straight silver medal and gold medal game loss to Canada.{{citation needed|date=May 2025}} Less than two months later, Malkin was given one of the final spots on Team Russia for the [[Ice hockey at the 2006 Winter Olympics|2006 Winter Olympics]] in [[Turin]], where he helped the team to a fourth-place finish with six points in seven games.<ref name=\":0\">{{Cite web |last=Anderson |first=Shelly |date=27 May 2025 |title=IOC Ruling Probably Ends Malkin's International Career |url=https://pittsburghhockeynow.com/pittsburgh-penguins-ioc-ruling-probably-ends-evgeni-malkin-international-career/ |access-date=28 April 2026 |website=Pittsburgh Hockey Now |language=en-US}}</ref> Then in May, Malkin played in the [[2006 Men's World Ice Hockey Championships|2006 World Championship]], where he led Russia in team scoring with nine points.{{citation needed|date=May 2025}}\n\nFollowing his NHL rookie campaign with the Pittsburgh Penguins, Malkin was named to the Russian squad for the [[2007 Men's World Ice Hockey Championships|2007 World Championships]], where he achieved a personal best for the tournament of ten points.<ref name=\"Potts 2019\">{{cite web |last1=Potts |first1=Andy |title=Eighth time lucky? |url=https://www.iihf.com/en/events/2019/wm/news/11181/eighth-time-lucky |website=IIHF.com |access-date=7 July 2026}}</ref> Malkin played in the first line of Team Russia together with [[Ilya Kovalchuk]] and [[Alexander Frolov]].{{citation needed|date=May 2025}} Malkin scored Russia's only goal in a 2-1 loss to Finland in the semifinals, with Russia going on to claim the bronze medal in the third place game.<ref name=\"Potts 2019\"></ref>\n\n2010 was an impressive year for Malkin internationally. Malkin was selected to play for the Russian Olympic Team at the [[2010 Vancouver Olympic Games]], where he led all players at the Olympic tournament in points-per-game average with 1.50 points per game, and led Team Russia in points yet again with three goals and six points in four games.{{citation needed|date=May 2025}} Russia ultimately lost to Canada in the quarter-finals, finishing sixth overall.{{citation needed|date=May 2025}} Malkin then joined the Russian team for the [[2010 IIHF World Championship]].{{citation needed|date=May 2025}} Despite joining the tournament partway through, as his NHL team was not eliminated until the second round of the Stanley Cup playoffs, Malkin scored at a goal-per-game pace and ended up with the distinction of being the player with the fewest games played who made the post-tournament IIHF World Championship All-star team.{{citation needed|date=May 2025}} His 5 goals and 2 assists in 5 games secured him a place in the tournament's top 10 point scorers, and he was the only player among the top 10 scorers who played less than 6 games.{{citation needed|date=May 2025}} He captured his first World Championships silver medal.{{citation needed|date=May 2025}}\n\nMalkin was named MVP, the best forward and to the All-Star team at the [[2012 IIHF World Championship]], where he scored 11 goals and made 8 assists, winning the scoring league with a total of 19 points.<ref>{{cite web|title=Malkin wins MVP honours|url=http://www.iihf.com/competition/272/news/news-singleview-2012/?tx_ttnews%5Btt_news%5D=6990&cHash=9adec90e4e9f67cb51f58dc295b8bd51|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140516235931/http://www.iihf.com/competition/272/news/news-singleview-2012/?tx_ttnews%5Btt_news%5D=6990&cHash=9adec90e4e9f67cb51f58dc295b8bd51|url-status=dead|archive-date=16 May 2014|website=iihf.com|access-date=26 April 2018|date=20 May 2012}}</ref> He recorded at least one point in every game played.{{citation needed|date=May 2025}} He also had two hat-tricks, against [[Sweden men's national ice hockey team|Sweden]] in the preliminary round and against [[Finland men's national ice hockey team|Finland]] in the semi-final.{{citation needed|date=May 2025}} Russia won the gold medal.{{citation needed|date=May 2025}} The 19 points is a new record for Russian players on World Championships.{{citation needed|date=March 2022}}\n\nIn 2014, Malkin was named to the 2014 Russian Olympic Ice Hockey Team.<ref name=\":0\" /> He played all five games for Russia as they finished fifth in the tournament after losing to Finland in the quarter-finals.{{citation needed|date=May 2025}} Malkin had one goal and two assists by the end of the tournament.{{citation needed|date=May 2025}}\n\nIn 2019, Malkin played in the [[2019 IIHF World Championship]], where he recorded the primary assist on Russia's game-winning goal against [[United States men's national ice hockey team|Team USA]] in the knockout stage.{{citation needed|date=May 2025}} Russia would lose their next game to Finland in the semifinal, and settle for a bronze medal.{{citation needed|date=May 2025}}\n\nIn 2020, Malkin was named to the IIHF All-Time Russian National Team ahead of Russian and Soviet all-time greats such as [[Sergei Makarov (ice hockey, born 1958)|Sergei Makarov]], [[Alex Ovechkin]], and [[Pavel Datsyuk]], among others.<ref name=\"potts list 2020\">{{cite web | url=https://www.iihf.com/en/events/2020/wm/news/19137/all-time-russia-team | title=IIHF - All-Time Russia Team}}</ref> The list included both Russian and Soviet players, part of a series of lists for 16 countries who would have participated in the canceled [[2020 IIHF World Championship]], to celebrate the 100-year anniversary of the IIHF World Championships.<ref name=\"potts list 2020\"></ref>\n\n==Playing style==\n{{BLP sources section|date=April 2026}}\nMalkin has been described as a centre with offensive abilities and defensive awareness.{{citation needed|date=May 2025}} He has also been known to play on the wing and on the point during the power play.{{citation needed|date=May 2025}} He is a skater with firm balance and above average top speed and agility at the NHL level.{{citation needed|date=May 2025}} In his early years, Malkin was a physical player who threw big hits.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1471685-where-does-evgeni-malkin-rank-among-the-all-time-great-penguins | title=Where Does Evgeni Malkin Rank Among the All-Time Great Penguins? |first=Michael |last=Prunka | website=[[Bleacher Report]]}}</ref> He relies on his hockey IQ and athleticism most times to avoid checks by opponents.{{citation needed|date=May 2025}} He has an arsenal of shots (slap, wrist, backhand, and snap), and has stick-handling ability.{{citation needed|date=May 2025}}\n\n{{blockquote|\"He's so big and strong and he doesn't mind the physicality. That's what separates him apart from other players that are gifted offensive players. He wants the puck all the time and he'll go through a check or take a check to make a play.\"<ref name=\"2012Hart\" />|[[Steven Stamkos]] on Malkin, June 2012}}\n\n{{blockquote|\"He's just one of those guys that wants the puck all the time. For me, it was get him the puck as much as possible. With his ability to feed me and my ability to shoot the puck, it worked really well. I just got open as much as I could. I'd just get him the puck as fast as I could because I knew I was going to get it back wherever I was on the ice, it was coming back.\"<ref>{{cite web|last1=Marrazza|first1=Dan|title=James Neal Reflects On Lessons Learned From Playing With Evgeni Malkin|url=https://www.nhl.com/goldenknights/news/james-neal-reflects-on-lessons-learned-from-playing-with-evgeni-malkin-294012180|website=NHL.com|access-date=15 March 2018|date=14 December 2017}}</ref>|[[James Neal (ice hockey)|James Neal]] on Malkin, December 2017}}\n\n==Personal life==\nIn 2006, Malkin opened a restaurant, VIP Zone, in Magnitogorsk, which had been designed to look like the inside of a prison.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 10, 2006 |title=Hockey Star Malkin Offers Lock-Down Dinners at Prison-Themed Restaurant |url=http://www.russianprospects.com/public/article.php?article_id=466 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150908100550/http://www.russianprospects.com/public/article.php?article_id=466 |archive-date=2015-09-08 |website=www.russianprospects.com}}</ref><ref name=\"auto\"/> In 2009, Malkin confirmed VIP Zone had been leased to new owners who had updated it.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Evgeni Malkin on playing in Russia, Stanley Cup plans and beach paparazzi shots: 'They were good. What else can I say?'|url = https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/nhl-puck-daddy/evgeni-malkin-playing-russia-stanley-cup-plans-beach--nhl.html?guccounter=1|website = Yahoo Sports |date = 22 July 2009|access-date = 19 January 2025|author= Chesnokov, Dmitry}}</ref>\n\nMalkin became engaged to Russian television personality {{ill|Anna Kasterova|ru|Кастерова, Анна Романовна}} in November 2015; they married in 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://thehockeywriters.com/evgeni-malkin-opens-up-in-russian-interview/|title=Evgeni Malkin Opens Up In Russian Interview|work=The Hockey Writers|date=8 February 2015}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Карасева |first=Александра |title=Хоккеист Евгений Малкин женился на матери своего ребенка |url=https://www.thevoicemag.ru/stars/news/04-06-2016/hokkeist-evgeniy-malkin-zhenilsya-na-materi-svoego-rebenka/ |website=www.thevoicemag.ru |language=ru-RU}}</ref> On 31 May 2016, their son was born.<ref>{{Cite web |date=31 May 2016 |title=У Малкина родился сын |url=https://news.sportbox.ru/Vidy_sporta/Hokkej/NHL/spbnews_NI615244_U_Malkina_rodilsa_syn |website=news.sportbox.ru |language=ru}}</ref> Malkin has American citizenship, saying Pittsburgh is his \"second home\" and that his child also has an American passport.<ref>{{Cite web |date= 28 October 2019|publisher=Pittsburgh Tribune-Review|title=Penguins' Evgeni Malkin pursues U.S. citizenship, brushes off report of investment gone wrong|url=https://triblive.com/sports/penguins-evgeni-malkin-pursues-u-s-citizenship-brushes-off-report-of-investment-gone-wrong/|website=triblive.com|author=Seth Rorabaugh}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=28 October 2019 |title=Malkin becomes dual citizen in U.S. and Russia; denies investment problems |url=https://www.wpxi.com/sports/nhl/pittsburgh-penguins/pittsburgh-penguins-malkin-becomes-dual-citizen-in-us-and-russia-denies-investment-problems/1002491407/ |website=WPXI |language=en}}</ref>\n\nIn November 2017, Malkin announced his membership of the [[PutinTeam]] social movement, launched by compatriot and fellow NHL player [[Alexander Ovechkin]] in support of the President of Russia [[Vladimir Putin]] during the [[2018 Russian presidential election]]. Malkin stated, \"We just try to offer our support because, in 2018, we have the [[2018 FIFA World Cup|World Cup]] in Russia; they have elections, too.\"<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nhl/penguins/2017/11/17/penguins-evgeni-malkin-joins-vladimir-putin-team/873638001/ |title=Penguins' Evgeni Malkin joins 'Putin Team' |last=Gleeson |first=Scott |date=17 November 2017 |newspaper=USA Today |access-date=26 November 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Mackey |first=Jason |date=16 November 2017 |title=Malkin discusses decision to join 'Putin Team' |url=https://www.post-gazette.com/sports/penguins/2017/11/16/Malkin-discusses-decision-to-join-Putin-Team/stories/201711160298 |website=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191212221850/http://www.post-gazette.com/sports/penguins/2017/11/16/Malkin-discusses-decision-to-join-Putin-Team/stories/201711160298 |archive-date=12 December 2019 |url-status=live |language=en}}</ref>\n\n==Career statistics==\n\n===Regular season and playoffs===\n<!-- PLEASE DO NOT UPDATE STATISTICS MID-SEASON, AS IT CREATES MORE PROBLEMS THAN IT SOLVES, AND WIKIPEDIA'S PURPOSE IS NOT TO PROVIDE UP-TO-THE-MINUTE STATISTICS. Nicknamed \"'''Showtime'''\",<ref name=\":0\" /> he was selected by the Blackhawks with the [[List of first overall NHL draft picks|first overall pick]] in the [[2007 NHL entry draft]] and initially played for them until February 2023, when he was traded to the [[New York Rangers]]. He has also played for the [[Detroit Red Wings]]. Kane has represented the United States at the [[2010 Winter Olympics|2010]] and [[2014 Winter Olympics]].\n\nKane established himself as one of the most productive and decorated players of his era. He won the 2008 [[Calder Memorial Trophy]] for NHL's rookie of the year and played a crucial role in the Blackhawks' three championships in [[2010 Stanley Cup Final|2010]], [[2013 Stanley Cup Final|2013]] and [[2015 Stanley Cup Final|2015]]. Kane's notable achievements include winning the [[Conn Smythe Trophy]] as the most valuable player of the playoffs in 2013,<ref>{{cite news |last=Roarke |first=Shawn P. |url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=675086 |title=Kane becomes fourth American to win Conn Smythe |via=NHL.com |publisher=Chicago Blackhawks |date=June 25, 2013 |access-date=July 22, 2015 |archive-date=August 2, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150802114347/http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=675086 |url-status=dead}}</ref> and later becoming the first American-born player to secure the [[Hart Memorial Trophy]] as the most valuable player and the [[Art Ross Trophy]] as the scoring champion in the [[2015–16 NHL season]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/patrick-kane-wins-hart-trophy-as-nhl-mvp-281020276 |title=Patrick Kane first U.S.-born player to win Hart |website=NHL.com |publisher=National Hockey League |access-date=November 4, 2016 |archive-date=August 30, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170830153741/https://www.nhl.com/news/patrick-kane-wins-hart-trophy-as-nhl-mvp/c-281020276 |url-status=live}}</ref>\n\nKane led all NHL players in scoring during the 2010s and was later named as one of the [[100 Greatest NHL Players]]. He is considered one of the best American players of all time. Kane became the youngest American player to reach 1,000 career regular season points in 2020,<ref name=kane1000>{{cite news |last1=Greenfield |first1=Jimmy |last2=Yoder |first2=Chad |title=Breaking down Patrick Kane's milestone points, from No. 1 to No. 1,000 |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/blackhawks/ct-num-chicago-blackhawks-patrick-kane-1000-points-20200120-jsragn2tnfawlfwlp3iwbk5uqq-story.html |access-date=January 20, 2019 |website=[[Chicago Tribune]] |date=January 20, 2019 |archive-date=January 20, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200120220506/https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/blackhawks/ct-num-chicago-blackhawks-patrick-kane-1000-points-20200120-jsragn2tnfawlfwlp3iwbk5uqq-story.html |url-status=live}}</ref> and holds the record for the most career points and career assists by an American-born player.<ref>{{cite news |last=Russo |first=Modano |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3899844/2022/12/07/nhl-99-mike-modano/ |title=NHL99: Mike Modano set a new standard for U.S.-born players, with grace and floppy-jersey flair |work=[[The Athletic]] |date=December 7, 2022 |access-date=December 19, 2022 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221219100431/https://theathletic.com/3899844/2022/12/07/nhl-99-mike-modano/ |archive-date=December 19, 2022}}</ref><ref name=\"Website-1\">{{Cite web |date=2026-10-16 |title=Patrick Kane breaks NHL assists record for US-born player in Chicago Blackhawks’ 4-3 OT win vs. Winnipeg Jets |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2026/10/16/chicago-blackhawks-patrick-kane-assists-record/ |access-date=2026-10-16 |website=Chicago Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref>\n\n==Early life==\nPatrick Kane was born to Donna and Patrick \"Tiki\" Kane in [[Buffalo, New York]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Rogers |first=Jesse |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/chicago/blackhawks/post/_/id/4664993/kane-hoping-to-celebrate-his-birthday-with-win |title=Kane hoping to celebrate his birthday with win |work=[[ESPN]] |date=November 11, 2010 |access-date=August 4, 2023 |archive-date=August 4, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230804194324/https://www.espn.com/blog/chicago/blackhawks/post/_/id/4664993/kane-hoping-to-celebrate-his-birthday-with-win |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=\"si-ice\">{{cite magazine |last=Price |first=S. L. |url=https://www.si.com/nhl/2016/03/09/patrick-kane-chicago-blackhawks-assault-case |title=On the ice, Patrick Kane is so good and still has so far to go |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=March 9, 2016 |access-date=June 1, 2023 |archive-date=May 31, 2023
