hockey.<ref name=\"si-ice\"/> His father was a season ticket holder for the [[Buffalo Sabres]], and frequently took his family to games.<ref name=\"si-ice\"/> Kane was inadvertently featured in the background of [[Sylvain Turgeon]]'s 1994–95 [[Pinnacle Brands|Pinnacle]] trading card while attending a Sabres' game as a child with his father.<ref name=\"trib-card\">{{cite news |last=Skrbina |first=Paul |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/blackhawks/ct-patrick-kane-hockey-card-htmlstory.html |title=See Patrick Kane's first hockey card, when he was 6 |work=[[Chicago Tribune]] |date=January 27, 2018 |access-date=June 1, 2023 |archive-date=May 31, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230531150854/https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/blackhawks/ct-patrick-kane-hockey-card-htmlstory.html |url-status=live}}</ref> Kane's favorite players while growing up were [[Pat Lafontaine]] and [[Joe Sakic]].<ref name=\"USA-Hockey\">{{cite news |last=Burns |first=Mark |url=https://www.usahockeymagazine.com/article/few-minutes-patrick-kane |title=A Few Minutes With Patrick Kane |work=USA Hockey Magazine |date=2015 |access-date=June 1, 2023 |archive-date=May 31, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230531150311/https://www.usahockeymagazine.com/article/few-minutes-patrick-kane |url-status=live}}</ref> In addition to hockey, he played [[baseball]], [[association football|soccer]], [[lacrosse]], and [[basketball]] in grade and middle school.<ref name=\"USA-Hockey\"/>\n\nKane began playing hockey when he was seven years old.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://nbcsports.msnbc.com/id/22032435/ |title=Kane up to task of helping revive Blackhawks |work=NBC Sports |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |date=January 17, 2020 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080425153220/http://nbcsports.msnbc.com/id/22032435/ |archivedate=April 25, 2008 |access-date=June 1, 2023}}</ref> His father allowed Kane to practice stick-handling and shooting in their house's basement, going as far as to set up a miniature rink that featured nets and boards.<ref name=\"athl-1\">{{cite news |last=Lazerus |first=Mark |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2417883/2021/03/08/the-incredible-stories-of-blackhawks-star-patrick-kanes-days-as-americas-most-dominant-youth-hockey-player-ever/ news |last=Roumeliotis |first=Charlie |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/chicago/blackhawks/why-darryl-belfry-benched-young-patrick-kane-after-scoring-goal |title=Why Belfry benched a young Patrick Kane |url-status=live}}</ref>\n\n==Playing career==\n===Minor and junior===\nKane played for the Buffalo Saints 14U AAA hockey club.<ref name=\"athl-1\"/> Donnie Harkins, the head coach of the Honeybaked 16U AAA hockey club, personally recruited Kane to join his team in [[Michigan]] after watching him play in a tournament.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2007/12/02/sports/hockey/02kane.html |title=A Child of the Game Is a Top N.H.L. Rookie |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=December 2, 2007 |access-date=June 1, 2023 |archive-date=May 31, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230531151154/https://www.nytimes.com/2007/12/02/sports/hockey/02kane.html |url-status=live}}</ref> At the age of 14, Kane relocated to [[Detroit]], Michigan, to play for Honeybaked during the 2003–04 season. He resided with former NHL player [[Pat Verbeek]] while living in Detroit, whom Kane regards as a mentor and one of his primary reasons for relocating.<ref name=\"USA-Hockey\"/> Honeybaked posted a 66–3–1 record that season, with Kane tallying 83 goals and 77 assists.<ref name=\"athl-1\"/>\n\nHis success caught the attention of the [[London Knights]], who drafted him in the fifth round, 88th overall, of the 2004 [[Ontario Hockey League]] (OHL) Midget Draft.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chl.ca/CHLTopProspects/2007_bios.html |title=2007 Home Hardware CHL/NHL Top Prospects Game Participant Bios |publisher=[[Canadian Hockey League|CHL]] |access-date=June 23, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070211012530/http://www.chl.ca/CHLTopProspects/2007_bios.html |archive-date=February 11, 2007 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Kane did not join the team and instead played for the [[USA Hockey National Team Development Program|United States National Team Development Program]] (NTDP), which was based in Michigan.<ref name=\"athl-1\"/> The US NTDP was initially hesitant to recruit Kane based on his short stature, describing him in a scouting report as, \"a little meek—and still has the body of a 12-year-old\".<ref name=\"si-ice\"/> Kane spent the next two years playing for the US NTDP, where he was given the chance to train and play a bigger role on a more frequent basis.<ref name=\"USA-Hockey\"/> He reflected on the US NTDP by commenting, \"The program really focuses on improving your body, you get a lot of practice time and you really learn how to play the game and how to treat yourself.\"<ref name=\"USA-Hockey\"/> He led the team in scoring with 102 points during the 2005–06 season, surpassing the previous record holder, [[Phil Kessel]].<ref name=\"OHL-ROY\">{{cite web|url=http://www.ontariohockeyleague.com/awards/?sub=&id=3666 |title=Patrick Kane Named OHL Rookie of the Year |publisher=[[Ontario Hockey League|OHL]] |access-date=June 23, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070709120007/http://www.ontariohockeyleague.com/awards/?sub=&id=3666 |archive-date=July 9, 2007 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=\"OHL-sign\">{{cite news |url=https://londonknights.com/knights-sign-patrick-kane |title=Knights Sign Patrick Kane |publisher=[[London Knights]] |date=August 27, 2006 |access-date=June 1, 2023 |archive-date=June 1, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230601190230/https://londonknights.com/knights-sign-patrick-kane |url-status=dead}}</ref>\n\nKane joined the London Knights for the [[2006–07 OHL season]].<ref name=\"OHL-sign\"/> He skated on a line with future NHL forwards [[Sergei Kostitsyn]] and [[Sam Gagner]].<ref name=\"OHL-2\">{{cite news |last=Pyette |first=Ryan |url=https://londonknights.com/knights-biggest-guns-unite-to-lead-attack |title=Knights' biggest guns unite to lead attack |publisher=[[London Knights]] |agency=Sun Media |date=March 22, 2007 |access-date=June 1, 2023 |archive-date=June 1, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230601174742/https://londonknights.com/knights-biggest-guns-unite-to-lead-attack |url-status=dead}}</ref> Kane appeared in 58 games for Knights, where he recorded 62 goals and 83 assists,<ref name=\"OHL3\">{{cite web |url=http://www.ontariohockeyleague.com/stats/player.php?id=4581 |title=Patrick Kane |publisher=[[Ontario Hockey League|OHL]] |access-date=June 23, 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070625211731/http://www.ontariohockeyleague.com/stats/player.php?id=4581 |archive-date=June 25, 2007}}</ref> while combining with his linemates for 394 points.<ref name=\"OHL-ROY\"/><ref name=\"OHL-2\"/> He accrued an additional 31 points in 16 playoff games as the Knights lost to the [[Plymouth Whalers]] in the OHL's Western Conference final.<ref name=\"OHL3\"/> Kane won the [[Emms Family Award]] for the OHL rookie of the year,<ref name=\"OHL-ROY\"/> and was the runner-up to [[John Tavares]] for the [[Red Tilson Trophy]] as league MVP.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ontariohockeyleague.com/awards/?sub=&id=3613 |title=Tavares wins Red Tilson Trophy as OHL's Most Outstanding Player |publisher=[[Ontario Hockey League|OHL]] |access-date=June 23, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070708233449/http://www.ontariohockeyleague.com/awards/?sub=&id=3613 |archive-date=July 8, 2007 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Kane also won the [[Canadian Hockey League]]'s (CHL) [[CHL Top Draft Prospect Award|Top Prospect]] and [[CHL Top Scorer Award|Top Scorer]] awards.<ref name=\"CHL1\">{{cite news |url=https://chl.ca/article/great-single-season-makes-kane-a-knight-to-remember |title=Great single season makes Kane a Knight to remember |publisher=[[Canadian Hockey League|CHL]] |date=January 24, 2020 |access-date=June 1, 2023 |archive-date=June 1, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230601194158/https://chl.ca/article/great-single-season-makes-kane-a-knight-to-remember |url-status=live}}</ref> His 145 points is the fifth most for a rookie in CHL history.<ref name=\"CHL1\"/> The Knights later retired Kane's No. 88 jersey on January 17, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |last=O'Leary |first=Dan |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/blackhawks-patrick-kane-has-jersey-retired-by-ohl-s-london-knights-314089648 |title=Blackhawks' Kane has jersey retired by OHL's London Knights |publisher=[[National Hockey League]] |website=NHL.com |date=January 17, 2020 |access-date=June 1, 2023 |archive-date=June 1, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230601190711/https://www.nhl.com/news/blackhawks-patrick-kane-has-jersey-retired-by-ohls-london-knights/c-314089648 |url-status=live}}</ref>\n\n===Professional===\n====Chicago Blackhawks (2007–2023)====\nHeading into the [[2007 NHL entry draft]], Kane was ranked second among North American prospects by the [[NHL Central Scouting Bureau]] and was chosen first overall by the [[Chicago Blackhawks]].<ref name=\"kelowna-2007\">{{cite news |url=https://www.westkelownawarriors.ca/turris-1-in-central-scouting-bureau-rankings |title=Turris #1 in Central Scouting Bureau Rankings |work=[[West Kelowna Warriors]] |date=May 6, 2007 |access-date=April 19, 2025}}</ref> The [[St. Louis Blues]] offered to trade the Blackhawks their 9th, 24th and 26th overall picks in the 2007 Draft in order to acquire Chicago's first overall selection and draft Kane.<ref>{{cite news |last=Timmermann |first=Tom |url=http://www.stltoday.com/sports/hockey/professional/morning-skate/blues-three-first-round-picks-from-draft-are-gone/article_58dc1c85-d99d-54ed-8683-9ccd1833a4e7.html |title=Blues' three first-round picks from 2007 draft are gone |work=[[St. Louis Post-Dispatch]] |date=March 3, 2015 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170220044440/http://www.stltoday.com/sports/hockey/professional/morning-skate/blues-three-first-round-picks-from-draft-are-gone/article_58dc1c85-d99d-54ed-8683-9ccd1833a4e7.html |archive-date=February 20, 2017 |access-date=February 20, 2017}}</ref> On July 25, 2007, Blackhawks' general manager [[Dale Tallon]] announced that they had signed Kane to a three-year contract. Kane threw the [[ceremonial first pitch]] at a [[Chicago Cubs]] game on June 25, 2007, at [[Wrigley Field]].<ref name=\"cubs\">{{cite news |last=Cronin |first=Tim |date=June 23, 2007 |title=Hawks grab Patrick Kane in first pick of NHL draft |url=https://www.rrstar.com/story/news/2007/06/23/hawks-grab-patrick-kane-in/46966603007/ |work=[[Rockford Register Star]] |access-date=July 7, 2007}}</ref> Kane later joined [[Denis Savard]], the Blackhawks' coach, in singing \"[[Take Me Out to the Ball Game]]\".<ref name=\"cubs\"/> Kane also threw the first pitch at a [[Buffalo Bisons]] (AAA) game in August. Kane chose to wear the No. 88 jersey as a reference to his birthyear, a tradition he practiced with his former teammates on the London Knights.<ref>{{cite news |last=Powers |first=Scott |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1241734/2020/03/02/why-the-blackhawks-wear-their-jersey-numbers-2019-20-season-edition/ |title=Why the Blackhawks wear their jersey numbers, 2019-20 season edition |work=[[The Athletic]] |date=March 2, 2020 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20230601022739/https://theathletic.com/1241734/2020/03/02/why-the-blackhawks-wear-their-jersey-numbers-2019-20-season-edition/ |archive-date=June 1, 2023 |url-status=live |access-date=June 1, 2023}}</ref>\n\n[[File:Kane Goal (2241044000).jpg|thumb|left|Kane with a [[breakaway (ice hockey)|breakaway]] during his inaugural NHL season, February 2008]]\nKane made his NHL debut on October 4, 2007, against the [[Minnesota Wild]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Backstrom makes 27 saves as Wild blank Blackhawks |url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/recap/_/gameId/271004030 |website=ESPN |access-date=February 25, 2023 |date=October 4, 2007 |archive-date=February 25, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230225181443/https://www.espn.com/nhl/recap/_/gameId/271004030 |url-status=dead}}</ref> He recorded his first assist and first shootout goal (a game-winner) two days later against [[Dominik Hašek]] of the [[Detroit Red Wings]]. He scored his first NHL goal on October 19, beating [[José Théodore]] of the [[Colorado Avalanche]]. With a quick start to his rookie campaign, on November 2, Kane was named the NHL Rookie of the Month for October after scoring 5 goals and 11 assists in 12 games. On December 15, Kane and the Blackhawks visited the Buffalo Sabres to mark Kane's first return to Buffalo as a professional hockey player. Kane received a special cheer from his hometown and a special ceremony was held before the game. The Blackhawks lost the game three–1, with Kane scoring their lone goal.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.cbssports.com/nhl/gametracker/recap/NHL_20071215_CHI@BUF |title=Sabres 3, Blackhawks 1 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=December 15, 2007 |access-date=October 15, 2015 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121103214252/https://www.cbssports.com/nhl/gametracker/recap/NHL_20071215_CHI@BUF/ |archive-date=November 3, 2012}}</ref> Kane finished his first NHL campaign atop the rookie scoring race with 72 points. On June 12, 2008, he received the [[Calder Memorial Trophy]], awarded to the NHL's rookie of the year, finishing ahead of teammate [[Jonathan Toews]] and [[Washington Capitals]] forward [[Nicklas Bäckström]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Blackhawks' Kane wins Calder as NHL's top rookie |url=https://www.tsn.ca/nhl/story/?id=240520 |website=[[The Sports Network|TSN]] |access-date=February 25, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080615195209/https://www.tsn.ca/nhl/story/?id=240520 |archive-date=June 15, 2008 |date=June 12, 2008}}</ref>\n\n[[File:Patrick Kane 2009.jpg|thumb|upright|Kane warming up with the [[Chicago Blackhawks]] in November 2009]]\nThe following season, Kane and Toews helped lead a rejuvenated Blackhawks team back to the [[Stanley Cup playoffs]]. After recording 70 points in the regular season and eliminating the fifth-seeded [[Calgary Flames]] in the opening round of the [[2009 Stanley Cup playoffs|2009 playoffs]], Kane scored his first career [[hat-trick]] in game six of the second round against the third-seeded [[Vancouver Canucks]] on May 11, 2009. The Blackhawks won the game seven–5 for a 4–2 victory in the series, clinching their spot in the [[Western Conference (NHL)|Western Conference]] Finals for the first time since 1995.<ref name=\"htrick\">{{cite news|first=Len |last=Ziehm |title=Trick, treat: Patrick Kane keys Hawks' win |date=May 12, 2009 |newspaper=[[Chicago Sun-Times]] ''[[Chicago Sun-Times]]'' that he was \"fired up\" after Canucks defenseman [[Willie Mitchell (ice hockey)|Willie Mitchell]] claimed that Kane \"couldn't play five-on-five\".<ref name=\"htrick\"/> He finished his first NHL playoffs with nine goals, five assists for 14 points in 16 out of 17 games as the Blackhawks were eliminated in the Western Conference Finals by the defending Stanley Cup champion and second-seeded Detroit Red Wings.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.hockey-reference.com/players/k/kanepa01/gamelog/2009#1-16-sum:gamelog_playoffs |title=Patrick Kane Gamelogs for Playoff They advanced to the [[2010 Stanley Cup Final]]. On June 9, 2010, in game six of the Finals, Kane scored the overtime winner when he shot the puck under the pads of [[Philadelphia Flyers]] goaltender [[Michael Leighton]] and into the net, winning the Blackhawks the [[Stanley Cup]]. The goal ended a 49-year Stanley Cup drought for the Blackhawks.<ref>{{cite news |last=Kuc |first=Chris |date=June 9, 2016 |title=June 9, 2010: Blackhawks beat Flyers to win Stanley Cup Kane was named a finalist for the [[Lady Byng Memorial Trophy]] as the \"player adjudged to have exhibited the best type of sportsmanship and gentlemanly conduct combined with a high standard of playing ability.\" The award would eventually go to Lightning' winger Martin St. Louis and Kane finishing second in the trophy voting. Kane scored his second career playoff hat-trick in the [[2013 Stanley Cup playoffs|2013 playoffs]] against the defending Stanley Cup champion and fifth-seeded [[Los Angeles Kings]], including the series-clinching goal in double overtime of game five of the Western Conference Finals on June 8, 2013. The Blackhawks advanced to the [[2013 Stanley Cup Final]] against the fourth-seeded [[Boston Bruins]]. Kane contributed by scoring three goals, one in game four and two in game five, to win the 2013 [[Conn Smythe Trophy]] as the Stanley Cup Playoffs MVP. In addition, Kane was the first winger since [[Claude Lemieux]] in {{scfy|1995}}, and the first [[List of first overall NHL draft picks|number one overall draft pick]] since [[Mario Lemieux]] in {{scfy|1992}}, to win the Conn Smythe Trophy.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nhl.com/gamecenter/stl-vs-chi/2014/03/19/2013021039|title=St. Louis Blues at Chicago Blackhawks – 03/19/2014|work=NHL.com |publisher=National Hockey League |access-date=July 23, 2015|archive-date=July 22, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150722014639/http://blackhawks.nhl.com/gamecenter/en/recap?id=2013021039|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=675063|title= Chicago's Patrick Kane wins Conn Smythe Trophy as Stanley Cup playoff MVP|date= June 24, 2013 |work= NHL.com |publisher=National Hockey League |agency=The Canadian Press |access-date= June 25, 2013|archive-date= December 7, 2013|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20131207050434/http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=675063|url-status= dead}}</ref>\n\nOn March 19, 2014, Kane injured his left leg following a collision with [[Brenden Morrow]] in a game against the St. Louis Blues. He missed the remainder of the regular season but returned for the [[2014 Stanley Cup playoffs|2014 playoffs]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Hedger|first=Brian|url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=710355|title=Blackhawks forward Kane injured, out three weeks|work=NHL.com|publisher=National Hockey League|date=March 19, 2014|access-date=March 30, 2014|archive-date=March 24, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140324173206/http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=710355|url-status=dead}}</ref> During the playoffs, he recorded a team-high 20 points in all 19 games with 8 goals and 12 assists. As part of that run, on May 2, in game one of Blackhawks' Western Conference Semifinals against the Minnesota Wild, Kane scored two goals, including the game-winning goal while coining his nickname \"Showtime\".<ref name=\":0\">{{cite news|last=Fogel|first=Anna|url=http://nesn.com/2014/05/patrick-kane-yells-showtime-after-tallying-unreal-game-winning-backhand-goal-video|title=Patrick Kane Yells 'Showtime' After Tallying Unreal Game-Winning Backhand Goal (Video)|work=NESN|date=May 3, 2014|access-date=June 17, 2015|archive-date=June 18, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150618235630/http://nesn.com/2014/05/patrick-kane-yells-showtime-after-tallying-unreal-game-winning-backhand-goal-video/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Hd-yP9odBp8 |title=Patrick Kane dazzles with awesome backhand goal |date=May 2, 2014 |access-date=July 24, 2026 |via=[[YouTube]] |work=[[National Hockey League]]}}</ref> On July 9, 2014, the Blackhawks announced that Kane and Jonathan Toews had both signed eight-year contract extensions, set to start running on July 1, 2015, with an annual average value of $10.5&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite web|title=Toews, Kane sign eight-year deals with Blackhawks|url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=725803|website=NHL.com |publisher=National Hockey League |access-date=July 12, 2014|archive-date=July 13, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140713015603/http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=725803|url-status=dead}}</ref>\n\n[[File:Kane-richards-2015rally (cropped).jpg|left|thumb|upright|Kane (88) during the Blackhawks' [[2015 Stanley Cup Final|2015 victory]] rally at [[Soldier Field]] with [[Brad Richards]] and [[Daniel Carcillo]]]]\nDuring the [[2014–15 NHL season|2014–15 season]], Kane emerged as one of the NHL's leading scorers. On January 20, 2015, in a 6–1 victory over the Arizona Coyotes, Kane scored his 200th NHL goal on Coyotes' goaltender [[Mike Smith (ice hockey, born 1982)|Mike Smith]]. Later the same month, he was elected to the [[2015 National Hockey League All-Star Game|2015 NHL All-Star Game]] in [[Columbus, Ohio]]. He scored 64 points (27 goals and 37 assists) through the regular season. He injured his left [[clavicle]] on February 24, after he was cross-checked into the boards while stumbling towards the ice by [[Alex Petrovic]] in a game against the [[Florida Panthers]]. Kane underwent surgery and was expected to miss 12 weeks. At the time of his injury, he was leading the NHL in points.<ref>{{cite news|last=Powers|first=Scott|url=https://www.espn.com/chicago/nhl/story/_/id/12383194/patrick-kane-chicago-blackhawks-undergoes-surgery-expected-12-weeks|title=Patrick Kane of Chicago Blackhawks undergoes surgery, expected out 12 weeks|work=ESPN|date=February 25, 2015|access-date=March 2, 2015|archive-date=March 1, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150301093029/http://espn.go.com/chicago/nhl/story/_/id/12383194/patrick-kane-chicago-blackhawks-undergoes-surgery-expected-12-weeks?|url-status=live}}</ref> However, he recovered weeks earlier than initially projected and returned to the Blackhawks at the start of the [[2015 Stanley Cup playoffs|2015 playoffs]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Hine|first=Chris|url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/hockey/blackhawks/chi-patrick-kane-game-1-return-20150414-story.html|title=Blackhawks' Patrick Kane to return for game one vs. Predators|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|date=April 14, 2015|access-date=June 16, 2015|archive-date=April 17, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150417183113/http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/hockey/blackhawks/chi-patrick-kane-game-1-return-20150414-story.html|url-status=live}}</ref> After initially playing on the second line with [[Bryan Bickell]] and [[Brad Richards]], Chicago head coach [[Joel Quenneville]] moved Kane to the Blackhawks' top line alongside Jonathan Toews and [[Brandon Saad]] after the [[Anaheim Ducks]] took a 3–2 game lead in the Western Conference Finals going into game six.<ref name=\"ducks1\">{{cite news|last=Cooper|first=Josh|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/nhl-puck-daddy/jonathan-toews-and-patrick-kane-on-same-line-help-hawks-fly-050122934.html|title=Jonathan Toews, Patrick Kane line makes Joel Quenneville look like a genius|work=[[Yahoo! Sports]]|date=May 31, 2015|access-date=June 16, 2015|archive-date=March 5, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305160904/http://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/nhl-puck-daddy/jonathan-toews-and-patrick-kane-on-same-line-help-hawks-fly-050122934.html|url-status=live}}</ref> The trio combined for nine points over the final two games against the top-seeded Ducks and propelled the Blackhawks to the [[2015 Stanley Cup Final|Stanley Cup Final]].<ref name=\"ducks1\"/> Kane helped the Blackhawks defeat the Tampa Bay Lightning by assisting on Duncan Keith's game-winning goal in game six and scoring an insurance goal on Lightning goaltender [[Ben Bishop]] with the help of linemates Brad Richards and Brandon Saad for his third Stanley Cup championship in six years.<ref>{{cite news|last=Belson|first=Ken|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2015/06/16/sports/hockey/chicago-blackhawks-win-stanley-cup.html|title=With Blackhawks' 3 Stanley Cups in 6 Years, Chicago Runneth playoff games and finished the playoffs with 11 goals and 12 assists, tying the Lightning's [[Tyler Johnson (ice hockey)|Tyler Johnson]] with a playoff-high 23 points.<ref>{{cite In doing so, Kane became the fourth player in Blackhawks franchise history to reach that mark with the club, along with Stan Mikita, [[Bobby Hull]] and Denis Savard.<ref>{{cite web |title=Patrick Kane gets 1,000th career point in Blackhawks' win over Jets |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/hockey/nhl/patrick-kane-gets-1000th-career-point-blackhawks-win-jets/ |website=Sportsnet |access-date=January 20, 2020 |date=January 19, 2020 |archive-date=May 13, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210513075741/https://www.sportsnet.ca/hockey/nhl/patrick-kane-gets-1000th-career-point-blackhawks-win-jets/ |url-status=live}}</ref> During the [[2019–20 Chicago Blackhawks season|2019–20 season]], the Blackhawks appointed Kane as an [[Captain (ice hockey)#Alternate captains|alternate captain]] after [[Brent Seabrook]] missed the remainder of the season due to multiple surgeries.<ref>{{cite news |last=Kuc |first=Chris |title=Feature: Patrick Kane Leading by Example |via=NHL.com |publisher=Chicago Blackhawks |date=April 21, 2020 |url=https://www.nhl.com/blackhawks/news/feature-patrick-kane-leading-by-example-316677722 |access-date=March 1, 2021 |archive-date=April 27, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200427172302/https://www.nhl.com/blackhawks/news/feature-patrick-kane-leading-by-example/c-316677722 |url-status=live}}</ref>\n\nKane retained his role as an alternate captain going into [[2020–21 NHL season|2020–21 season]], which shortened to a 56-game schedule due to the ongoing [[COVID-19 pandemic in North America|COVID-19 pandemic]]. He ended the season with 15 goals and tallied 51 assists for a team-high 66 points in all 56 games played.<ref name=\"2020stats\">{{cite news |last=Pope |first=Ben |url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2021/5/15/22426670/blackhawks-player-evaluations-2021-season-patrick-kane-alex-debrincat-connor-murphy |title=Blackhawks 2021 player evaluations: Who met expectations? Who fell short? |work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]] |date=May 15, 2021 |access-date=May 15, 2021 |archive-date=November 2, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211102140832/https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2021/5/15/22426670/blackhawks-player-evaluations-2021-season-patrick-kane-alex-debrincat-connor-murphy |url-status=live}}</ref> He finished with the fifth-most points among all skaters in the NHL for the season.<ref name=\"2020stats\" /> On February 28, 2021, Kane recorded his 400th career goal against the Detroit Red Wings on Wings' goaltender [[Thomas Greiss]], becoming the 100th player in NHL history to reach 400 career goals.<ref>{{cite web|title=Patrick Kane the 100th NHL player to 400 goals|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/patrick-kane-100th-nhl-player-050007537.html|access-date=March 1, 2021|website=[[Yahoo! |url-status=live}}</ref> After the season's conclusion, Kane was named the Best NHL Player at the [[2021 ESPY Awards]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/espys/story/_/page/voting-winners/2021-espys-award-winners |title=2021 ESPYS award winners |work=ESPN |date=July 10, 2021 |access-date=July 11, 2021 |archive-date=July 12, the Blackhawks during the [[2021–22 NHL season|2021–22 season]] where he recorded 26 goals, 66 assists and 92 points, tying his career high in assists from three years prior in the 2018–19 season, despite playing the entire season with a persistent undisclosed injury.<ref name=\"2021-22\">{{cite news |last=Pope |first=Ben |url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2022/4/26/23042997/blackhawks-patrick-kane-nagging-injury-health-production-rebuild-alex-debrincat-kyle-davidson |title=Blackhawks' Patrick Kane proud of Rangers (2023)====\n[[File:PatrickKane.jpg|thumb|right|175px|Kane skating with the Rangers in March 2023]]\nThe Blackhawks and Kane parted ways at the trade deadline, with the team opting to acquire future draft capital and initiate a full-scale rebuild.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Stephens |first1=Mike |title=Jonathan Toews to play final game for Chicago Blackhawks in season finale second-round pick in the [[2023 NHL entry draft]], a fourth-round pick, and defenseman [[Andy Welinski]]. To help facilitate the trade, the Rangers sent the Arizona Coyotes a fifth-round selection in the [[2025 NHL entry draft|2025 draft]].<ref>{{cite news five assists in the postseason, as the Rangers lost to the New Jersey Devils in seven games.<ref>{{cite news |last=Roumeliotis |first=Charlie play==\n{{MedalTableTop|name=no |USA vs Norway - Kane (cropped1).jpg|150px|Kane at the [[Ice hockey at the 2010 Winter Olympics – Men's tournament|2010 Winter Olympics]]}}\n{{MedalSport|Men's [[ice hockey]]}}\n{{MedalCountry|the {{ih|USA}}}}\n{{MedalCompetition|[[Ice hockey at the Olympic Games|Winter Olympics]]}}\n{{MedalSilver|[[Ice hockey at the 2010 Winter Olympics – Men's tournament|2010 Vancouver]]|}}\n{{MedalCompetition|[[IIHF World Championships|World Championships]]}}\n{{Medal|Bronze|[[2018 Men's World Ice Hockey Championships|2018 Denmark]]|}}\n{{MedalCompetition|[[World Junior Ice Hockey Championships|World Junior Championships]]|}}\n{{MedalBronze|[[2007 World Junior Ice Hockey Championships|2007 Sweden]]|}}\n{{MedalCompetition|[[IIHF World U18 Championships|World U18 Championships]]}}\n{{MedalGold|[[2006 IIHF World U18 Championships|2006 Sweden]]|}}\n{{MedalBottom}}\nKane has competed internationally for the [[United States men's national ice hockey team|United States]]. He first represented the United States in the [[2006 IIHF World U18 Championships|2006 IIHF U18 Championships]], in which he led the tournament in scoring with 12 points (five goals and seven assists) in only six games played. His two points per game pace led the United States to the gold medal and earned him individual all-star team honors.<ref name=\"OHL-ROY\"/>\n\n[[File:Men's Gold Medal- Canada vs. USA (4399271553).jpg|thumb|left|Kane, alongside [[Erik Johnson]], celebrates a goal by [[Ryan Kesler]] during the [[2010 Winter Olympics]].]]\nThe next year, he moved onto the United States' U20 team at the [[2007 World Junior Ice Hockey Championships|2007 World Juniors]]. He was one of only three players on the team playing [[major junior hockey]]. He continued his international pace with five goals and four assists in seven games to finish second in tournament scoring and, once again, garner an all-star team selection. His team did not perform as well as his U18 team, but they did manage to go home with the bronze medal. After making the [[National Hockey League|NHL]] and being unable to play in the 2008 WJC due to professional commitments with the Chicago Blackhawks, he played in the [[2008 Men's World Ice Hockey Championships|2008 World Championships]]. He posted 10 points (three goals and seven assists) in seven games<ref>{{cite web |url=https://teamusa.usahockey.com/page/show/2671494-2008-statistics |title=2008 Statistics |publisher=USA Hockey |access-date=October 7, 2022 |archive-date=August 19, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230819030909/https://teamusa.usahockey.com/page/show/2671494-2008-statistics |url-status=live}}</ref> as the United States finished sixth.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://teamusa.usahockey.com/page/show/2668976-2008-iihf-men-s-world-championship |title=2008 IIHF Men's World Championship |publisher=USA Hockey |access-date=October 7, 2022 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180210103335/https://teamusa.usahockey.com/page/show/2668976-2008-iihf-men-s-world-championship |archive-date=February 10, 2018}}</ref>\n\nKane was selected to represent the United States in the [[Ice hockey at the 2010 Winter Olympics|2010 Olympic Games]] in [[Vancouver]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/olympics/olyhockey/news/story?id=4790711 |title=Breaking down 2010 U.S. team |last1=Burnside |first1=Scott |last2=LeBrun |first2=Pierre |date=January 2, 2010 |website=ESPN |access-date=October 7, 2022 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210125152906/https://www.espn.com/olympics/olyhockey/news/story?id=4790711 |archive-date=January 25, 2021}}</ref> where he and the team won the silver medal. During the tournament he scored three goals and two assists in six games.<ref>{{cite news |last=Klein |first=Jeff Z. |date=February 28, 2010 |title=Crosby's Goal Ends Thriller as Canada Beats U.S. |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2010/03/01/sports/olympics/01hockey.html |work=The New York Times |access-date=October 7, 2022 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221006183313/https://www.nytimes.com/2010/03/01/sports/olympics/01hockey.html |archive-date=October 6, 2022}}</ref> Kane represented the United States again in the [[Ice Hockey at the 2014 Winter Olympics|2014 Olympic Games]] in [[Sochi]]. He missed two penalty shots in a loss against Finland in the bronze medal game.<ref>{{cite news |last=Allen |first=Kevin |date=February 22, 2014 |title=Finland rout sends USA home without hockey medal |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/olympics/sochi/2014/02/22/usa-finland-bronze-medal-olympic-hockey-game/5725465/ |work=[[USA Today]] |access-date=October 7, 2022 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220123152755/https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/olympics/sochi/2014/02/22/usa-finland-bronze-medal-olympic-hockey-game/5725465/ |archive-date=January 23, 2022}}</ref>\n\nOn April 9, 2018, Kane was named the captain of Team USA for the [[2018 IIHF World Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Patrick Kane To Serve As Captain Of 2018 U.S. Men's National Hockey Team|url=https://www.teamusa.org/News/2018/April/09/Patrick-Kane-To-Serve-As-Captain-Of-2018-US-Mens-National-Hockey-Team|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180502140311/https://www.teamusa.org/News/2018/April/09/Patrick-Kane-To-Serve-As-Captain-Of-2018-US-Mens-National-Hockey-Team|url-status=dead|archive-date=May 2, 2018|publisher=USA Hockey |access-date=May 2, 2018|date=April 9, 2018}}</ref> Kane scored two goals including a game winner in a 3–2 victory against the Czech Republic in the quarterfinals. The U.S. team finished the competition with the bronze medal after losing to Sweden in the semifinals but beating Canada. Kane finished the championships as the tournament's leading scorer with eight goals and 12 assists in 10 games. He was named the Most Valuable Player of 2018 Men's World Championship.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://teamusa.usahockey.com/news_article/show/919745?referrer_id=695820 |title=Patrick Kane Named Most Valuable Player of 2018 MWC |publisher=USA Hockey |date=May 20, 2018 |access-date=May 20, 2018 |archive-date=May 21, 2018 Kane, were arrested in Buffalo. According to a police report, Kane was apprehended around 5:00&nbsp;a.m. after allegedly punching cab driver Jan Radecki when he claimed to not have proper change for their trip fare. Kane and his cousin's cab fare came out to be $14.80, and they gave him $15.00.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://thehockeynews.com/news/news/lawyer-says-blackhawks-star-patrick-kanes-charges-overblown |title=Lawyer says Blackhawks star Patrick Kane's charges overblown |agency=The Canadian Press |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090814202834/http://thehockeynews.com/articles/27479-Lawyer-says-Blackhawks-star-Patrick-Kanes-charges-overblown.html |work=The Hockey News |archive-date=August 14, 2009 |date=August 10, 2009 |access-date=September 23, 2015}}</ref>\n\nKane was charged with second-degree robbery, fourth-degree criminal mischief, and theft of services. He pleaded not guilty. On August 17, Kane apologized for the distress he caused, saying he had been \"at the wrong place at the wrong time,\" and mentioned his family, the Chicago Blackhawks organization, and their fan base—but not Radecki.<ref name=\"NHL.com 2009-08-18\">{{cite news|title=Patrick Kane Press Conference|date=August 18, 2009|url=http://www.nhl.tv/team/console.jsp?catid=618&id=45537|access-date=August 18, 2009|archive-date=August 20, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090820215904/http://www.nhl.tv/team/console.jsp?catid=618&id=45537|url-status=dead |publisher=National Hockey League}}</ref> Kane and his cousin appeared before a [[grand jury]] on August 19.<ref name=\"grandjury\">{{cite news|first=Scott|last=Burnside|title=Hawks' Kane indicted on misdemeanors|date=August 19, 2009|work=ESPN|url=https://www.espn.com/chicago/news/story?id=4409633|agency=Associated Press|access-date=August 22, 2009|archive-date=June 5, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140605081946/http://sports.espn.go.com/chicago/news/story?id=4409633|url-status=live}}</ref> Although cleared of any felony charges, the two were still indicted on less severe misdemeanor assault, theft, and harassment charges.<ref name=\"grandjury\"/> Kane and his cousin reiterated their not guilty pleas when appearing in court the next day. On August 27, Kane and cousin pleaded guilty to noncriminal disorderly conduct charges, and were both given conditional discharges, avoiding any penalties if they stayed out of trouble for a year, and also ordered to apologize to Radecki.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.buffalonews.com/Kane_plea_deal_brings_conditional_discharge.html |title=Kane plea deal brings conditional discharge to trial |first1=Gene |last1=Warner |first2=Matt |last2=Gryta |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150925100728/http://www.buffalonews.com/Kane_plea_deal_brings_conditional_discharge.html |archive-date=September 25, 2015 |work=The Buffalo News |date=August 28, 2009 |access-date=September 23, 2015 |url-status=dead}}</ref>\n\n===2015 police investigation===\nOn August 6, 2015, ''[[The
