players]]"}}}]},{"pageid":10804874,"ns":0,"title":"Steven Stamkos","revisions":[{"slots":{"main":{"contentmodel":"wikitext","contentformat":"text/x-wiki","content":"{{Short description|Canadian ice hockey player (born 1990)}}\n{{Use Canadian English|date=January 2024}}\n{{Use mdy dates|date=July 2024}}\n{{Infobox ice hockey player\n| name = Steven Stamkos\n| image = Steve Stamkos - Tampa Bay Lightning.jpg\n| caption = Stamkos with the [[Tampa Bay Lightning]] in February 2013\n| birth_date = {{birth date and age|1990|2|7}}\n| birth_place = [[Markham, Ontario]], Canada\n| height_ft = 6\n| height_in = 1\n| weight_lb = 193\n| position = [[Forward (ice hockey)|Forward]]\n| shoots = Right\n| league = [[National Hockey League|NHL]]\n| team = [[Nashville Predators]]\n| former_teams = [[Tampa Bay Lightning]]\n| ntl_team = Canada\n| draft = 1st overall\n| draft_year = 2008\n| draft_team = [[Tampa Bay Lightning]]\n| career_start = 2008\n| career_end = \n}}\n'''Steven Stamkos''' (born February 7, 1990) is a Canadian professional [[ice hockey]] player who is a [[Forward (ice hockey)|forward]] and [[Captain (ice hockey)#Alternate captains|alternate captain]] for the [[Nashville Predators]] of the [[National Hockey League]] (NHL). Stamkos was selected [[List of first overall NHL draft picks|first overall]] in the [[2008 NHL entry draft]] by the [[Tampa Bay Lightning]]. Stamkos \nholds the Lightning franchise record for most goals and points scored and captained the Lightning to back-to-back [[Stanley Cup]] championships in [[2020 Stanley Cup Final|2020]] and [[2021 Stanley Cup Final|2021]] as well as appearances in the Stanley Cup Final in [[2015 Stanley Cup Final|2015]] and [[2022 Stanley Cup Final|2022]].\n\nHe is a two-time [[Maurice \"Rocket\" Richard Trophy]] winner as the NHL's leading goal-scorer ([[2009–10 NHL season|2010]] and [[2011–12 NHL season|2012]]), while also the runner-up three other times (in [[2010–11 NHL season|2011]], [[2012–13 NHL season|2013]] and [[2014–15 NHL season|2015]]), a [[Mark Messier Leadership Award]] winner ([[2022–23 NHL season|2023]]), a two-time [[NHL All-Star team|NHL second team All-Star]] (2011, 2012), and has been named to seven [[NHL All-Star Game]]s. Nicknamed \"'''Stammer'''\", he has scored the most goals and the most points of any player born in the 1990s. He was also a [[Hart Memorial Trophy]] finalist in 2012 as the most valuable player to his team as voted by the [[Professional Hockey Writers' Association]], a two-time [[Ted Lindsay Award]] finalist (2011 and 2012) as the best player judged by the [[National Hockey League Players' Association]]. In addition, he was the runner-up for the [[Art Ross Trophy]] as the leading point-scorer two consecutive times (2012 and 2013).\n\n==Early life==\nStamkos is of [[Macedonians (ethnic group)|Macedonian]]<ref name=\"thestar\">{{cite news|url=https://www.thestar.com/article/289569|title=Steven Stamkos: Hockey player|date=December 30, 2009 | work=The Star | location=Toronto | first=Sunaya | last=Sapurji | access-date=May 24, 2010}}</ref> and [[Scottish people|Scottish]] descent.<ref name=\"hockeyplayer\">The Hockey News Magazine&nbsp;– Draft Preview 08 Special Issue&nbsp;– Article \"Believe in Steven\" page 8</ref> He grew up in [[Unionville, Ontario|Unionville]], [[Ontario]], and played for the Markham Waxers in the [[Eastern AAA Hockey League]] of the [[Ontario Minor Hockey Association]] (OMHA). During one of his seasons with the North York Canadiens, he was teammates with NHLer [[P. K. Subban]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Zeisberger |first1=Mike |title=Stamkos, Subban bring childhood bond to All-Star Game |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/steven-stamkos-p-k-subban-share-childhood-bond-295341992 |website=NHL.com |access-date=January 23, 2024 |date=January 26, 2018}}</ref> Stamkos won eight OMHA titles in a row in minor hockey and led his Waxers club to the OHL Cup title in March 2006.{{citation needed|date=February 2019}} He played in the 2003 [[Quebec International Pee-Wee Hockey Tournament]] with the Markham Waxers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.publicationsports.com/ressources/files/439/Joueurs_Pro.pdf|title=Pee-Wee players who have reached NHL or WHA|year=2018|website=Quebec International Pee-Wee Hockey Tournament|access-date=February 16, 2019|archive-date=March 6, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190306085544/https://www.publicationsports.com/ressources/files/439/Joueurs_Pro.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>\n\nStamkos attended [[Central Park Public School]] and [[St. Brother André Catholic High School]] in [[Markham, Ontario|Markham]], Ontario.{{citation needed|date=February 2019}} After being drafted by the OHL's [[Sarnia Sting]], he attended [[Northern Collegiate Institute and Vocational School]] in [[Sarnia]].{{citation needed|date=February 2019}}\n\n==Playing career==\n\n===Junior===\nFollowing a season with the [[minor ice hockey|minor]] Waxers in which he scored 197 points over 66 games, Stamkos was selected [[Jack Ferguson Award|first overall]] in the 2006 OHL Draft by the Sarnia Sting. Stamkos played with other notable current and former NHLers in his minor and junior hockey career, including [[Logan Couture]], [[John Tavares]], [[Michael Del Zotto]], [[Cameron Gaunce]], [[Cody Hodgson]], and [[P. K. Subban]] during his minor hockey career in the [[Greater Toronto Area]].{{Citation needed|date=April 2012}} Joining the Sting in [[2006–07 OHL season|2006–07]], he recorded 92 points (42 goals and 50 assists) over 63 games as a junior rookie. He was named to the OHL Second All-Rookie Team, ranking behind [[Sam Gagner]] at the center position.<ref>{{cite web|title=OHL First All-Rookie Team|url=http://www.eliteprospects.com/awards.php?award=OHL |access-date=January 3, 2012|publisher=EliteProspects.com}}</ref> Stamkos also won the [[Bobby Smith Trophy]] as the OHL's scholastic player of the year for his academic efforts off the ice.\n\nThe following season, Stamkos improved to 58 goals and 105 points over 61 games. He was named to the OHL second All-Star team, but was later selected to the [[Canadian Hockey League|CHL]] first All-Star team, which encompasses all three national major junior leagues. Playing in his NHL [[NHL Entry Draft|draft-eligible]] season in 2007–08, Stamkos was top-ranked throughout the campaign by the [[NHL Central Scouting Bureau]] and International Scouting Services. He also won the CHL's Top Draft Prospect Award.\n\n===Professional (2008–present)===\n====Tampa Bay Lightning (2008–2024)====\n{{Very long section|date=October 2026}}\nAs the [[2008 NHL entry draft]] approached, Stamkos was largely seen as the best available center. His primary competition for the top overall pick was top prospect defencemen [[Drew Doughty]] and [[Zach Bogosian]], as well as Russian winger [[Nikita Filatov]]. The [[Tampa Bay Lightning]], by virtue of their [[2007–08 NHL season|previous season]] in which they won an NHL-worst 31 games, owned the first pick.<ref>{{cite web |title=Lightning take Stamkos with top selection in 2008 NHL draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/news/story?id=3454622 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=January 23, 2024 |date=June 20, 2008}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Joyce |first1=Gare |title=Yes, Stamkos can score, but his smarts are winning scouts over |url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/news/story?id=3334070 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=January 23, 2024 |date=April 7, 2008}}</ref> As expected, Stamkos was selected first overall by Tampa Bay. On July 29, 2008, he signed a three-year, entry-level contract with the Lightning in which he could earn as much as $8.55&nbsp;million in performance bonuses.<ref>{{cite news | url = https://www.tsn.ca/nhl/story/?id=244724 | title = Lightning officially sign Stamkos to three-year contract | publisher = TSN | date = July 29, 2008 | access-date = July 29, 2008}}</ref> Leading up to the start of the upcoming [[2008–09 NHL season|2008–09 season]], the Lightning centered their promotional efforts around Stamkos, including a website with the slogan \"Seen Stamkos?\"\n[[File:Steven Stamkos.JPG|thumb|left|Stamkos with the Lightning in March 2009. The [[2008–09 NHL season|2008–09 season]] was his rookie season in the NHL.]]\nStamkos played in his first NHL game on October 4, 2008, in [[Prague]], Czech Republic, the first game of the 2008–09 season. The Lightning fell to the [[New York Rangers]] 2–1 and were eventually swept in Prague. He recorded his first point – a secondary assist – in his eighth game, on a goal scored by [[Vincent Lecavalier]] which was against his hometown team, the [[Toronto Maple Leafs]].<ref>{{cite news | url = http://www.nhl.com/ice/boxscore.htm?id=2008020128 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110628182943/http://www.nhl.com/ice/boxscore.htm?id=2008020128 | url-status = dead | archive-date = June 28, 2011 | title = Game Boxscore: Tampa Bay @ Toronto | publisher = NHL.com | date = October 28, 2008 | access-date = October 28, 2008}}</ref> Following the game, Stamkos commented that his hometown support was \"louder than when the Leafs scored\".<ref>{{cite news | url = https://www.nhl.com/gamecenter/tbl-vs-tor/2008/10/28/2008020128 | title = Recap: Tampa Bay @ Toronto | publisher = NHL.com | date = October 28, 2008 | access-date = October 28, 2008}}</ref> He scored his first goal the next game against [[Ryan Miller]] of the [[Buffalo Sabres]]. After 54 games, Stamkos recorded the first NHL hat-trick of his career, on February 17, 2009. The Lightning held a 3–1 lead midway through the second period on the strength of Stamkos' natural hat-trick, but were still beaten by the visiting [[Chicago Blackhawks]], 5–3. The three goals enabled Stamkos to become the first rookie in Lightning history to score three goals in a game. He also became the second-youngest player in NHL history to record a natural hat-trick; current record-holder [[Bobby Carpenter (ice hockey)|Bobby Carpenter]] was 18 when he scored three on February 25, 1982.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=410245|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090227161623/http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=410245|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 27, 2009|title = Stamkos glad his first hat trick happened at home}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://thehockeynews.com/news/news/thn-com-blog-stamkos-finally-finds-his-way |title=Stamkos finally finds his way - Archived copy |access-date=November 16, 2013 |archive-date=October 6, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006070252/http://www.thehockeynews.com/articles/24530-THNcom-Blog-Stamkos-finally-finds-his-way.html |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Cristodero |first1=Damian |title=Lightning wastes Steven Stamkos' first hat trick |url=https://www.tampabay.com/archive/2009/02/18/lightning-wastes-stamkos-first-hat-trick/ |website=Tampa Bay Times |access-date=January 23, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150604135723/http://www.tampabay.com/sports/hockey/lightning/tampa-bay-lightning-wastes-steven-stamkos-first-hat-trick-in-5-3-loss-to/976891 |archive-date=June 4, 2015 |date=February 17, 2009}}</ref> Though Stamkos was heavily criticized for his lack of production during the first half of the season, in which he was limited to less than ten minutes of ice time some games (largely due to a dispute amongst then-head coach [[Barry Melrose]] and upper \nmanagement, mainly co-owner [[Len Barrie]] on how to approach the development of Stamkos in the NHL),<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/news/story?id=3762151|title=Melrose, Lightning owner still feuding over firing|date=December 11, 2008}}</ref> he finished the season with 19 points in his final 20 games.<ref>{{cite news | url = https://thehockeynews.com/news/news/the-straight-edge-stamkos-set-to-take-nhl-by-storm-in-sophomore-season | title = The Straight Edge: Stamkos set to take NHL by storm in sophomore season | publisher = thehockeynews.com | date = May 15, 2009 | access-date = June 27, 2009}}</ref> In his rookie season, Stamkos totaled 23 goals, 23 assists and 46 points, as well as a −13 [[Plus–minus (sports)|plus-minus]] rating in 79 games.\n\nIn the 2009 off-season, Stamkos spent the summer training extensively with newly retired NHL player [[Gary Roberts (ice hockey)|Gary Roberts]], working on adding strength and endurance.<ref name=roberts>{{cite magazine|title=Chelios looks old, Steven Stamkos looks super, more notes|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2010/writers/allan_muir/03/12/head.shots.notes/1.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100323034157/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2010/writers/allan_muir/03/12/head.shots.notes/1.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 23, 2010|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|author=Muir, Allan|date=March 12, 2010|access-date=March 28, 2010}}</ref> Roberts got to know Stamkos as a teammate on the Lightning in the 2008–09 season, his last season in the NHL. He oversaw Stamkos' off-season workouts north of [[Toronto]] in Roberts' in-house gym, which is a quick drive from Stamkos' family home in Unionville.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Cristodero |first1=Damian |title=Proving his worth |url=https://www.tampabay.com/archive/2009/10/31/proving-his-worth/ |website=Tampa Bay Times |access-date=January 23, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240123192628/https://www.tampabay.com/archive/2009/10/31/proving-his-worth/ |archive-date=January 23, 2024 |date=October 31, 2009}}</ref> Stamkos spoke highly regarding the workouts: \"It helped me a lot,\" Stamkos said. \"I learned a lot about what I needed to improve on. There are certain aspects of my game that have improved because of that, and I'll be there again this summer working hard. It definitely gave me that extra jump for this season.\"<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/nhl/blog/_/name/lebrun_pierre/id/4986879/pierre-lebrun-blog-look-scoring-steven-stamkos-join-elite-company-coming-days|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140115001513/http://espn.go.com/nhl/blog/_/name/lebrun_pierre/id/4986879/pierre-lebrun-blog-look-scoring-steven-stamkos-join-elite-company-coming-days|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 15, 2014|title = Look who's scoring! Stamkos could join elite company in coming days}}</ref> In the [[2009–10 NHL season|2009–10 season]], his second year in the NHL, Stamkos began to find his range as an NHL sharpshooter and had a breakout season. Playing the bulk of the season on the first line with [[Martin St. Louis]] and [[Steve Downie]], Stamkos started the campaign with 10 goals and five assists for 15 points in his first 11 games. Through mid-January, the entirety of February and mid-March, Stamkos had an 18-game point streak (17 goals and 16 assists for 33 points in all 18 games between January 19, 2010, in a 8–2 loss to the New York Rangers and March 11, in a 4–3 OT loss to his hometown team, the Toronto Maple Leafs). By the time he turned 20 in February 2010, he was in the top five in the NHL in scoring (with 32 goals and 29 assists for 61 points in every game up to that point in the season), challenging the likes of the generational talents of [[Washington Capitals]] forward and captain [[Alexander Ovechkin]] and [[Pittsburgh Penguins]] forward and captain [[Sidney Crosby]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/604628-why-the-tampa-bay-lightnings-steven-stamkos-is-the-nhls-next-big-thing |title=Why Steven Stamkos Will Be in the Same Category As Sidney Crosby & Alex Ovechkin |website=bleacherreport.com |publisher=Bleacher Report |author=Henry Dorgan |date=February 10, 2011 |access-date=January 25, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://archive.triblive.com/news/stamkos-likely-the-only-real-mvp-challenger-to-crosby-2/ |title=Stamkos likely the only real MVP challenger to Crosby |author=Josh Yohe |website=triblive.com |publisher=Trib Live |date=January 5, 2011 |access-date=August 22, 2024}}</ref> On April 10, the second-to-last day of the season, Stamkos reached the 50-goal mark for the season when he scored two goals against Tampa Bay's inner-state rival, the [[Florida Panthers]]. He also recorded an assist on a Martin St. Louis goal in the same game as the Lighting would go on to win the game 4–3 in a shootout. He ended the season with 51 goals, tied for most in the NHL with Sidney Crosby of the Pittsburgh Penguins; the two shared the [[Maurice \"Rocket\" Richard Trophy|Rocket Richard Trophy]] as the NHL's goal-scoring leaders; he tied Crosby in the final minute of the last game of the season with an empty-net goal. Stamkos became the third-youngest player to score 50 goals in a season, after [[Wayne Gretzky]] and [[Jimmy Carson]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://tsn.ca/nhl/story/?id=317517 |title=Stamkos becomes third-youngest to score 50 goals in win |access-date=April 11, 2010 |archive-date=July 6, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110706210053/http://tsn.ca/nhl/story/?id=317517 |url-status=dead}}</ref> His number of goals (51) was five more than his total points amount in the previous season (46). Additionally, Stamkos' 44 assists gave him 95 points within the season, good for fifth in the NHL behind [[Henrik Sedin]], Alexander Ovechkin, Sidney Crosby and [[Nicklas Bäckström]], respectively. Despite Stamkos’ rise to stardom individually, however, Tampa Bay as a team finished the year 12th in the East with 34 wins and 80 points, eight points out of a playoff spot. After the season, the team's poor record prompted new team owner [[Jeffrey Vinik]] to terminate [[Brian Lawton]] and [[Rick Tocchet]]'s contracts as general manager and head coach, respectively.\n[[File:Lecavalier and Stamkos (5738714232).jpg|thumb|Stamkos (right) with [[Vincent Lecavalier]] in May 2011 during the Eastern Conference Final of the [[2011 Stanley Cup playoffs]].]]\nStamkos began the [[2010–11 NHL season|2010–11 season]] with nine goals and 10 assists for 19 points in the first 10 games. This resulted in him being named the NHL’s first star of the month for the month of October.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nhl/news/octobers-three-stars-steve-stamkos-tim-thomas-and-chris-stewart |title=October's three stars: Steve Stamkos, Tim Thomas and Chris Stewart |website=nbcsports.com |publisher=NBC Sports |author=James O’ Brien |date=November 2, 2010 |access-date=October 5, 2025}}</ref> Following his high-scoring start to the season in which he scored 19 goals (along with 15 assists for 34 points) in his first 19 games, Stamkos began to attract media attention for challenging the elite \"[[50 goals in 50 games]]\" standard.<ref>{{cite news|title=Will Steven Stamkos be the NHL's next 50-in-50 player?|url=https://ca.sports.yahoo.com/nhl/blog/puck_daddy/post/Will-Steven-Stamkos-be-the-NHL-s-next-50-in-50-p?urn=nhl-287431|access-date=January 3, 2012|date=November 19, 2010|publisher=[[Yahoo!]]}}</ref> Wayne Gretzky, who scored 50 goals in a record 39 games in [[1981–82 NHL season|1981–82]], told reporters he thought Stamkos was surrounded by enough talent in Tampa Bay to achieve the feat.<ref>{{cite news|title=Dreger: Gretzky believes Stamkos can score 50 in 50|url=https://www.tsn.ca/nhl/story/?id=342586|access-date=January 3, 2012|date=November 23, 2010|publisher=[[The Sports Network]]}}</ref> Gretzky also followed up by saying on Stamkos' individual playing style by saying \"He's got tremendous speed and such a quick release. He understands the game and goes into the holes and gets into the right areas.\"<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/nhl/post/_/id/2060/gretzky-weighs-in-onstamkos-50-50-chances |title=Gretzky on Stamkos' 50 in 50 chances |website=[[ESPN]] |publisher=ESPN |author=Pierre Leburn |date=November 23, 2010 |access-date=January 6, 2024}}</ref> On December 20, 2010, Stamkos scored his 26th goal of the season and the 100th of his career, leading the Lightning past the [[Carolina Hurricanes]] 5–1. Stamkos had one of three Lightning goals late in the second period that put Tampa Bay ahead 5–1. The centre's milestone goal came in his 194th NHL game.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.foxnews.com/sports/stamkos-scores-100th-career-goal-in-lightning-win/ | work=Fox News | title=Stamkos scores 100th career goal in Lightning win | date=December 20, 2010}}</ref> Stamkos became the sixth player in history (joining Wayne Gretzky, [[Dale Hawerchuk]], [[Ilya Kovalchuk]], Jimmy Carson and [[Brian Bellows]]) to record his first 100 goals before turning the age of 21. In January 2011, Stamkos was named by the NHL to play in the [[2011 National Hockey League All-Star Game|NHL All-Star Game]] for the first time in his career. Stamkos was drafted second overall by Team [[Nicklas Lidström|Lidstrom]], joining teammate Martin St. Louis on the squad.<ref>{{cite news | url = http://www.nhl.com/ice/page.htm?id=66980 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110112110551/http://www.nhl.com/ice/page.htm?id=66980 | url-status = dead | archive-date = January 12, 2011 | title = 2011 NHL All-Star Weekend Rosters | publisher = nhl.com}}</ref> On February 8, 2011, Stamkos recorded his 100th career assist on a goal by Vincent Lecavalier in a 7–4 loss to the Buffalo Sabres.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sbnation.com/nhl/2011/2/8/1983181/sabres-vs-lightning-bergenheim-and-stafford-each-score-game-tied-at |title=Sabres Vs. Lightning: Bergenheim And Stafford Each Score; Game Tied At One |website=sbnation.com |publisher=SB Nation |author=Zachary Zielonka |date=February 8, 2011 |access-date=December 26, 2024}}</ref> As the season progressed it became apparent Stamkos would not achieve the 50-in-50 mark. By the 57th game, he had recorded an NHL-leading 40 goals as well as 34 assists for 74 points. Stamkos' latter portion of the season was markedly less successful; he recorded just five more goals and 12 assists for 17 points in the last 25 games.<ref>{{cite news|title=Last season's slump gives Stamkos much-needed perspective|url=http://tsn.ca/nhl/story/?id=384126|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120715125441/http://tsn.ca/nhl/story/?id=384126|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 15, 2012|access-date=January 3, 2012|date=January 3, 2012|publisher=[[The Sports Network]]}}</ref> Finishing the [[2010–11 Tampa Bay Lightning season|2010–11 season]] with 45 goals, he ranked second in NHL scoring, only behind [[Corey Perry]] of the [[Anaheim Ducks]]. He also recorded 46 assists for a new career high in assists and 91 points and maintained durability by having played in all 82 games for the second consecutive season. His 91 points placed him fifth in the NHL for the second consecutive season behind [[Daniel Sedin]], linemate Martin St. Louis, Corey Perry and Henrik Sedin, respectively. Stamkos was named a finalist for the [[Ted Lindsay Award]] as the most outstanding player in the regular season as judged by the members of the [[NHL Players' Association]] alongside Anaheim Ducks' forward Corey Perry and [[Vancouver Canucks]] forward Daniel Sedin, which was eventually won by Daniel Sedin.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/news/story?page=11awardsfinalsits |title=NHL awards: 2011 finalists |author=ESPN |website=[[ESPN]] |publisher=ESPN |date=April 22, 2011 |access-date=January 6, 2024}}{{dead link|date=July 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> As the Lightning ranked fifth in the [[Eastern Conference (NHL)|Eastern Conference]] and eighth in the NHL overall to qualify for the playoffs for the first time since [[2007 Stanley Cup playoffs|2007]], Stamkos made his [[Stanley Cup playoffs|Stanley Cup playoff]] debut on April 13, 2011, against the Pittsburgh Penguins. On April 23, he scored his first two career playoff goals, as well an assist on a Vincent Lecavalier goal, in an 8–2 victory over the Penguins in game five for his first career three-point playoff game. The Lightning overcame a 3–1 series deficit and defeated the fourth-seeded Penguins in seven games and advanced to the second round for the first time since the teams Stanley Cup championship run in [[2004 Stanley Cup playoffs|2004]] (four years before Stamkos was selected by the team and made his NHL debut) and swept the top-seeded Washington Capitals and eventually clinched a spot in the Eastern Conference Final against the [[Boston Bruins]]. In Game two on May 17, Stamkos recorded his second three-point playoff game scoring a goal on Bruins' goaltender [[Tim Thomas (ice hockey, born 1974)|Tim Thomas]] and recording two assists on goals by Martin St. Louis and Vincent Lecavalier, respectively. Despite this, the Lighting would lose the game 6–5.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wbur.org/news/2011/05/18/bruins-lightning-4 |title=Seguin's 2 Goals, 2 Assists Lift Bruins To 6-5 Win |website=wbur.org |publisher=The Wbur festival |author=AP |date=May 18, 2011 |access-date=February 18, 2025}}</ref> In game six on May 25, with the Lightning with a 3–2 series deficit and on the brink of elimination, Stamkos would record his second three point game of the series and third in the playoffs and in his career altogether scoring a goal and adding two assists, both were on goals by Martin St. Louis as the Lightning would go on to win 5–4 to extend the series to a seventh game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nydailynews.com/2011/05/25/martin-st-louis-steven-stamkos-tampa-bay-lightning-force-game-7-with-5-4-win-over-boston-bruins/ |title=Martin St. Louis, Steven Stamkos, Tampa Bay Lightning force Game 7 with 5-4 win over Boston Bruins |website=nydailynews.com |publisher=Daily News |agency=Associated Press |date=May 25, 2011 |access-date=February 18, 2025}}</ref> During the deciding game seven on May 27, Stamkos took a slapshot from Bruins defenseman [[Johnny Boychuk]] to the face; the impact broke his nose and bloodied his face, forcing him to momentarily leave the game, though he eventually returned wearing a full-caged mask.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ca.sports.yahoo.com/sports/news/lightning-star-steven-stamkos-no-201700896--nhl.html |title=Lightning star Steven Stamkos: No pain, no gain |website=yahoo.com |publisher=Yahoo Sports |author=Yahoo Sports |date=September 26, 2011 |access-date=May 11, 2026}}</ref> The Lightning went on to lose the game 1–0 against the third-seeded and eventual Stanley Cup champion Bruins with Bruins forward [[Nathan Horton]] scoring the loan goal in the game to lose the series 4–3, eliminating them from the [[2011 Stanley Cup playoffs|2011 playoffs]], one win short from reaching the Stanley Cup Final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wbur.org/news/2011/05/28/bruins-30 |title=Bruins Reach Stanley Cup Final |author=The Associated Press |website=wbur.org |publisher=wbur |date=May 28, 2011 |access-date=March 22, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://beyondthehockeystars.wordpress.com/tag/tampa-bay-lightning/ |title=Mucho respect for Steven Stamkos |website=beyondthehockeystars.com |publisher=Beyond the Hockey Stars |author=Beyond the Hockey Stars |date=May 27, 2011 |access-date=May 11, 2026}}</ref> Stamkos ended the playoffs scoring below his regular season pace with 13 points (six goals, seven assists) over all 18 games played during his first playoff year, ranking fifth in team-scoring. Days after the Lightning's elimination from the playoffs, it was revealed that in addition to his broken nose in the seventh game of the third round against the Bruins, Stamkos was playing through a nagging shoulder injury that he initially sustained in the first round against the Penguins.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nhl/news/stamkos-suffered-shoulder-injury-during-playoffs |title=Stamkos suffered shoulder injury during playoffs |website=nbcsports.com |publisher=NBC Sports |author=Matt Reitz |date=May 30, 2011 |access-date=January 1, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://nesn.com/2011/05/in-addition-to-broken-nose-lightning-forward-stamkos-battled-through-shoulder-injury/ |title=Steven Stamkos Played With Shoulder Injury in Addition to Broken Nose |website=nesn.com |publisher=NESN |author=NESN |date=May 31, 2011 |access-date=January 3, 2025}}</ref>\n[[File:Steven Stamkos Lightning 2012-02-12.JPG|upright|thumb|left|Stamkos as an alternate captain with the [[Tampa Bay Lightning]] in February 2012.]]\nDuring the 2011 off-season on July 1, 2011, Stamkos became a [[restricted free agent]]. 18 days later on July 19, he re-signed with Tampa Bay on a five-year, $37.5&nbsp;million contract.<ref>{{cite news|last=Wyshynski|first=Greg|title=Steven Stamkos Watch is over: Tampa Bay signs star for 5 years|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nhl/blog/puck_daddy/post/Steven-Stamkos-Watch-is-over-Tampa-Bay-signs-st?urn=nhl-wp9402|access-date=July 19, 2011|newspaper=Yahoo! Sports|date=July 19, 2011}}{{Dead link|date=March 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> Stamkos was also named [[alternate captain (ice hockey)|alternate captain]] by the Lightning on September 23, two weeks before the start of the [[2011-12 NHL season|2011–12 season]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/hockey/lightning-s-stamkos-ready-to-be-a-leader/article_47d7c365-9fd1-58ac-8b1a-e4bfab4618e5.html |title=Lightning's Stamkos ready to be 'A' leader |author= DAMIAN CRISTODERO |website=thestar.com |publisher=Toronto Star |date=September 24, 2011 |access-date=January 25, 2024}}</ref> Lightning head coach [[Guy Boucher]] quoted Stamkos’ role by saying, “Leaders aren't born; they are made, and you need courage. He has to be a leader and we know it. He wants it. The 2011 playoffs showed that he was ready and he's earned it.\"<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.heraldtribune.com/story/news/2011/10/06/stamkos-leadership-a-key-for-lightning/29050400007/ |title=Stamkos' leadership a key for Lightning |website=heraldtribute.com |publisher=Herald Tribute |author=Judy Royce |date=October 5, 2011 |access-date=March 21, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1368072-tampa-bay-lightning-make-no-mistake-this-is-steven-stamkos-team |title=Tampa Bay Lightning: Make No Mistake, This Is Steven Stamkos' Team |website=bleacherreport.com |publisher=Bleacher Report |author=Eric Steitz |date=October 12, 2012 |access-date=January 3, 2025}}</ref> On March 13, 2012, Stamkos scored his 50th goal of the season in a 6–1 win over the Boston Bruins on Bruins' goaltender [[Marty Turco]]. In so doing, he became the sixth player in NHL history to record more than one 50-goal season before his 23rd birthday.<ref>{{cite news | url = http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=622118 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120315102130/http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=622118 | url-status = dead | archive-date = March 15, 2012 | title = Stamkos reaches 50 again to join exclusive club | publisher = NHL.com | date = March 13, 2012 | access-date = March 14, 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/nhl/post/_/id/15829/is-stamkos-in-the-hart-running |title=Is Steven Stamkos in the Hart running? |publisher=ESPN |website=espn.com |author=ESPN |date=March 29, 2012 |access-date=September 6, 2025}}</ref> He then scored his 53rd goal on March 26 against the [[Philadelphia Flyers]] on goaltender [[Ilya Bryzgalov]], breaking Vincent Lecavalier's team record for goals in a season, set in [[2006–07 NHL season|2006–07]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=624300|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120328121104/http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=624300|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 28, 2012|title=Stamkos sets new franchise record with 53rd goal|last=Kimmelman|first=Adam|date=March 26, 2012|publisher=NHL.com|access-date=March 26, 2012}}</ref> Five days later, Stamkos set an NHL record by scoring his fifth overtime goal of the regular season, beating [[Winnipeg Jets]] goaltender [[Ondřej Pavelec]] from the left circle, Stamkos' \"trademark\" shot during his first three seasons prior similar to Washington Capitals forward and captain Alexander Ovechkin.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nhl.com/gamecenter/wpg-vs-tbl/2012/03/31/2011021174|title=Stamkos sets OT record as Lightning beat Jets 3–2|last=Herman|first=Lonnie|date=April 1, 2012|publisher=NHL.com|access-date=April 1, 2012}}</ref> On April 7, the final day of the 2011–12 season, Stamkos recorded his 60th goal in a 4–3 overtime win against the Winnipeg Jets, becoming the 20th player in NHL history to achieve the feat and the first since Alexander Ovechkin did so in [[2007–08_NHL_season#Scoring_leaders|2007–08]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Lightning's Steven Stamkos scores 60th goal vs. Jets|url=http://www.cbc.ca/sports/hockey/nhl/lightning-s-steven-stamkos-scores-60th-goal-vs-jets-1.1205841|access-date=January 22, 2018|date=April 7, 2012|publisher=CBC Sports|agency=Canadian Press}}</ref> His 60 goals led to him being awarded his second Rocket Richard Trophy as the NHL's leading goal scorer.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rawcharge.com/bolts-past-reviewing-stamkos-60-goal-2011-12-season/ |title=Bolt’s Past: Reviewing Stamkos’ 60 goal 2011-12 season |website=rawcharge.com |publisher=Raw Charge |author=Justin G |date=August 14, 2017 |access-date=October 4, 2025}}</ref> Despite Stamkos' continued individual success, the Lightning struggled as a team, finishing the season eight points out of a spot for the [[2012 Stanley Cup playoffs|playoffs]], putting them at tenth in the East and twenty first in the NHL overall. In addition, Stamkos also holds the distinction of being the only player to have scored 60 or more goals in an NHL season during the 2010s decade, placing him among a distinguished group of NHL players who have achieved this rare feat in the salary cap era (following the [[2004–05 NHL lockout|2004–05 lockout]]). Adding to his 60 goals, Stamkos also recorded 37 assists for a career high 97 points and played in all 82 games for the third consecutive season. His 97 points ranked second in the NHL as the runner-up for the [[Art Ross Trophy]], 12 behind Pittsburgh Penguins forward [[Evgeni Malkin]]. He ranked first overall in the league in even strength goals with 48 of his 60 goals coming at even strength (the most even strength goals in a season since [[Teemu Selänne]] and [[Alexander Mogilny]] in [[1992–93 NHL season|1992–93]]) and also tying [[Arizona Coyotes|Phoenix Coyotes]] forward [[Radim Vrbata]] in game-winning goals as 12 of his Stamkos' 60 total goals and 17 of Vrbata's 35 total goals were game-winners for their respective teams. Despite playing every game for the third season in a row, it was revealed that Stamkos played the final month of the season with an irritated bursa sac in his shoulder.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nhl/news/steven-stamkos-scored-60-goals-with-a-bum-shoulder |title=Steven Stamkos scored 60 goals with a bum shoulder |website=nbcsports.com |publisher=NBC Sports |author=Joe Yerdon |date=April 10, 2012 |access-date=January 5, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tampabay.com/archive/2012/04/10/tampa-bay-lightning-star-steven-stamkos-skipping-worlds-with-irritated-bursa-sac-in-left-shoulder/ |title=Tampa Bay Lightning star Steven Stamkos skipping Worlds with irritated bursa sac in left shoulder |website=tampabaytimes.com |publisher=Tampa Bay Times |author=Damian Cristodero |date=April 11, 2012 |access-date=January 5, 2025}}</ref> For the first time in his career, Stamkos was a finalist for the [[Hart Memorial Trophy]] as the NHL's most valuable player the regular season along with and Malkin and New York Rangers goaltender [[Henrik Lundqvist]], making Stamkos the first player since [[Calgary Flames]] winger [[Jarome Iginla]] in [[2001–02 NHL season|2002]] to become a top three finalist for the Hart Trophy despite being on a non-playoff team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/nhl-puck-daddy/hart-trophy-finalists-henrik-lundqvist-vs-evgeni-malkin-154523211.html |title=Hart Trophy Finalists: Henrik Lundqvist vs. Evgeni Malkin vs. Steven Stamkos |author=Greg Wyshynski |website=yahoosports.com |publisher=Yahoo Sports |date=April 27, 2012 |access-date=December 17, 2024}}</ref> The award would eventually be awarded to Malkin with Stamkos finishing second in the voting. Stamkos was also a finalist for the Ted Lindsay Award for the second straight season and second time in his career altogether along with Malkin and Lundqvist (which also went to Malkin), finishing second in that award as well.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nhl/news/poll-who-will-win-the-2012-ted-lindsay-award |title=Poll: Who will win the 2012 Ted Lindsay Award? |author=Mike Halford |website=nbcsports.com |publisher=NBC Sports |date=May 2, 2012 |access-date=May 14, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thehockeyfanatic.com/2012/05/2012-nhl-awards-finalists-who-wed-pick/ |title=2012 NHL Awards Finalists – Who We'd Pick |website=thehockeyfantastic.com |publisher=The Hockey Fanatic |author=The Hockey Fanatic |date=May 2, 2012 |access-date=February 5, 2025}}</ref>\n\nDuring the [[2012–13 NHL lockout|2012 NHL lockout]], Stamkos trained with a handful of other NHL players at Gary Roberts' training academy in Ontario.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/nhl/post/_/id/20472/lockout-life-agonizing-for-steven-stamkos|title = Lockout life agonizing for Steven Stamkos|date = November 29, 2012}}</ref> The lockout also gave Stamkos an opportunity to do things in his hometown of Toronto he normally would not get to do during an NHL season. That included playing in his father's pick-up hockey league every Thursday night, when he and former Lightning forward Steve Downie would mix it up with a group that varied as much in age (22–65) as ability. In January 2013, right when the [[2012–13 NHL season|2012–13 season]] began play after a three month delay and was abbreviated to 48 games over the normal 82 game schedule due to the lockout, Stamkos said when reflecting on playing in his father’s pick-up league, \"It was a blast, those guys loved it they don't get a chance to play with NHL guys very often.\" He added, \"It was a lot of fun and something I'll cherish forever.\"<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tampabay.com/sports/hockey/lightning/lightnings-steven-stamkos-eager-to-get-back-to-more-competitive-hockey/1269532/|title = Lightning's Steven Stamkos eager to get back to more competitive hockey}}</ref> On March 1, 2013, nearly two months after play started for the shortened season, Stamkos was named the NHL's First Star of the Month for February. He joined Pittsburgh forward and captain Sidney Crosby and Chicago goaltender [[Ray Emery]], who ranked as the Second and Third Stars, respectively. Stamkos had a season-high six-game goal streak and six multi-point outings, and recorded at least one point in 11 of 14 games for February 2013, with 10 goals and assists for 20 points within the 14 games played through the entire month. He ended the month of February on an eight-game point streak between February 14–28 (seven goals and seven assists for 14 points).<ref>{{cite news| url=http://www.cbc.ca/sports/hockey/nhl/steven-stamkos-named-nhl-1st-star-for-february-1.1362023 | work=CBC News|title = Steven Stamkos named NHL 1st star for February|date = March 1, 2013|agency = Associated Press|access-date = October 5, 2014}}</ref> On March 18, Stamkos scored his 200th career goal on Philadelphia Flyers' goaltender Ilya Bryzgalov as he the Lightning would eventually collect a 4–2 victory over the Flyers.<ref>{{Cite news|url = http://www.abcactionnews.com/sports/sports-blogs/steven-stamkos-scores-his-200th-career-goal|title = Steven Stamkos scores his 200th career goal in the Lightning's victory over the Flyers|date = March 18, 2013|work = abcactionnews.com WFTS Tampa Bay|access-date = October 5, 2014|agency = Associated Press|archive-date = October 6, 2014|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20141006123124/http://www.abcactionnews.com/sports/sports-blogs/steven-stamkos-scores-his-200th-career-goal|url-status = dead}}</ref> Stamkos finished the season playing in all 48 games with 29 goals, ranking him second in the NHL behind Alexander Ovechkin's NHL-leading 32. He also had 28 assists, which gave him a total of 57 points for the runner-up for the Art Ross Trophy for the second straight season behind teammate and linemate Martin St. Louis. Despite the continuation of his individual dominance, the Lightning still continued to struggle heavily as a team as they finished second-to-last in the league.\n[[File:Steven Stamkos 2014-03-22.JPG|thumb|250x250px|Stamkos as captain of the Lightning in March 2014.]]\nOn November 11, 2013, 17 games into the [[2013–14 NHL season|2013–14 season]], Stamkos suffered a broken [[tibia]] in a game against the Boston Bruins at [[TD Garden]]. He was backchecking on a play late in the second period when he was tied up with Boston [[defenceman]] [[Dougie Hamilton]]. His left skate appeared to hit the post first before his right leg slid into it around the shin area. He tried to get up twice before going down to the ice in agony, grabbing his leg just above the ankle with the training staff along with teammates Martin St. Louis, [[Alex Killorn]], [[Victor Hedman]], [[Sami Salo]] and [[Ryan Malone]] (who were on the ice with Stamkos when he slid into the net) rushing to his side.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://nationalpost.com/sports/hockey/nhl/steven-stamkos-taken-off-on-stretcher-with-leg-injury-after-gruesome-collision-in-tampa-bay-lightnings-game-against-boston-bruins |title= Steven Stamkos taken off on stretcher with leg injury after gruesome collision in Tampa Bay Lightning&#039;s game against Boston Bruins |website=nationalpost.com |publisher=National Post |author=The Associated Press |date=November 11, 2013 |access-date=October 7, 2025}}</ref> After a brief delay, a stretcher was brought out by the trainers and he was taken off the ice to a loud applause from the audience and the rest of his teammates and the Lightning coaches looking on. He was taken to [[Massachusetts General Hospital]].<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nhl/2013/11/11/lightning-steven-stamkos-stretcher/3498333/ | work=USA Today | title=Lightning's Steven Stamkos breaks leg, to have surgery | date=November 11, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Star Tampa Bay centre Steven Stamkos out with broken leg|url=https://www.nhl.com/news/star-tampa-bay-centre-steven-stamkos-out-with-broken-leg/c-690912|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160308014311/https://www.nhl.com/news/star-tampa-bay-centre-steven-stamkos-out-with-broken-leg/c-690912|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 8, 2016|website=NHL.com|access-date=March 13, 2018|date=November 11, 2013}}</ref> Stamkos entered the day with 14 goals and nine assists for 23 points in the first 17 games of the season. His 14 goals tied for the NHL's lead in goal scoring with [[St. Louis Blues]] forward [[Alexander Steen]] and his 23 points tied with Pittsburgh Penguins forward and captain Sidney Crosby for league-leading point scorer.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://fansided.com/2013/11/12/sidney-crosby-reaches-steven-stamkos-following-injury/ |title=Sidney Crosby reaches out to Steven Stamkos following injury |author=Franklin Steele |website=fansided.com |publisher=Fansided |date=November 12, 2013 |access-date=August 22, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://archive.triblive.com/sports/penguins/penguins-notebook-crosby-reaches-out-to-injured-stamkos/#axzz2kNodUiur |title=Penguins notebook: Crosby reaches out to injured Stamkos |author=Rob Rossi |website=triblive.com |publisher=Trib Live |date=November 12, 2013 |access-date=August 22, 2024}}</ref> He also entered the day on an [[Iron man (sports streak)|iron man streak]] of 344 consecutive games played (having last missed a game on January 29, 2009, where he was a healthy scratch against the Carolina Hurricanes).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tampabay.com/sports/hockey/lightning/lightnings-steven-stamkos-injured/2151885/ |title=Lightning's Steven Stamkos out indefinitely with broken tibia |website=tampabay.com |publisher=Tampa Bay Times |author=Times staff writer |date=November 12, 2013 |access-date=February 11, 2025}}</ref> The next day, Stamkos underwent successful surgery in [[Boston]] to stabilize the fracture in his right tibia and he began rehabilitation immediately.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lightning's Stamkos has successful surgery|url=https://www.nhl.com/news/lightnings-stamkos-has-successful-surgery/c-691194|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180314043217/https://www.nhl.com/news/lightnings-stamkos-has-successful-surgery/c-691194|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 14, 2018|website=NHL.com|access-date=March 13, 2018|date=November 12, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.dailyfaceoff.com/news/stamkos-leaves-mondays-game-on-stretcher |title=Update: Lightning confirm Stamkos has broken tibia, surgery on Tuesday |website=dailyfaceoff.com |publisher=Daily Faceoff |author= Brock Seguin |date=November 11, 2013 |access-date=September 28, 2024}}</ref> On November 25, prior to the Lightning's upcoming game against the New York Rangers, Stamkos made a press appearance to the media where he was seen walking without the use of crutches or a walking boot. He updated the media on his miraculous progress and was hopeful that he could return to the Lightning before commencement of the [[Ice hockey at the 2014 Winter Olympics – Men's tournament|2014 Winter Olympics]] in [[Sochi]], which he was widely considered to play in for [[Canada men's national ice hockey team|Canada]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.tsn.ca/nhl/teams/story/?id=437474&hubname=nhl-lightning |title=Stamkos walks without crutches just two weeks after injury |access-date=December 7, 2017 |archive-date=December 3, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203003121/http://www.tsn.ca/nhl/teams/story/?id=437474&hubname=nhl-lightning |url-status=dead}}</ref> Ultimately, he was unable to recover in time to participate in the Olympics. After missing 45 games and the Olympics, Stamkos was cleared to play for the Lightning on March 5, 2014, the same day former teammate and linemate Martin St. Louis was traded to the New York Rangers – and returned the next day, in a game against the [[Buffalo Sabres]], which the team lost 3–1.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://torontosun.com/2014/03/05/lightnings-steven-stamkos-cleared-to-return |title=NHL notes: Lightning's Steven Stamkos cleared to return |website=torontosun.com |publisher=Toronto Sun |author=QMI agency |date=March 6, 2014 |access-date=September 28, 2024}}</ref> Stamkos was named the new captain of the Lightning before the game, replacing the departed St. Louis. Lightning head coach [[Jon Cooper (ice hockey)|Jon Cooper]] stated that Stamkos was \"destined to be our leader\" and his leadership puts the Lightning \"one step closer to achieving our ultimate goal in winning a Stanley Cup.\"<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.sbnation.com/nhl/2014/3/6/5479652/steven-stamkos-named-captain-of-lightning |title=Steven Stamkos named captain of Lightning |website=sbnation.com |publisher=SB Nation |author=Adam Gretz |date=March 6, 2014 |access-date=January 6, 2024}}</ref> He finished the injury-shortened season playing in 37 games with 25 goals, 15 assists and 40 points. Despite his lengthy absence during the season, the Lightning as a team qualified for the playoffs for the first time in three years as the team would finish third in the East. The Lightning, however, would be upset in the opening round of the [[2014 Stanley Cup playoffs|2014 playoffs]] as they were swept by sixth-seeded Montreal Canadiens.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/recap/_/gameId/400552526 |title=Max Pacioretty lifts Habs to 2nd round in sweep of Lightning |agency=Associated Press |website=[[ESPN]] |publisher=ESPN |date=April 23, 2014 |access-date=May 22, 2024}}</ref> Stamkos would finish the playoffs with two goals and assists for four points in all four games played. He was the Lightning's nominee for the [[Bill Masterton Memorial Trophy]] as the player who shows best qualities of perseverance, sportsmanship, and dedication to the game of ice hockey although Stamkos was left out of the three finalists selected by the [[Professional Hockey Writers' Association]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nhl/2014/04/10/nhls-2014-masterton-trophy-nominees-stories-favorites-to-win |title=NHL's 2014 Masterton Trophy: Nominees, stories, favorites to win |website=si.com |publisher=Sports Illustrated |last=Muir | first=Allan |date=April 10, 2014 |access-date=April 15, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.sportsnet.ca/hockey/nhl/stand-up-as-soon-as-possible/ |title=Inside the return of hockey's top sniper |website=sportsnet.ca |publisher=Sportsnet |author=Luke Fox |date=March 6, 2014 |access-date=September 28, 2024}}</ref>\n\nOn November 11, 2014, Stamkos recorded his 200th career NHL assist on a goal scored by [[Nikita Kucherov]] in a Lightning 3–2 shootout loss to the Chicago Blackhawks at [[United Center]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/gamecenter/tbl-vs-chi/2014/11/11/2014020228|title=Bolts fall in shootout to Blackhawks|first=Bryan|last=Burns|work=Lightning Beat Writer|date= November 11, 2014|access-date=December 13, 2014}}</ref> Stamkos finished the [[2014–15 Tampa Bay Lightning season|2014–15 season]] playing in all 82 games and recording 43 goals, 29 assists and 72 points. His 43 goals were once again second overall in the league only behind Washington Capitals forward and captain Alexander Ovechkin who had 53 goals. On May 24, 2015, during game five of the Eastern Conference Final of the [[2015 Stanley Cup playoffs|2015 playoffs]] against the [[Presidents' Trophy]]-winning New York Rangers, Stamkos scored a goal in a 2–0 Lightning victory over the Rangers on goaltender Henrik Lundqvist, tying him with the Lightning playoff record for goals in consecutive games (four).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/gamecenter/tbl-vs-nyr/2015/05/24/2014030315|title=Ben Bishop's shutout leads Lightning to game five victory|first=Bryan|last=Burns|work=Lightning Beat Writer|date=May 24, |website=thehockeynews.com |publisher=The Hockey News |author=Adam Proteau |date=June 16, 2015 |access-date=May 11, 2026}}</ref> After the playoffs ended, Lightning general manager [[Steve Yzerman]] revealed that Stamkos played through an undisclosed injury during the Finals.<ref>{{cite 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>\n\nOn October 12, 2015, Stamkos recorded his 500th career NHL point off a power-play goal against Boston Bruins goaltender [[Tuukka Rask]]. The Lightning would go on to win the game 6–3.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/gamecenter/tbl-vs-bos/2015/10/12/2015020032|title=Stamkos earns 500th point in Lightning's win at Bruins|first=Matt|last=Kalman|work=NHL.com|date= October 12, 2015|access-date=October 12, 2015}}</ref> With his 500th career point, Stamkos became the third player in Lightning history to record over 500 points. He joined both Martin St. Louis (953) and Vincent Lecavalier (874) as the only players to do so.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tampabay.com/sports/hockey/lightning/coach-jon-cooper-lightning-interested-in-staying-together/2249631/|title=Coach Jon Cooper, Lightning interested in staying together|first=Joe|last=Smith|work=Tampa Bay Times|date= October 13, 2015|access-date=October 14, 2015}}</ref> On October 23, Stamkos played in his 500th career NHL game in a 4–3 overtime Lightning victory over the Winnipeg Jets.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/gamecenter/tbl-vs-wpg/2015/10/23/2015020102|title=Palat gives Lightning win against Jets|first=Patrick|last=Williams|work=NHL.com|date= October 23, 2015|access-date=October 25, 2015}}</ref> On November 1, Stamkos moved into second place for the most power-play goals in Lightning history with 97. Stamkos moved from a tie with former teammate Martin St. Louis, who had 96 power-play goals in his time with the Lightning<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/gamecenter/tbl-vs-car/2015/11/01/2015020165|title=Vasilevskiy wins in return, Lightning defeat Hurricanes|first=Kurt|last=Dusterberg|work=NHL.com|date= November 1, 2015|access-date=November 1, 2015}}</ref> On January 6, 2016, Stamkos was selected to his fourth All-Star Game, joining teammate [[Ben Bishop]]. On February 20, Stamkos scored his 300th career NHL goal, which came in a 4–2 Lightning win over the Pittsburgh Penguins. Stamkos became the third Lightning player in franchise history to record 300 goals, joining Vincent Lecavalier (383) and Martin St. Louis (365). During a post-game interview, Stamkos said of his feat, \"[F]irst of all, it means you've been around for a while and secondly, I've been fortunate to play with a lot of good players. I've been able to be put in positions to score goals and obviously it was special coming in a big win for our team.\"<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/gamecenter/tbl-vs-pit/2016/02/20/2015020874|title=Stamkos' 300th goal helps Lightning past Penguins|first=Wes|last=Crosby|work=NHL.com|date=February 20, 2016|access-date=February 20, 2016}}</ref> On February 26, Stamkos played in his 553 game in Lightning history, which came in a 4–0 win over the [[New Jersey Devils]]. With the game, Stamkos surpassed [[Brad Richards]] (552) for fourth all-time in games played for the Lightning.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/gamecenter/tbl-vs-njd/2016/02/26/2015020916|title=Stamkos, Bishop help Lightning defeat Devils|first=Mike|last=Morreale|work=NHL.com|date=February 26, 2016|access-date=March 3, 2016}}</ref> On February 28, Stamkos recorded his 245 career assist as a member of the Lightning in a 4–1 over the Boston Bruins on a goal by [[Ryan Callahan]]. The assist moved Stamkos past [[Václav Prospal]] (244) to become fourth all-time in assists with the Lightning.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/gamecenter/tbl-vs-bos/2016/02/28/2015020933|title=Stamkos, Lightning win sixth straight, top Bruins|first=Mike|last=Kalma|work=NHL.com|date=February 28, 2016|access-date=March 3, 2016}}</ref> On April 2, after the first 77 games of the season, the Lightning announced Stamkos was diagnosed with [[thoracic outlet syndrome]], the same injury that sidelined teammate [[Andrei Vasilevskiy]] at the start of the 2015–16 season; it is a condition that is rare among hockey players. Stamkos said he first felt some discomfort in his arm after the game against the [[Montreal Canadiens]] on March 31. He was scheduled for surgery on the following Monday with Dr. Karl Illig, who performed Vasilevskiy's surgery. Lightning general manager Steve Yzerman said there would be no long-term impact on Stamkos' health or his career. In addition, Yzerman indicated Stamkos recovery time would be between one and three months, but the club would have a better idea in a couple of weeks where he falls within that time frame. Yzerman also said the team's desire is for Stamkos to remain with the organization, which came after a question of whether Stamkos had played his last game in a Lightning uniform.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.home.tampabay.com/sports/hockey/lightning/lightning-tops-devils-with-stamkos-out-hurt/2271716|title=Lightning's Stamkos out 1-3 months with blood clot (w/video)|first=Joe|last=Smith|work=Tampa Bay Times|date=April 2, 2016|access-date=April 3, 2016|archive-date=April 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160404203857/http://www.home.tampabay.com/sports/hockey/lightning/lightning-tops-devils-with-stamkos-out-hurt/2271716|url-status=dead}}</ref> On April 4, Stamkos had successful surgery at Tampa General Hospital. Stamkos' surgeon said they plan on evaluating him in approximately two weeks and that should clear up his prognosis.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tbo.com/sports/bucs/lightning-star-steven-stamkos-has-successful-surgery-20160404/|title=Lightning's Stamkos has successful surgery for rare condition|first=Ira|last=Kaufman|work=The Tampa Tribune|date=April 4, 2016|access-date=April 6, 2016|archive-date=April 6, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160406210618/http://www.tbo.com/sports/bucs/lightning-star-steven-stamkos-has-successful-surgery-20160404/|url-status=dead}}</ref> In the first 77 games played for the [[2015–16 NHL season|2015–16 season]], Stamkos recorded 36 goals, 28 assists and 64 points, ranking first in goals, third in assists and second in points for the team. After missing the final five games of the season, the first two rounds of the [[2016 Stanley Cup playoffs|2016 playoffs]] against the [[Detroit Red Wings]] and [[New York Islanders]] and first six games of the Eastern Conference Finals against the Pittsburgh Penguins, Stamkos dressed for Game 7 of the Eastern Conference Finals against the Penguins on May 27, despite still being on blood thinners following surgery. He registered five shot attempts during the game, but the Lightning lost the game 2–1 for a 4–3 defeat in the series resulting in their elimination from the playoffs, falling one win short from a second consecutive appearance in the Stanley Cup Final and surrendering a 3–2 series lead in doing so.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ca.sports.yahoo.com/blogs/nhl-puck-daddy/steven-stamkos-emotional-after-storybook-game-7-spoiled-by-penguins-040452980.html|title=Steven Stamkos emotional after storybook Game 7 spoiled by Penguins| website = Yahoo Sports Canada|date=May 27, 2016 |access-date=June 14, 2016}}</ref>\n\nOn June 29, 2016, two days before Stamkos was set to become an unrestricted free agent, the Lightning signed him to an eight-year, $68&nbsp;million contract extension with an annual average value of $8.5&nbsp;million. absence the year prior. His 59 assists and +18 rating were career highs. His 86 points ranked second on the Lightning and 12th in the league overall. Stamkos also ended the season as the team leader in penalty minutes (72). Stamkos' healthy 2017–18 campaign saw him be named as the Lightning's nominee for the Bill Masterton Memorial Trophy for the second straight season and third time in his career altogether, although he wasn't named a top three finalist by the NHL.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tampabay.com/blogs/lightning/2018/03/27/stamkos-nominated-against-for-masterton-trophy/ |title=Lightning's Steven Stamkos nominated again for Masterton Trophy |author=Roger Mooney |website=tampabaytimes.com |publisher=Tampa Bay Times |date=March 27, 2018 |access-date=April 15, 2024}}</ref> In the [[2018 Stanley Cup playoffs|2018 playoffs]], Stamkos and the Lightning would go on another lengthy run as they beat the eighth-seeded New Jersey Devils in five games in the first round and the third-seeded Boston Bruins in five games in the second round to reach the Eastern Conference Final for the third time in four seasons and third time among Stamkos' captaincy and fourth time in Stamkos' tenure with the team altogether. On May 17, during game four of the third round series, Stamkos recorded his 11th career playoff power-play goal in a 4–2 Lightning win over the Washington Capitals at [[Capital One Arena]] against Capitals goaltender [[Braden Holtby]] to even the series at two wins apeice. The goal moved Stamkos past Martin St. Louis for most playoff power-play goals in franchise history.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/tampa-bay-lightning-washington-capitals-game-4-recap-298667954|title=Lightning win game four against Capitals, even Eastern Final|first=Dan|last=Rosen|work=[[National Hockey League]]|date=May 17, 2018|access-date=May 24, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite tweet |user=TBLightning |number=997277836871421954 |date = May 17, 2018 |title=You're looking at your new franchise leader for most power-play goals all time in #Bolts playoff history: Steven Stamkos (11 PPGs).}}</ref> The Lightning would eventually go on to lose the series against the second-seeded and eventual Stanley Cup champion Capitals in seven games, coming one win short from the Stanley Cup Final and surrendering a 3–2 series lead in the process once more. He also scored the second most goals in the decade with 363 in that timeframe, only behind the 437 scored by Alexander Ovechkin.<ref>{{cite web| url = https://nhl.nbcsports.com/2020/01/24/crosby-kane-ovechkin-highlight-nhls-all-decade-team/ | title = Crosby, Kane, Ovechkin highlight NHL's All-Decade Team | publisher = [[NBC Sports]] | date = January 24, 2020 | access-date = January 27, 2020}}</ref> On February 4, Stamkos recorded his 61st game-winning goal of his career against [[Vegas Golden Knights]] goaltender [[Marc-Andre Fleury]]. Stamkos recovery was projected at six to eight weeks from the procedure, which caused him to miss the remainder of the regular season.<ref>{{cite web| url = https://www.si.com/nhl/2020/02/29/lightning-steven-stamkos-injury-surgery | title = Lightning Captain Steven Stamkos to Miss 6-8 Weeks After Surgery | publisher = [[Sports Illustrated]] | date = February 29, 2020 | access-date = March 7, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url = https://www.nhl.com/lightning/news/lightning-captain-steven-stamkos-to-have-surgery-315697614 | title = Lightning Captain Steven Stamkos to have surgery | publisher = [[NHL]] | date = February 29, 2020 | access-date = March 7, 2020}}</ref> Up to that point in the [[2019–20 Tampa Bay Lightning season|2019–20 season]], he had played in 57 games and recorded 29 goals and 37 assists adding up to 66 points. In Stamkos' absence, the Lightning would defeat the Columbus Blue Jackets in five games in the first round of the [[2020 Stanley Cup playoffs|2020 playoffs]] followed by the Presidents' Trophy-winning Boston Bruins in five games and New York Islanders in six games to reach the [[2020 Stanley Cup Final|Stanley Cup Final]] for the first time since 2015. On September 23, Stamkos returned to the Lightning lineup in the third game of the Finals<ref>{{cite web| url = https://www.nhl.com/lightning/news/steven-stamkos-set-to-return-in-game-3-319164186 | title = Steven Stamkos set to return in game three | publisher =[[NHL]] | date = September 23, 2020 | access-date = September 24, 2020}}</ref> where he scored on his first (and only) shot of the game on Dallas Stars goaltender [[Anton Khudobin]].<ref>{{Cite tweet |user=BBurnsNHL |number = 1308926261524398081 |date = September 23, 2020 |title=Steven Stamkos scores on his first shot of the game against Dallas Stars goaltender Anton Khudobin.}}</ref> Stamkos' goal was the second time in NHL history that a player skating in their first game of the playoffs in the Stanley Cup Final scored a goal, the previous being [[Billy Taylor (ice hockey, born 1919)|Billy Taylor Sr.]] in [[1940 Stanley Cup Final|1940]].<ref>{{Cite tweet |user=PR_NHL |number = 1308931603310292992 |date = September 23, 2020 |title=Steven Stamkos became the second NHL player – and first in more than 80 years – to score a goal while skating in his first game of the playoffs during the Stanley Cup Final. He finished the [[2021 Stanley Cup playoffs|2021 playoffs]] with eight goals and 10 assists for 18 points in all 23 contests played.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://insidetherink.com/stamkos-finding-a-new-stride-in-his-game-despite-injury-and-age/#google_vignette |title=Stamkos finding a new stride in his game despite injury, and age |website=insidetherink.com |publisher=Inside the Rink |author=Nick Krell |date=November 4, 2021 |access-date=September 28, 2024}}</ref> Stamkos was also named the Lightning's nominee for the Bill Masterton Memorial Trophy for the fourth time in his career but wasn't named a top three finalist by the NHL.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nhl.com/lightning/news/tampa-bay-lightning-forward-steven-stamkos-named-tampa-bay-s-masterton-324598178 |title=Steven Stamkos named Tampa Bay's Masterton nominee for the fourth time |website=nhl.com |publisher=Tampa Bay Lightning |author=Bryan Burns |date= May 15, 2021 |access-date=April 15, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportsology.com/steven-stamkos-a-born-leader/ |title=Steven Stamkos – – A Born Leader |website=sportsology.com |publisher=Sportsology |author=Russ Cohen |date=July 8, 2021 |access-date=October 7, 2025}}</ref>\n\nOn April 26, 2022, in a game against the Columbus Blue Jackets which saw the Lightning win 4–1, Stamkos recorded his 100th point of the season on a second period goal. His 39th goal of the season on [[Elvis Merzlikins]] would make this be the first time he recorded 100 points in a season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://thehockeywriters.com/lightning-stamkos-lady-byng-messier-award-candidate/ |title=Steven Stamkos Should be in the Lady Byng & Messier Award Discussions |website=thehockeywriters.com |publisher=The Hockey Writers |author=Jim Bay |date=April 28, 2022 |access-date=December 24, 2022}}</ref> In that game, he also became the first player since [[Jari Kurri]] in [[1992–93 NHL season|1992–93]] to record at least three points in at least five consecutive games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rawcharge.com/tampa-bay-lightning-round-steven-stamkos-creates-a-new-milestone-as-auston-matthews-matches-his-nhl/ |title=Lightning Round: Stamkos creates a new milestone as Matthews matches his |website=rawcharge.com |publisher=Raw Charge |author=Hardev |date=April 27, 2022 |access-date=December 24, 2022}}</ref> In the [[2021–22 NHL season|2021–22 season]] finale against the New York Islanders on April 29, Stamkos recorded his 10th career hat-trick to bump his goal scoring total to 40, 41 and 42 in the season, which saw the Lightning win 6–4. This would mark the sixth time in his career where he recorded 40 or more goals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://thehockeywriters.com/revisiting-under-appreciated-2021-22-lightning/ |title=Revisiting the Under-Appreciated 2021-22 Tampa Bay Lightning |website=thehockeywriters.com |publisher=The Hockey Writers |author=Jack Pilots |date=September 16, 2024 |access-date=October 4, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rawcharge.com/a-look-back-at-the-2021-22-tampa-bay-lightning-nhl-steven-stamkos/ |title=A look back on the 2021-22 Tampa Bay Lightning |author=Matthew Esteves |website=rawcharge.com |publisher=Raw Charge |date=June 29, 2022 |access-date=October 4, 2025}}</ref> For April 2022, Stamkos recorded 33 points (12 goals and 21 assists) in all 16 games for the month, which surpassed Nikita Kucherov’s 30 points in December 2018 for a franchise record for most points in a single calendar month. His 33 points would also be the most points in a calendar month by an NHL player since Mario Lemieux’s 34 points in December 1995.<ref>{{citation |url= https://patch.com/florida/southtampa/lightning-captain-steven-stamkos-makes-history-seasons-final-game |title=Lightning Captain Steven Stamkos Makes History In Season's Final Game |website=patch.com |publisher=Patch |author=D’Ann Lawrence White |date=May 2, 2022 |access-date=August 4, 2025}}</ref> Stamkos finished the [[2021–22 Tampa Bay Lightning season|2021–22 season]] altogether recording 42 goals and 64 assists for 106 total points with a career-best +24 [[Plus–minus (sports)|plus-minus]] rating in 81 games played. His 42 goals led the team for goal scoring and tied with Nashville Predators’ forward [[Filip Forsberg]] and Calgary Flames’ forwards [[Matthew Tkachuk]] and [[Elias Lindholm]] for ninth most goals in the league altogether. His 64 assists and 106 points recorded would be new individual career highs with his 64 assists being second most on the team (only behind the 65 Victor Hedman recorded) and ninth in the league overall. His 106 points also led the team in points as well and in a two-way tie with Toronto Maple Leafs’ forward [[Auston Matthews]] for sixth most points in the league overall. His +24 rating was third on the team only behind Victor Hedman's team-leading +26 rating and [[Jan Rutta]]’s +25 rating. 11 of the 42 goals Stamkos scored during the season were game-winners, tying Edmonton Oilers forward Leon Draisaitl, Dallas Stars forward [[Jason Robertson]] and New York Rangers forward [[Chris Kreider]] for league leaders in game-winning goals. In the [[2022 Stanley Cup playoffs|2022 playoffs]], Stamkos and the Lightning would defeat the fourth-seeded Toronto Maple Leafs in seven games in the first round (erasing a 3–2 series deficit in doing so), the Presidents' Trophy-winning Florida Panthers in a four-game sweep to clinch a third consecutive appearance in the Eastern Conference Final (sixth appearance under his captaincy and seventh time in his tenure overall), where they defeated the third-seeded New York Rangers in six games to clinch a third consecutive appearance in the [[2022 Stanley Cup Final|Stanley Cup Final]] (fourth altogether under his captaincy and tenure with the Lightning).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://thehockeywriters.com/lightning-stamkos-playoff-run-best-all-time/ |title=Steven Stamkos' Playoff-Run Puts Him Among the Best of All-Time |website=thehockeywriters.com |publisher=The Hockey Writers |author=Connor Ziparo |date=June 13, 2022 |access-date=October 4, 2025}}</ref> On June 11, in game six of the third round, Stamkos scored both goals (including the series-winning goal) against Rangers  goaltender [[Igor Shesterkin]] as the Lightning won the game two–1 to end the series in six.<ref name=\"NYRTBLG6\">{{cite web|url=https://www.nhl.com/news/new-york-rangers-tampa-bay-lightning-game-6-recap-334410874|title=Lightning defeat Rangers in game six, advance to third straight Cup Final|last=Long|first=Corey|publisher=NHL Enterprises, L. P.|date=June 11, 2022|website=NHL.com|access-date=June 11, 2022}}</ref> Going into the Finals, Stamkos was seen as a top candidate for the [[Conn Smythe Trophy]] as the playoff MVP if the Lightning were to win  third consecutive Stanley Cup title.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/story/_/id/34086150/2022-stanley-cup-final-picks-lightning-avalanche-conn-smythe-trophy |title=2022 Stanley Cup Final: Picks for Lightning-Avalanche, Conn Smythe Trophy |publisher=ESPN |website=espn.com |date=June 14, 2022 |access-date=December 24, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://thehockeynews.com/news/news/conn-smythe-trophy-betting-steven-stamkos-is-undervalued |title=Conn Smythe Trophy Betting: Steven Stamkos is Undervalued |website=thehockeynews.com |publisher=The Hockey News |author=BetMGM |date=June 15, 2022 |access-date=December 24, 2024}}</ref> The Lightning, however, would go on to lose in six games to the top-seeded Colorado Avalanche. Stamkos finished the playoffs with 11 goals, eight assists and 19 points in all 23 games played.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rawcharge.com/a-look-back-at-the-2021-22-tampa-bay-lightning-nhl-steven-stamkos/ |title=A look back at the 2021-22 Tampa Bay Lightning |website=rawcharge.com |author=Matthew Esteves |date=June 29, 2022 |access-date=March 18, 2025}}</ref>\n\nThe [[2022–23 NHL season|2022–23 season]] would be full of milestones for Stamkos. On November 15, 2022, Stamkos recorded his 500th assist against the Dallas Stars on an OT goal scored by Alex Killorn. On December 1, Stamkos recorded his 1,000th point, assisting on a [[Nick Paul]] goal in a 4–1 win against the Philadelphia Flyers. He became the 95th player, the 14th first overall pick, and the first player in Lightning history to record 1,000 NHL points. On January 18, 2023, in a 5–2 win over the Vancouver Canucks, Stamkos became the first player in Lightning history to record 500 career goals, the third active player at the time and the 47th player ever to achieve the feat. He capped off the night with his 11th career hat-trick, becoming the eighth player in NHL history to do so. He said it was \"a humbling experience when you have a moment like that.\"<ref>{{cite web|url=https://thehockeynews.com/news/news/steven-stamkos-celebrates-500th-goal-as-the-lightning-heat-up|title=Steven Stamkos celebrates 500th goal as the Lightning heat up |last=Schram|first=Carol|date=January 19, 2023|work=[[The Hockey News]]|access-date=January 19, 2023}}</ref> Lightning head coach Jon Cooper expressed elation for Stamkos' milestone by saying, \"I have watched him grow into a man, a phenomonal leader and to be honest, a generational goal scorer. Those guys don't come around that often.\"<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theobserver.ca/sports/local-sports/former-sting-star-stamkos-scores-500th-nhl-goal |title=Former Sting star Stamkos scores 500th NHL goal |author=Gemma Karstens-Smith |website=theobserver.com |publisher=The Observer |date=January 19, 2023 |access-date=April 23, 2024}}</ref> On April 6, Stamkos played his 1,000th NHL game against the New York Islanders, becoming the second player from the Lightning to play all their games with the team, after Vincent Lecavalier. Stamkos ended the 2022–23 season with 34 goals, 50 assists and 84 points having played in 81 games as the Lightning as a team finished sixth in the East. Going into the [[2023 Stanley Cup playoffs|2023 playoffs]] against the Toronto Maple Leafs in the opening round of the for the second consecutive season and this time falling to the third-seeded Maple Leafs in six games, Stamkos would record two goals and assists for four points in all six games. On June 26, at the 2023 NHL Awards show, Stamkos was named the winner of the [[Mark Messier Leadership Award]] by former NHL player [[Mark Messier]] for contributions both on and off the ice.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/steven-stamkos-wins-mark-messier-leadership-award-345017982 |title= Stamkos of Lightning wins Messier NHL leadership award |author=David Satriano |publisher=National Hockey League |website=nhl.com |date=June 23, 2023 |access-date=January 4, 2024}}</ref> After being awarded the trophy, Stamkos went on to say \"When you you have someone with the caliber of leadership that Mark Messier has and what he's meant to our game, it's pretty special to have him hand select the winner. I am very proud of everything we have been able to accomplish in Tampa\".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.wfla.com/sports/tampa-bay-lightning/tampa-bay-lightning-star-steven-stamkos-wins-mark-messier-nhl-leadership-award/ |title=Tampa Bay Lightning star Steven Stamkos wins Mark Messier NHL Leadership Award |first=Kaycee |last=Sloan |website=wfla.com |publisher=WFLA |date=June 29, 2023 |access-date=July 4, 2023}}</ref>\n\nOn December 14, 2023, Stamkos recorded his first career four-goal game and 12th career hat-trick in a 7–4 win over the Edmonton Oilers.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tampabay.com/sports/lightning/2023/12/15/steven-stamkos-jon-cooper-edmonton-oilers-mikhail-sergachev-stuart-skinner/ |title= How Lightning's Steven Stamkos broke out with four goals vs. Oilers |author=Eduardo A. Encina |publisher=Tampa Bay Times |website=tampabaytimes.com |date=December 15, 2023 |access-date=January 4, 2024}}</ref> On December 31, Stamkos played his 1,038th NHL game (all with the Lightning) in a 4–3 win over the Montreal Canadiens and recorded an assist on a goal by [[Calvin de Haan]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/recap/_/gameId/401559797 |title=Calvin de Haan ends 46-game Sabres for his seventh season with 40 goals or more.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.caledonianrecord.com/sports/regional/sabres-lightning-hockey/image_5e0a8e83-eb93-5f44-8ae4-b805101a6eab.html |publisher=AP News |author=Fred Goodall |date=May 1, 2024 |access-date=October 7, 2025}}</ref>\n\n==== Nashville Predators (2024–present) ====\nOn July 1, 2024, Stamkos ended his 16-year tenure with the Lightning after being unable to negotiate an extension with the club and was signed as a free agent to a four-year, $32 million dollar contract with the [[Nashville Predators]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 1, 2024 |title=Stamkos signs 4-year contract with Predators after leaving Lightning {{!}} NHL.com |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/steven-stamkos-signs-with-nashville-predators-as-free-agent During the first period of the game, Stamkos was given a standing ovation and was honored by the Lightning as the team presented a video tribute on the jumbotron capturing his tenure and Stamkos would take a solo lap around the ice to salute the fans.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dailyfaceoff.com/news/tampa-bay-lightning-honor-steven-stamkos-with-tribute-video |title=Tampa Bay Lightning honor Steven Stamkos with tribute video |website=dailyfaceoff.com |publisher=Daily Faceoff |author=Colton Davies |date=October 28, 2024 |access-date=October 28, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.abcactionnews.com/sports/steven-stamkos-set-for-emotional-return-to-face-the-lightning |title=Steven Stamkos set for emotional return to face the Lightning |website=abcactionnews.com |publisher=ABC News |author=Kyle Burger |date=October 28, 2024 |access-date=April 19, 2025}}</ref> Stamkos would record his first two assists of the season as a Predator that game on goals by [[Ryan O'Reilly]] and [[Gustav Nyquist]], respectively. Despite being no longer on the Lightning, Lightning fans cheered for both goals the Predators scored largely because of Stamkos recording assists on both of them. The Predators would eventually fall to the Lightning 3–2 in overtime. On March 4, 2025, Stamkos recorded his 600th career assist on a Ryan O'Reilly goal in a 6–3 win over the [[Boston Bruins]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nhl.com/predators/news/stamkos-o-reilly-lead-preds-to-win-over-bruins-2025-03-04 |title=Stamkos, O'Reilly Lead Preds to Win Over Bruins |website=nhl.com |publisher=National Hockey League |author=Brooks Batten |date=March 4, 2025 |access-date=March 4, 2025}}</ref> On March 8, Stamkos recorded his first hat trick as a Predator and the 14th of his career altogether as he scored all three goals in the Predators 3–2 OT win over the [[Chicago Blackhawks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nhl.com/news/chicago-blackhawks-nashville-predators-game-recap-march-8 |title=Stamkos hat trick lifts Predators past Blackhawks in OT |website=nhl.com |publisher=NHL |author=Robby Stanley |date=March 8, 2025 |access-date=March 8, 2025}}</ref> Stamkos ultimately ended the season with 27 goals and 26 assists for 53 points ranking second on the team in goals, fourth in assists and fifth in points while also recording a career low -36 plus-minus rating. His 53 points was the lowest in a full season since his rookie season. This would be despite playing in all 82 games.\n\nOn December 31, 2025, Stamkos scores his 600th goal in a 4–2 victory over the [[Vegas Golden Knights]], becoming the 2second player all time to reach the mark. On April 11, 2026, Stamkos recorded his 40th goal of the [[2025–26 NHL season|2025–26 season]] in a 2–1 win over the [[Minnesota Wild]], marking the eighth time of hitting the 40-goal plateau within his career and becoming the third player in Predators history to hit the mark.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.nhl.com/predators/news/stamkos-scores-40th-as-preds-beat-wild-to-stay-in-playoff-hunt-2026-04-11 |title=Predators hold off Wild, keep pace in Western wild-card race |website=nhl.com |author=Robby Stanley |date=April 11, 2026 |access-date=April 12, 2026}}</ref> He ended the season with 42 goals and 24 assists for 66 points in all 82 games played for the second consecutive season. His 66 points were third most on the Predators, trailing the 75 points by [[Filip Forsberg]] and 74 points by Ryan O'Reilly. His 42 goals were most on the Predators and tied with Minnesota Wild’ forward [[Matt Boldy]] for ninth most in the league. 10 of his 42 goals were game-winners, which were second most in the league, only behind the 12 of the 51 total goals scored by [[Montreal Canadiens]]’ forward [[Cole Caufield]].\n\n==Player profile==\n{{Quote box|width=31%|align=right|quote=You have so many guys that they skate fast and they can shoot hard, but the quickness of his release [stands out].
