2022 |access-date=11 October 2022}}</ref>\n\nStamkos has also been widely praised by his superiors for his leadership abilities and his ability to lead by example on and off the ice.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/already-a-scorer-stamkos-emerging-as-a-leader/c-590262 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190919110603/https://www.nhl.com/news/already-a-scorer-stamkos-emerging-as-a-leader/c-590262 |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 19, 2019 |title=Already a scorer, Stamkos emerging as a leader |website=nhl.com |publisher=National Hockey League |author=Dan Rosen |date=September 30, 2011 |access-date=July 6, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nhl.com/lightning/news/o-captain-my-captain |title=Bolts leaning on Stamkos's leadership in 3-1 series hole |author=Chris Krenn |website=nhl.com |publisher=Tampa Bay Lightning |date=April 29, 2024 |access-date=May 5, 2024}}</ref> In June 2015, during the [[2015 Stanley Cup Final]], Lightning teammate [[Valtteri Filppula]] described Stamkos as \"an example for everybody that works hard\".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.yahoo.com/entertainment/bp/jonathan-toews--steven-stamkos-and-how-leadership-is-born-203610118.html |title=Jonathan Toews, Steven Stamkos and how [[Jeremy Roenick]] also expressed admiration for Stamkos' leadership abilities in August 2016 by saying \"Every time I’ve talked to him, I’m so impressed. I am impressed with his leadership, his professionalism. I’m obviously impressed with his talent and what he can do.”<ref>{{cite web |url= https://thehockeywriters.com/jeremy-roenick-praises-lightning-and-stamkos-during-podcast/ |title=Jeremy Roenick Praises Lightning and Stamkos During Podcast |website=thehockeywriters.com |publisher=The Hockey Writers |author=Steven DiOssi |date=August 11, 2016 |access-date=July 11, 2023}}</ref> During the [[2022 Stanley Cup Final]] in June 2022, Lightning teammate [[Patrick Maroon]] labeled Stamkos as the \"heartbeat\" of the team.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3705716/2022/11/09/nhl99-steven-stamkos/ |title=Steven Stamkos evolved from a scorer into a complete player - and champion |website=theathletic.com |publisher=The Athletic |author=Joe Smith and Shayana Goldman |date=November 9, 2022 |access-date=July 10, 2023}}</ref> In June 2023, Stamkos was named the recipient of the [[Mark Messier Leadership Award]] for the [[2022–23 NHL season|2022–23 season]] by [[Mark Messier]] himself as the most superior leader within their sport by setting a positive example through on-ice performance and as a contributing member of society.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.wfla.com/sports/tampa-bay-lightning/tampa-bay-lightning-star-steven-stamkos-wins-mark-messier-nhl-leadership-award/ |title=Tampa Bay Lightning star Steven Stamkos wins Mark Messier NHL Leadership Award |first=Kaycee |last=Sloan |website=wfla.com |publisher=WFLA |date=June 29, 2023 |access-date=July 4, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://thehockeywriters.com/lightning-stamkos-lady-byng-messier-award-candidate/ |title= Steven Stamkos Should be in the Lady Byng & Messier Award Discussions |website=thehockeywriters.com |publisher=The Hockey Writers |author=Jim Bay |date=April 28, 2022 |access-date=August 5, 2025}}</ref>\n\nConsidered a [[franchise player]] while with the Lightning from 2008–2024, drafting Stamkos changed the Lightning's fortunes as a team both on and off the ice.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/325462-have-you-seen-stamkos |title=Steven Stamkos Is Making an Impact: Have You \"Seen Stamkos\"? |author=STEVE MEZ |website=bleacherreport.com |publisher=Bleacher Report |date=January 13, 2010 |access-date=May 5, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nhl/video/veterans-stamkos-hedman-lightnings-married-couple/ |title=Veterans Stamkos and Hedman are Lightning's 'married couple' |website=sportsnet.ca |publisher=Sportsnet |author=Colby Armstrong |date=May 4, 2022 |access-date=September 12, 2025}}</ref> Leading up to the start of the [[2008–09 NHL season|2008–09 season]], the Lightning centered their promotional efforts around Stamkos, including a website with the slogan \"Seen Stamkos?\", which included advertisements of Stamkos on billboards, signs and bumper stickers across the Tampa area.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tampabay.com/sports/2019/02/26/steven-stamkos-from-franchise-savior-to-franchise-leader/ |title=Steven Stamkos: From franchise savior to franchise leader |website=tampabaytimes.com |publisher=Tampa Bay Times |author=John Romano |date=February 26, 2019 |access-date=March 21, 2024}}</ref>\n\nFrom 2011 until 2024, Stamkos was known for his philanthropy as a major supporter of the charity, Ronald House Charities of Tampa with a lot of donations and telling fans after he and his wife Sandra got married in June 2017 to donate to the RHCO rather than give them wedding gifts, and has been known for welcoming families and fans with open arms within that charity to Lightning home games. In September 2019, Stamkos joined Tampa mayor [[Jane Castor]] in helping refurbish and reopen the local hockey rink, Tom Oliver Memorial Hockey Rink. This rink was originally donated to the city of Tampa in 1999 through a legacy initiative the NHL has.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.thescore.com/s/25076478 |title=Stamkos wins Mark Messier Leadership Award |website=thescore.com |publisher=thescore |author=Sean O'Leary |date=June 26, 2023 |access-date=May 5, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fox13news.com/news/steven-stamkos-left-lasting-impact-bay-area-nonprofits |title=Steven Stamkos left a lasting impact on Bay Area nonprofits |website=fox13news.com |publisher=Fox 13 News |author=Jennifer Kveglis |date=July 3, 2024 |access-date=December 31, 2024}}</ref>\n\nUpon unexpectedly leaving the Lightning in free agency and signing with the [[Nashville Predators]] in July 2024 after being unable to negotiate an extension with the Lightning, Lightning' defenceman [[Erik Černák]] reflected on Stamkos' leadership, the culture he built with the Lightning and his ability to welcome new teammates with open arms by saying when he first arrived to the team in 2018: \"He was the first guy who text men and welcomed me to the team: Don't worry we've got you. Just feel comfortable here.\"<ref>{{cite web|url=https://thehockeynews.com/nhl/nashville-predators/players/great-player-great-leader-great-friend-lightnings-cernak-on-predators-steven-stamkos |title='Great Player, Great Leader, Great Friend': Lightning's Cernak on Predators' Steven Stamkos |author=ROB COUCH |website=thehockeynews.com |publisher=The Hockey News |date=August 29, 2024 |access-date=September 6, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://thehockeynews.com/nhl/tampa-bay-lightning/latest-news/lightning-defender-opens-up-about-steven-stamkos-departure |title=Lightning Defender Opens Up About Steven Stamkos' Departure |author=Michael Derosa |website=thehockeynews.com |publisher=The Hockey News |date=August 28, 2024 |access-date=September 6, 2024}}</ref> In September 2024, [[Edmonton Oilers]] forward and captain [[Connor McDavid]] summarized Stamkos' tenure with the Lightning by portraying Stamkos as \"somebody who gave everything to that city, drafted first overall when they're not very good and becomes the captain and they go year after year running at the cup, I feel like he should've been a Tampa Bay Lightning for life, and ultimately that's not the way it worked.\"<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/onsi/breakaway/news-feed-page/nhl-stars-react-steven-stamkos-nashville-predators-jersey |title=NHL Stars React to Steven Stamkos in Predators Jersey |website=si.com |publisher=Sports Illustrated |author=Jon Alfano |date=October 8, 2024 |access-date=October 15, 2024}}</ref> The following month, longtime Lightning teammate and close friend [[Victor Hedman]], who was named the Lighting's new captain leading into the [[2024–25 NHL season|2024–25]] season, said Stamkos' departure was \"shocking and tough\" and reflected his legacy and culture created by saying “Everything speaks for itself, but just the person himself is going to be missed in the locker room, on the road, everywhere. It’s obviously going to be very different going into that locker room and not seeing No. 91.”<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nhl.com/news/steven-stamkos-set-for-emotional-return-to-face-tampa-bay-with-nashville |title=Stamkos set for emotional return to face Lightning with Predators |website=nhl.com |publisher=National Hockey League |author=Amaile Benjamin |date=October 27, 2024 |access-date=October 27, 2024}}</ref> Lightning head coach Jon Cooper followed up by saying: \"Coming into camp and not having him there, there was definitely a different feeling. Let's be honest: Steven Stamkos and the Tampa Bay Lightning are going to be synonymous with each other until the end of time. He did everything we asked of him for many, many years.\"<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/story/_/id/42055217/ex-lightning-star-steven-stamkos-returns-tampa-predator |title=Ex-Lightning star Steven Stamkos returns to Tampa with Predators |website=espn.com |publisher=ESPN |author=Greg Wyshynski |date=October 28, 2024 |access-date=October 30, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadspin.com/preds-steven-stamkos-returns-to-tampa-for-first-time-since-exit/ |title=Preds' Steven Stamkos returns to Tampa for first time since exit |website=deadspin.com |publisher=Deadspin |author=Field Level Media |date=October 27, 2024 |access-date=October 30, 2024}}</ref> Stamkos himself reflected on his lengthy tenure in Tampa and abrupt departure earlier in the 2024 off-season in by saying in his farewell article on ''[[The Players' Tribune]]'' published in July 2024, shortly after signing in Nashville earlier that month: \"I wanted to be the one who lived up to the hype, who took the organization where it dreamt to go. I remember those “Seen Stamkos?” billboards in 2008, and how much faith the Lightning put in me, and I hope I repaid it\".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theplayerstribune.com/posts/steven-stamkos-nhl-tampa-bay-lightning-hockey |title=Thank You, Tampa Bay |website=theplayerstribune.com |publisher=The Players tribune |author=Steven Stamkos |date=July 15, 2024 |access-date=October 15, 2024}}</ref>\n\n==Personal life==\nOn June 30, 2017, Stamkos married his long-time girlfriend Sandra Porzio. The ceremony was held in Toronto and was attended by several of his current and former teammates.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/tampa-bay-lightning-steven-stamkos-gets-married-in-toronto-290265496 |title=Steven Stamkos gets married in Toronto |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=July 1, 2017 |website=NHL.com |publisher=[[National Hockey League]] |access-date=October 26, 2017}}</ref> He and Sandra have two sons and a daughter.<ref>{{cite web |author=Mario Tirabassi |date=December 1, 2021 |title=Slavin's Stock Rising, Powerplay Changes? A Child is Being Born, and Other Blackhawks Bullets |url=https://www.bleachernation.com/blackhawks/2021/12/01/slavins-stock-rising-powerplay-changes-a-child-being-born-and-other-blackahwks-bullets/ |access-date=January 6, 2024 |website=bleachernation.com |publisher=Bleach Nation}}{{Dead link|date=January 2024}}</ref>\n\nOn October 26, 2017, the Sarnia Sting announced it was retiring Stamkos' number 91. This was done in a ceremony on January 12, 2018.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://sarniasting.com/?p=11498&preview=true |title=Sting to Retire Steven Stamkos' Number 91 |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=October 26, 2017 |website=sarniasting.com |publisher=[[Sarnia Sting]] |access-date=October 26, 2017}}</ref> Stamkos was the first player to have his jersey retired in the 23-year history of the Sting.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/lightning/news/steven-stamkos-to-have-jersey-retired-by-sarnia-sting-292473370|title=Stamkos to have sweater retired by Sarnia Sting|first=Bryan|last=Burns|work=[[Tampa Bay Lightning]]|date=October 31, 2017|access-date=November 1, 2017}}</ref>\n\n==International play==\n{{MedalTableTop|name=no}}\n{{MedalSport|Men's [[ice hockey]]}}\n{{MedalCountry | {{ihj|CAN}}}}\n{{MedalCompetition|[[Ice Hockey World Championship|World Championship]]}}\n{{MedalSilver | [[2009 IIHF World Championship|2009 Switzerland]] |}}\n{{MedalCompetition|[[World Cup of Hockey|Canada Cup / World Cup]]}}\n{{MedalGold | [[2016 World Cup of Hockey|2016 Toronto]] |}}{{MedalCompetition|[[IIHF World U20 Championship|World Junior Championships]]}}\n{{MedalGold | [[2008 World Junior Ice Hockey Championships|2008 Canada]] |}}\n{{MedalBottom}}\nStamkos played for [[Canada men's national junior ice hockey team|Canada]] in the [[2008 World Junior Ice Hockey Championships]], where he helped the team win a gold medal. After his rookie season with the Lightning, Stamkos was named to [[Canada men's national ice hockey team|Canada]]'s senior roster for the [[2009 Men's World Ice Hockey Championships]]. Stamkos continued to impress at the 2009 IIHF World Championships, scoring on his first career shift and meshing with fellow Lightning forward Martin St. Louis for seven goals, 11 points and a +9 plus-minus rating en route to a 2–1 loss to [[Russia men's national ice hockey team|Russia]] in the finals.<ref>{{cite news | url = http://lightning.nhl.com/team/app/?service=page&page=NewsPage&articleid=422307 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110714180437/http://lightning.nhl.com/team/app/?service=page&page=NewsPage&articleid=422307 | url-status = dead | archive-date = July 14, 2011 | title = St. Louis, Stamkos Net Silver at World Championships | publisher = lightning.nhl.com | date = May 11, 2009 | access-date = June 27, 2009}}</ref> He was also selected as a reserve by Canada for the [[Ice hockey at the 2010 Winter Olympics – Men's tournament|2010 Winter Olympics]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.tsn.ca/story/?id=310072 |title=Blues' Mason on Canada's stand-by list |access-date=December 7, 2017 |archive-date=December 1, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131201042946/http://www.tsn.ca/story/?id=310072 |url-status=dead}}</ref> and scored seven goals in Canada's fifth-place finish at the [[2013 IIHF World Championships|2013 World Championships]]. Stamkos was expected to be a major contributor for Canada in [[Sochi]] for the [[Ice hockey at the 2014 Winter Olympics – Men's tournament|2014 Winter Olympics]] and was named to the roster, but his leg injury sustained prior to the NHL Olympic break, including a broken [[tibia]] sustained in November 2013, prevented him from participating.<ref name=GLOBEMAIL>{{cite news|last1=Mirtle|first1=James|title=Steven Stamkos ruled out for Sochi Olympics|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/sports/olympics/steven-stamkos-announces-he-wont-play-in-sochi-olympics/article16714843/|access-date=October 5, 2014|work=The Globe and Mail|date=February 5, 2014}}</ref> The NHL prohibited its players to take part in the [[Ice hockey at the 2018 Winter Olympics – Men's tournament|2018]] and [[Ice hockey at the 2022 Winter Olympics – Men's tournament|2022 Winter Olympics]], which prevented him from participating in those games as well, and he was not selected for Team Canada at the [[Ice hockey at the 2026 Winter Olympics - Men's tournament|2026 Winter Olympics]], meaning he has never represented Canada at the Olympics during his entire career and is very likely at the point of his career where he will never be able to.<ref name=TAMPABAYTIMES>{{cite news|last1=Encina|first1=Eduardo|title=Lightning players won't get to live out Olympic dream|url=https://www.tampabay.com/sports/lightning/2021/12/22/lightning-players-wont-get-to-live-out-olympic-dream/|access-date=February 12, 2022|work=[[Tampa Bay Times]]|date=December 22, 2021}}</ref>\n\nOn March 2, 2016, Hockey Canada named Stamkos to its roster for the [[2016 World Cup of Hockey]] in [[Toronto]]. Stamkos won the tournament with Team Canada after a 2–1 win over Team Europe in game two of the best-of-three series. He recorded a goal as well as an assist in the tournament, with a plus-minus rating of +3.<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.si.com/nhl/2016/03/02/world-cup-of-hockey-rosters-announced-team-by-team-breakdown#|title=Analyzing 2016 World Cup of Hockey preliminary rosters|first=Allan|last=Muir|magazine=Sports Illustrated|date= March 2, 2016|access-date=March 3, 2015}}</ref>\n\n==Endorsements==\n[[File:Steve Stamkos - NHL Store 2011.jpg|thumb|upright|Stamkos doing press at the NHL Store in [[New York City]] in September 2011.]] \nFollowing his selection into the NHL in 2008, Stamkos signed a number of sponsorships, including an athlete's agreement with [[Nike, Inc.|Nike]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=El-Bashir|first1=Tarik|title=Capitals' Alex Ovechkin signs endorsement deal with Nike|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/capitals-insider/post/capitals-alex-ovechkin-signs-endorsement-deal-with-nike/2011/09/01/gIQASgqZvJ_blog.html|access-date=March 13, 2018|newspaper=The Washington Post|date=September 1, 2011|quote=Tampa Bay's Steven Stamkos also has a deal with the iconic shoe company}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Erlendsson|first1=Erik|title=Bolts' Stamkos 'in awe' during Nike star-studded shoot|url=http://www.tbo.com/sports/lightning/bolts-stamkos-in-awe-during-nike-star-studded-shoot-20151108/|access-date=March 13, 2018|date=November 8, 2015|archive-date=March 14, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180314174102/http://www.tbo.com/sports/lightning/bolts-stamkos-in-awe-during-nike-star-studded-shoot-20151108/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was featured in a web-only Nike commercial called ''Forget Everything'', which was released to coincide with his first game in his hometown of Unionville on October 28, 2008. He has also endorsed [[Tissot]] watches as of October 2008.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Williamson|first1=Cameron|title=They suit, they score: Are hockey players the next style icons?|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/life/fashion-and-beauty/fashion/they-suit-they-score-are-hockey-players-the-next-style-icons/article9354563/|access-date=March 13, 2018|newspaper=The Globe and Mail|date=March 9, 2013|quote=Ontario-born Steven Stamkos, a top scorer with the Tampa Bay Lightning, is currently an ambassador for the Swiss watch brand Tissot}}</ref> On June 22, 2011, at the 2011 NHL Awards Show, Stamkos was named the cover athlete for the [[EA Sports]]' ''[[NHL 12]]'' video game.<ref>{{cite web|title=Steven Stamkos the New Face of EA Sports NHL 12|url=https://www.nhl.com/lightning/news/steven-stamkos-the-new-face-of-ea-sports-nhl-12/c-566827|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180314042850/https://www.nhl.com/lightning/news/steven-stamkos-the-new-face-of-ea-sports-nhl-12/c-566827|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 14, 2018|website=NHL.com|access-date=March 13, 2018|date=June 23, 2011}}</ref> In October 2013, he played the leading role in a web commercial for [[Coca-Cola Zero]] named \"Shawn Warford's Moment Zero.\" Most recently, in January 2014, Stamkos signed a multi-year sponsorship with [[Sport Chek]], Canada's largest sports retailer.<ref>{{cite web|title=Sport Chek Signs Multi-Year Strategic Partnership with Canadian NHL Superstar Steven Stamkos|url=https://investors.canadiantire.ca/English/media/news-releases/press-release-details/2014/Sport-Chek-Signs-Multi-Year-Strategic-Partnership-with-Canadian-NHL-Superstar-Steven-Stamkos/default.aspx|website=investors.canadiantire.ca|access-date=March 13, 2018|date=January 6, 2014}}</ref>\n\n==Career statistics==\n\n===Regular season and playoffs===\n<small>'''Bold''' indicates led league</small>\n{| border=\"0\" cellpadding=\"1\" cellspacing=\"0\" style=\"text-align:center; width:60em;\"\n|- bgcolor=\"#e0e0e0\"\n! in 2020 (Quintin Soloviev).jpg |bSize=450 |cWidth=230 |cHeight=300 |oTop=30 |oLeft=120 |Location=center}}\n| image_size = \n| caption = MacKinnon with the [[Colorado Avalanche]] in January 2020\n| birth_date = {{birth date and age|1995|9|1}}\n| birth_place = [[Halifax, Nova Scotia]], Canada\n| height_ft = 6\n| height_in = 0\n| weight_lb = 200\n| position = [[Centre (ice hockey)|Centre]]\n| shoots = Right\n| league = [[National Hockey League|NHL]]\n| team = [[Colorado Avalanche]]\n| ntl_team = CAN\n| draft = 1st overall\n| draft_year = 2013\n| draft_team = [[Colorado Avalanche]]\n| career_start = 2013\n| career_end = \n| website = \n}}\n\n'''Nathan Raymond MacKinnon''' (born September 1, 1995) is a Canadian professional [[ice hockey]] player who is a [[Centre (ice hockey)|centre]] and [[Captain (ice hockey)#Alternate captains|alternate captain]] for the [[Colorado Avalanche]] of the [[National Hockey League]] (NHL). MacKinnon was selected [[List of first overall NHL draft picks|first overall]] by the Avalanche in the [[2013 NHL entry draft]].\n\nMacKinnon won the [[Stanley Cup]] with the Avalanche in [[2022 Stanley Cup Final|2022]]. Individually, MacKinnon has been awarded the [[Calder Memorial Trophy]] in [[2013–14 NHL season|2014]] as the top rookie, the [[Lady Byng Memorial Trophy]] in [[2019–20 NHL season|2020]] for sportsmanship and performance, the [[Hart Memorial Trophy]] in as the most valuable player in [[2023–24 NHL season|2024]], the [[Ted Lindsay Award]] in 2024 as the most outstanding player and the [[Maurice \"Rocket\" Richard Trophy]] winner as the NHL's leading goal-scorer in [[2025–26 NHL season|2026]]. He was also a finalist for the Hart Trophy in [[2017–18 NHL season|2018]], 2020, [[2020–21 NHL season|2021]] and 2026 and the Ted Lindsay Award in 2018, 2020 and [[2024–25 NHL season|2025]]. These achievements have made him widely regarded as one of the best ice hockey players of his generation.<ref>{{cite news |last=Baugh |first=Peter |title=Nathan MacKinnon, at long last, is a Hart Trophy winner: 'I didn't know if it was going to happen' |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5598640/2024/06/27/nathan-mackinnon-hart-trophy-avalanche/ |access-date=2024-06-29 |work=The New York Times |date=June 28, 2024 |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Nathan MacKinnon Cements Himself Among NHL Greats After Winning Hart Memorial Trophy and Ted Lindsay Award |url=https://www.nhl.com/avalanche/news/nathan-mackinnon-2024-nhl-awards |access-date=2024-06-29 |website=NHL.com |date=2024-06-28}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Joyce |first1=Gare |title=How Nathan career==\n\n===Early life===\nMacKinnon was born in [[Halifax, Nova Scotia]], and grew up playing in the [[minor ice hockey]] system of [[Cole Harbour, Nova Scotia]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Joyce |first1=Gare |title=Nate the kid |url=https://insider.espn.com/nhl/insider/news/story?id=4943564 |publisher=ESPN |access-date=May 14, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161008083621/https://insider.espn.com/nhl/insider/news/story?id=4943564 |archive-date=October 8, 2016 |date=February 25, 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://canadiansportscene.com/mackinnon-scores-overtime-winner-for-avalanche-in-3-2-win-over-flames/ |title=Nathan MacKinnon when he scores overtime winner for Avalanche in 3-2 win over Flames |date=April 15, 2019 |access-date=February 6, 2021 |archive-date=October 30, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201030034447/https://canadiansportscene.com/mackinnon-scores-overtime-winner-for-avalanche-in-3-2-win-over-flames/ |url-status=live}}</ref> As an atom aged player (under 11), MacKinnon recorded 200 points in 50 games.<ref name=\"nextnextone\">{{cite news|last=Penton|first=Kirk|title=The next Next One?|url=http://www.torontosun.com/sports/hockey/2011/01/02/16737616.html|publisher=[[Toronto Sun]]|date=2011-01-02|access-date=2011-01-05|archive-date=January 6, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110106033952/http://www.torontosun.com/sports/hockey/2011/01/02/16737616.html|url-status=live}}</ref> When MacKinnon was 12 and 13, he played Bantam AAA for the Cole Harbour Red Wings, recording seasons of 110 and 145 points, respectively.<ref name=\"nextnextone\"/> After these two seasons, MacKinnon enrolled at [[Shattuck-Saint Mary's]] in [[Faribault, Minnesota]].<ref name=\"comparisons\">{{cite news|last=McDonald|first=Alyssa|title=Crosby comparisons: MacKinnon brings offence to U17s|url=http://www.hockeycanada.ca/index.php/ci_id/16980/la_id/1/ss_id/74637/nr_id/156356.htm|publisher=[[Hockey Canada]]|date=2011-01-02|access-date=2011-01-05|archive-date=May 14, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110514182703/http://www.hockeycanada.ca/index.php/ci_id/16980/la_id/1/ss_id/74637/nr_id/156356.htm|url-status=live}}</ref> MacKinnon chose to leave his hometown and attend the Minnesota [[boarding school]] because of the strength of its ice hockey program.<ref name=\"comparisons\"/> In his first season at Shattuck-Saint Mary's playing with the Bantam Tier I program, he scored 101 points in 58 games to finish second in team scoring.<ref>{{cite web|title=2009–2010 Boys Bantam Tier I stats|url=http://hockey.s-sm.org/teams/2009-2010/boys/bantam-tier-i/boys-bantam-tier-i-stats|publisher=[[Shattuck-Saint Mary's]]|access-date=2011-01-05|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101220024027/http://hockey.s-sm.org/teams/2009-2010/boys/bantam-tier-i/boys-bantam-tier-i-stats|archive-date=December 20, 2010|df=mdy-all}}</ref> For the 2010–11 season, MacKinnon joined the under-16 Midget program at the school. Despite being the team's second-youngest player, MacKinnon was averaging more than two points a game and was second in team scoring at the midway point of the season.<ref name=\"nextnextone\"/> During the season, MacKinnon was named to the team that represented Nova Scotia in the [[Ice hockey at the 2011 Canada Winter Games|ice hockey tournament]] at the [[2011 Canada Winter Games]]. MacKinnon scored eight goals and eleven points to finish fourth in tournament scoring as Nova Scotia finished in seventh place.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Clark |first1=Ryan S. |title=The legend of Nathan MacKinnon at the 2011 Canada Games |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2010250/2020/08/24/the-legend-of-nathan-mackinnon-at-the-2011-canada-games/ |publisher=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=May 15, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250515021603/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2010250/2020/08/24/the-legend-of-nathan-mackinnon-at-the-2011-canada-games/ |archive-date=May 15, 2025 |date=August 24, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Standings/statistics - 2011 Canada Winter Games|url=http://www.hockeycanada.ca/index.php/ci_id/158776/la_id/1.htm|publisher=Hockey Canada|access-date=2011-12-26}}</ref> MacKinnon finished his second season at Shattuck-Saint Mary's with 93 points in 40 games played, and was second on the team with 45 goals scored.<ref>{{cite web|title=2010–2011 Boys U16 Stats|url=http://hockey.s-sm.org/teams/2010-2011/boys/u16/boys-u16-stats|publisher=Shattuck-Saint Mary's|access-date=2011-05-06|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110817232409/http://hockey.s-sm.org/teams/2010-2011/boys/u16/boys-u16-stats|archive-date=August 17, 2011|df=mdy-all}}</ref>\n\n[[File:Nathan MacKinnon Mooseheads-1.jpg|thumb|upright|left|MacKinnon in October 2012. He played with the [[Halifax Mooseheads]] for two years during his [[major junior]] career.]]\n\n===Junior===\nHeading into the 2011 [[Quebec Major Junior Hockey League]] (QMJHL) Draft, MacKinnon was widely regarded as the favourite to be selected first overall and was ranked by QMJHL Central Scouting as the best available player.<ref>{{cite news|last=Wuest|first=Matthew|title=MacKinnon tops QMJHL draft ranking|url=http://www.metronews.ca/halifax/blog/post/847646|publisher=[[Metro International|Metro Halifax]]|date=2011-05-01|access-date=2011-07-24}}{{dead link|date=February 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes}}</ref> Despite this, MacKinnon spent the day of the draft skating with the [[Omaha Lancers]] of the [[United States Hockey League]] (USHL), as he was considering playing either [[college ice hockey]] in the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA) or [[Junior ice hockey#Major junior|major junior ice hockey]] in the QMJHL.<ref>{{cite news|last=Sager|first=Neate|title=QMJHL: Nathan MacKinnon skates in Omaha on draft day|url=https://ca.sports.yahoo.com/juniorhockey/blog/buzzing_the_net/post/QMJHL-Nathan-MacKinnon-skates-in-Omaha-on-draft?urn=juniorhockey-360208|publisher=[[Yahoo! Sports]]|date=2011-06-04|access-date=2011-07-24|archive-date=March 13, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160313152100/https://ca.sports.yahoo.com/juniorhockey/blog/buzzing_the_net/post/QMJHL-Nathan-MacKinnon-skates-in-Omaha-on-draft?urn=juniorhockey-360208|url-status=live}}</ref> On June 4, 2011, MacKinnon was selected first overall by the [[Baie-Comeau Drakkar]] in the 2011 QMJHL Draft.<ref>{{cite news|title=Baie-Comeau takes Cole Harbour's Nathan MacKinnon first in QMJHL draft|url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=564819|publisher=[[National Hockey League]]|date=2011-06-04|access-date=2011-07-24|archive-date=October 25, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121025020701/http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=564819|url-status=dead}}</ref> Because MacKinnon did not speak [[French language|French]], there was speculation that he would follow through with his option to play in the USHL until he was eligible for the NCAA, unless his rights were traded to a different QMJHL team.<ref>{{cite news|last=Walling|first=Alex|title=Walling: MacKinnon the second coming of Sid the Kid?|url=https://www.tsn.ca/nhl/story/?id=372355|publisher=[[The Sports Network]]|date=2011-07-23|access-date=2011-07-24|archive-date=August 27, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110827174928/http://www.tsn.ca/nhl/story/?id=372355|url-status=live}}</ref> On July 13, 2011, MacKinnon's rights were traded to the [[Halifax Mooseheads]] for Carl Gélinas, Francis Turbide, the Mooseheads' first round draft picks in 2012 and 2013 and the [[Quebec Remparts]]' first round draft pick in 2013, previously acquired by Halifax.<ref>{{cite news|title=Mooseheads acquire top draft pick MacKinnon from Drakkar|url=https://www.tsn.ca/chl/story/?id=371647|publisher=The Sports Network|date=2011-07-19|access-date=2011-07-24|archive-date=October 6, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131006092923/http://www.tsn.ca/chl/story/?id=371647|url-status=live}}</ref> The Mooseheads had been attempting to acquire MacKinnon since Baie-Comeau was awarded the first overall pick in the 2011 draft.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 13, 2011 |title=Mooseheads land Q's top pick MacKinnon |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/hockey/juniors/qmjhl-mooseheads-mackinnon/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251220180840/https://www.sportsnet.ca/hockey/juniors/qmjhl-mooseheads-mackinnon/ |archive-date=December 20, 2025 |access-date=December 20, 2025 |website=www.sportsnet.ca |language=en}}</ref> MacKinnon scored his first QMJHL [[hat-trick]] on December 3, 2011, scoring five goals in a 6–4 victory over the Quebec Remparts.<ref>{{cite news|last=Palov|first=Willy|title=5-goal game for Moose rookie|url=http://thechronicleherald.ca/sports/39262-5-goal-game-moose-rookie|publisher=[[The Chronicle Herald]]|date=2011-12-04|access-date=2011-12-04|archive-date=December 7, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111207041855/http://thechronicleherald.ca/sports/39262-5-goal-game-moose-rookie|url-status=live}}</ref> In a league of 18- and 19-year-olds, MacKinnon was only 16 when he accomplished this. The opposing coach for the Remparts was his future coach with the [[Colorado Avalanche]], NHL Hall of Famer [[Patrick Roy]]. With five goals in one game, he tied the Mooseheads record for the most goals in a single game held by [[Jason King (ice hockey)|Jason King]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Sager|first=Neate|title=Saturday's 3 Stars: Nathan MacKinnon makes some memories for Mooseheads by making mincemeat of Remparts|url=https://ca.sports.yahoo.com/juniorhockey/blog/buzzing_the_net/post/Saturday-s-3-Stars-Nathan-MacKinnon-makes-some-?urn=juniorhockey-wp4370|publisher=Yahoo! Sports|date=2011-12-04|access-date=2011-12-26|archive-date=June 11, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150611133223/https://ca.sports.yahoo.com/juniorhockey/blog/buzzing_the_net/post/Saturday-s-3-Stars-Nathan-MacKinnon-makes-some-?urn=juniorhockey-wp4370|url-status=live}}</ref>\n\nOn May 26, 2013, MacKinnon led the Mooseheads to their first [[Memorial Cup]] championship. He was also named Most Valuable Player, scoring a tournament-best seven goals and six assists in four games, and earned a spot on the Tournament All-Star team.<ref>{{cite news |date=2013-05-26 |title=Nathan MacKinnon's hat trick leads Halifax Mooseheads to Memorial Cup win |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/hockey/nhl/nathan-mackinnon-s-hat-trick-leads-halifax-mooseheads-to-memorial-cup-win-1.1305498 |access-date=2024-02-12 |work=CBC News}}</ref>\n\n===Colorado Avalanche (2013–present)===\n====Early years, team and scoring difficulties (2013–2017)====\n[[File:Nathan MacKinnon Avalanche-2.jpg|thumb|MacKinnon with the [[Colorado Avalanche]] in December 2013]]\nOn June 19, 2013, leading up to the [[2013 NHL entry draft]], Avalanche head coach [[Patrick Roy]], who owned the first overall selection, stated publicly that his team would select MacKinnon if the draft were held then, despite widespread speculation that the team was likely to select defenceman [[Seth Jones]], who grew up in [[Denver|Denver, Colorado]].<ref>{{cite web |author=Sager, Neate |date=June 19, 2013 |title=Colorado Avalanche pass on Seth Jones, will take a forward |url=https://ca.sports.yahoo.com/blogs/jrhockey-buzzing-the-net/colorado-avalanche-pass-seth-jones-forward-140243426.html |publisher=[[Yahoo!]] |access-date=June 27, 2013 |archive-date=June 24, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130624194614/http://ca.sports.yahoo.com/blogs/jrhockey-buzzing-the-net/colorado-avalanche-pass-seth-jones-forward-140243426.html? |url-status=live}}</ref> \"It would be tough for us not to take MacKinnon,\" Roy told ''[[ESPN The Magazine]]''. Roy also refused to rule out trading the pick.<ref>{{cite news |date=June 25, 2013 |title=Roy: MacKinnon Would Be Selection If Draft Was Held Now|url=https://www.tsn.ca/nhl/story/?id=426239 |publisher=[[The Sports Network]] |access-date=January 6, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131231235627/http://www.tsn.ca/nhl/story/?id=426239 |archive-date= December 31, 2013}}</ref> On June 26, Avalanche Director of Amateur Scouting Richard Pracey reiterated the team's decision to pick MacKinnon.<ref>{{cite news |date=June 27, 2013 |title=Avalanche Reiterate They Have F MacKinnon In Their Sights |url=https://www.tsn.ca/nhl/story/?id=426374 |publisher=[[The Sports Network]] |access-date=January 6, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131205231624/http://www.tsn.ca/nhl/story/?id=426374 |archive-date=December 5, 2013}}</ref> On June 30, the Avalanche did indeed use their first overall pick in the draft to select MacKinnon (while Seth Jones was chosen fourth overall by the [[Nashville Predators]].<ref>{{cite web |author=The Canadian Press |date=June 30, 2013 |title=Avs pick MacKinnon first overall in NHL draft |url=http://www.sportsnet.ca/hockey/nhl/avs-select-mackinnon-with-first-pick-in-nhl-draft/ |publisher=[[Sportsnet]] |access-date=June 30, 2013 |author-link=The Canadian Press |archive-date=July 3, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130703035655/http://www.sportsnet.ca/hockey/nhl/avs-select-mackinnon-with-first-pick-in-nhl-draft/ |url-status=live}}</ref> MacKinnon was signed to his first NHL contract, a three-year entry-level deal, with the Avalanche on July 9.<ref>{{cite news| author=The Canadian Press| url = https://www.tsn.ca/nhl/story/?id=427347 | title = Avs sign first-overall pick to entry-level deal | publisher = [[The Sports Network]] |date=July 9, 2013 |access-date=January 6, 2015 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20131212020642/http://www.tsn.ca/nhl/story/?id=427347 | archive-date=December 12, 2013}}</ref> MacKinnon made his NHL debut to begin the [[2013–14 NHL season|2013–14]] season on October 2, becoming the youngest hockey player to ever dress in a regular season game for the Colorado Avalanche franchise, registering two assists on two goals by [[Jamie McGinn]] in a 6–1 victory over the visiting [[Anaheim Ducks]].<ref>{{cite web |agency=Associated Press |date=October 3, 2013 |title=Avs' MacKinnon gets 2 points in rout of Ducks |url=http://www.sportsnet.ca/hockey/nhl/avs-mackinnon-gets-2-points-in-rout-of-ducks/ |publisher=[[Sportsnet]] |access-date=October 3, 2013 |archive-date=October 5, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131005045725/http://www.sportsnet.ca/hockey/nhl/avs-mackinnon-gets-2-points-in-rout-of-ducks/ |url-status=live}}</ref> MacKinnon scored his first NHL goal October 12, against [[Michal Neuvirth]] of the [[Washington Capitals]] during the second period at the [[Capital One Arena|Verizon Center]].<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.sbnation.com/nhl/2013/10/12/4832460/avs-vs-capitals-nathan-mackinnon-scores-first-nhl-goal | title = Nathan MacKinnon scores first NHL goal | publisher = sbnation.com | date = 2013-10-12 | access-date = 2013-10-12 | archive-date = October 12, 2018 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20181012231857/https://www.sbnation.com/nhl/2013/10/12/4832460/avs-vs-capitals-nathan-mackinnon-scores-first-nhl-goal | url-status = live}}</ref> As the season went on, MacKinnon's role increased, as he was placed on the top two offensive lines. He claimed his first NHL record in becoming the youngest player to record back-to-back two-goal games from January 4–6, 2014, beating [[Dale Hawerchuk]]'s of the original [[Winnipeg Jets (1972–1996)|Winnipeg Jets]] from 1981. MacKinnon later compiled a 13-game point streak from January 25 to March 6, surpassing [[Wayne Gretzky]] (who turned 19 during his first season having a January birthday) to have the longest scoring streak by an 18-year-old in NHL history.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.cbssports.com/nhl/eye-on-hockey/24471662/nathan-mackinnons-extends-streak-breaks-wayne-gretzkys-record | title = Nathan MacKinnon extends streak, break Wayne Gretzky's record | work = [[CBS Sports]] | date = 2014-03-07 | access-date = 2014-03-07 | archive-date = January 26, 2015 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150126092046/http://www.cbssports.com/nhl/eye-on-hockey/24471662/nathan-mackinnons-extends-streak-breaks-wayne-gretzkys-record | url-status = live}}</ref> MacKinnon finished the season appearing in all 82 games and led all rookies with 24 goals and 39 assists for 63 points as the Avalanche finished the season as the second seed in the Western Conference to qualify for the playoffs for the first time since [[2010 Stanley Cup playoffs|2010]]. MacKinnon became just the third player in the NHL to record seven points in his first two playoff games with a goal and six assists in the first two contests against the seventh-seeded [[Minnesota Wild]] in the opening round of the [[2014 Stanley Cup playoffs|2014 playoffs]] although the Avalanche would eventually fall to the Wild in seven games, despite initially building a 3–2 series lead. On June 24, MacKinnon won the [[Calder Memorial Trophy]] for the rookie of the year, becoming the youngest player to ever win this trophy and third in Avalanche history behind [[Chris Drury]] in [[1998–99 NHL season|1998–99]] and [[Gabriel Landeskog]] in [[2011–12 NHL season|2011–12]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=723668 | title = Avalanche's Nathan MacKinnon wins Calder Trophy | publisher = [[National Hockey League]] | date = 2014-06-24 | access-date = 2014-06-24 | archive-date = May 2, 2015 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150502112931/http://www.nhl.com/ice/news.htm?id=723668 | url-status = dead}}</ref> He was subsequently selected to the [[NHL All-Rookie Team]].\n\nMacKinnon recorded his first career NHL hat trick on February 22, 2015, in a 5–4 win over the [[Tampa Bay Lightning]] to become the youngest player in Avalanche history to record a hat trick.<ref>{{cite news |last=Chambers |first=Mike |title=Nathan MacKinnon scores hat trick as Avs top Lightning |work=[[The Denver Post]] |date=February 22, 2015 |url=http://www.denverpost.com/avalanche/ci_27580005/nathan-mackinnon-scores-hat-trick-avs-top-lightning |access-date=February 23, 2015 |archive-date=February 23, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150223184523/http://www.denverpost.com/avalanche/ci_27580005/nathan-mackinnon-scores-hat-trick-avs-top-lightning |url-status=live}}</ref> \nLater in the same game, MacKinnon blocked a shot, resulting in a broken foot. He continued to play several more games and sustained a broken nose on February 26 in a 3–1 loss to the Minnesota Wild as a result from a hit by Wild’ forward [[Sean Bergenheim]]. He played one more game after these ailments, which was a 4–3 victory over the [[Pittsburgh Penguins]] on March 4 before missing the last 18 games of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.denverpost.com/2015/03/06/nathan-mackinnon-suffers-broken-foot-to-miss-rest-of-avs-regular-season/ |title=Nathan MacKinnon suffers broken foot, to miss rest of Avs' regular season |website=denverpost.com |publisher=Denver Post |author=Trey Frei |date=March 6, 2015 |access-date=April 20, 2026}}</ref> Prior to getting sidelined, MacKinnon saw his individual production drop having recorded 14 goals and 24 assists for 38 points in the first 64 games of his sophomore NHL season and the Avalanche would struggle as a team having not qualifying for the [[2015 Stanley Cup playoffs|playoffs]].\n[[File:Nathan MacKinnon - Colorado Avalanche.jpg|thumb|upright|left|MacKinnon with the Avalanche in November 2014]]\nOn March 18, 2016, in a 4–3 victory over the [[Calgary Flames]], MacKinnon suffered a torn [[medial collateral ligament]] (MCL), causing him to miss the final 10 games of the [[2015–16 NHL season|2015–16 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/nhl-puck-daddy/nathan-mackinnon-injures-knee-in-colorado-shootout-win-060203097.html |title=Nathan MacKinnon injures knee in Colorado shootout win |website=yahoo.com |publisher=Yahoo Sports |author=Josh Cooper |date=March 19, 2026 |access-date=April 20, 2026}}</ref> Prior to his injury, MacKinnon recorded 21 goals and 31 assists for 52 points in the first 72 games. Despite his increased productivity compared to the year prior, the Avalanche continued to struggle as a team as they missed the [[2016 Stanley Cup playoffs|playoffs]] once more.\n\nOn July 8, 2016, MacKinnon as a restricted free agent re-signed with the Avalanche, agreeing to a seven-year, $44.1&nbsp;million contract that averages $6.3&nbsp;million per season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Avs sign MacKinnon to seven-year, $44.1M deal|url=https://www.tsn.ca/avs-sign-mackinnon-to-seven-year-44-1m-deal-1.523726|website=TSN.ca|access-date=March 4, 2018|date=July 8, 2016|archive-date=March 5, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180305142619/https://www.tsn.ca/avs-sign-mackinnon-to-seven-year-44-1m-deal-1.523726|url-status=live}}</ref> On October 13, two days before the [[2016–17 NHL season|2016–17 season]] started, MacKinnon was announced as an alternate captain for the Avalanche.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.nhl.com/avalanche/news/avs-name-2016-17-alternate-captains-282624108 | title = Avs Name Alternate Captains For 2016-17 Season | publisher = [[Colorado Avalanche]] | date = October 16, 2016 | access-date = October 14, 2016 | archive-date = May 18, 2021 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20210518140117/https://www.nhl.com/avalanche/news/avs-name-2016-17-alternate-captains/c-282624108 | url-status = live}}</ref> MacKinnon would be named to his first [[National Hockey League All-Star Game|NHL All-Star Game]] on January 10, 2017, as the lone representative of the Avalanche.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Frei|first1=Terri|title=Nathan MacKinnon named Colorado Avalanche rep at NHL All-Star Game|url=https://www.denverpost.com/2017/01/10/nathan-mackinnon-nhl-all-star-game-2017/|access-date=March 4, 2018|publisher=The Denver Post|date=January 10, 2017|archive-date=March 5, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180305142817/https://www.denverpost.com/2017/01/10/nathan-mackinnon-nhl-all-star-game-2017/|url-status=live}}</ref> MacKinnon ended the season playing in all 82 games with 16 goals and 37 assists for 53 points as the Avalanche missed the [[2017 Stanley Cup playoffs|playoffs]] for the third consecutive season and finished last place in the standings overall.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nhl/news/2017-18-team-by-team-nhl-season-outlook-previewing-the-colorado-avalanche/ |title=2017-18 team-by-team NHL season outlook: Previewing the Colorado Avalanche |author=Cody Benjamin |work=CBS Sports |date=August 14, 2017 |access-date=June 28, 2024}}</ref>\n\n====Ascent to stardom, Hart Trophy, Rocket Richard Trophy, Stanley Cup championship (2017–present)====\nIn the 2017 off-season, MacKinnon hired a [[Sport psychology|sports psychologist]], which drastically helped him improve his play and emerge as one of the league's premier players during the [[2017–18 NHL season|2017–18 season]].<ref>{{cite web|title='I need him': Meet the behind-the-scenes trainer who has helped Nathan MacKinnon take off|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2756990/2021/08/11/i-need-him-meet-the-behind-the-scenes-trainer-who-has-helped-nathan-mackinnon-take-off/|website=[[The Athletic]]|access-date=January 19, 2022|date=August 11, 2021|archive-date=January 19, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220119194212/https://theathletic.com/2756990/2021/08/11/i-need-him-meet-the-behind-the-scenes-trainer-who-has-helped-nathan-mackinnon-take-off/|url-status=live}}</ref> On November 16, 2017, MacKinnon recorded his first career five-point game in a 6–2 win over the [[Washington Capitals]] having done so with a goal on Capitals' goaltender [[Philipp Grubauer]] and four assists on two goals by captain [[Gabriel Landeskog]] and goals by [[Colin Wilson (ice hockey)|Colin Wilson]] and [[Mikko Rantanen]], respectively.<ref name = \"first star\"/> He was again selected the following year for the [[2018 NHL All-Star Game]].<ref>{{cite web|title=MacKinnon Selected To NHL All-Star Game|url=https://www.nhl.com/avalanche/news/mackinnon-selected-to-2018-nhl-all-star-game-294839910|website=NHL.com|access-date=March 4, 2018|date=January 5, 2018|archive-date=March 5, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180305202717/https://www.nhl.com/avalanche/news/mackinnon-selected-to-2018-nhl-all-star-game/c-294839910|url-status=live}}</ref> On January 30, 2018, in a 4–3 loss to the [[Vancouver Canucks]], MacKinnon suffered a shoulder injury from a hit by Canucks’ defenseman [[Alexander Edler]], resulting in him missing the next eight games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.denverpost.com/2018/01/30/nathan-mackinnon-avalanche-injury-update/ |title=Avalanche center Nathan MacKinnon leaves game with upper body injury after collision with Vancouver defensemen |website=denverpost.com |publisher=Denver Post |author=Teh Denver Post |date=February 1, 2018 |access-date=April 20, 2026}}</ref> MacKinnon was named the NHL's First Star of the Week for February 26–March 4, 2018, after scoring five goals, six assists, with four power play points, a +6 rating, and 31 shots in four games.<ref name = \"first star\">{{cite web|title=MacKinnon leads 3 Stars of the Week|url=https://www.nhl.com/news/nathan-mackinnon-patrik-laine-aleksander-barkov-named-nhl-3-stars-296635006|website=NHL.com|access-date=March 5, 2018|date=March 5, 2018|archive-date=April 14, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230414203941/https://www.nhl.com/news/nathan-mackinnon-patrik-laine-aleksander-barkov-named-nhl-3-stars/c-296635006|url-status=live}}</ref> MacKinnon recorded his second career five-point game in a 7–1 win over the [[Minnesota Wild]] (scoring two goals on Wild goaltender [[Devan Dubnyk]] and adding three assists on goals by [[Tyson Barrie]], [[Matt Nieto]] and Mikko Rantanen) on March 2, 2018.<ref name = \"first star\"/> MacKinnon finished his breakout [[2017–18 Colorado Avalanche season|season]] playing in 74 games with 39 goals and 58 assists for 97 points to help the Avalanche finish the season as the eighth and final seed in the Western Conference to clinch a playoff spot for the first time since [[2013–14 NHL season|2014]], when MacKinnon was rookie. His 97 points ranked first on the Avalanche and fifth in the league. His 39 goals were most on the Avalanche and tied [[Tampa Bay Lightning]] forward [[Nikita Kucherov]] and [[New Jersey Devils]] forward [[Taylor Hall]] for seventh in the league. 12 of MacKinnon’s 39 goals were game winners, tying Tampa Bay Lightning’ forward [[Brayden Point]] for league leaders in game winning goals. In the [[2018 Stanley Cup playoffs|2018 playoffs]], the Avalanche were defeated in the first round in six games by the [[Presidents' Trophy]]-winning [[Nashville Predators]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/recap/_/gameId/401029159 |title=Predators beat Avs 5-0 in Game 6 to win first-round series |author=AP |website=[[ESPN]] |publisher=ESPN |date=June 15, 2024 |access-date=April 22, 2018}}</ref> MacKinnon recorded six points (three goals and three assists) in all six playoff games during the playoffs. On April 26, MacKinnon was named a finalist for the [[Ted Lindsay Award]] as the NHL's most outstanding player for the first time in his career which was eventually won by [[Edmonton Oilers]] forward and captain [[Connor McDavid]].<ref>{{cite web|last1=Amadon|first1=Brett|title=Ted Lindsay finalists unveiled|url=https://www.nhl.com/news/ted-lindsay-award-finalists-unveiled-nhl-most-outstanding-player-298278196|website=NHL.com|access-date=April 27, 2018|date=April 26, 2018|archive-date=April 28, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180428011659/https://www.nhl.com/news/ted-lindsay-award-finalists-unveiled-nhl-most-outstanding-player/c-298278196|url-status=live}}</ref> The following day he was named a [[Hart Memorial Trophy]] finalist for the first time in his career as the NHL's most valuable player in the regular season. The award was eventually won by New Jersey Devils' forward Taylor Hall as MacKinnon finished second in the voting.<ref>{{cite web |title=Avalanche's MacKinnon Edged Out Of NHL's MVP Award |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/colorado/news/mackinnon-edged-out-mvp/ |publisher=CBS News |access-date=May 15, 2025 |date=June 20, 2018}}</ref>\n\nMacKinnon finished the [[2018–19 NHL season|2018–19 season]] with 99 points (41 goals, 58 assists) in all 82 games played, one-point short of his first career 100-point season. After the Avalanche as a team clinched the eighth and final playoff spot in the West for the second straight season, MacKinnon and the Avalanche defeated the top-seeded [[Calgary Flames]] in five games, marking the first time the Avalanche won a playoff series during MacKinnon's tenure with the team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nhl.com/news/colorado-avalanche-calgary-flames-game-5-recap-306888892 |title=Avalanche win Western series, top Flames in Game 5 |author=Aaron Vickers |website=nhl.com |publisher=NHL |date=April 20, 2019 |access-date=June 15, 2024}}</ref> After upsetting the Flames in the opening round, MacKinnon and the Avalanche would eventually be defeated in the second round in seven games by the [[San Jose Sharks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/recap/_/gameId/401129143 |title=Pavelski leads Sharks past Avalanche in game 7 |author=AP |website=[[ESPN]] |publisher=ESPN |date=May 9, 2019 |access-date=June 15, 2024}}</ref> MacKinnon finished the [[2019 Stanley Cup playoffs|2019 playoffs]] with six goals and seven assists for 13 points in all 12 games played.\n\nOn January 7, 2020, MacKinnon played in his 500th NHL game in a 5–3 loss to the [[New York Rangers]] where he was able to score a goal on Rangers' goaltender [[Igor Shesterkin]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.denverpost.com/2020/01/09/nathan-mackinnon-500-games-avalanche/ |title=It's been 500 games and Avalanche's Nathan MacKinnon still doesn't think he's famous |author=Joe Nyguen |website=denverpost.com |publisher=The Denver Post |date=January 9, 2020 |access-date=June 15, 2024}}</ref> MacKinnon was on pace to record his first career 100-point season during the [[2019–20 NHL season|2019–20 season]] until the last three weeks of the regular season got cancelled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] restrictions, having 35 goals and 58 assists for 93 points in 69 games at the time of the stoppage in March 2020. In the [[2020 Stanley Cup playoffs|2020 playoffs]], MacKinnon set personal bests, tallying nine goals and 16 assists for 25 points in just 15 games as Colorado was eliminated in Game 7 of the second round by the [[Dallas Stars]]. On September 11, MacKinnon won the [[Lady Byng Memorial Trophy]], which is awarded to the \"player adjudged to have exhibited the best type of sportsmanship and gentlemanly conduct combined with a high standard of playing ability, becoming the third player in franchise history to win the award after [[Joe Sakic]] in [[2000–01 NHL season|2000–01]] and [[Ryan O'Reilly]] in 2013–14.<ref name=\"Byng\">{{cite web |last1=Satriano |first1=David |title=MacKinnon of Avalanche wins Lady Byng Trophy for gentlemanly conduct |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/colorado-avalanche-forward-nathan-mackinnon-wins-lady-byng-trophy-318985834 |publisher=National Hockey League |access-date=May 15, 2025 |date=September 11, 2020}}</ref> MacKinnon was also named a finalist for both the Hart Memorial Trophy and Ted Lindsay Award for the second time in his career which were both eventually awarded to Edmonton Oilers forward [[Leon Draisaitl]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Hart Trophy finalists unveiled|url=https://www.nhl.com/news/taylor-hall-anze-kopitar-nathan-mackinnon-named-hart-finalists-298297282|website=NHL.com|access-date=April 28, 2018|date=April 27, 2018|archive-date=April 28, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180428114142/https://www.nhl.com/news/taylor-hall-anze-kopitar-nathan-mackinnon-named-hart-finalists/c-298297282|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Rosen |first1=Dan |title=Hall honored to become first Devils player to win Hart Trophy |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/taylor-hall-honored-to-become-first-new-jersey-devils-player-to-win-ha-299156142 |website=NHL.com |access-date=June 21, 2018 |archive-date=July 4, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180704082708/https://www.nhl.com/news/taylor-hall-honored-to-become-first-new-jersey-devils-player-to-win-hart-trophy/c-299156142 |url-status=live}}</ref>\n\nAfter the COVID-shortened [[2020–21 NHL season|2020–21 season]], the Avalanche won the Presidents' Trophy as the regular season champions. MacKinnon was once again the Avalanche's top scorer with 65 points (20 goals, 45 assists) in 48 games in the regular season. He followed that up with 15 points (eight goals and seven assists) in 10 playoff games as the Avalanche lost in the second round in six games to the [[Vegas Golden Knights]]. MacKinnon was named a finalist for the Hart Memorial Trophy for the third time in his career with it eventually being given to Edmonton Oilers forward and captain Connor McDavid.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.milehighhockey.com/2021/6/10/22527877/colorado-avalanche-nathan-mackinnon-is-one-of-the-hart-trophy-finalists-again |title=Nathan MacKinnon is one of the Hart Trophy finalists again |website=milehighhockey.com |publisher=Mile High Hockey |author=Jackie Kay |date=June 10, 2021 |access-date=April 5, 2024}}</ref>\n\nOn November 6, 2021, in a 4–2 loss to the [[Columbus Blue Jackets]], MacKinnon sustained an undisclosed lower-body injury, resulting in him missing the next eight games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nhl/article/avalanches-nathan-mackinnon-approximately-three-weeks/ |title=Avalanche's Nathan MacKinnon out for approximately three weeks |website=sportsnet.ca |date=November 10, 2021 |access-date=April 20, 2026}}</ref> On January 26, 2022, MacKinnon suffered a broken nose and a [[concussion]] after receiving a stick to his face by [[Boston Bruins]] forward Taylor Hall, causing him to miss four games and the [[2022 NHL All-Star Game]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/story/_/id/33168118/colorado-avalanche-say-nathan-mackinnon-facial-fracture-concussion |title=Colorado Avalanche center, All-Star captain Nathan MacKinnon sidelined by facial fracture, concussion |author=ESPN |website=[[ESPN]] |publisher=ESPN |date=January 28, 2022 |access-date=June 27, 2024}}</ref> MacKinnon finished the [[2021–22 NHL season|2021–22 season]] with 32 goals and 56 assists for 88 points recorded in 65 games played while the Avalanche as a team finished as the top seed in the Western Conference and the Presidents' Trophy runner-up being only behind the [[Florida Panthers]]. On June 26, MacKinnon won his first Stanley Cup championship with the Avalanche, defeating the two-time defending Stanley Cup champion and fifth-seeded Tampa Bay Lightning in six games in the [[2022 Stanley Cup Final]]. MacKinnon led all skaters with 13 goals in the [[2022 Stanley Cup playoffs|2022 playoffs]] (tied with [[Evander Kane]] of the Edmonton Oilers). He also recorded 11 assists for 24 points in all 20 games played. His performance throughout the playoffs put MacKinnon in the spot as a potential candidate for the [[Conn Smythe Trophy]] as the playoff MVP although the award eventually was given to Avalanche defenceman and teammate [[Cale Makar]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nhl/news/conn-smythe-2022-winner-cale-makar-nathan-mackinnon-nhl-playoff-mvp/aaq2frqe4d5dzkvphyajmsjw |title=Who should win the 2022 Conn Smythe Trophy? Cale Makar, Nathan MacKinnon favorites to be NHL playoff MVP winner |website=sportingnews.com |publisher=Sporting News |author=Bryan Murphy |date=June 24, 2022 |access-date=June 15, 2024}}</ref>\n\n[[File:Colorado Avalanche at Seattle Kraken - 2023-04-24 - Round 1 Game 4 - Eeli Tolvanen, Oliver Bjorkstrand, Nathan MacKinnon, Bowen Byram and Alexandar Georgiev (52846688174).jpg|thumb|upright|right|MacKinnon (top center) in April 2023 during the first round of the [[2023 Stanley Cup playoffs]].]]\nOn September 20, 2022, MacKinnon signed an eight-year, $100.8 million contract extension with the Avalanche.<ref>{{cite web|title=Nathan MacKinnon signs eight-year contract extension with Avalanche|url=https://www.denverpost.com/2022/09/20/nathan-mackinnon-avalanche-contract-extension/|website=[[The Denver Post]]|access-date=September 20, 2022|date=September 20, 2022|archive-date=September 20, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220920163802/https://www.denverpost.com/2022/09/20/nathan-mackinnon-avalanche-contract-extension/|url-status=live}}</ref> The contract carries an average annual value of $12.6 million, the highest in league history. This record would be surpassed in August 2023 when [[Toronto Maple Leafs]] forward [[Auston Matthews]] signed a deal with an AAV of $13.25 million.<ref>{{cite web |title=Maple Leafs make Auston Matthews highest-paid player in NHL history with 4-year, $53M US deal |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/hockey/nhl/auston-matthews-maple-leafs-4-year-extension-1.6945557 |publisher=Canadian Broadcasting Corporation |access-date=May 14, 2025 |date=August 24, 2023}}</ref> On December 5, in a 5–3 loss to the [[Philadelphia Flyers]], MacKinnon suffered an undisclosed upper-body injury as a result from blocking a shot from Flyers’ forward [[Scott Laughton]], causing him to miss the next 11 games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ca.sports.yahoo.com/news/nhl-avalanche-nathan-mackinnon-out-approximately-4-weeks-with-injury-005721366.html |title=Avalanche star Nathan MacKinnon out approximately 4 weeks with injury |website=yahoosports.com |publisher=Yahoo Sports |author=Michael Hoad |date=December 6, 2022 |access-date=April 20, 2026}}</ref> MacKinnon ended the [[2022–23 NHL season|2022–23 season]] with 42 goals and a career high 69 assists for 111 points in 71 games along with three goals and four assists for seven points in all seven games in the Avalanche first round exit in the [[2023 Stanley Cup playoffs|2023 playoffs]] against the seventh-seeded [[Seattle Kraken]].\n\nOn December 5, 2023, MacKinnon recorded his 500th career assist on a [[Logan O'Connor]] goal in a 3–2 win over the [[Anaheim Ducks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://thehockeynews.com/nhl/colorado-avalanche/latest-news/nathan-mackinnon-earns-500th-career-assist-in-3-2-win-over-ducks |title=Nathan MacKinnon earns 500th career assist in 3-2 win over Ducks |author=Colleen Flynn |website=thehockeynews.com |publisher=The Hockey News |date=December 6, 2023 |access-date=April 5, 2023}}</ref> On December 21, MacKinnon scored his 300th career goal and seventh career hat-trick in a 6–4 win over the [[Ottawa Senators]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/colorado/news/nathan-mackinnon-300-goals-colorado-avalanche-nhl-hat-trick-ottawa-senators/ |title=Nathan MacKinnon scores 4 times, eclipses 300 career goals with Colorado Avalanche in comeback win over Ottawa Senators |author=Jack Lowenstein |website=cbsnews.com |publisher=CBS news |date=December 22, 2023 |access-date=April 5, 2024}}</ref> On April 18, 2024, MacKinnon notched two assists on goals by Mikko Rantanen and [[Valeri Nichushkin]], bringing him to an Avalanche-record 140 points. His [[2023–24 NHL season|2023–24 season]] ended with MacKinnon playing in all 82 games, earning career highs in goals (51), assists (89) and points (140); he finished second for the [[Art Ross Trophy]] behind the 144 points by Tampa Bay Lightning forward Nikita Kucherov.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.denver7.com/sports/avalanche/mackinnon-has-2-assists-breaks-franchises-single-season-points-mark-as-avs-beat-oilers-5-1 |title=MacKinnon has 2 assists, breaks franchise's single-season points mark as Avs beat Oilers 5-1 |website=denver7.com |publisher=Denver 7 |author=Pat Graham |date=18 April 2024 |access-date=19 April 2024}}</ref> The Avalanche defeated the [[Winnipeg Jets]] in five games in the opening round of the [[2024 Stanley Cup playoffs|2024 playoffs]] before falling in six games against the Dallas Stars. MacKinnon finished the playoffs with four goals and 10 assists for 14 points in all On June 27, MacKinnon won the Ted Lindsay Award, beating out fellow finalists Kucherov and Auston Matthews of the Toronto Maple Leafs, becoming the third player in franchise history to win the Hart after Joe Sakic in 2000–01 and [[Peter Forsberg]] in [[2002–03 NHL season|2002–03]] and the second in franchise history to win the Lindsay after Joe Sakic in 2000–01.<ref name=\"2024lindsay\">{{cite web|url=https://www.nhl.com/news/colorado-avalanche-nathan-mackinnon-wins-ted-lindsay-award |title=MacKinnon wins Lindsay Award as best player voted on by NHLPA |website=nhl.com |publisher=National Hockey League |author=NHL |date=June 27, 2024 |access-date=June 27, 2024}}</ref> Additionally, he was also the recipient for the Hart Memorial Trophy as the regular season's most valuable player, beating out the other two finalists of Kucherov and Edmonton Oilers forward and captain Connor McDavid.<ref name=\"2024hart\">{{cite web|url=https://www.tsn.ca/nhl/colorado-avalanche-s-nathan-mackinnon-wins-hart-trophy-1.2141343 |title=Avalanche's MacKinnon wins Hart Trophy as NHL's MVP |website=tsn.ca |publisher=TSN |date=June 27, 2024 |access-date=June 27, 2024}}</ref>\n\nOn December 10, 2024, in a 6–2 victory over the [[Pittsburgh Penguins]], MacKinnon recorded his 600th career assist on a goal by Mikko Rantanen. He ended that game with five points (a goal and four assists).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nhl.com/avalanche/news/game-recap-12-10-24 |title=Rantanen Posts Hat Trick in 600th NHL Game and MacKinnon Records 600th Assist As Avalanche Beat Penguins 6-2 |website=nhl.com |publisher=Colorado Avalanche |author=Coby Maeir |date=December 10, 2024 |access-date=December 12, 2024}}</ref> On March 10, 2025, in a 3–0 victory over the [[Chicago Blackhawks]], Mackinnon recorded his 1,000th career point with an assist on a goal by [[Artturi Lehkonen]], becoming the 100th player in league history to reach the marker. He was named a Ted Lindsay finalist for the fourth time after the [[2024-25 NHL season|2024–25 season]], which was eventually awarded to Nikita Kucherov. MacKinnon recorded earned 116 points (32 goals, 84 assists) during the 2024–25 campaign. His 84 assists along with Nikita Kucherov's 84 assists led the league in assists and MacKinnon's 116 points was good for second place in points behind Kucherov, once more.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kucherov, MacKinnon, Makar named Ted Lindsay Award finalists |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/ted-lindsay-award-finalists-for-most-outstanding-player-for-2024-25-announced-by-nhlpa |website=NHL.com |date=April 30, 2025 |access-date=April 30, 2025}}</ref> He also had seven goals and four assists for 11 points in all seven games in the Avalanche first round exit to the Dallas Stars. \n\nOn October 7, 2025, in Colorado's [[2025–26 NHL season|2025–26 season]]-opening game, MacKinnon recorded two assists in a 4–1 win over the [[Los Angeles Kings]], and became the all-time leader in points of the franchise since its relocation before the [[1995–96 NHL season|1995–96 season]], passing Joe Sakic.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Greenspan |first1=Dan |title=MacKinnon sets Avalanche points record in opening win against Kings |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/colorado-avalanche-los-angeles-kings-game-recap-october-7-2025 |website=NHL.com |access-date=October 8, 2025 |date=October 7, 2025}}</ref> Following a 6–2 win over the Florida Panthers on December 11, MacKinnon scored his 392nd career goal moving him to the top of the franchise goal scored rankings ahead of Joe Sakic since their relocation from Quebec in 1995.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/avalanche/news/game-recap-12-11-25 |title=MacKinnon Sets Record For Most Goals in Avalanche Team History as Colorado Defeats Florida 6-2 |author=Coby Maeir |date=December 11, 2025 |access-date=2025-12-11}}</ref> MacKinnon became the 70th player in NHL history to record 1,100 points after he scored a goal during a 5–2 win against the Washington Capitals on January 19, 2026.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Boulding |first1=Ryan |title=MacKinnon has 3 points, leads Avalanche past Capitals |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/washington-capitals-colorado-avalanche-game-recap-january-19-2026 |website=NHL.com |access-date=January 20, 2026 |date=January 19, 2026}}</ref> During a March 10 game against the Edmonton Oilers, MacKinnon received the first career ten-minute game misconduct penalty of his career when he collided with Oilers goalie [[Connor Ingram]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nhl/article/avalanches-nathan-mackinnon-ejected-after-colliding-with-oilers-connor-ingram/ |title=Avalanche's Nathan MacKinnon ejected after colliding with Oilers' Connor Ingram |website=Sportsnet.ca |date=March 11, 2026 |access-date=March 10, 2026}}</ref> The NHL rescinded the penalty on March 12.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7112928/2026/03/12/nathan-mackinnon-avalanche-penalty-oilers-nhl/ |website=[[The New York Times]] |title=NHL rescinds major penalty given to Avalanche's Nathan MacKinnon against Oilers |author=Sean Gentille |date=March 12, 2026 |access-date=March 12, 2026}}</ref> He set the Colorado Avalanche franchise record for even-strength points in a season, at 93, following an April 4 game against the Dallas Stars.<ref>{{cite web |title=Sunday Against St. Louis |url=https://www.nhl.com/avalanche/news/game-preview-04-05-26 |access-date=April 5, 2026 |author=Colby Maier |website=NHL.com |date=April 5, 2026}}</ref> On April 9, he scored his 52nd goal of the season during a game against the Calgary Flames, setting a new season high.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-04-10 |title=Avalanche extinguish Flames, clinch Presidents' Trophy for fourth time |url=https://www.denverpost.com/2026/04/09/avs-clinch-presidents-trophy-flames-score/ |access-date=2026-04-10 |website=The Denver Post |language=en-US}}</ref> He ended the season with a career-high and league-leading 53 goals, earning him his first career [[Maurice \"Rocket\" Richard Trophy]]. He became the second player in franchise history to win the award after [[Milan Hejduk]] in 2002–03.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.denvergazette.com/2026/04/16/avalanche-forward-nathan-mackinnon-wins-the-2025-26-rocket-richard-trophy-goaltenders-win-william-jennings-trophy/ |author=Evan Rawal |website=denvergazette.com |publisher=Denver Gazette |title=Avalanche forward Nathan MacKinnon wins the 2025-26 Rocket Richard Trophy, goaltenders win William Jennings Trophy |date=April 16, 2026 |access-date=April 16, 2026}}</ref> He also recorded 74 assists for 127 total points in 80 contests played. His 127 points ranked him third in the league in points (only behind Nikita Kucherov’s 130 points and Connor McDavid’s league-leading 134 points, respectively). 97 of Mackinnon’s points were at even strength, marking the highest even strength point total since [[Wayne Gretzky]] in [[1990–91 NHL season|1990–91]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.denvergazette.com/2026/04/16/avalanche-forward-nathan-mackinnon-wins-the-2025-26-rocket-richard-trophy-goaltenders-win-william-jennings-trophy/ |author=Evan Rawal |website=denvergazette.com |publisher=Denver Gazette |title=Avalanche forward Nathan MacKinnon wins the 2025-26 Rocket Richard Trophy, goaltenders win William Jennings Trophy |date=April 16, 2026 |access-date=April 16, 2026}}</ref> MacKinnon also had a league-leading +57 [[NHL Plus-Minus Award|plus-minus]] rating. For the fifth time in his career, MacKinnon was named a finalist for the Hart Memorial Trophy.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7243751/2026/05/08/hart-trophy-finalists-2026-nhl-awards/ |title=NHL names Hart Trophy finalists: McDavid, MacKinnon, Kucherov up for league MVP |author=Eric Stephens |publisher=The Athletic |website=theathletic.com |date=May 8, 2026 |access-date=May 8, 2026}}</ref>\n\n==International play==\n{{MedalTableTop|name=}}\n{{MedalSport|Men's [[ice two assists to be named player of the game as Canada Atlantic defeated [[Finland]] 4–3.<ref>{{cite news|last=Nicholson|first=Matthew|title=MacKinnon's four points lead Atlantic to first was named to the [[Canada men's national junior ice hockey team|Canadian junior team]] for the [[2013 World Junior Ice Hockey Championships]], alongside with Mooseheads teammate [[Jonathan Drouin]].<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.tsn.ca/world_jrs/story/?id=411608 | title = Team Canada heading overseas with lockout questions looming | publisher = [[The Sports Network]] | date = live}}</ref> The tournament ended in disappointment for the Canadians, who were eliminated in the quarterfinals and finished in fifth place overall.<ref name=NBC260220>{{cite web|url= https://www.nbcolympics.com/news/nathan-mackinnon-road-milan-cortina-2026 |title= Nathan MacKinnon: Road to Milan Cortina 2026 |last=Gomes |first=Maya |website= [[NBC Sports]] |date= November 19, 2025 |access-date= February 20, 2026 }}</ref>\n\nMacKinnon made his [[Canada men's national ice hockey team|senior national team]] debut at the [[2014 IIHF World Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.theglobeandmail.com/sports/hockey/nathan-mackinnon-joins-canada-for-world-championship/article18453570/ |title= Nathan MacKinnon joins Canada for world championship |newspaper= [[Globe & Mail]] |date= May 14, 2014 |access-date= February 20, 2026 }}</ref> He returned for the [[2015 IIHF World Championship]], where Canada won the gold medal for the first time since 2007 with a perfect 10–0 record. MacKinnon finished the tournament with 4 goals and 5 assists.<ref>{{cite web|title=Canada's National Men's Team wins gold medal at 2015 IIHF Ice Hockey World Championship|url=http://www.hockeycanada.ca/en-ca/news/canadas-national-mens-team-wins-gold-medal-at-2015-iihf-ice-hockey-world-championship|publisher=Hockey Canada|access-date=June 21, 2015|date=May 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161207052824/http://www.hockeycanada.ca/en-ca/news/Canadas-National-Mens-Team-wins-gold-medal-at-2015-IIHF-Ice-Hockey-World-Championship|url-status=live}}</ref> The following year, the NHL held the [[2016 World Cup of Hockey]], where MacKinnon competed as a member of [[Team North America]], a squad composed of the best Canadian and American players under the age of 24.<ref name=NBC260220/> The year after that, he returned to the Canadian national team for the [[2017 IIHF World Championship]], where he led the team in points on the way to a silver medal, having been defeated by [[Sweden men's national ice hockey team|Sweden]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Hossain|first1=Asif|title=Canada strikes silver following Sweden shootout at IIHF worlds|url=https://olympic.ca/2017/05/21/canada-wins-third-consecutive-iihf-world-championship-gold/|website=olympic.ca|access-date=April 23, 2018|date=May 21, 2017|archive-date=April 25, [[2016-17 NHL season|season in the NHL]], MacKinnon called his experience with the national team beneficial.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/hockey/nhl/mackinnon-reinvigorated-worlds-tough-year-avalanche/ |title=MacKinnon reinvigorated at worlds after tough year with Avalanche |last=Nugent-Bowman |first=Daniel |publisher=[[Sportsnet]] |date=May 16, 2017 |access-date=February 20, 2026}}</ref>\n\nAfter nearly a decade without a major international tournament held with full NHL participation, the league hosted the [[2025 4 Nations Face-Off|4 Nations Face-Off]] in February 2025. MacKinnon was again part of Canada, and scored four goals in four games, including the first goal in Canada's 3–2 win in the championship game against the [[United States men's national ice hockey team|United States]] He was named the most valuable player of the tournament.<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Horwat |first=Nick |date=February 20, 2025 |title=Avalanche Star Nathan MacKinnon Named 4 Nations MVP |url=https://www.si.com/onsi/breakaway/news-feed-page/colorado-avalanche-nathan-mackinnon-named-4-nations-mvp |access-date=February 21, 2025 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]}}</ref> After the Avalanche were eliminated from [[2025 Stanley Cup playoffs]] in the first round, he rejoined the national team for the [[2025 IIHF World Championship]].<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.tsn.ca/hockey-canada/colorado-avalanche-confirm-nathan-mackinnon-will-play-for-canada-at-worlds-1.2302601 |title= Avalanche confirm MacKinnon will play for Canada at Worlds |publisher= [[The Sports Network]] |date= May 8, 2025 |access-date= February 20, 2026 }}</ref> Canada finished first in its group, with MacKinnon leading the team in scoring,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/ice-hockey-world-championship/article/mackinnon-has-three-points-canada-finishes-first-in-group-a-with-win-over-sweden/ |title=MacKinnon has three points, Canada finishes first in Group A with win over Sweden |publisher=[[Sportsnet]] |date=May 20, 2025 |access-date=February 20, 2026}}</ref> but was upset in the quarterfinals by tournament co-host [[Denmark men's national ice hockey team|Denmark]].<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.tsn.ca/hockey-canada/denmark-beats-canada-in-stunning-quarterfinals-upset-at-iihf-men-s-worlds-1.2310537 |title= Denmark beats Canada in stunning quarterfinals upset at IIHF men's worlds |publisher= [[The Sports Network]] |date= May 22, 2025 |access-date= February 20, 2026 }}</ref>\n\nMacKinnon was named to the [[Canada at the 2026 Winter Olympics|Canadian team]] for the [[Ice hockey at the 2026 Winter Olympics - Men's tournament|2026 Winter Olympics]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/milano-cortina-2026/results/athlete-details/53862 |title=Nathan MacKinnon |work=[[Milano Cortina 2026 Olympics]] |access-date=February 14, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260211094740/https://www.olympics.com/en/milano-cortina-2026/results/athlete-details/53862 |archive-date=February 11, 2026 |url-status=dead}}</ref> the first edition with full NHL participation since 2014.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/olympics/article/canada-names-olympic-mens-hockey-roster/ |title=Canada names Olympic men's hockey roster |publisher=[[Sportsnet]] |date=December 31, 2025 |access-date=December 31, 2025}}</ref>\n\nIn the round robin stage, MacKinnon took a forearm hit in the jaw from French player [[Pierre Crinon]] which was seen as a dirty hit; later in the game his Canadian teammate [[Tom Wilson (ice hockey)|Tom Wilson]] retaliated by fighting Crinon (Wilson achieved the first [[Gordie Howe hat trick]] in Olympic hockey) and both were ejected.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/olympics/story/_/id/47940390/canada-tom-wilson-drops-gloves-rare-olympic-hockey-fight |website=ESPN.com |title=Canada's Tom Wilson drops gloves in rare Olympic hockey fight |date=February 15, 2026 |access-date=February 16, 2026}}</ref> France later suspended Crinon for jeering the crowd as he left the ice.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7050885/2026/02/16/french-pierre-crinon-suspended-hockey-olympics-fighting/ |author=Mark Lazerus |website=[[The New York Times]] |title=Pierre Crinon suspended by French hockey federation after Tom Wilson fight |date=February 16, 2026 |access-date=February 16, 2026}}</ref> On February 20, MacKinnon scored the winning goal in Canada's 3–2 semifinal victory over [[Finland men's national ice hockey team|Finland]], taking the team to the championship final.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/olympics/winter/hockey/olympics-mens-hockey-canada-semifinal-finland-february-20-9.7097502 |title=MacKinnon sends Canada to gold-medal game after sinking Finns with game winner in dying seconds |last= Clipperton |first=Joshua |publisher=[[CBC Sports]] |date=February 20, 2026 |access-date=February 20, 2026 }}</ref> During the third period of the final, MacKinnon would end up missing on a wide-open net that would have put Canada up 2–1 over the [[United States men's national ice hockey team|United States]] with 10:50 left to play.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/olympic-men-hockey/video/canadas-mackinnon-sends-shot-wide-of-open-cage-to-miss-great-chance/ |title=Canada's MacKinnon sends shot wide of open cage to miss great chance |date=February 22, 2026 |access-date=February 22, 2026 }}</ref> Canada would end up falling to the States 2–1 in overtime.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/gamecenter/usa-vs-can/2026/02/22/2025090030 |title=Jack Hughes scores in OT, Team USA wins Olympic gold medal game against Canada |date=February 22, 2026 |access-date=February 22, 2026 }}</ref> MacKinnon was visibly upset during the medal ceremony, with him being spotted shaking his head in annoyance at the [[plush animal]] awarded to all medalists in the games.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://nationalpost.com/sports/olympics/nathan-mackinnon-canada-usa-hockey-game-stuffed-animal |title=Video shows Nathan MacKinnon's priceless expression when handed Olympic stuffed animal |date=February 22, 2026 |access-date=February 22, 2026 }}</ref> To further express his frustration, MacKinnon would go on record stating, \"You be the judge of who was the better team.\"<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.thescore.com/wolym/news/3483959 |title=MacKinnon: 'You be the judge of who was the better team' |date=February 22, 2026 |access-date=February 22, 2026 }}</ref>\n\nIn 2026,
