season|2023–24]])\n\n==Acting career==\nMacKinnon has appeared in a recurring role (along with former [[Halifax Mooseheads]] teammate Cameron Critchlow) on the Canadian television show ''[[Mr. D]]'', playing a fictionalized version of himself. He first appeared in season 2 episode 4, when he and a teammate have to leave an exam early to play in a school hockey game. When the teammates tell Mr. D (portrayed by [[Gerry Dee]]) that they did not finish the exam, he tells them to take it home and return it completed the next day.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://thechronicleherald.ca/sports/125102-mooseheads-called-to-the-show | title = Mooseheads called to the show | author = Willy Palov | work = The Chronicle Herald | date = August 9, 2012 | access-date = November 7, 2017 | archive-date = November 7, 2017 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20171107225005/http://thechronicleherald.ca/sports/125102-mooseheads-called-to-the-show | url-status = live}}</ref> In season 3 episode 7, he is in detention for missing too much school to play hockey. Mr. D is oblivious to his talent and reprimands him (\"Hockey's not a job\"), although it is implied that, in the show's timeline, this takes place before the [[2013 NHL entry draft]], where MacKinnon was drafted first overall, despite airing in 2014. In season 4 episode 11, MacKinnon returns to give tickets to an Avalanche game to the school principal. When Mr. D enters the room a moment later, he calls MacKinnon \"Mr. Calder\" and tells him that he always believed in him. When Mr. D. asks for tickets to a game, MacKinnon tells him that all the games, including those in the exhibition and the following season, are sold out.<ref>{{cite web | url = biography\n| name = Connor McDavid\n| image = {{CSS image crop |Image=Connor McDavid 2-FEB-2022.jpg |bSize=500 |cWidth=230 |cHeight=300 |oTop=0 |oLeft=225 |Location=center}}\n| caption = McDavid with the [[Edmonton Oilers]] in 2022\n| birth_date = {{birth date and age|1997|1|13}}\n| birth_place = [[Richmond Hill, Ontario]], Canada<!--- Hometown ≠ birthplace; do not change to Newmarket --->\n| height_ft = 6\n| height_in = 2\n| weight_lb = 190\n| position = [[Centre (ice hockey)|Centre]]\n| shoots = Left\n| league = [[National Hockey League|NHL]]\n| team = [[Edmonton Oilers]]\n| ntl_team = CAN\n| draft = 1st overall\n| draft_year = 2015\n| draft_team = [[Edmonton Oilers]]\n| career_start = 2015\n}}\n'''Connor Andrew McDavid''' (born January 13, 1997) is a Canadian professional [[ice hockey]] player who is a [[Centre (ice hockey)|centre]] and [[Captain (ice hockey)|captain]] for the [[Edmonton Oilers]] of the [[National Hockey League]] (NHL). Selected [[List of first overall NHL draft picks|first overall]] by the Oilers in the [[2015 NHL entry draft]], McDavid is widely considered one of the best players of all time.\n\nMcDavid spent his childhood playing ice hockey against older children. Coached by his father, McDavid won four [[Ontario Minor Hockey Association]] championships with the York Simcoe Express, but he left the team in 2011 to join the [[Toronto Marlboros]] of the [[Greater Toronto Hockey League]] (GTHL). There, McDavid was named the GTHL Player of the Year and the winner of the [[Tim Adams Memorial Trophy]]. He was granted [[Canadian Hockey League#Exceptional player status|exceptional player status]] in 2012 by [[Hockey Canada]], which allowed him to begin playing [[junior ice hockey]] at the age of 15. The [[Erie Otters]] of the [[Ontario Hockey League]] (OHL) selected him first overall in that year's draft, and he played there until 2015. McDavid's OHL career concluded with a [[2014–15 OHL season|2014–15 season]] in which he recorded 120 [[Point (ice hockey)|points]] and received a number of OHL and [[Canadian Hockey League]] (CHL) awards, including the [[Red Tilson Trophy]], [[Wayne Gretzky 99 Award]], and [[CHL Player of the Year]] awards. McDavid also represented [[Canada men's national junior ice hockey team|Canada]] at several international competitions during this time, winning gold medals at the [[2013 IIHF World U18 Championships|2013 World U18 Championships]] and [[2015 World Junior Ice Hockey Championships|2015 World Junior Championships]].\n\nAfter finishing his junior hockey career, McDavid joined the Oilers for their [[2015–16 NHL season|2015–16 season]]. Despite missing three months of his rookie season due to a fractured [[clavicle]], he was named to the [[NHL All-Rookie Team]] and was a finalist for the [[Calder Memorial Trophy]]. The following year, the Oilers appointed 19-year-old McDavid the youngest captain in NHL history. Recording 100 points during the [[2016–17 NHL season|2016–17 season]], at the age of 20, McDavid became the second youngest player to win the [[Art Ross Trophy]] for the leading scorer in the NHL. He was also awarded the [[Hart Memorial Trophy]], [[Ted Lindsay Award]], and was selected to the [[NHL All-Star team|NHL First All-Star Team]]. Although the Oilers missed the [[Stanley Cup]] playoffs during the next two seasons, McDavid scored 41 goals in consecutive years. He injured his knee in the final game of the [[2018–19 NHL season|2018–19 season]] but underwent a nonsurgical rehabilitation process that allowed him to return in time for the start of the [[2019–20 NHL season|2019–20 season]]. In [[2020–21 NHL season|2020–21]], despite the [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports|COVID-19 pandemic]] shortening the NHL season to only 56 games, McDavid recorded 100 points for the fourth time in his career. In [[2023–24 NHL season|2023–24]], McDavid captained the Oilers to the [[2024 Stanley Cup Final|Stanley Cup Final]], their first since [[2006 Stanley Cup Final|2006]]. McDavid won the [[Conn Smythe Trophy]] as the most valuable player in the [[2024 Stanley Cup playoffs]], becoming only the sixth player, second skater, and first since [[Jean-Sébastien Giguère]] in [[2003 Stanley Cup Final|2003]], to win the award despite not winning the Stanley Cup.\n\nHe is a four-time NHL First Team All-Star, a six-time recipient of the [[Art Ross Trophy]], a five-time winner of the [[Ted Lindsay Award]], a three-time recipient of the Hart Memorial Trophy, and the [[Maurice \"Rocket\" Richard Trophy]] winner for [[2022–23 NHL season|2022–23]] as the league's leading goal-scorer. His opponents have praised his speed on the ice, and McDavid has won Fastest Skater at the [[NHL All-Star Skills Competition]] four times. He is one of only two players{{snd}}after fellow Oilers captain [[Wayne Gretzky]] in [[1981–82 NHL season|1982]]{{snd}}to unanimously win the Hart Memorial Trophy as the league's [[most valuable player]].\n\n==Early life==\nMcDavid was born on January 13, 1997, in [[Richmond Hill, Ontario]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Connor McDavid Stats and News |url=https://www.nhl.com/oilers/player/connor-mcdavid-8478402 |publisher=[[National Hockey League]] |access-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205084753/https://www.nhl.com/player/connor-mcdavid-8478402 |url-status=live }}</ref> His mother, Kelly, played one year of recreational ice hockey as a child before turning her attention towards skiing, while his father, Brian, was a high school ice hockey player and dedicated [[Boston Bruins]] fan.<ref>{{cite news |last=Nugent-Bowman |first=Daniel |title=Protector, supporter, confidant: Connor McDavid's mom, Kelly, is his off-ice rock through good times and bad 2022 |url-access=subscription |archive-date=February 5, 2022 McDavid began playing hockey around the age of three, practicing on [[rollerblade]]s in the family basement.<ref>{{cite news |last=Klinkenberg |first=Marty |title=Family Ties: While his father helped develop Connor McDavid's hockey skills, it was his mother who nurtured his heart |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/sports/hockey/family-ties-while-his-father-helped-develop-connor-mcdavids-hockey-skills-it-was-his-mother-who-nurtured-his-heart/article26423586/ |work=[[The Globe |url-status=live }}</ref> He began playing organized youth hockey the next year, as his parents lied about his age to allow him to play with five-year-olds.<ref>{{cite news |last=Rohan |first=Tim |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2013/02/18/sports/hockey/connor-mcdavid-excels-in-ontario-hockey-league-and-is-on-way-to-stardom.html?pagewanted=1&_r=2&seid=auto&smid=tw-nytimessports |work=[[The New |url-status=live }}</ref> When he was six, the local youth hockey association in his hometown of [[Newmarket, Ontario|Newmarket]] forbade McDavid to play against older children, and his parents, believing that he would be \"bored out of his mind\" in [[house league]] hockey, enrolled him in an [[Aurora, Ontario]], hockey program.<ref name=\"woods\">{{cite news |last=Woods |first=Michael |title=Connor McDavid was born to play hockey |url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/hockey/2012/03/17/connor_mcdavid_was_born_to_play_hockey.html |work=[[Toronto Star]] |date=March 17, 2012 |access-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205193534/https://www.thestar.com/sports/hockey/2012/03/17/connor_mcdavid_was_born_to_play_hockey.html |url-status=live }}</ref> From there, he won four [[Ontario Minor Hockey Association]] championships with the York Simcoe Express, a team coached by his father.<ref name=\"woods\" /> In 2009, McDavid participated in the [[Quebec International Pee-Wee Hockey Tournament]] with his York Simcoe team, which also featured future professional ice hockey player [[Sam Bennett (ice hockey)|Sam Bennett]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.publicationsports.com/ressources/files/439/Joueurs_Pro.pdf|title=Pee-Wee players who have reached NHL or WHA|year=2018|website=Quebec International Pee-Wee Hockey Tournament|page=135|access-date=February 15, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190306085544/https://www.publicationsports.com/ressources/files/439/Joueurs_Pro.pdf|archive-date=March 6, 2019}}</ref>\n\nIn 2011, McDavid left the Express for the [[Toronto Marlboros]] of the [[Greater Toronto Hockey League]] (GTHL), the team that he and his father had defeated in the previous year's [[Ontario Hockey Federation]] championship. The decision came at a social cost, as he lost many of the friends that he had made with York Simcoe.<ref>{{cite news |title=Newmarket's McDavid talks about OHL draft |url=https://www.yorkregion.com/community-story/1433974-newmarket-s-mcdavid-talks-about-ohl-draft/ |work=[[The Newmarket Era]] |date=April 11, 2012 |access-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205193535/https://www.yorkregion.com/community-story/1433974-newmarket-s-mcdavid-talks-about-ohl-draft/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He won the GTHL Player of the Year Award in 2012 after scoring 33 [[Goal (ice hockey)|goals]] and recording 39 [[Assist (ice hockey)|assists]] in 33 regular season games. McDavid added another 19 [[Point (ice hockey)#Personal statistic|points]] (11 goals and eight assists) in seven [[OHL Cup]] games, the most by any player since [[Sam Gagner]] recorded 17 points in five games during the 2005 tournament.<ref name=\"minor\">{{cite news |last=Kimelman |first=Adam |title=McDavid granted exceptional player status |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/mcdavid-granted-exceptional-player-status/c-623367 |publisher=National Hockey League |date=March 21, 2012 |access-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205195209/https://www.nhl.com/news/mcdavid-granted-exceptional-player-status/c-623367 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Although he received the [[Tim Adams Memorial Trophy]] as the tournament MVP, McDavid's team was defeated 2–1 in the OHL Cup final by the Mississauga Rebels.<ref name=\"ohl cup\">{{cite news |last=Campbell |first=Ken |title=Mississauga Rebels defeat Connor McDavid's Toronto Marlboros in OHL Cup final |url=https://thehockeynews.com/news/news/mississauga-rebels-defeat-connor-mcdavids-toronto-marlboros-in-ohl-cup-final |work=[[The Hockey News]] |publisher=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=March 19, 2012 |access-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205195210/https://thehockeynews.com/news/mississauga-rebels-defeat-connor-mcdavids-toronto-marlboros-in-ohl-cup-final |url-status=live }}</ref>\n\nMcDavid attended [[Sir William Mulock Secondary School]] in Newmarket, Ontario, until his graduation in 2015.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2015-03-22 |title=Juggling hockey and school, Connor McDavid plays it cool |url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/hockey/juggling-hockey-and-school-connor-mcdavid-plays-it-cool/article_c5f8dcbc-6d4a-5608-9c30-99ecea6e775a.html |access-date=2026-10-01 |work=The Toronto Star |language=en-CA |issn=0319-0781}}</ref>\n\n==Playing career==\n===Junior===\nAlthough McDavid contemplated playing [[NCAA Division I]] hockey, he decided to enter the [[junior ice hockey]] circuit as an adolescent rather than waiting to begin a college career.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Saraceno |first=Jon |title=OHL star Connor McDavid, 16, called the next big thing |url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/hockey/2013/02/19/ohl_star_connor_mcdavid_15_called_the_next_big_thing.html |work=[[Toronto Star]] |date=February 19, 2013 |access-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205164158/https://www.thestar.com/sports/hockey/2013/02/19/ohl_star_connor_mcdavid_15_called_the_next_big_thing.html |url-status=live }}</ref> McDavid applied for [[Canadian Hockey League#Exceptional player status|exceptional player status]] through [[Hockey Canada]], and after passing through evaluations of his athleticism, academics, and maturity, he was allowed to enter the junior hockey draft at the age of 15 rather than 16.<ref>{{cite news |title=OHF Announces Exceptional Player Status for Connor McDavid |url=https://ontariohockeyleague.com/ohf-announces-exceptional-player-status-for-connor-mcdavid/ |publisher=[[Ontario Hockey League]] |date=March 21, 2012 |access-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205165637/https://ontariohockeyleague.com/ohf-announces-exceptional-player-status-for-connor-mcdavid/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He was only the third [[Ontario Hockey League]] (OHL) player to be granted such an exception, following [[John Tavares]] in 2005 and [[Aaron Ekblad]] in 2011.<ref>{{cite news |last=Pollack |first=Dustin |title=Connor McDavid granted exceptional status, now eligible for OHL draft |url=https://nationalpost.com/sports/connor-mcdavid-granted-exceptional-status-now-eligible-for-ohl-draft |work=[[National Post]] |date=March 21, 2012 |access-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-date=February 22, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220222193449/https://nationalpost.com/sports/connor-mcdavid-granted-exceptional-status-now-eligible-for-ohl-draft |url-status=live }}</ref> On April 7, 2012, the [[Erie Otters]] selected McDavid first overall in the [[2011–12 OHL season|2012 OHL Priority Selection]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Erie Otters select 15-year-old McDavid as No. 1 pick in OHL draft |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/sports/hockey/erie-otters-select-15-year-old-mcdavid-as-no-1-pick-in-ohl-draft/article4098530/ |work=[[The Globe and Mail]] |agency=The Canadian Press |date=April 7, 2012 |access-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205165635/https://www.theglobeandmail.com/sports/hockey/erie-otters-select-15-year-old-mcdavid-as-no-1-pick-in-ohl-draft/article4098530/ |url-status=live }}</ref> and he signed with the team that June.<ref>{{cite news |title=Otters sign first overall pick McDavid |url=https://ottershockey.com/otters-sign-first-overall-pick-mcdavid |publisher=Ontario Hockey League |agency=[[Erie Otters]] |date=June 20, 2012 |access-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205165638/https://ottershockey.com/otters-sign-first-overall-pick-mcdavid |url-status=live }}</ref> As the first overall selection in that year's OHL draft, McDavid was the recipient of the 2012 [[Jack Ferguson Award]].<ref name=\"fergie\">{{cite web |title=Jack Ferguson Award |url=https://ontariohockeyleague.com/priority-selection-jack-ferguson-award/ |publisher=Ontario Hockey League |access-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-date=January 21, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220121104012/https://ontariohockeyleague.com/priority-selection-jack-ferguson-award/ |url-status=live }}</ref>\n\n[[File:Connor McDavid (9525014410).jpg|thumb|McDavid with the [[Erie Otters]] in 2013]]\nMcDavid joined the Otters for the [[2012–13 OHL season|2012–13 season]], where he scored his first OHL goal on September 21, in an 8–2 loss to the [[London Knights]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Otters Gameday vs. London |url=https://ottershockey.com/mcdavid-scores-first-ohl-goal-in-otters-loss |publisher=Ontario Hockey League |agency=[[Erie Otters]] |date=September 21, 2012 |access-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205184906/https://ottershockey.com/mcdavid-scores-first-ohl-goal-in-otters-loss |url-status=live }}</ref> That October, he was named the OHL Rookie of the Month after recording at least one point in all 10 games he played.<ref>{{cite news |title=OHL Top Performers of October |url=https://ontariohockeyleague.com/ohl-top-performers-of-october/ |publisher=Ontario Hockey League |date=November 1, 2012 |access-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205182626/https://ontariohockeyleague.com/ohl-top-performers-of-october/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He took home the award again in November with a rookie-leading 17 points in 13 games.<ref>{{cite news |title=OHL Top Performers of November |url=https://ontariohockeyleague.com/ohl-top-performers-of-november_133347/ |publisher=Ontario Hockey League |date=December 5, 2012 |access-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205182630/https://ontariohockeyleague.com/ohl-top-performers-of-november_133347/ |url-status=live }}</ref> That same month, McDavid became the youngest OHL player ever to participate in the [[CHL Canada/Russia Series|Subway Super Series]].<ref name=\"subway\">{{cite news |title=McDavid selected to Subway Super Series |url=https://ottershockey.com/connor-mcdavid-set-to-play-in-subway-super-series |work=[[Tri-City Herald]] |date=November 8, 2012 |access-date=February 5, 2022 |via=Erie Otters |archive-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205184909/https://ottershockey.com/connor-mcdavid-set-to-play-in-subway-super-series |url-status=live }}</ref> In January and February, the physical toll of moving from minor to junior hockey, as well as frustration playing for the last-place Otters, limited McDavid's effectiveness on the ice, and his scoring began to slow.<ref>{{cite news |last=Saraceno |first=Jon |title=Connor McDavid, 'the LeBron James of Hockey,' is next |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/hockey/minors/2013/02/17/connor-mcdavid-nhl-hockey-ontario-hockey-league/1926709/ |work=[[USA Today]] |date=February 17, 2013 |access-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205190129/https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/hockey/minors/2013/02/17/connor-mcdavid-nhl-hockey-ontario-hockey-league/1926709/ |url-status=live }}</ref>\n\nOn March 10, 2013, despite the Otters falling 6–4 to the [[Owen Sound Attack]], McDavid picked up his 37th assist of the season, setting a franchise record for rookie assists. It was also his 62nd point of the season, tying with [[Tim Connolly]] for the most rookie points in Otters history.<ref>{{cite news |title=Attack complete weekend sweep of Otters |url=http://www.goerie.com/article/20130310/HOCKEY01/303099891/Attack-complete-weekend-sweep-of-Otters |work=[[Erie Times-News]] |date=March 10, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131110210942/http://www.goerie.com/article/20130310/HOCKEY01/303099891/Attack-complete-weekend-sweep-of-Otters |archive-date=November 10, 2013 |access-date=February 5, 2022 |url-status=live }}</ref> He recorded four more points in the regular season, breaking Connolly's record.<ref>{{cite news |title=Otters win in dramatic fashion in season finale |url=https://ottershockey.com/otters-win-in-dramatic-fashion-in-season-finale |publisher=Ontario Hockey League |agency=Erie Otters |date=March 16, 2013 |access-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205184914/https://ottershockey.com/otters-win-in-dramatic-fashion-in-season-finale |url-status=live }}</ref> McDavid finished his rookie season with 25 goals and 41 assists in 63 regular season games, second in scoring to [[Nikolay Goldobin]] among all OHL rookies. In addition to being named to the OHL First All-Rookie Team, McDavid took home the 2013 [[Emms Family Award]] for OHL rookie of the year.<ref name=\"emms\">{{cite news |title=Connor McDavid is OHL Rookie of Year |url=https://ontariohockeyleague.com/connor-mcdavid-is-ohl-rookie-of-year/ |publisher=Ontario Hockey League |date=April 4, 2013 |access-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205182629/https://ontariohockeyleague.com/connor-mcdavid-is-ohl-rookie-of-year/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He was also a finalist for [[CHL Rookie of the Year]], a title which went to [[Valentin Zykov]] of the [[Baie-Comeau Drakkar]].<ref>{{cite news |title=2013 CHL Award winners |url=https://www.tri-cityherald.com/sports/spt-columns-blogs/article32126892.html |work=Tri-City Herald |agency=[[Western Hockey League]] |date=May 26, 2013 |access-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-date=February 22, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220222193504/https://account.tri-cityherald.com/paywall/subscriber-only?resume=32126892&intcid=ab_archive |url-status=live }}</ref>\n\nIn contrast to their poor finish during the previous season, the Otters opened the [[2013–14 OHL season|2013–14 season]] with 25 points in their first 15 games, including a 10-game winning streak. During this stretch, McDavid personally had five goals and 28 points, three points behind OHL leader and teammate [[Connor Brown (ice hockey)|Connor Brown]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Bell |first=Aaron |title=Otters finding their stride early |url=https://ontariohockeyleague.com/otters-finding-their-stride-early/ |publisher=Ontario Hockey League |date=October 30, 2013 |access-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205190131/https://ontariohockeyleague.com/otters-finding-their-stride-early/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He was named the OHL Player of the Month in October and received another Subway Super Series selection, appearing as the youngest player in the tournament for the second year in a row.<ref name=\"subway 2\">{{cite news |title=OHL Top Performers of October |url=https://ontariohockeyleague.com/ohl-top-performers-of-october_151704/ |publisher=Ontario Hockey League |date=November 1, 2013 |access-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205190129/https://ontariohockeyleague.com/ohl-top-performers-of-october_151704/ |url-status=live }}</ref> After experiencing two consecutive four-point outings in an 11–2 win against the [[Plymouth Whalers]] and 6–1 victory over the [[Windsor Spitfires]] in March, McDavid was named both the OHL and CHL Player of the Week. Later that week, his 25th goal of the season helped the Otters to reach 100 points as a team for the first time since 2001.<ref>{{cite news |last=Hayakawa |first=Michael |title=Newmarket's Connor McDavid named CHL player of the week |url=https://www.toronto.com/community-story/4408186-newmarket-s-connor-mcdavid-named-chl-player-of-the-week/ |work=The Newmarket Era |date=March 12, 2014 |access-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205200751/https://www.toronto.com/community-story/4408186-newmarket-s-connor-mcdavid-named-chl-player-of-the-week/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He finished the regular season fourth in the OHL with 99 points (28 goals and 71 assists) in 56 games. His 20 [[penalty minutes]], meanwhile, were the lowest among the top 12 scorers in the league, and McDavid was awarded the [[William Hanley Trophy]] for the most sportsmanlike player in the OHL.<ref name=\"hanley\">{{cite news |title=Connor McDavid wins OHL sportsmanship award |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/sports/hockey/connor-mcdavid-wins-ohl-sportsmanship-award/article17945667/ |work=The |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205200755/https://www.theglobeandmail.com/sports/hockey/connor-mcdavid-wins-ohl-sportsmanship-award/article17945667/ |url-status=live }}</ref> With a 92 per cent average at [[McDowell High School (Pennsylvania)\n|McDowell High School]], McDavid both won the 2014 [[Bobby Smith Trophy]] for the OHL's Scholastic Player of the Year<ref name=\"bobby\">{{Cite news |title=McDavid Named OHL Scholastic Player of the Year |url=https://ottershockey.com/mcdavid-named-scholastic-player-of-the-year |publisher=Ontario Hockey League |agency=Erie Otters |date=April 23, 2014 |access-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205200759/https://ottershockey.com/mcdavid-named-scholastic-player-of-the-year |url-status=live }}</ref> and was named the 2014 [[CHL Scholastic Player of the Year]].<ref name=\"scholastic\">{{cite news |title=Brown, McDavid Take Home CHL Hardware |url=https://ottershockey.com/brown-mcdavid-take-home-chl-hardware |publisher=Ontario Hockey League |agency=Erie Otters |date=May 27, 2014 |access-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205200802/https://ottershockey.com/brown-mcdavid-take-home-chl-hardware |url-status=live }}</ref> He was also named to the OHL Second All-Star Team alongside Otters [[defenceman]] [[Adam Pelech]] and coach [[Kris Knoblauch]].<ref name=\"second\">{{cite news |title=Six Otters Named to OHL All-Star Teams |url=https://ottershockey.com/six-otters-named-to-ohl-all-star-teams |publisher=Ontario Hockey League |agency=Erie Otters |date=May 14, 2014 |access-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205200755/https://ottershockey.com/six-otters-named-to-ohl-all-star-teams |url-status=live }}</ref> The Otters, meanwhile, finished the regular season second in the OHL, and McDavid added an additional four goals and 19 points in 14 postseason games before Erie fell to the [[Guelph Storm]] in the Western Conference finals.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Nicholson |first1=Lorna Schultz |title=Connor McDavid: The Threat with the Puck |date=2017 |publisher=Scholastic Canada Ltd. |location=Toronto, ON |isbn=978-1-4431-5778-0 |page=24 season|2014–15 season]] during training camp.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Connor McDavid Named Captain |url=https://ottershockey.com/article/connor-mcdavid-named-captain |publisher=Ontario Hockey League the first 18 games of the season and led the OHL with 51 points before breaking his hand in a [[Fighting in ice hockey|fight]] with Bryson Cianfrone of the [[Mississauga Steelheads]] on November 11. McDavid had already recorded a goal and assist at the time of his injury, giving him a [[Gordie Howe hat trick]], but was forced to miss both the Subway Super Series and several regular season games.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Sager |first=Neate |title=Top NHL draft prospect Connor McDavid injured in fight, out indefinitely for Erie Otters |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/jrhockey-buzzing-the-net/top-nhl-draft-prospect-connor-mcdavid-injured-in-fight--ejected-from-erie-otters-game--video-004323026.html |work=Buzzing the Net |publisher=[[Yahoo! Sports]] |date=November 11, 2014 |access-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205202841/https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/jrhockey-buzzing-the-net/top-nhl-draft-prospect-connor-mcdavid-injured-in-fight--ejected-from-erie-otters-game--video-004323026.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Fox |first=Luke |title=The great myth of the Gordie Howe hat trick |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/hockey/nhl/gordie-howe-hat-trick-goal-assist-fight-double-gordie-two-iginla-shanahan-tocchet/ |work=[[Sportsnet]] |date=June 10, 2016 |access-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205202841/https://www.sportsnet.ca/hockey/nhl/gordie-howe-hat-trick-goal-assist-fight-double-gordie-two-iginla-shanahan-tocchet/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He missed six weeks of the regular OHL season, first to injury and then international competition, before returning on January 8 for a 4–3 defeat from the [[Sarnia Sting]].<ref>{{cite news |title=OHL Roundup: Sting stun Otters to spoil McDavid's return from world juniors |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/ohl-roundup-sting-stun-otters-to-spoil-mcdavids-return-from-world-juniors/c-747776 |publisher=National Hockey League |date=January 8, 2015 |access-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205202841/https://www.nhl.com/news/ohl-roundup-sting-stun-otters-to-spoil-mcdavids-return-from-world-juniors/c-747776 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Shortly after his return, McDavid was named the captain of Team Cherry at the 2015 [[CHL/NHL Top Prospects Game]]; teammate [[Dylan Strome]] was selected to captain Team Orr.<ref name=\"cherry\">{{cite news |title=McDavid named Captain for Team Orr, Strome alternate for Team Cherry |url=https://ottershockey.com/mcdavid-named-captain-for-team-orr-strome-alternate-for-team-cherry |publisher=Ontario Hockey League |agency=Erie Otters |date=January 14, 2015 |access-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205202841/https://ottershockey.com/mcdavid-named-captain-for-team-orr-strome-alternate-for-team-cherry |url-status=live }}</ref> After recording his first OHL [[hat-trick]] on February 25 against the Guelph Storm, McDavid recorded his 100th point of the season with a goal and assist against the Owen Sound Attack. He was the fourth OHL player that season to reach 100 points, doing so in only 38 games due to his injury, and was named OHL Player of the Month for February.<ref>{{cite news |title=Connor McDavid named OHL Player of the Month |url=https://ottershockey.com/connor-mcdavid-named-ohl-player-of-the-month |publisher=Ontario Hockey League |agency=Erie Otters |date=March 4, 2015 |access-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205202840/https://ottershockey.com/connor-mcdavid-named-ohl-player-of-the-month |url-status=live }}</ref> He finished the regular season with 44 goals and 120 points in 47 games, with at least one point in all but two of those games, and he led the OHL with a +60 [[Plus–minus (sports)|plus–minus]] rating.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Otters trio enjoys remarkable finish |url=https://ontariohockeyleague.com/otters-trio-enjoys-remarkable-finish/ |publisher=Ontario Hockey League |date=March 22, 2015 |access-date=February 6, 2022 |archive-date=February 6, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220206205521/https://ontariohockeyleague.com/otters-trio-enjoys-remarkable-finish/ |url-status=live }}</ref>\n\nAt the end of the 2014–15 season, McDavid received a number of awards from the OHL and CHL. In addition to winning the Bobby Smith Trophy and CHL Scholastic Player of the Year for the second consecutive year, he was also named to the OHL First All-Star Team, received the [[Red Tilson Trophy]] for the most outstanding player in the OHL, the [[CHL Player of the Year]] title, and the [[CHL Top Draft Prospect Award]].<ref name=\"tilson\">{{cite news |title=2014–15 OHL Awards Ceremony Recap |url=https://ontariohockeyleague.com/2014-15-ohl-awards-ceremony-recap/ |publisher=Ontario Hockey League |date=June 10, 2015 |access-date=February 6, 2022 |archive-date=February 6, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220206205511/https://ontariohockeyleague.com/2014-15-ohl-awards-ceremony-recap/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=\"links\">{{cite news |title=CHL announces 2014–15 Award winners |url=https://ontariohockeyleague.com/chl-announces-2014-15-award-winners/ |publisher=Ontario Hockey League |date=May 30, 2015 |access-date=February 6, 2022 |archive-date=February 6, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220206205513/https://ontariohockeyleague.com/chl-announces-2014-15-award-winners/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=\"first team\">{{cite news |title=OHL Announces 2014–15 All-Star Teams |url=https://ontariohockeyleague.com/ohl-announces-2014-15-all-star-teams/ |publisher=Ontario Hockey League |date=May 20, 2015 |access-date=February 6, 2022 |archive-date=February 6, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220206205514/https://ontariohockeyleague.com/ohl-announces-2014-15-all-star-teams/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Although the Otters were defeated in the [[J. Ross Robertson Cup]] finals by the [[Oshawa Generals]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Oshawa Generals win Robertson Cup |url=https://ontariohockeyleague.com/oshawa-generals-win-robertson-cup/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220206210127/https://ontariohockeyleague.com/oshawa-generals-win-robertson-cup/ |url-status=live }}</ref> McDavid recorded 21 goals and 49 points in 20 postseason games, including two goals and six points in five championship series games, and received the [[Wayne Gretzky 99 Award]] for the most valuable player in the OHL playoffs.<ref name=\"gretzky\">{{cite news |title=McDavid wins '99' Award as OHL Playoff MVP |url=https://ontariohockeyleague.com/mcdavid-wins-99-award-as-ohl-playoff-mvp/ |publisher=Ontario Hockey League |date=May |url-status=live }}</ref> With five individual OHL awards in his three-year career, McDavid also finished his junior hockey tenure as the most decorated player in league history.<ref name=\"mcgran\">{{cite news |last=McGran |first=Kevin |title=Connor McDavid named OHL's most valuable player Altogether, McDavid had 285 points in his career with the Otters, 24 fewer than franchise leader [[Brad Boyes]], and led the franchise with 188 assists.<ref>{{cite news |last=Fernandes |first=Victor (2015–present)===\n\n====2015–2017: Rookie season, captaincy and playoff debut====\nThe [[Edmonton Oilers]] of the [[National Hockey League]] (NHL), who were coming off of a 24–44–14 season, selected McDavid [[List of first overall NHL draft picks|first overall]] in the [[2015 NHL entry draft]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Strang |first=Katie |title=Connor McDavid goes No. 1 to Oilers; Sabres get Jack |url-status=live }}</ref> On July 3, 2015, he signed a three-year, [[entry-level contract]] with the team; the total deal was worth $11.3 million, including up to $3.775 million annually in bonus incentives.<ref>{{cite news |last=Van Diest |first=Derek |title=No. 1 pick McDavid agrees to first contract with Oilers game, McDavid suffered a fractured left [[clavicle]] after a collision into the boards with [[Brandon Manning]] and [[Michael Del Zotto]] of the [[Philadelphia Flyers]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Van Diest |first=Derek |title=Oilers' McDavid has fractured clavicle, out months |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/oilers-mcdavid-has-fractured-clavicle-out-months/c-786300 |publisher=National Hockey League hometown [[Toronto Maple Leafs]], McDavid was involved in all five of the Oilers' points: in addition to scoring twice, he also had assists on every part of [[Jordan Eberle]]'s [[hat trick]]. That single-game performance helped boost McDavid to tenth overall in NHL rookie scoring at that point, despite playing in only his 19th game of the [[2015–16 NHL season|2015–16 season]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Feschuk |first=Dave |title=Connor McDavid has five-point night as Oilers down Leafs |url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/leafs/2016/02/11/connor-mcdavid-has-five-point-night-as-oilers-down-leafs.html |work=Toronto Star |date=February 11, 2016 |access-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205191700/https://www.thestar.com/sports/leafs/2016/02/11/connor-mcdavid-has-five-point-night-as-oilers-down-leafs.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Despite appearing in only 45 games due to injury, McDavid finished his rookie season with 16 goals and 32 assists, fourth in rookie scoring. He was third place in [[Calder Memorial Trophy]] voting, behind [[Shayne Gostisbehere]] of the Philadelphia Flyers and winner [[Artemi Panarin]] of the [[Chicago Blackhawks]], and all three players were named to the 2015–16 [[NHL All-Rookie Team]].<ref name=\"rookie\">{{cite news |title=Oilers' Connor McDavid finishes 3rd in voting for rookie of the year |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/edmonton/mcdavid-calder-voting-1.3648573 |publisher=[[CBC News]] |date=June 22, 2016 |access-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205191700/https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/edmonton/mcdavid-calder-voting-1.3648573 |url-status=live }}</ref>\n\nOn October 5, 2016, the Oilers named McDavid their captain for the [[2016–17 NHL season|2016–17 season]]. At 19 years and 266 days old, McDavid became the youngest captain in NHL history, unseating [[Gabriel Landeskog]], who was 20 days older when he became captain of the [[Colorado Avalanche]] in September 2012.<ref name=\"youngest\">{{cite news |last=Custance |first=Craig |title=Oilers make Connor McDavid the youngest captain in NHL history |url-status=live }}</ref> After a 10-game goal drought early in the season, McDavid recorded his first NHL hat-trick on November 19 in a 5–2 victory over the Dallas Stars.<ref>{{Cite news Oilers|url=https://edmontonsun.com/sports/hockey/nhl/edmonton-oilers/connor-mcdavid-its-cup-or-bust-for-the-edmonton-oilers |last=Tychkowski |first=Robert |newspaper=[[The Edmonton Sun]] |date=May 16, 2023 |access-date=June 24, 2024 }}</ref> The team had a \"disastrous\" start to the season, winning only two of their first ten games and sitting second-to-last in the NHL. McDavid missed games due to injury in this period, and at the same point was tied for 57th in league scoring.<ref>{{cite news |title=Sifting through the rubble of Edmonton Oilers' disastrous first 10 games|url=https://edmontonjournal.com/sports/hockey/nhl/cult-of-hockey/sifting-through-the-rubble-of-edmonton-oilers-disastrous-first-10-games |last=McCurdy |first=Bruce |newspaper=[[Edmonton Journal]] |date=November 5, 2023 |access-date=June 24, 2024 }}</ref> On November 12, the team fired coach Woodcroft and replaced him with Kris Knoblauch, who had previously been McDavid's coach with the Erie Otters. At the time of the coaching change, the Oilers had a 3–9–1 record.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 12, 2023 |title=Woodcroft fired as Oilers coach, replaced by Knoblauch |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/jay-woodcroft-fired-as-oilers-coach-replaced-by-kris-knoblauch |access-date=June 24, 2024 |website=NHL.com |publisher=National Hockey League}}</ref> ''[[The Athletic]]'' remarked that the hirings of Jackson and Knoblauch \"have put the spotlight squarely on McDavid,\" given their prior relations to him.<ref>{{cite news |title=A new Oilers coach, Connor McDavid and a problem of perception|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5061182/2023/11/13/oilers-knoblauch-mcdavid-woodcroft/ |last=Nugent-Bowman |first=Daniel |website=[[The Athletic]] |date=November 13, 2023 |access-date=June 24, 2024 }}</ref> The team's fortunes soon revived under Knoblauch, and McDavid saw his scoring surge. On April 15, 2024, McDavid recorded his 100th assist of the 2023–24 season on a goal by [[Zach Hyman]] in a 9–2 win over the San Jose Sharks to become the first NHL player in over three decades and the fourth player in NHL history (alongside Wayne Gretzky, Mario Lemieux and [[Bobby Orr]]) to achieve the feat.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nhl.com/news/connor-mcdavid-gets-100-assists-in-season-for-edmonton-oilers |title=McDavid becomes 4th player in NHL history to get 100 assists in season |author=National Hockey League |website=nhl.com |publisher=National Hockey League |date=April 16, 2024 |access-date=April 16, 2024}}</ref> After ending the season with 32 goals and 100 assists for 132 points in 76 games, McDavid and the Oilers eliminated the Los Angeles Kings in the first round for the third straight season in five games, the Vancouver Canucks in seven games and the Dallas Stars in six games in the [[NHL conference finals|third round]] to help clinch the Oilers first appearance in the [[2024 Stanley Cup Final|Stanley Cup Final]] since 2006.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Moddejonge |first1=Gerry |title=Oilers withstand late Stars rally in Game 6, advance to Stanley Cup Final |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/dallas-stars-edmonton-oilers-game-6-recap-june-2 |website=NHL.com |access-date=June 2, 2024 |date=June 2, 2024}}</ref> After losing the first three games of the series against the Florida Panthers, McDavid led the team on a comeback to avert elimination with a historic scoring surge in the next two games. In game four, he registered his 32nd assist of the playoffs on a goal by [[Dylan Holloway]], breaking Wayne Gretzky's record for most assists in one playoff year in an 8–1 victory.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Crowther |first1=Hunter |title=Oilers' Connor McDavid breaks NHL record for most assists in a single post-season |url=https://www.dailyfaceoff.com/news/oilers-connor-mcdavid-breaks-nhl-record-for-most-assists-in-a-single-post-season |access-date=June 18, 2024 |date=June 16, 2024}}</ref> Following a dominant performance in which he scored four points during a 5–3 victory in the fifth game, McDavid achieved a historic feat by becoming the first player in NHL history to achieve back-to-back games with four points or more in the Stanley Cup Finals. Additionally, he also holds the record for most points accumulated over two games in the Stanley Cup Finals.<ref>{{cite news |title='He did what?': Oilers' McDavid wows with spectacular assist, scoring record |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nhl/article/he-did-what-oilers-mcdavid-wows-with-spectacular-assist-in-game-5 |work=[[Sportsnet]] |access-date=June 20, 2024 |date=June 18, 2024}}</ref> The Oilers forced the series to seven games, but were ultimately defeated. McDavid was awarded the [[Conn Smythe Trophy]] as the most valuable player of the postseason. He was the sixth person from the losing finalist team to receive the award, only the second forward (after [[Reggie Leach]] in [[1976 Stanley Cup Final|1976]]) to do so, and the first person since [[Jean-Sébastien Giguère]] of the [[Mighty Ducks of Anaheim]] in [[2003 Stanley Cup Final|2003]].<ref name=ConnSmythe>{{cite news |title=Consolation prize: Oilers' McDavid wins Conn Smythe Trophy in losing effort|url=https://edmontonjournal.com/sports/hockey/nhl/oilers-mcdavid-wins-conn-smythe-trophy |last=Matheson |first=Jim |newspaper=[[Edmonton Journal]] |date=June 25, 2024 |access-date=June 25, 2024 }}</ref> McDavid did not accept the trophy when it was presented on the ice and remained with his teammates in the locker room, later commenting that \"[he] wouldn't have gone out there for a million dollars.\"<ref>{{cite web |last1=Aditi |first1=Abhilasha |title=Connor McDavid addresses his refusal of Conn Smythe Trophy |url=https://www.sportskeeda.com/us/nhl/news-connor-mcdavid-addresses-refusal-conn-smythe-trophy |website=[[Sportskeeda]] |access-date=5 February 2026 |date=3 October 2024 }}</ref>\n\nOn January 20, 2025, McDavid was handed a three-game suspension for [[cross-checking]] [[Conor Garland]] in a game against the Vancouver Canucks on January 18, 2025.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.nhl.com/news/oilers-connor-mcdavid-suspended-three-games-for-cross-checking|title= McDavid of Oilers suspended 3 games for cross-checking|website=NHL.com|date= January 20, 2025|access-date= January 20, 2025}}</ref> McDavid tied for the lead in points in the [[2025 Stanley Cup playoffs|2025 playoffs]] with teammate [[Leon Draisaitl]], with seven goals and 33 points in 21 playoff games, but the Oilers once again lost to the [[Florida Panthers]] in the [[2025 Stanley Cup Final|Cup Final]], four games to two.\n\n====2025–present: Contract renewal, sixth Art Ross and fifth Ted Lindsay ====\n\nOn October 6, 2025, McDavid signed a two-year extension to remain with the Oilers for an average annual value of $12.5 million.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-10-06 |title=McDavid signs 2-year, $25M extension with Oilers |url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/story/_/id/46510665/connor-mcdavid-signs-2-year-25m-extension-oilers |access-date=2025-10-06 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> McDavid's [[2025–26 NHL season|2025–26 season]] saw him lead the league in points (138) and assists (90), winning his sixth Art Ross Trophy; this tied [[Gordie Howe]] and [[Mario Lemieux]] for the second-most scoring titles in league history. He recorded points in all 41 of Edmonton's wins, and had a career-high point streak of 20 games, in which he had 19 goals and 27 assists for 46 points.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://records.nhl.com/awards/trophies/art-ross-trophy|title= Art Ross Trophy|website=NHL.com|date= April 27, 2026|access-date= April 27, 2026}}</ref> He was named a finalist for the Ted Lindsay Award and the Hart Memorial Trophy, for the seventh time in both cases.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-04-28 |title=Celebrini, Kucherov, McDavid named Ted Lindsay Award finalists |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/ted-lindsay-award-finalists-for-most-outstanding-player-for-2025-26-announced-by-nhlpa |access-date=2026-04-28 |website=NHL.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Kucherov, MacKinnon, McDavid named Hart Trophy finalists |url=https://www.nhl.com/news//hart-trophy-finalists-for-most-valuable-player-for-2025-26-announced-by-nhl |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260508172506/https://www.nhl.com/news/hart-trophy-finalists-for-most-valuable-player-for-2025-26-announced-by-nhl |url-status=dead |archive-date=May 8, 2026 |website=NHL.com |date=May 8, 2026 |access-date=May 8, 2026}}</ref> The Oilers qualified for the [[2026 Stanley Cup playoffs]], but were ousted by the [[Anaheim Ducks]] in the first round, four games to two.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-04-30 |title=Ducks win Game 6, eliminate Oilers in Western 1st Round |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/edmonton-oilers-anaheim-ducks-game-6-recap-april-30-2026 |access-date=2026-04-30 |website=NHL.com |language=en}}</ref> McDavid would say afterward that \"we were an average team all year; an average team with high expectations, you're going to be disappointed. We just never found it.\"<ref>{{Cite web |date= May 1, 2026 |title=Oilers fall short of 'high expectations' with 1st round loss to Ducks |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/edmonton-oilers-fall-short-of-expectations-with-early-playoff-exit |access-date= May 1, 2026 |website=NHL.com |language=en}}</ref> On June 7, 2026, it was announced McDavid was voted as the winner of the Ted Lindsay Award for the fifth time; tying him with Wayne Gretzky for most award wins.<ref name=\"fifthtedlindsay\">{{Cite web |date=2026-06-07 |title=McDavid wins Ted Lindsay Award for 5th time with Oilers |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/connor-mcdavid-wins-ted-lindsay-award-for-5th-time-with-edmonton-oilers |access-date=2026-06-07 |website=NHL.com |language=en}}</ref>\n\nOn October 21, McDavid became the fastest player in NHL history to reach twenty assists in a season, doing so in his ninth game of the [[2026–27 NHL season|2026-27 season]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-10-21 |title=Bouchard scores in OT, Oilers recover against Wild to stay hot {{!}} NHL.com |language=en}}</ref>\n\n==International play==\n{{MedalTableTop|McDavid CAN.png|220px|McDavid with Canada in 2016|name=}}\n{{MedalSport|Men's [[ice Russia]]|}}\n{{MedalBottom}}\n\n===Junior===\nMcDavid's international ice hockey career began with the [[2013 World U-17 Hockey Challenge]], where he led the sixth-place Team Ontario with nine points in five games, including two goals and an assist in their 7–6 tournament-ending loss to Team Pacific.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Ontario finishes sixth place at 2013 WU17 |url=https://ontariohockeyleague.com/ontario-finishes-sixth-place-at-2013-wu17/ |work=Ontario Hockey League |date=January 3, 2013 |access-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205181838/https://ontariohockeyleague.com/ontario-finishes-sixth-place-at-2013-wu17/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Despite his team's disappointing performance, McDavid was named to the tournament all-star team.<ref name=\"wu17\">{{cite news |title=Connor McDavid named 2013 WU17 All-Star |url=https://ontariohockeyleague.com/2013-wu17-final-results/ |publisher=Ontario Hockey League |date=January 5, 2013 |access-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205182033/https://ontariohockeyleague.com/2013-wu17-final-results/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The next year, a 16-year-old McDavid was the youngest player in the [[2013 IIHF World U18 Championships|2013 World U18 Championships]]. Playing for the [[Canada men's national under-18 ice hockey team]], he skated on a line with [[Sam Reinhart]] and Sam Bennett, recording two goals and two assists in Canada's 4–1 opening-round win over [[Slovakia men's national under-18 ice hockey team|Slovakia]].<ref>{{cite news |title=McDavid, Canada win U-18 opener; USA defeated |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/mcdavid-canada-win-u-18-opener-usa-defeated/c-666504 |publisher=National Hockey League |date=April 18, 2013 |access-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-date=February 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205180933/https://www.nhl.com/news/mcdavid-canada-win-u-18-opener-usa-defeated/c-666504 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He led the tournament in scoring with eight goals and 14 assists, including a hat-trick during Canada's 6–0 quarterfinal win over the [[Czech Republic men's national under-18 ice hockey team|Czech Republic]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Aykroyd |first=Lucas |title=From U18 glory to WJC gold |url=https://www.iihf.com/en/news/18928/from-u18-glory-to-wjc-gold |publisher=[[International Ice Hockey Federation]] |date=May 5, 2020 |access-date=February 22, 2022 |archive-date=August 3, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200803123805/https://www.iihf.com/en/news/18928/from-u18-glory-to-wjc-gold |url-status=live }}</ref> Canada defeated the [[USA Hockey National Team Development Program|United States team]] 3–2 in the gold medal match, breaking United States' four-year championship streak, and McDavid was named both the Best Forward and Tournament MVP after the win.<ref name=\"u18\">{{Cite news |last=O'Brien |first=James |title=Canada tops U.S. to win 2013 IIHF U18 tournament gold |url=https://nhl.nbcsports.com/2013/04/28/canada-tops-u-s-to-win-2013-iihf-u18-tournament-gold/ |work=Pro Hockey Talk |publisher=NBC Sports |date=April 28, 2013 |access-date=February 22, 2022 |archive-date=October 23, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201023095447/https://nhl.nbcsports.com/2013/04/28/canada-tops-u-s-to-win-2013-iihf-u18-tournament-gold/ |url-status=live }}</ref>\n\nIn 2014, McDavid became the sixth 16-year-old in history to join the [[Canada men's national junior ice hockey team|Canadian junior team]] for that year's [[2014 World Junior Ice Hockey Championships|World Junior Championships]]. Although McDavid recorded a goal and three assists in the tournament, he went pointless in the last three games and spent most of the bronze medal match, in which Canada fell 2–1 to [[Russia men's national junior ice hockey team|Russia]], on the [[Substitution (sports)|bench]].<ref>{{cite news |title=World juniors 2014: Connor McDavid's youth shines through at all the wrong times |url=https://nationalpost.com/sports/world-juniors-2014-connor-mcdavids-youth-shines-through-at-all-the-wrong-times |work=[[National Post]] |date=January 5, 2014 |access-date=February 22, 2022}}</ref> He rejoined the team for the [[2015 World Junior Ice Hockey Championships|2015 World Junior Championships]], serving as an alternate captain and as the only 17-year-old on a team that was otherwise 19 years of age.<ref>{{cite news |last=Beacon |first=Bill |title=Connor McDavid leads stacked Canadian junior roster |url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/hockey/2014/12/01/mcdavid_and_fucale_lead_stacked_canadian_junior_roster.html |work=Toronto Star |date=December 1, 2014 |access-date=February 22, 2022 |archive-date=October 30, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151030131035/http://www.thestar.com/sports/hockey/2014/12/01/mcdavid_and_fucale_lead_stacked_canadian_junior_roster.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=McDavid named Alternate Captain for Team Canada |url=https://ottershockey.com/mcdavid-named-alternate-captain-for-team-canada |publisher=Ontario Hockey League |agency=Erie Otters |date=December 23, 2014 |access-date=February 22, 2022 |archive-date=February 22, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220222193729/https://ottershockey.com/mcdavid-named-alternate-captain-for-team-canada |url-status=live }}</ref> Canada took the gold medal in the tournament, defeating Russia 5–4 in the championship match, and McDavid's 11 points (three goals and eight assists) tied Sam Reinhart and [[Nic Petan]] for first in the tournament. He was named to the media all-star team at the end of the championships.<ref name=\"wjc all-star\">{{cite news |title=Canada's National Junior Team wins gold medal at 2015 IIHF World Junior Championship |url=https://www.hockeycanada.ca/en-ca/news/canadas-national-junior-team-wins-gold-medal-at-2015-iihf-world-junior-championship |publisher=Hockey Canada |date=January 5, 2015 |access-date=February 22, 2022 |archive-date=September 23, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200923101430/https://www.hockeycanada.ca/en-ca/news/canadas-national-junior-team-wins-gold-medal-at-2015-iihf-world-junior-championship |url-status=live }}</ref>\n\n===Senior===\nMcDavid first joined the [[Canada men's national ice hockey team|Canadian senior team]] for the [[2016 IIHF World Championship|2016 World Championship]]. Although he had eight assists in the tournament, McDavid did not score a goal until the gold-medal match against [[Finland men's national ice hockey team|Finland]], who the Canadians shut out 2–0 to win the tournament.<ref>{{cite news |last=Rodney |first=Ken |title=McDavid returns to Worlds with gold medal pedigree game until the final second, when [[Matt Duchene]] scored in the opposition's [[Empty net goal|empty net]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Schram |first=Carol |title=Connor McDavid helps Canada win 2nd straight World Hockey Championship, beating Finland 2–0 |url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/toronto/article/connor-mcdavid-helps-canada-win-2nd-straight-world-hockey-championship-beating-finland-2-0/ }}</ref> That same year, McDavid was named captain of [[Team North America]], a team of Canadian and American players aged 23 or under, at the [[2016 World Cup of Hockey]].<ref>{{cite news |last=McGran |first=Kevin |title=McDavid, 'Millennial' squad have plenty to prove despite low expectations in World Cup of Hockey |url-status=live }}</ref> Centring a line with [[Auston Matthews]] and [[Mark Scheifele]],<ref>{{cite news |last=Spector |first=Mark |title=Memories of electric Team North America have not faded games during the pre-tournament and round robin stages of the World Cup.<ref>{{cite news |last=Di Michele |first=Marcy |title=Can McDavid Be the Best Without Scoring? after the round-robin portion of the tournament, with Russia winning the tiebreaker.<ref>{{cite news |last=Peterson |first=Torie |title=Team North America eliminated from World Cup [[Ryan Nugent-Hopkins]] and [[Darnell Nurse]], finished the tournament third in scoring with five goals and 17 points in 10 games.<ref>{{cite news |last=Gazzola |first=Paul |title=Worlds: Medal round McDavid intended to play for Canada again at the [[2019 IIHF World Championship|2019 World Championship]], but suffered a leg injury at the end of the NHL season that kept him from participating.<ref>{{cite news |last=Suleymanov |first=Mark |title=Oilers' Connor McDavid won't play for Canada at world championships |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/ca/nhl/news/oilers-connor-mcdavid-wont-play-for-canada-world-championships/gx2d087cxbnz12la8bsktb7bx |work=The Sporting News |date=April 8, 2019 |access-date=February 22, 2022}}</ref>\n\nMcDavid was one of the first three players named to the [[Canada at the 2022 Winter Olympics|Canadian roster]] for the [[Ice hockey at the 2022 Winter Olympics – Men's tournament|2022 Winter Olympics]], joining Sidney Crosby and [[Alex Pietrangelo]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Crosby, McDavid, Pietrangelo named to Olympic team |url=https://www.tsn.ca/sidney-crosby-connor-mcdavid-alex-pietrangelo-team-canada-2022-olympics-1.1701671 |work=[[TSN Hockey]] |date=October 3, 2021 |access-date=February 22, 2022 |url-status=live }}</ref> However, in December 2021, the NHL declared that no players would be allowed to participate in the Winter Olympics, citing COVID-19 outbreaks throughout the league. McDavid, who had already missed a chance to participate in the [[Ice hockey at the 2018 Winter Olympics – Men's tournament|2018 Winter Olympics]] due to financial concerns from the NHL, was upset with the league's decision, saying, \"It's always been a dream of mine to play at the Olympics since I was a little kid. He described his childhood bedroom as \"pretty embarrassing\" for its volume of Maple Leafs memorabilia.<ref>{{cite news |last=Matheson |first=Jim |title=Oilers notes: McDavid was unabashed Maple Leafs fan as a youngster |url=https://edmontonjournal.com/sports/hockey/nhl/edmonton-oilers/snapshots-mcdavid-was-unabashed-leafs-fan-as-a-youngster |work=Edmonton Journal |date=February 11, 2016 |access-date=February 22, 2022 |archive-date=May 16, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210516211905/https://edmontonjournal.com/sports/hockey/nhl/edmonton-oilers/snapshots-mcdavid-was-unabashed-leafs-fan-as-a-youngster |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2023, he stated that he \"likes watching players more than teams\", and named the Maple Leafs and the [[Pittsburgh Penguins]] as the two teams he most enjoys watching for that reason.<ref>{{cite news |last= Zeisberger |first=Mike |title=McDavid talks pressure before draft, Bedard in exclusive Q&A with NHL.com |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/connor-mcdavid-exclusive-q-a-with-nhl-com-part-3-343314406 |work=NHL.com |date=April 10, 2023 |access-date=June 25, 2023 }}</ref> Outside of hockey, he supports the [[Toronto Blue Jays]] of [[Major League Baseball]] and threw out the [[ceremonial first pitch]] at a Blue Jays game in 2016.<ref>{{cite news |last=McGrath |first=Kaitlyn |title=Connor McDavid throws first pitch at Blue Jays game |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/eh-game/connor-mcdavid-throws-first-pitch-at-blue-jays-game-235027255.html |work=Eh Game |publisher=Yahoo! Sports |date=June 10, 2016 |access-date=February 22, 2022}}</ref>\n\nOn June 21, 2017, [[Electronic Arts]] revealed that McDavid would be the cover athlete for ''[[NHL 18]]'', their annual installment
