Pearson Award winners]]\n[[Category:Medalists at the 2026 Winter Olympics]]\n[[Category:National Hockey League All-Stars]]\n[[Category:Olympic gold medalists for the United States in ice hockey]]\n[[Category:People from Scottsdale, Arizona]]\n[[Category:First overall NHL draft picks]]\n[[Category:Sportspeople from San Ramon, California]]\n[[Category:Rocket Richard Trophy winners]]\n[[Category:Toronto Maple Leafs draft picks]]\n[[Category:Toronto Maple Leafs players]]\n[[Category:USA Hockey National Team Development Program players]]\n[[Category:ZSC Lions players]]\n[[Category:21st-century American sportsmen]]\n[[Category:4 Nations Face-Off players]]"}}}]},{"pageid":53736994,"ns":0,"title":"Cale Makar","revisions":[{"slots":{"main":{"contentmodel":"wikitext","contentformat":"text/x-wiki","content":"{{short description|Canadian ice hockey player (born 1998)}}\n{{Use Canadian English|date=November 2019}}\n{{Use mdy dates|date=June 2022}}\n{{Infobox ice hockey biography\n| name = Cale Makar\n| image = Cale Makar playing with the Avalanche in 2020 (Quintin Soloviev) (cropped).jpg\n| image_size = 230px\n| caption = Makar with the [[Colorado Avalanche]] in January 2020\n| birth_date = {{birth date and age|1998|10|30}}\n| birth_place = [[Calgary]], Alberta, Canada\n| height_ft = 6\n| height_in = 0\n| weight_lb = 187\n| position = [[Defenceman|Defence]]\n| shoots = Right\n| league = [[National Hockey League|NHL]]\n| team = [[Colorado Avalanche]]\n| ntl_team = Canada\n| draft = 4th overall\n| draft_year = 2017\n| draft_team = [[Colorado Avalanche]]\n| career_start = 2019\n| career_end = \n}}\n'''Cale Douglas Makar'''<ref>{{cite web |title=2018-19 Hockey Roster - Cale Makar |url=https://umassathletics.com/sports/mens-ice-hockey/roster/cale-makar/10697 |website=umassathletics.com |access-date=March 1, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201112003514/https://umassathletics.com/sports/mens-ice-hockey/roster/cale-makar/10697 |archive-date=November 12, 2020}}</ref> (born October 30, 1998) is a Canadian professional [[ice hockey]] player who is a [[defenceman]] and [[Captain (ice hockey)#Alternate captains|alternate captain]] for the [[Colorado Avalanche]] of the [[National Hockey League]] (NHL). He was selected with the fourth overall pick by the Avalanche in the [[2017 NHL entry draft]].<ref>{{cite news | url = https://calgaryherald.com/sports/hockey/nhl/calgarys-cale-makar-becomes-highest-drafted-player-from-ajhl | title = Calgary's Cale Makar becomes highest drafted player from AJHL | newspaper = [[Calgary Herald]] | date = June 23, 2017 | accessdate = June 23, 2017 | archive-date = June 24, 2017 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170624063036/http://calgaryherald.com/sports/hockey/nhl/calgarys-cale-makar-becomes-highest-drafted-player-from-ajhl | url-status = live}}</ref>\n\nAfter two seasons in the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA) with the [[UMass Minutemen ice hockey|UMass Minutemen]], Makar debuted in the NHL during the [[2019 Stanley Cup playoffs|2019 playoffs]]. Playing his first full season in [[2019–20 NHL season|2019–20]], he made an immediate impact and won the [[Calder Memorial Trophy]] as rookie of the year. In his second professional season he was nominated for the [[James Norris Memorial Trophy]], awarded to the league's best defenceman, and won the Norris in the following [[2021–22 NHL season|2022]]; he later won a second Norris in the [[2024–25 NHL season|2025]], in his fifth nomination. Makar won the [[Stanley Cup]] with the Avalanche in [[2022 Stanley Cup Final|2022]], winning the [[Conn Smythe Trophy]] as the most valuable player in the [[2022 Stanley Cup playoffs|2022 playoffs]]. He has been widely cited as one of the best defencemen and best players in the modern NHL.<ref>{{cite web |title=Avs' Cale Makar has a strong case for being a top-five player in the NHL after his dominant 2022 playoffs |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/ca/nhl/news/cale-makar-top-five-player-nhl-avalanche/zfrjd7e3h7d1yjjghmocscil |last=Murphy |first=Bryan |website=[[The Sporting News]] |access-date=June 28, 2022 |date=June 28, 2022 |archive-date=June 27, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220627220826/https://www.sportingnews.com/ca/nhl/news/cale-makar-top-five-player-nhl-avalanche/zfrjd7e3h7d1yjjghmocscil |url-status=live}}</ref>\n\nInternationally, Makar has played for the [[Canada men's national junior ice hockey team|Canadian junior team]], winning gold at the [[2018 World Junior Ice Hockey Championships|2018 World Junior Championships]]. With the [[Canada men's national ice hockey team|senior national team]], he won gold at the [[2025 4 Nations Face-Off]] and silver at the [[Ice hockey at the 2026 Winter Olympics - Men's tournament|2026 Winter Olympics]].\n\n==Playing career==\n\n===Junior===\nMakar, a [[Calgary]] native, first played within the Crowchild Blackhawks minor-hockey program before moving to play with the Northwest Calgary Athletic Association (NWCAA) Bruins at the [[Minor ice hockey#Age categories|Bantam level]] in 2011. He also played bantam with the Calgary Flames before moving to minor midget with the NWCAA Stampeders.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.ammhl.ca/ | title = AMMHL congratulates NHL draft choices of 2017 | publisher = AMMHL.com | date = June 29, 2017 | accessdate = June 29, 2017 | archive-date = July 6, 2017 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170706145647/http://www.ammhl.ca/ | url-status = live}}</ref> Makar was originally drafted at the [[Junior ice hockey|major junior level]] by the [[Western Hockey League]] (WHL)'s [[Medicine Hat Tigers]] in the eighth round, 164th overall, of the 2013 WHL Bantam Draft.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Vickers|first1=Aaron|title=2017 Draft: Cale Makar rapidly gaining attention|url=https://www.nhl.com/news/cale-makar-nhl-draft-profile-287984570|publisher=[[National Hockey League]]|date=April 10, 2017|access-date=April 10, 2017|archive-date=April 10, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170410215135/https://www.nhl.com/news/cale-makar-nhl-draft-profile/c-287984570|url-status=live}}</ref>\n\nHaving returned to the Calgary Flames for the minor midget level, in his only full season with the club in 2014–15, Makar led the team in scoring with 23 points in 34 league games, being named the team's Most Valuable Player and selected to the [[Alberta Midget Hockey League]] First All-Star Team. To retain his [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] eligibility, Makar joined as an affiliate player to the [[Brooks Bandits]] of the [[Alberta Junior Hockey League]] (AJHL) at the tail end of the season, recording five points in three regular season games. In helping the Bandits reach the finals, Makar was third among defenceman in scoring with 7 points in 20 games. Having agreed to return with the Bandits in the forthcoming seasons, Makar announced his commitment to play collegiate hockey with the [[UMass Minutemen ice hockey|University of Massachusetts Amherst]] of the [[Hockey East]] NCAA conference on August 29, 2015.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.juniorhockey.ca/news/news_detail.php?news_id=87733 | title = Cale Makar commits to the University of Massachusetts | website = juniorhockey.ca | date = August 29, 2015 | accessdate = August 29, 2015 | archive-date = November 13, 2017 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20171113060153/http://www.juniorhockey.ca/news/news_detail.php?news_id=87733 | url-status = dead}}</ref>\n\nAs a 17-year-old, Makar established himself as a standout defenceman with the Bandits in 2015–16, logging 55 points in 54 games, en route to earning AJHL All-League and All-Rookie recognition. He scored 14 points in 13 games to help the Bandits claim the AJHL championship. His productive season collected AJHL and CJHL Rookie of the Year Awards, the Western Canada Cup Top Defenceman Award, and the RBC Cup Top Defenceman, Top Scorer and Most Valuable Player awards.<ref name=\"AJHL\">{{cite web | url = http://dailycollegian.com/2017/10/19/cale-makar-umass-hockeys-crowned-jewel/ | title = Cale Makar: UMass hockey's crown jewel | website = daileycollegian.com | date = October 19, 2017 | accessdate = October 19, 2017 | archive-date = October 19, 2017 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20171019133912/http://dailycollegian.com/2017/10/19/cale-makar-umass-hockeys-crowned-jewel/ | url-status = live}}</ref>\n\nMakar sustained and built upon his previous success in the 2016–17 season to lead all defencemen and finished sixth among all skaters in the AJHL with 75 points (24 goals and 51 assists) in 54 games, collecting the league's MVP and top defenceman accolades. He had 16 points in 13 playoff games to help Brooks to a second straight AJHL championship and six points in five games to help the Bandits to a second-place finish in the [[Royal Bank Cup]]. He was chosen as the RBC Cup Top Defenceman and Most Valuable Player, the first player to ever be named RBC Cup MVP in back-to-back seasons. He received the CJHL Most Valuable Player Award and won the prestigious RBC National Junior A Player of the Year Award.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.nhl.com/news/cale-makar-of-brooks-5-things-to-know-for-2017-nhl-draft-289683602 | title = 5 things to know about Cale Makar | publisher = [[National Hockey League]] | date = June 1, 2017 | access-date = June 1, 2017 | archive-date = September 5, 2017 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170905200321/https://www.nhl.com/news/cale-makar-of-brooks-5-things-to-know-for-2017-nhl-draft/c-289683602 | url-status = live}}</ref>\n\n[[File:2017 NHL Entry Draft (34671833934).jpg|thumb|230px|left|Makar selected by the [[Colorado Avalanche]] at the [[2017 NHL entry draft]].]]\nThrough Makar's rapid rise up the rankings before the [[2017 NHL entry draft]], he was considered a top prospect and one of the top defencemen available.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nhl.com/avalanche/news/cale-makar-2017-nhl-draft-prospect-profile-289940168|title=Makar Following Jost's Path To The NHL|website=NHL.com|date=June 15, 2017|access-date=June 16, 2017|archive-date=November 13, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171113112712/https://www.nhl.com/avalanche/news/cale-makar-2017-nhl-draft-prospect-profile/c-289940168|url-status=live}}</ref> He was described as a dynamic skater that creates offence whenever he is on the ice.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nhl.com/canucks/news/prospect-profile-cale-makar-289843066|title=Prospect Profile: Cale Makar|website=NHL.com|date=June 9, 2017|access-date=June 16, 2017|archive-date=November 13, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171113114234/https://www.nhl.com/canucks/news/prospect-profile-cale-makar/c-289843066|url-status=live}}</ref> Makar was ultimately selected fourth overall by the [[Colorado Avalanche]], the second defenceman selected in the draft, after third overall selection [[Miro Heiskanen]]. Makar became the highest-drafted player to come straight from the AJHL, and just the second in the first round since [[Joe Colborne]] in [[2008 NHL entry draft|2008]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.cjhlhockey.com/view/cjhl/news-848/news_488072 | title = CJHL's Cale Makar goes fourth overall in draft | publisher = [[Canadian Junior Hockey League]] | date = June 24, 2017 | accessdate = June 24, 2017 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20171113060242/http://www.cjhlhockey.com/view/cjhl/news-848/news_488072 | archive-date = November 13, 2017 | url-status = dead}}</ref>\n\n===College===\nDespite his blue-chip prospect status, Makar opted to remain loyal to his commitment to joining the rebuilding UMass Minuteman program for the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's ice hockey season|2017–18 season]].<ref name=\"develop\">{{cite web | url = https://www.nhl.com/avalanche/news/cale-makar-excited-to-develop-at-umass-290735510 | title = Makar excited to develop at UMass | publisher = [[Colorado Avalanche]] | date = August 23, 2017 | access-date = August 23, 2017 | archive-date = November 13, 2017 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20171113114236/https://www.nhl.com/avalanche/news/cale-makar-excited-to-develop-at-umass/c-290735510 | url-status = live}}</ref> As a freshman, he immediately assumed a top-pairing role, alongside Jake McLaughlin, and recorded his first collegiate point in his debut against [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's ice hockey|Arizona State University]] on October 6, 2017. He recorded his first goal in a 4–0 victory over [[Merrimack Warriors men's ice hockey|Merrimack College]] on October 27, 2017.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://dailycollegian.com/2017/10/27/umass-defensemen-register-all-four-goals-in-4-0-victory-over-merrimack/ | title = UMass defenseman register all four goals in 4–0 victory over Merrimack | website = dailycollegian.com | date = October 27, 2017 | accessdate = October 27, 2017 | archive-date = October 28, 2017 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20171028060200/http://dailycollegian.com/2017/10/27/umass-defensemen-register-all-four-goals-in-4-0-victory-over-merrimack/ | url-status = live}}</ref>\n\nWhile showing an adjustment period to the collegiate level, Makar raised his game through the new year to help the Minutemen to turnaround their program to make the postseason before suffering a 7–2 defeat to the hands of [[Northeastern Huskies men's ice hockey|Northeastern University]]. He finished fifth on the team in scoring, second amongst defenceman, with 5 goals and 16 assists for 21 points in 34 games.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.masslive.com/umass/2018/04/cale_makar_umass_hockey_defens_1.html | title = Cale Makar to return to Minutemen for another season | publisher = [[MassLive.com]] | date = April 2, 2018 | url-status = live}}</ref> He was selected with co-Rookie of the Year honors by the New England Hockey Writers Association and by finishing ninth in defenceman scoring in the [[Hockey East]], he was selected to the conference's All-Rookie and Third All-Star Teams.<ref name=\"HE\">{{cite web | url = https://milehighsticking.com/2018/09/05/colorado-avalanche-getting-ready-watch-cale-makar-succeed/ | title = Avalanche getting ready to watch Makar succeed | website = milehighstickting.com | date = September 5, 2018 | accessdate = September 5, 2018 | archive-date = December 17, 2018 | archive-url and despite interest from the Colorado Avalanche in turning pro, Makar opted to continue his development in returning for his sophomore season with UMass in [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's ice hockey season|2018–19]].<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.gazettenet.com/Star-UMass-defenseman-Cale-Makar-returning-for-his-sophomore-season-16588183 | title = Star defenseman Cale Makar returning for his the first Minutemen honored as [[List of Hockey East Player of the Year|Hockey East Player of the Year]] after he led the league in scoring and finished second in the conference.<ref name=\"POY\">{{cite web | url = http://hockeyeastonline.com/men/articles/2019/03/cale-makar-tabbed-as-hockey-easts-best-player.php | title = Cale Makar tabbed as Hockey East's best player | publisher Award]] finalist.<ref>{{cite web |title=Makar Chosen As Hobey Baker Top 10 Finalist |url=https://umassathletics.com/news/2019/3/19/hockey-makar-chosen-as-hobey-baker-top-10-finalist.aspx |url-status=dead}}</ref>\n\n===Professional===\n\n====Debut and Calder Trophy (2019–2021)====\nOn April 14, 2019, the Avalanche signed Makar to a three-year, entry-level contract.<ref>{{cite web |title=Avalanche Signs Cale Makar to Entry-Level Contract |url=https://www.nhl.com/avalanche/news/avalanche-signs-cale-makar-to-entry-level-contract-306747474 |website=Colorado Avalanche |date=April |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190414162138/https://www.nhl.com/avalanche/news/avalanche-signs-cale-makar-to-entry-level-contract/c-306747474 |url-status=live}}</ref> He scored his first career NHL goal with his first shot in the league in his debut a day later, during game 3 of the first round of the [[2019 Stanley Cup playoffs]] against the [[Calgary Flames]]. In so doing, he became the first defenceman to score a playoff goal in his NHL debut.<ref>{{cite tweet|user=PR_NHL|number=1117987569827045376|date=April 15, 2019|title=Cale Makar of the @Avalanche is opening lineup for the [[2019–20 NHL season|2019–20 season]] and he scored his first career regular season goal in a 6–1 win over the [[Vegas Golden Knights]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Ex-UMass star Cale Makar scores first NHL regular-season goal in Colorado Avalanche win (video) |url-status=live}}</ref> He was subsequently named a Third Star of the Week for the week of November 10, becoming the first Avalanche rookie to earn the honor.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Parmele 4–0 road win against the [[Winnipeg Jets]], Makar became the second Avalanche defenceman to record 18 points in 18 games as a rookie.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Knabenbauer |first1=Ron |title=Rapid Recap: in a game against the [[Boston Bruins]] on December 7 and was listed as day-to-day. |url-status=live}}</ref> During the second round of the NHL playoffs, Makar surpassed the record for most points in a postseason by a rookie defenceman, before it was beaten by Hughes the following night.<ref>{{cite tweet|user=PR_NHL|number=1301731716852256768|date=September 4, 2020|title=Quinn Hughes (2–14—16) also set the NHL record for most points in a postseason by a rookie defenseman, a year.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Chambers |first1=Mike |title=Avalanche's Cale Makar wins Calder Trophy as NHL rookie of the year |url=https://www.denverpost.com/2020/09/21/cale-makar-calder-trophy-winner-avalanche/ |newspaper=[[The Denver Post]] |access-date=November 3, 2021 |date=September 21, 2020 |archive-date=June 22, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220622061729/https://www.denverpost.com/2020/09/21/cale-makar-calder-trophy-winner-avalanche/ |url-status=live}}</ref>\n\nAfter the [[COVID-19 pandemic|pandemic]]-shortened 2020–21 season, which saw the Avalanche win the [[Presidents' Trophy]], Makar was named a finalist for the [[James Norris Memorial Trophy]] and finished second in the voting for the trophy, behind [[Adam Fox]] of the [[New York Rangers]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Myers |first1=Tracey |title=Fox of Rangers wins Norris Trophy as best defenseman in NHL |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/new-york-rangers-adam-fox-wins-norris-trophy-325520492 |website=NHL.com |access-date=July 25, 2021 |date=June 29, 2021 |archive-date=June 17, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220617075122/https://www.nhl.com/news/new-york-rangers-adam-fox-wins-norris-trophy/c-325520492 |url-status=live}}</ref>\n\n====Stanley Cup, Norris and Conn Smythe trophies (2021–present)====\nOn July 24, 2021, Makar signed a six-year, $54 million extension with the Avalanche.<ref>{{cite web |title=Cale Makar Signs Six-Year Contract |url=https://www.nhl.com/avalanche/news/avalanche-re-signs-cale-makar-to-six-year-contract-325775878 |website=NHL.com |access-date=July 25, 2021 |date=July 24, 2021 |archive-date=April 3, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220403212407/https://www.nhl.com/avalanche/news/avalanche-re-signs-cale-makar-to-six-year-contract/c-325775878 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Wyshynski |first1=Greg |title=Colorado Avalanche re-sign Cale Makar to six-year, $54M contract |url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/story/_/id/31875002/colorado-avalanche-re-sign-cale-makar-six-year-54m-contract |website=ESPN.com |access-date=November 3, 2021 |date=July 24, 2021 |archive-date=June 22, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220622061730/https://www.espn.com/nhl/story/_/id/31875002/colorado-avalanche-re-sign-cale-makar-six-year-54m-contract |url-status=live}}</ref> On October 28, Makar scored two points (one goal and one assist) in a 4–3 win against the [[St. Louis Blues]], in doing so, he scored his 100th point in just 108 games, which tied him with [[Sergei Zubov]] as the sixth-fastest defenceman to accomplish this feat.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Parmele |first1=Callie |title=Makar Hits Century Mark in St. Louis |url=https://www.nhl.com/avalanche/news/makar-records-100th-career-point-327355166 |website=NHL.com |access-date=November 3, 2021 |date=October 28, 2021 |archive-date=June 22, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220622061731/https://www.nhl.com/avalanche/news/makar-records-100th-career-point/c-327355166 |url-status=live}}</ref> On March 25, 2022, Makar scored his 24th goal of the 2021–22 season in a 6–3 win against the [[Philadelphia Flyers]], breaking the Avalanche's single-season record for goals scored by a defenceman.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Fredrickson |first1=Kyle |title=Cale Makar sets Avalanche franchise record for defenseman goals in victory over Flyers |url=https://www.denverpost.com/2022/03/25/cale-makar-goals-record-avalanche-flyers/ |newspaper=[[The Denver Post]] |access-date=April 12, 2022 |date=March 25, 2022 |archive-date=April 20, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220420183509/https://www.denverpost.com/2022/03/25/cale-makar-goals-record-avalanche-flyers/ |url-status=live}}</ref> He finished the season with 28 goals, the most by a defenceman in the NHL since [[Brent Burns]] in the [[2016–17 NHL season|2016–17 season]], and 58 assists. 19 of his 28 goals were at even strength. Makar was named a James Norris Memorial Trophy finalist for the second consecutive season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Hedman, Josi, Makar finalists for 2021–22 Norris Trophy |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nhl/article/hedman-josi-makar-finalists-for-2021-22-norris-trophy/ |website=[[Sportsnet]] |access-date=May 10, 2022 |date=May 9, 2022 |archive-date=April 17, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230417100412/https://www.sportsnet.ca/nhl/article/hedman-josi-makar-finalists-for-2021-22-norris-trophy/ |url-status=live}}</ref> He won the Norris Trophy, the first Avalanche defenceman to do so, and finished eighth in voting for the [[Hart Memorial Trophy]], awarded by the [[Professional Hockey Writers' Association]] to the league's [[most valuable player]].<ref>{{cite web |date=June 21, 2022 |title=2022 NHL Awards: Full list of winners |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nhl/article/2022-nhl-awards-full-list-of-winners/ |access-date=June 22, 2022 |website=[[Sportsnet]] |archive-date=June 22, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220622195717/https://www.sportsnet.ca/nhl/article/2022-nhl-awards-full-list-of-winners/ |url-status=live}}</ref> The Avalanche finished first in the [[Western Conference (NHL)|Western Conference]], and second in the league overall, advancing into the [[2022 Stanley Cup playoffs|2022 playoffs]] to meet the [[Nashville Predators]] in the first round. Makar scored 10 points in a four-game sweep of the Predators, setting a record for points by a defenceman in the first four games of a postseason. Teammate [[Nathan MacKinnon]] remarked, \"he might be the best player in the league right now.\"<ref>{{cite web |title=Stanley Cup Playoffs Takeaways: Makar's magic on display as Avalanche sweep Predators |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nhl/article/stanley-cup-playoffs-takeaways-makars-magic-on-display-as-avalanche-sweep-predators/ |last=Sadler |first=Emily |website=[[Sportsnet]] |access-date=May 10, 2022 |date=May 10, 2022 |archive-date=May 11, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220511192512/https://www.sportsnet.ca/nhl/article/stanley-cup-playoffs-takeaways-makars-magic-on-display-as-avalanche-sweep-predators/ |url-status=live}}</ref> He would amass a further 19 points in the next three rounds, as the Avalanche ousted the Blues and the [[Edmonton Oilers]] before defeating the two-time defending champion [[Tampa Bay Lightning]] in the [[2022 Stanley Cup Final]], winning his first Stanley Cup. Makar finished the playoffs with a team-leading 29 points (eight goals and 21 assists), the fourth-most for a defenceman in a single postseason in league history.<ref>{{cite web |title=Cale Makar Wins 2022 Conn Smythe Award After Avalanche Capture Stanley Cup |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10040035-cale-makar-wins-2022-conn-smythe-award-after-avalanche-capture-stanley-cup |last=Zucker |first=Joseph |website=[[The Bleacher Report]] |access-date=June 27, 2022 |date=June 27, 2022 |archive-date=June 27, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220627065051/https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10040035-cale-makar-wins-2022-conn-smythe-award-after-avalanche-capture-stanley-cup |url-status=live}}</ref> He was awarded the [[Conn Smythe Trophy]] as the most valuable player in the postseason, and became only the third defenceman to win the Norris and Conn Smythe Trophies in the same season, after [[Bobby Orr]] ([[1969–70 NHL season|1970]] and [[1971–72 NHL season|1972]]) and [[Nicklas Lidström]] ([[2001–02 NHL season|2002]]).<ref>{{cite web |title=Avalanche's Cale Makar wins Conn Smythe Trophy as Stanley Cup Playoffs MVP |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nhl/article/avalanches-cale-makar-wins-conn-smythe-trophy-as-stanley-cup-playoffs-mvp/ |website=[[Sportsnet]] |access-date=June 27, 2022 |date=June 26, 2022 |archive-date=June 27, 2022 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Avalanche's Cale Makar wins Conn Smythe to cap historic season: 'We're watching greatness' |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3385053/2022/06/27/cale-makar-conn-smythe-avalanche/ |last=Baugh |first=Peter |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=June 27, 2022 |date=June 27, 2022 |archive-date=June 27, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220627124129/https://theathletic.com/3385053/2022/06/27/cale-makar-conn-smythe-avalanche/ |url-status=live}}</ref>\n\nMakar recorded 20 points in the first 17 games of the [[2022–23 NHL season|2022–23 season]], his 20th being a power play goal scored in a November 21, 2022, game against the [[Dallas Stars]]. This was his 200th career point in 195 games, the fastest pace of any NHL defenceman to that milestone.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://denvergazette.com/csg-web/cale-makar-sets-major-nhl-defensemen-record-in-shootout-victory-at-dallas-stars/article_98c835c2-6a0c-11ed-b293-4fd947c89274.html | title = Cale Makar sets major NHL defenseman record in shootout victory at Dallas Stars | publisher = The Denver Gazette | date = November 21, 2022 | accessdate = November 21, 2022 | archive-date = November 22, 2022 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20221122044032/https://denvergazette.com/csg-web/cale-makar-sets-major-nhl-defensemen-record-in-shootout-victory-at-dallas-stars/article_98c835c2-6a0c-11ed-b293-4fd947c89274.html | url-status = live}}</ref> Previous record holder [[Sergei Zubov]] reached the mark in 207 games.<ref>{{cite web |last=Davies |first=Colton |title=Cale Makar becomes fastest defenseman in NHL history to reach 200 points |url=https://www.dailyfaceoff.com/cale-makar-becomes-fastest-defenseman-in-nhl-history-to-reach-200-points/ |access-date=November 22, 2022 |website=Daily Faceoff |date=November 22, 2022 |archive-date=November 22, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221122061244/https://www.dailyfaceoff.com/cale-makar-becomes-fastest-defenseman-in-nhl-history-to-reach-200-points/ |url-status=live}}</ref> He attracted notice when, during a December 19 game against the [[New York Islanders]], he convinced the referee to rescind a tripping penalty that had been incorrectly assessed against Islanders forward [[Mathew Barzal]], with Makar clarifying that he had fallen on his own rather than being tripped. Barzal remarked that it was \"obviously, good sportsmanship on his part. I don't know if I would have done the same, to be honest with you.\"<ref>{{cite web |title=Why Avalanche's Cale Makar waved off penalty: 'I felt pretty guilty' |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4020267/2022/12/20/avalanche-cale-makar-penalty-islanders/ |last=Baugh |first=Peter |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=December 20, 2022 |date=December 20, |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Good guy Cale: Avalanche's Makar convinces ref to rescind Islanders' penalty |archive-date=December 20, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221220125415/https://www.sportsnet.ca/nhl/article/good-guy-cale-avalanches-makar-convinces-ref-to-rescind-islanders-penalty/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Injuries caused Makar to miss 22 games in the regular season, but he finished with 17 goals and 49 assists in 60 games, and was named a Norris Trophy finalist for the third consecutive year.<ref>{{cite web |title=Fox, Karlsson, Makar named Norris Trophy finalists |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/adam-fox-erik-karlsson-cale-makar-named-norris-trophy-finalists-344153866 |last=Lane |first=Jon |website=NHL.com |access-date=May 10, 2023 |date=May 4, 2023 |archive-date=May 10, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230510072730/https://www.nhl.com/news/adam-fox-erik-karlsson-cale-makar-named-norris-trophy-finalists/c-344153866 |url-status=live}}</ref>\n\n[[File:Cale Makar and Jared Mccann.jpg|thumb|upright|Makar after hitting [[Jared McCann]] during game four of the [[2023 Stanley Cup playoffs]].]]\nDuring game four of the first round of the [[2023 Stanley Cup playoffs]], Makar was involved in a controversial on-ice incident after delivering what many deemed to be a hard, late hit into the boards on [[Seattle Kraken]] forward [[Jared McCann]]. Although the play had not officially been whistled dead, the puck had been deflected into the upper safety netting and McCann had slowed his pace in anticipation of a whistle when Makar delivered the hit. The officials initially appeared to assess Makar for a five-minute major penalty; he ultimately received a two-minute interference call. McCann, who was ruled out for game five, was injured as a result of the hit and did not return for the rest of the game, which was ultimately a 3–2 overtime victory for the Kraken. After the game, Makar stated that he had not intended to injure McCann and that he was unsure if the puck was still in play at the time.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Clark |first1=Ryan S. |title=Kraken win but lose Jared McCann for Game 5, 'probably longer' |url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/story/_/id/36285258/kraken-lose-lw-mccann-injury-game-4-vs-avalanche |website=ESPN.com |access-date=April 25, 2023 |date=April 24, 2023 |archive-date=April 25, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230425055425/https://www.espn.com/nhl/story/_/id/36285258/kraken-lose-lw-mccann-injury-game-4-vs-avalanche |url-status=live}}</ref> The next day, Makar received a one-game suspension for the hit on McCann; this was the first suspension (and first disciplinary offense) of Makar's NHL career.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Clark |first1=Ryan S. |title=Colorado Avalanche top D-man Cale Makar suspended 1 game for hit |url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/story/_/id/36289816/colorado-avalanche-top-d-man-cale-makar-suspended-1-game-hit |website=ESPN.com |access-date=April 25, 2023 |date=April 25, 2023 |archive-date=April 25, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230425192047/https://www.espn.com/nhl/story/_/id/36289816/colorado-avalanche-top-d-man-cale-makar-suspended-1-game-hit |url-status=live}}</ref> Makar returned for the remainder of the series, which saw the Avalanche upset by the Kraken in seven games.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Durando |first1=Bennett |title=Avalanche's Stanley Cup defense sputters to end in Game 7 of first round vs. underdog Seattle Kraken |url=https://www.denverpost.com/2023/04/30/avalanche-kraken-game-7-loss-stanley-cup-playoffs/ |newspaper=[[The Denver Post]] |access-date=May 10, 2023 |date=April 30, 2023 |archive-date=May 11, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230511010457/https://www.denverpost.com/2023/04/30/avalanche-kraken-game-7-loss-stanley-cup-playoffs/ |url-status=live}}</ref>\n\nOn March 6, 2024, Makar recorded his first career NHL [[Hat-trick#Hockey|hat trick]] in a 7–2 victory over the [[Detroit Red Wings]]; becoming the first Avalanche defenceman to do so since [[Sandis Ozoliņš]] back on December 6, 1999.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Boulding |first1=Ryan |title=Makar's 1st hat trick helps Avalanche ease past Red Wings |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/detroit-red-wings-colorado-avalanche-game-recap-march-6 |website=NHL.com |access-date=March 7, 2024 |date=March 7, 2024 |archive-date=March 7, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240307083502/https://www.nhl.com/news/detroit-red-wings-colorado-avalanche-game-recap-march-6 |url-status=live}}</ref> He was voted a Norris Trophy finalist for the fourth consecutive season, having finished second in points and first in points-per-game among defencemen.<ref>{{cite web |title=Hughes, Josi, Makar named Norris Trophy finalists |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/2024-nhl-norris-trophy-finalists-announced |last=Satriano |first=David |work=NHL.com |date=May 1, 2024 |access-date=May 1, 2024 |archive-date=May 7, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240507203428/https://www.nhl.com/news/2024-nhl-norris-trophy-finalists-announced |url-status=live}}</ref> \n\nThe following [[2024–25 NHL season|2024–25 season]] would see Makar reach new offensive achievements. On April 3, 2025, he recorded his 30th goal of the season, becoming the ninth defenceman in NHL history to reach that mark, and only second in the post-[[2004–05 NHL lockout|lockout]] era.<ref>{{cite web |title=Avalanche's Cale Makar joins exclusive club with 30th goal |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nhl/article/avalanches-cale-makar-joins-exclusive-club-with-30th-goal/ |website=[[Sportsnet]] |date=April 3, 2025 |access-date=April 4, 2025}}</ref> In 80 games, he finished the season with 92 points (30 goals, 62 assists), ninth in league scoring overall. In addition to being a Norris Trophy finalist for the fifth time, he was for the first time a finalist for the [[Ted Lindsay Award]], awarded by the [[National Hockey League Players' Association]] to the \"most outstanding\" player in the NHL, ultimately going to Tampa Bay Lightning's forward [[Nikita Kucherov]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Quinn Hughes, Makar, Werenski named Norris Trophy finalists |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/norris-trophy-finalists-for-best-defenseman-for-2024-25-announced-by-nhl |website=NHL.com |date=April 29, 2025 |access-date=April 30, 2025 |archive-date=April 30, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250430014351/https://www.nhl.com/news/norris-trophy-finalists-for-best-defenseman-for-2024-25-announced-by-nhl |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Kucherov, MacKinnon, Makar named Ted Lindsay Award finalists |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/ted-lindsay-award-finalists-for-most-outstanding-player-for-2024-25-announced-by-nhlpa |website=NHL.com |date=April 30, 2025 |access-date=April 30, 2025 |archive-date=May 25, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250525000506/https://www.nhl.com/news/ted-lindsay-award-finalists-for-most-outstanding-player-for-2024-25-announced-by-nhlpa |url-status=live}}</ref> Makar was subsequently awarded his second career Norris Trophy on June 11, 2025, receiving 176 of 191 first-place votes.<ref name=\"2025Norris\">{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/cale-makar-wins-norris-trophy-for-2024-25-season |title=Makar of Avalanche surprised with Norris Trophy after golf outing |website=NHL.com |date=June 11, 2025 |access-date=June 11, 2025}}</ref>\n\nDuring a March 18, 2026, game against the Dallas Stars, Makar scored his 20th goal of the [[2025–26 NHL season]], becoming the first defenceman since [[Phil Housley]] to score 20 goals in three straight seasons.<ref>{{cite web |title=Avalanche's Cale Makar joins exclusive club after 20th goal of season vs. Stars |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/avalanche-cale-makar-joins-exclusive-175416804.html |access-date=March 19, 2026 |website=Yahoo Sports |author=Bryan Logan |date=March 19, 2026}}</ref> He scored the 500th point of his career when he assisted on a [[Brock Nelson]] goal in a 4–2 loss to the Winnipeg Jets on March 28.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Boulding |first1=Ryan |title=Perfetti breaks tie in 3rd, Jets cool off Avalanche |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/winnipeg-jets-colorado-avalanche-game-recap-march-28-2026 |website=NHL.com |access-date=March 29, 2026 |date=March 28, 2026}}</ref> Makar finished the regular season with 20 goals and 59 assists in 75 games, helping the Avalanche to win the [[Presidents' Trophy]] for the second time in his tenure. He was a Norris Trophy finalist for the sixth year in a row.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dahlin, Makar, Werenski named Norris Trophy finalists |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/norris-trophy-finalists-for-best-defenseman-for-2025-26-announced-by-nhl |website=NHL.com |access-date=May 7, 2026 |date=May 7, 2026}}</ref>\n\nEntering the [[2026–27 NHL season|2026–27 season]], the final year of his contract, Makar signed an eight-year extension on August 28, 2026. With a total value of $163.2 million and an average annual value of $20.4 million, it was the most expensive contract in NHL history, and the first with an average annual value in excess of $20 million.<ref>{{cite web |title=Makar signs record 8-year, $163.2 million contract with Avalanche, worth $20.4M annually |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/cale-makar-signs-eight-year-contract-with-colorado-avalanche |website=NHL.com |date=August 28, 2026 |access-date=August 29, 2026}}</ref> This milestone came at a time of explosive projected growth in the league's [[salary cap]] as a result of revenue increases.<ref>{{cite web |last=Sachdeva |first=Sonny |title=Cap Comparables: Why Cale Makar became NHL's first $20M player |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nhl/article/cap-comparables-why-cale-makar-became-the-nhls-first-20-million-player/ |website=Sportsnet.ca |date=August 28, 2026 |access-date=August 29, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Hornby |first=Lance |title=Why Cale Makar became the NHL's highest paid player - for now |url=https://torontosun.com/sports/hockey/why-cale-makar-became-the-nhls-highest-paid-player-for-now |newspaper=[[The Toronto Sun]] |date=August 28, 2026 |access-date=August 29, 2026}}</ref>\n\n==International play==\n{{MedalTableTop|name=}}\n{{MedalSport|Men's [[ice hockey]]}}\n{{MedalCountry|{{ih|CAN}}}}\n{{MedalCompetition|[[Ice hockey at the Olympic Games|Winter Olympics]]}}\n{{MedalSilver|[[Ice hockey at the 2026 Winter Olympics – Men's tournament|2026 Milano Cortina]]|}}\n{{MedalCompetition|[[4 Nations Face-Off]]}}\n{{MedalW|[[2025 4 Nations Face-Off|2025 Canada/United States]]|}}\n{{MedalCompetition|[[IIHF World Junior Championship|World Junior Championships]]}}\n{{MedalGold|[[2018 World Junior Ice Hockey Championships|2018 United States]]|}}\n{{MedalBottom}}\nMakar was first selected by [[Hockey Canada]] to compete for Canada West at the [[World Junior A Challenge]] in 2015 and 2016. He was selected to the Tournament All-Star Team in both years and helped Canada West to a gold medal in 2015.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.tsn.ca/creating-nhl-draft-buzz-at-the-world-jr-a-challenge-1.630129 | title = Creating NHL draft buzz at the World Jr A Challenge | publisher = [[The Sports Network]] | author = Bob Mckenzie | date = December 12, 2016 | accessdate = March 2, 2019 | archive-date = March 7, 2019 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190307054308/https://www.tsn.ca/creating-nhl-draft-buzz-at-the-world-jr-a-challenge-1.630129 | url-status = live}}</ref> Unable to defend the gold medal, Makar followed up by setting a tournament single-game record for points by a defenceman in 2016.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Mooney|first1=Patrick|title=Maple Leafs Pre-Playoff Draft Preview: Cale Makar|url=https://realsport101.com/news/sports/nhl/leafs-pre-playoff-preview-of-the-2017-draft-cale-makar|publisher=Real Sport 101|accessdate=April 10, 2017|date=March 23, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107170208/https://realsport101.com/news/sports/nhl/leafs-pre-playoff-preview-of-the-2017-draft-cale-makar/|archive-date=November 7, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> Makar appeared for Canada at the World Junior Summer Showcase. He had one goal and one assist during the exhibition. His single goal came at a pivotal time on August 4, 2017, against Sweden, tying the game 4–4 in the third period. The marker re-energized the Canadians as they registered three more goals to pull off a 7–4 win.<ref name=\"develop\" />\n\nMakar was selected to the [[Canada men's national junior ice hockey team|Canada national junior team]] for the [[2018 World Junior Ice Hockey Championships|2018 World Junior Championships]], winning gold. Makar finished the tournament leading all defenceman with three goals and eight points in seven games, and was the only Canadian named to the All-Tournament Team.<ref name=\"WJC\">{{cite web|last1=Yerdon|first1=Joe|title=Canada defeats Sweden for gold medal at World Juniors|url=https://www.nhl.com/news/canada-beats-sweden-to-win-gold-medal-at-world-juniors-294704816|website=NHL.com|access-date=January 10, 2018|location=Buffalo|date=January 6, 2018|archive-date=January 6, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180106140455/https://www.nhl.com/news/canada-beats-sweden-to-win-gold-medal-at-world-juniors/c-294704816|url-status=live}}</ref>\n\nFollowing the World Juniors, Makar reportedly turned down an invite to join the [[Canada men's national ice hockey team|Canada senior team]] for the [[Ice hockey at the 2018 Winter Olympics – Men's tournament|2018 Winter Olympics]] to focus on his season at UMass, as he would have had to miss three weeks for the tournament.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sbnation.com/2018/1/10/16875448/cale-makar-2018-olympics-hockey-team-canada-invite-turned-down-avalanche|title=Avalanche prospect Cale Makar turns down 2018 Olympics invite from Team Canada, per report|work=SBNation.com|access-date=March 22, 2018|archive-date=July 1, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180701055218/https://www.sbnation.com/2018/1/10/16875448/cale-makar-2018-olympics-hockey-team-canada-invite-turned-down-avalanche|url-status=live}}</ref>\n\nWith NHL players not being permitted to play in the [[2022 Winter Olympics]], and Colorado seeing extensive postseason success after Makar's NHL breakthrough, he did not play for Canada's national team until the [[4 Nations Face-Off]] in 2025. After missing Canada's group stage game against the [[United States men's national ice hockey team|United States]] due to illness,<ref>{{cite web |title=Makar out for Canada against United States at 4 Nations Face-Off |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/cale-makar-injury-status-for-canada-at-4-nations-face-off |access-date=November 21, 2025 |website=NHL.com |date=February 16, 2025}}</ref> he was able to return in time for the subsequent game against [[Finland men's national ice hockey team|Finland]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Canada's Cooper: No reason why Makar won't play in 4 Nations final vs. USA |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nhl/article/canadas-cooper-no-reason-why-makar-wont-play-in-4-nations-final-vs-usa/ |website=[[Sportsnet]] |date=February 18, 2025 |access-date=February 8, 2026 |archive-date=October 12, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251012045359/https://www.sportsnet.ca/nhl/article/canadas-cooper-no-reason-why-makar-wont-play-in-4-nations-final-vs-usa/ |url-status=live}}</ref> In the event final, a rematch against the United States, Makar had an assist on [[Connor McDavid]]'s winning goal in overtime, earning his first senior international title.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/oilers/news/4-nations-mcdavid-scores-ot-winner-for-canada-in-final-to-defeat-the-united-states |title=4 NATIONS: McDavid scores OT winner for Canada in |url-status=live}}</ref>\n\nMakar was one of the first six players named to [[Canada at the 2026 Winter Olympics|Canada's team]] for the [[Ice hockey at the 2026 Winter Olympics – Men's tournament|2026 Winter Olympics]], the first edition with NHL participation since [[Ice hockey at the 2014 Winter Olympics – Men's tournament|2014]].<ref>{{cite web |title=First six men's hockey players named to Team Canada for 2026 Olympic Winter Games |url=https://www.hockeycanada.ca/en-ca/news/first-six-named-for-olympics-2026-olym |access-date=November 21, 2025 |website=hockeycanada.ca |date=June 16, 2025 |archive-date=November 26, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251126214948/https://www.hockeycanada.ca/en-ca/news/first-six-named-for-olympics-2026-olym |url-status=live}}</ref> He was also selected as one of the team's alternate captains.<ref>{{cite web |title=Crosby named Team Canada captain for Milano Cortina Games |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/sidney-crosby-captain-of-canada-for-2026-olympics |website=NHL.com |date=February 8, 2026 |access-date=February 8, 2026}}</ref> Canada reached the final against the United States, where Makar scored the game-tying goal in the second period, but the Americans ultimately prevailed 2–1 in overtime to win the gold medal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/olympics/winter/hockey/olympics-mens-hockey-gold-medal-canada-usa-february-22-milano-cortina-9.7101237 |title=Jack Hughes delivers golden goal as U.S. beats Canada in 2026|website=IIHF|date=February 22, 2026}}</ref>\n\n==Personal life==\nMakar is the son of Gary Makar and Laura MacGregor.<ref name=\"AJHL\" /> He was named after former NHL player [[Cale Hulse]].<ref Hughes 2026-01-08.jpg\n| caption = Hughes with the [[Minnesota Wild]] in 2026\n| birth_date = {{birth date and age|1999|10|14}}\n| birth_place = [[Orlando, Florida]], U.S.\n| height_ft = 5\n| height_in = 10\n| weight_lb = 180\n| position = [[Defenceman|Defense]]\n| shoots = Left\n| league = [[National Hockey League|NHL]]\n| team = [[Minnesota Wild]]\n| former_teams = [[Vancouver Canucks]]\n| ntl_team = USA\n| draft = 7th overall\n| draft_year = 2018\n| draft_team = [[Vancouver Canucks]]\n| career_start = 2019\n| career_end = \n}}\n'''Quintin Jerome Hughes'''<ref name=\"2018quinn\" /><ref name=\"nyt1\">{{cite web |last1=Russo |first1=Michael |title=Hughes Bowl 3: Quinn, Jack and Luke Hughes face off for the first time in Minnesota |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6959903/2026/01/12/wild-quinn-devils-luke-jack-hughes-brothers-game/ |website=The Athletic |publisher=The New York Times |access-date=January 12, 2026 |date=January 12, 2026 |url-access=subscription |archive-date=January 12, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260112180358/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6959903/2026/01/12/wild-quinn-devils-luke-jack-hughes-brothers-game/ |url-status=live}}</ref> (born October 14, 1999) is an American professional [[ice hockey]] player who is a [[Defenceman|defenseman]] for the [[Minnesota Wild]] of the [[National Hockey League]] (NHL). Hughes was drafted seventh overall by the [[Vancouver Canucks]] in the [[2018 NHL entry draft]] and played his first seven seasons with the team, serving as captain from 2023 until his trade to the Wild in 2025. Before the draft, he was considered a top prospect. Showing impressive offensive prowess as a defenseman since the beginning of his time with the Canucks, he was nominated for the [[Calder Memorial Trophy]] as the league's best rookie in 2020. He holds several Canucks and NHL records for defensemen, and won the [[James Norris Memorial Trophy]] in 2024 as the NHL's best defenseman.\n\nFollowing success with the [[USA Hockey National Team Development Program]], Hughes joined the [[University of Michigan]] for the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's ice hockey season|2017–18 season]]. There he set a new record for most assists by a Michigan freshman defenseman and was named to the [[List of All-Big Ten Hockey Teams#Freshman Team|All-Big Ten Freshman Team]] and the [[List of All-Big Ten Hockey Teams#Second Team|All-Big Ten Second Team]].\n\nInternationally, Hughes has represented the [[United States men's national junior ice hockey team|United States]] at the [[2018 World Junior Ice Hockey Championships|2018]] and [[2019 World Junior Ice Hockey Championships|2019 World Junior Championships]]. He made his [[United States men's national ice hockey team|senior national team]] debut at the [[2018 IIHF World Championship|2018 World Championship]] where he helped them win bronze, and played a pivotal role in the American victory at the [[Ice hockey at the 2026 Winter Olympics – Men's tournament|2026 Winter Olympics]].\n\nHughes is from a family of ice hockey players; his younger brother [[Jack Hughes|Jack]] was [[List of first overall NHL draft picks|drafted first overall]] by the [[New Jersey Devils]] in the [[2019 NHL entry draft]], while his youngest brother [[Luke Hughes (ice hockey)|Luke]] was drafted fourth overall in the [[2021 NHL entry draft]], also by the Devils. His mother [[Ellen Weinberg-Hughes]] played for the [[United States women's national ice hockey team]] and his father was the director of player development for the [[Toronto Maple Leafs]].\n\n==Early life==\nHughes was born in [[Orlando, Florida]], to mother, [[Ellen Weinberg-Hughes]], and father, Jim Hughes. The family lived in Orlando while his father was an assistant coach for the [[Orlando Solar Bears (IHL)|Orlando Solar Bears]].<ref name=\":4\">{{cite news|url=http://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/solar-bears/os-sp-2001-orlando-solar-bears-nhl-draft-prospect-20180329-story.html|title=Link to IHL's Solar Bears connects NHL Draft prospect to Orlando|last=Ruiz|first=Stephen|work=Orlando Sentinel|access-date=March 31, 2018|archive-date=March 31, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180331104534/http://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/solar-bears/os-sp-2001-orlando-solar-bears-nhl-draft-prospect-20180329-story.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Hughes' mother is [[Jews|Jewish]] and his father is [[Catholic]].<ref name=\"JSR\">{{cite journal|title=Sports Shorts|journal=[[Jewish Sports Review]]|date=January–February 2018 |volume=11|issue=125|page=13}}</ref>\n\nHughes comes from a \"hockey family.\" In college, his mother was captain of the [[New Hampshire Wildcats women's ice hockey|Wildcats women's ice hockey team]] at the [[University of New Hampshire]] during its \"powerhouse\" era under head coach [[Russ McCurdy]],<ref>{{cite web |last=Snierson |first=Lynne |title=UNH's Breakout Sports Star |url=https://www.nhmagazine.com/unhs-breakout-sports-star/ |access-date=February 25, 2026 |website=New Hampshire Magazine |date=June 18, 2024}}</ref> and was named to the 1991 ECAC Division I All-Star Team, the highest honor in women's collegiate ice hockey at the time. She then went on to win silver in the [[1992 IIHF Women's World Championship|1992 Women's World Championship]] and was one of the six players named to the tournament All-Star team at its conclusion.<ref>{{cite web |title=Who is Ellen Weinberg-Hughes? Mother of Olympic heroes Jack, Quinn has ties to Dallas |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/stars/2026/02/22/who-is-ellen-weinberg-hughes-mother-of-olympic-heroes-jack-quinn-has-ties-to-dallas/ |access-date=February 25, 2026 |website=The Dallas Morning News |date=February 22, 2026}}</ref> Like Hughes, she also played defense. Weinberg-Hughes also served as an advisor to the [[Norwegian Ice Hockey Association]] to help grow the women's ice hockey ahead of the [[1994 Winter Olympics]]. She joined the [[United States women's national ice hockey team|United States women's team]] as a development consultant in 2023, and has been credited with helping the team win gold at the [[2023 IIHF Women's World Championship|2023]] and [[2025 IIHF Women's World Championship|2025]] World Championships and gold at the [[Ice hockey at the 2026 Winter Olympics – Women's tournament|2026 Winter Olympics]]. Hughes' father, Jim Hughes, also has a career in ice hockey. He was a team captain for [[Providence Friars men's ice hockey|Providence College]], assistant coach for the [[Orlando Solar Bears (IHL)|Orlando Solar Bears]],<ref name=\":4\" /> assistant coach for the [[Boston Bruins]], and director of player development for the [[Toronto Maple Leafs]].<ref>{{cite web|last1=Mullen|first1=Liz|title=CAA Hockey adds longtime coaches in staff positions to develop players|url=http://www.sportsbusinessdaily.com/Journal/Issues/2016/04/11/Labor-and-Agents/CAA-Hockey.aspx|website=sportsbusinessdaily.com|access-date=January 15, 2018|date=April 11, 2016|archive-date=January 18, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180118182402/http://www.sportsbusinessdaily.com/Journal/Issues/2016/04/11/Labor-and-Agents/CAA-Hockey.aspx|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=\"family\">{{cite web|last1=Krupa|first1=Gregg|title=Hockey runs deep in Hughes' family bloodline|url=http://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/2018/01/14/hockey-runs-deep-hughes-family-bloodline/109473720/|website=detroitnews.com|access-date=January 15, 2018|location=Ann Arbor|date=January 14, 2018|archive-date=January 17, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180117000844/http://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/2018/01/14/hockey-runs-deep-hughes-family-bloodline/109473720/|url-status=live}}</ref>\n\nHughes' grandfather, Marty, is a [[United States Marine Corps|Marine]] veteran and [[battalion chief]] with the [[New York City Fire Department]]; he came out of retirement to assist firefighters in [[Queens]] during the [[September 11 attacks]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kuzma |first1=Ben |title=Canucks: The right choice at the right time, Quinn Hughes named captain |url=https://theprovince.com/sports/hockey/nhl/vancouver-canucks/quinn-hughes-named-team-captain |publisher=The Province |access-date=14 September 2023}}</ref>{{better citation needed|date=September 2026|reason=Source does not say anything about grandfather being in Marines forces}}\n\nThe family moved to Toronto in 2006, after Hughes' father got a job as an assistant with the [[American Hockey League]]'s [[Toronto Marlies]], and the brothers practiced primarily at Toronto's Wedgewood Park outdoor rink. The family also billeted [[William Nylander]] after he was drafted in [[2014 NHL entry draft|2014]].<ref name=\":3\">{{cite web |last=Peters |first=Chris |title=Meet the Hughes brothers, America's future first family of hockey |url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/story/_/id/23031303/meet-hughes-brothers-america-future-first-family-hockey-nhl |access-date=February 23, 2026 |website=ESPN.com |date=June first year with the USNTDP team, Hughes scored seven goals and recorded 17 assists in 57 games. During the [[2016–17 USHL season|2016–17 season]], he recorded four goals and 22 assists in 26 games, making him the first defenseman in [[United States Hockey League]] (USHL) history to post such high points-per-game ratio two seasons before his NHL draft eligibility.<ref name=\"hot prospect\" /> For his efforts, he was named to the [[2016–17 USHL season#All-USHL Second Team|All-USHL Second Team]].<ref name=\"USHL Second Team\">{{cite web |title=Hughes, St. Cyr Receive USHL End of Year Awards |url=https://www.usahockeyntdp.com/news_article/show/781031 |website=usahockeyntdp.com |access-date=October 4, 2018 |date=April 13, 2017 |archive-date=December 3, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201203004125/https://www.usahockeyntdp.com/news_article/show/781031 |url-status=live}}</ref>\n\n===College===\n[[File:Quinn Hughes 20181006 (2).jpg|thumb|left|Hughes playing for the [[Michigan Wolverines men's ice hockey|University of Michigan]] in October 2018]]\nHughes played for the [[Michigan Wolverines men's ice hockey|Michigan Wolverines]] at the University of Michigan from 2017 to 2019. There, he enrolled in the [[University of Michigan School of Kinesiology|School of Kinesiology]] and majored in Sport Management.<ref name=\"Michigan bio\">{{cite web|title=QUINN HUGHES|url=https://mgoblue.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=18518|website=mgoblue.com|publisher=University of Michigan|access-date=January 15, 2018}}</ref> His roommate at Michigan was his Wolverines teammate, former USNDTP teammate, and future NHL player [[Josh Norris]]. Hughes has described Norris as his best friend in news reports,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Kuzma |first1=Ben |title=Canucks notebook: Quinn Hughes' best friend Josh Norris rocked by fatal hometown school shooting |url=https://theprovince.com/sports/hockey/nhl/vancouver-canucks/canucks-notebook-quinn-hughes-best-friend-josh-norris-rocked-by-fatal-hometown-school-shooting |access-date=June 26, 2026 |access-date=June 26, 2026 |publisher=The Athletic |date=April 28, 2021}}</ref> but in November 2024 Hughes also received his first-ever game-misconduct and ejection from a hockey game for cross-checking Norris from behind in a game between Ottawa and Vancouver.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Fournier |first1=Mikael |title=Vancouver Canucks Captain Quinn Hughes Given Game Misconduct for |url-status=live}}</ref> His 29 points ranked tied for 12th in the NCAA and third in the Big Ten among freshmen, while his 24 assists ranked third in the NCAA and first overall in the Big Ten among freshman.<ref name=\"Awards2018\">{{cite web | url = http://mgoblue.com/news/2018/3/13/ice-hockey-marody-headlines-group-of-wolverines-to-garner-big-ten-hockey-awards.aspx?path=mhockey | title = /> After signing, Hughes underwent an [[Magnetic resonance imaging|MRI]] by the Canucks medical staff and was discouraged from skating for a week as a result of his foot injury sustained from the Big season|2019–20 season]]. After the signing of Brock Boeser, Hughes was tested on the first unit of the powerplay alongside Boeser and [[J. T. Miller]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Wagner |first1=Daniel |title=Canucks new-look power play features Quinn Hughes on first unit, Bo Horvat on second |url=https://www.vancourier.com/pass-it-to-bulis/canucks-new-look-power-play-features-quinn-hughes-on-first-unit-bo-horvat-on-second-1.23954180 |access-date=October 9, 2019 |publisher=Vancouver Courier |date=September 22, 2019 |archive-date=December 7, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191207061259/https://www.vancourier.com/pass-it-to-bulis/canucks-new-look-power-play-features-quinn-hughes-on-first-unit-bo-horvat-on-second-1.23954180 |url-status=live}}</ref> After going scoreless to begin the season, Hughes recorded his first career NHL goal in their home opening game against the [[Los Angeles Kings]] while the Canucks were on a power play.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Woodley |first1=Kevin |title=Hughes gets first NHL goal in Canucks win against Kings |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/los-angeles-kings-vancouver-canucks-game-recap-309926900 |website=nhl.com |access-date=October 10, 2019 |date=October 10, 2019 |archive-date=October 10, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191010050719/https://www.nhl.com/news/los-angeles-kings-vancouver-canucks-game-recap/c-309926900 |url-status=live}}</ref> He became the youngest Canuck defenseman since [[J. J. Daigneault]] to score a goal for the team.<ref>{{cite tweet|user=Canucks|number=1182140841764249600|date=October 9, 2019|title=Quinn Hughes (19 years, 360 days) is the youngest @Canucks defenseman to score since J.J Daigneault (19 years, 176 days) on April 6, 1985. #NHLStats}}</ref> A month later, Hughes bruised his left knee in a game against the [[Anaheim Ducks]] on November 1, 2019.<ref>{{cite web |title=Canucks' Quinn Hughes skates, still day to day with bruised knee |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/hockey/nhl/canucks-quinn-hughes-skates-still-day-day-bruised-knee/ |website=sportsnet.ca |access-date=November 6, 2019 |date=November 4, 2019 |archive-date=November 6, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191106093406/https://www.sportsnet.ca/hockey/nhl/canucks-quinn-hughes-skates-still-day-day-bruised-knee/ |url-status=live}}</ref> He returned to the lineup after missing one game, where he scored the game-tying goal in an eventual 2–1 overtime loss to the [[St. Louis Blues]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Woodley |first1=Kevin |title=Schwartz, Blues recover to top Canucks in OT |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/st-louis-blues-vancouver-canucks-game-recap-310915964 |website=nhl.com |access-date=November 6, 2019 |date=November 6, 2019}}</ref> As a result, he became the fourth under-twenty Canuck in franchise history to record 14 or more points by their 20th game.<ref>{{cite tweet|user=StatsCentre|number=1191950596955344896|date=November 6, 2019|title=Tying it at 1 late in the 3rd vs STL tonight, Quinn Hughes's 14 points are the 4th most by a @Canucks player 20 or younger before reaching their 20th career NHL game. Only with more in that regard: Elias Pettersson (19), Brock Boeser (18), Rick Vaive (15)}}</ref> During a game on November 21, Hughes recorded three power-play assists in the 6–3 win.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Iain MacIntyre |title=Struggling Canucks show excellence on power play to beat Predators |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/hockey/nhl/struggling-canucks-show-excellence-power-plays-beat-predators/ |website=sportsnet.ca |access-date=November 22, 2019 |date=November 21, 2019 |archive-date=January 23, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200123221524/https://www.sportsnet.ca/hockey/nhl/struggling-canucks-show-excellence-power-plays-beat-predators/ |url-status=live}}</ref> This achievement made him the first rookie defenseman in NHL history to record three power-play assists in multiple games in a season.<ref>{{cite tweet|user=SNstats|number=1197731038253981696|date=November 21, 2019|title=#Canucks Quinn Hughes First rookie defenceman in NHL history with multiple 3 PP assist games in a season.2nd rookie defenceman in NHL history with multiple 3 PP point games in a season, joining the Flyers Rick Foley in 1971-72.}}</ref> By November 27, he became the first Canucks rookie defenseman to register three three-point games. It also made him one of the first rookies of the 2019–20 season to reach 20 points.<ref>{{cite web |author1=Steven Ellis |title=BETTER IN BUNCHES: QUINN HUGHES' MULTI-POINT EFFORTS PUT HIM ON PACE TO [[David Perron]], and [[T. J. Oshie]].<ref name=\"2020ASG\">{{cite web |title=Leafs' Marner, Canucks' Hughes among final all-star picks |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/hockey/nhl/mitch-marner-quinn-hughes-all-star-game-1.5424012 |website=cbc.ca |access-date=January 12, 2020 |date=January 11, 2020 |archive-date=January 29, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200129024702/https://www.cbc.ca/sports/hockey/nhl/mitch-marner-quinn-hughes-all-star-game-1.5424012 |url-status=live}}</ref> As a result, the Vancouver Canucks became the first team in the Expansion Era to have a rookie play in the All-Star Game in three consecutive seasons.<ref>{{cite tweet|user=PR_NHL|number=1221100466748129281|date=January 25, 2020|title= With Quinn Hughes set to take the ice tonight in St. Louis, the @Canucks will become the first NHL team in the expansion era (since 1967-68) to have a rookie in three consecutive #NHLAllStar Games.}}</ref> At the [[NHL All-Star Skills Competition]], Hughes partook in the Fastest Skater contest, finishing with a time of 14.263.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Joy |first1=Derek |title=Canucks impress at NHL All-Star skills competition |url=https://www.nhl.com/canucks/news/vancouver-canucks-nhl-all-star-skills-314281870 |website=nhl.com |access-date=January 25, 2020 |date=January 25, 2020 |archive-date=January 25, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200125093230/https://www.nhl.com/canucks/news/vancouver-canucks-nhl-all-star-skills/c-314281870 |url-status=live}}</ref> The next day, Hughes became the second rookie defenseman to score a goal in the NHL All-Star Game.<ref>{{cite tweet|user=PR_NHL|date=January 25, 2020|number=1221259403220987905|title=Quinn Hughes became the second rookie defenseman to score a goal in an #NHLAllStar Game. Denis Potvin tallied once for Team All-Stars East in the 27th All-Star Game in 1974. #NHLStats}}</ref> \n\nUpon returning from the All-Star break, Hughes continued his record-breaking season with the Canucks. On February 27, he recorded an assist on J. T. Miller's power-play goal against the Ottawa Senators, replacing Boeser as the franchise record holder for most powerplay points in a season by a rookie. That assist was also his 43rd of the season, moving him into first place for most single assists by a rookie in franchise history.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Jory |first1=Derek |title=Hughes' record-breaking season |url=https://www.nhl.com/canucks/news/vancouver-canucks-quinn-hughes-315667174 |website=nhl.com |access-date=February 28, 2020 |date=February 28, 2020}}</ref> He was subsequently named Rookie of the Month for February.<ref name=\"ROM\">{{cite web |title=Hughes of Canucks named NHL Rookie of Month for February |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/nhl-rookie-of-the-month-february-quinn-hughes-vancouver-canucks-315739260 |publisher=National Hockey League|website=nhl.com |access-date=March 1, 2020 |date=March 1, 2020}}</ref> Although the 2019–20 season was eventually paused due to the [[coronavirus]], Hughes ended his rookie season as the lead rookie in points league-wide, becoming the third rookie defensemen since [[Bobby Orr]] and [[Brian Leetch]] to do so in the modern era.<ref>{{cite web |title=Quinn Hughes joins Bobby Orr and Brian Leetch with rookie scoring title win |url=https://www.bardown.com/quinn-hughes-joins-bobby-orr-and-brian-leetch-with-rookie-scoring-title-win-1.1481116 |website=bardown.com |date=May 29, 2020 |publisher=Bardown |access-date=June 6, 2020 |url-status=live}}</ref> As a result of his play, he was named a [[Calder Memorial Trophy]] finalist alongside [[Cale Makar]] and [[Dominik Kubalík]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Hughes, Makar and Kubalik |url-status=live}}</ref>\n\nHughes returned to the Canucks for their Return to Play Initiative months following the conclusion of the regular season, saying he felt \"as strong as I've ever been.\" During the play pause, he lived in Plymouth, Michigan with his family and played sports with his brothers daily to remain in shape.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Jensen |first1=Pete |title=Hughes 'strong as postseason debut during the team's qualifying round against the [[Minnesota Wild]] and recorded his first multi-point playoff game on August 6, 2020, as the Canucks took a 2–1 lead in the series.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bennett |first1=Dean |title=Canucks shut out Wild, pull within 1 win of advancing to next round of playoffs tweet|user=SNstats|number=1291481413896863745|date=August 6, 2020|title=Quinn Hughes (20 years, 297 days old) Youngest defenceman in #Canucks history with a multi-point game in the postseason}}</ref> During the second round against the [[Vegas Golden Knights]], Hughes set a new NHL record for most playoff assists by a rookie defenseman with 13 assists in 15 playoff games.<ref>{{cite web |url-status=live}}</ref>\n\n=====COVID-19, new contract, and setting records=====\nDue to the COVID-19 pandemic, the [[2020–21 NHL season|2020–21 season]] was pushed back until January 13, 2021, for a 56-game regular season. The Canucks were also temporarily realigned into the [[North Division (NHL)|North Division]] where they would only compete against Canadian teams.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Blackburn |first1=Pete |title=NHL announces 56-game 2021 season will start Jan. 13 and realignment with Canadian division |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nhl/news/nhl-announces-56-game-2021-season-will-start-jan-13-and-realignment-with-canadian-division/ |work=CBS Sports |access-date=November 16, 2023 |date=December 20, 2020 |archive-date=November 16, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231116180616/https://www.cbssports.com/nhl/news/nhl-announces-56-game-2021-season-will-start-jan-13-and-realignment-with-canadian-division/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Hughes began the season with eight assists through the team's nine games, becoming the fourth player in franchise history to reach this milestone in the same number of games.<ref>{{cite web |title=Game Notes: Canucks vs Senators (3/9) |url=https://www.nhl.com/canucks/news/canucks-senators-game-notes-320789766 |publisher=National Hockey League |access-date=November 16, 2023 |date=January 28, 2021 |archive-date=November 16, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231116180620/https://www.nhl.com/canucks/news/canucks-senators-game-notes-320789766 |url-status=live}}</ref> As the season continued, Hughes continued collecting points and matching NHL records. After collecting his 18th point on February 13 against the [[Calgary Flames]], Hughes tied the NHL record for fourth-most points by an NHL defenseman in the first 18 games of a season since 1985–86.<ref>{{cite web |title=Game Notes: Canucks vs Flames (5/10) |url=https://www.nhl.com/canucks/news/canucks-flames-game-notes-321415020 |publisher=National Hockey League |access-date=November 16, 2023 |date=February 15, 2021 |archive-date=November 16, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231116180618/https://www.nhl.com/canucks/news/canucks-flames-game-notes-321415020 |url-status=live}}</ref> In March, Hughes became the seventh quickest defenseman in franchise history to reach the 25-point mark<ref>{{cite web |title=Game Notes: Canucks at Senators (5/9) |url=https://www.nhl.com/canucks/news/canucks-senators-game-notes-322604384 |publisher=National Hockey League |access-date=November 16, 2023 |date=March 17, 2021 |archive-date=November 16, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231116180617/https://www.nhl.com/canucks/news/canucks-senators-game-notes-322604384 |url-status=live}}</ref> and later became the sixth fastest to exceed 30 points.<ref>{{cite web |title=Game Notes: Canucks vs Senators (6/9) |url=https://www.nhl.com/canucks/news/canucks-senators-game-notes-323905622 |publisher=National Hockey League |access-date=November 16, 2023 |date=April 22, 2021}}</ref> On March 30, Hughes was one of 22 players on the Canucks who were infected with an aggressive [[SARS-CoV-2 Gamma variant|Gamma variant]] of [[COVID-19]]. He returned to the ice on April 21, 2021, where he collected three points in a 6–3 win over the Toronto Maple Leafs.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Kuzma |first1=Ben |title=Canucks: Hughes clears COVID-19 hurdle, starts to strut offensive stuff |url=https://theprovince.com/sports/canucks-hughes-clears-covid-19-hurdle-starts-to-strut-offensive-stuff |access-date=May 3, 2021 |publisher=The Province |date=April 21, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210421204147/https://theprovince.com/sports/canucks-hughes-clears-covid-19-hurdle-starts-to-strut-offensive-stuff|archive-date=April 21, 2021}}</ref> Preliminary contract discussion also began for Hughes and [[Elias Pettersson]], who were both to become restricted free agents and the conclusion of the season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Canucks begin preliminary contract talks with Hughes, Pettersson |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nhl/article/canucks-begin-preliminary-contract-talks-hughes-pettersson/ |website=sportsnet.ca |publisher=Sportsnet |access-date=May 3, 2021 |date=April 3, 2021 |archive-date=May 4, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210504005520/https://www.sportsnet.ca/nhl/article/canucks-begin-preliminary-contract-talks-hughes-pettersson/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Shortly following his return to the lineup, Hughes tallied his 77th assist to tie Pettersson for the second-most assists before age 22 in franchise history and third-most overall points by a Canucks defenseman.<ref>{{cite web |title=Game Notes: Canucks vs Senators (8/9) |url=https://www.nhl.com/canucks/news/canucks-senators-game-notes-324031542 |publisher=National Hockey League |access-date=November 16, 2023 |date=April 26, 2021}}</ref> Hughes finished the season leading all team defensemen in points and ranked third overall in scoring with three goals and 38 assists for 41 points. In recognition of his efforts, Hughes was awarded the [[Babe Pratt Trophy]] as the team's best defenseman.<ref>{{cite web |title=Canucks Announce Team Awards For 2020.21 Season |url=https://www.nhl.com/canucks/news/vancouver-canucks-announce-team-awards-for-2020-21-season-324801946 |publisher=National Hockey League |access-date=November 16, 2023 |date=May 18, 2021}}</ref>\n\n[[File:Sam Reinhart stands next to Quinn Hughes during a game against the Vancouver Canucks in November 2025.jpg|alt=Quinn Hughes stands next to Sam Reinhart during a game against the Florida Panthers in November 2025|thumb|Hughes and [[Sam Reinhart]] of the [[Florida Panthers]] during a game in November 2025]]\nAs contract discussions continued into the following season, Hughes Hughes was not one of the top three finalists for the [[James Norris Memorial Trophy|Norris Trophy]] as the NHL's best defenseman, he received two fourth-place votes and three fifth-place votes.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Satriano |first1=David |title=Makar of Avalanche wins Norris Trophy as best defenseman in NHL |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/cale-makar-of-colorado-avalanche-wins-norris-trophy-as-best-defenseman-334687506 |publisher=National Hockey League |access-date=November 16, 2023 |date=June 21, 2022 |archive-date=November 16, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231116194231/https://www.nhl.com/news/cale-makar-of-colorado-avalanche-wins-norris-trophy-as-best-defenseman-334687506 |url-status=live}}</ref> He also received three second place and 11 third place votes for the [[NHL All-Star team#Post-lockout era (2005–06 to present)|2021–22 first and second All-Star teams]].<ref>{{cite web |title=NHL announces 2021-22 First and Second All-Star Teams |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/nhl-2021-22-first-and-second-all-star-teams-334688828 |publisher=National Hockey by breaking his previous franchise record for most points by a defenseman in a single season. Leading up to the start of the [[2022–23 NHL season|2022–23 season]], Hughes admitted he wished to score more and develop a shoot-first mentality.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Cotsonika |first1=Nicholas J. Boudreau, Hughes accumulated five assists through five games<ref name=\"cleared\">{{cite web |last1=Woodley |first1=Kevin |title=Hughes cleared to play for Canucks against Devils |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/canucks-quinn-hughes-expects-to-return-against-devils-337001274 |publisher=National Hockey League |access-date=November 16, 2023 |date=October 31, 2022}}</ref> although the Canucks began the season with a losing 0–5–2 record.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Woodley |first1=Kevin |title=Boudreau supported as coach by Canucks GM after 0-5-2 start missing four games with a lower-body injury, Hughes returned to the Canucks lineup on October 31 for their game against the [[New Jersey Devils]].<ref name=\"cleared\" /> On January 22, the Canucks fired Boudreau after he led the team to an 18–25–3 record to rank sixth in the Pacific Division and 14 points out of a playoff spot.<ref>{{cite web |title=Canucks fire head coach Bruce Boudreau, hire Rick Tocchet |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nhl/article/canucks-fire-head-coach-bruce-boudreau-hire-rick-tocchet/ |publisher=Sportsnet |access-date=November 16, 2023 |date=January 22, 2023 |url-status=live}}</ref> On March 4, 2023, Hughes tallied two assists in the Canucks 4–1 win over the [[Toronto Maple Leafs]] to become the fastest defenseman in NHL history to reach the 200-assist milestone. He reached this milestone in his 263rd career NHL game, one fewer than the second place defenseman [[Brian Leetch]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Schram |first1=Carol |title=NHL STAT PACK: QUINN HUGHES SETS |date=March 7, 2023}}</ref>\n\n=====Canucks captain=====\nBefore the start of the [[2023–24 NHL season|2023–24 season]], Hughes was named the 15th [[Vancouver Canucks#Team captains|captain in Canucks history]], making him both the youngest active captain in the NHL and the first American-born captain of the Canucks.<ref>{{cite web |title=Introducing 'Captain Quinn' |url=https://www.nhl.com/canucks/news/introducing-captain-quinn |publisher=National Hockey League|access-date=September 11, 2023 |date=September 11, 2023}}</ref> Hughes and his defensive partner [[Filip Hronek]] played important roles in helping the Canucks find early success through October and November.<ref name=\"notes\">{{cite web |title=Game notes: Canucks at Avalanche |url=https://www.nhl.com/canucks/news/game-notes-canucks-at-avalanche-112223 |publisher=National Hockey League |access-date=November 22, 2023 |date=November 22, 2023}}</ref> On November 6, Hughes was stars of the week |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nhl/article/canucks-defenceman-quinn-hughes-tops-nhls-three-stars-of-the-week/ |publisher=Sportsnet |access-date=November 16, 2023 |date=November 6, |url-status=live}}</ref> A few days later, Hughes and Hronek became the third defensemen pairings in NHL history to each register 14 or more assists through the first 13 games of a season.<ref name=\"notes\" /> Following a win over the San Jose Sharks on November 20, Hughes matched his career-high eight goals and became the first player to reach the 30-point mark in the 2023–24 NHL regular season. This also made him the third defenseman in NHL history to reach 30 points through the first 17 games of the season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Canucks: Quinn Hughes credits coaching staff after hitting 30 |url-status=live}}</ref> The following month, Hughes became the first defenseman in the 2023–24 season to reach 40 points and the first Canucks defenseman to do so in less than 40 games.<ref>{{cite web |title=#NHLStats: Live Updates for December 19 |url=https://media.nhl.com/public/live-updates?date=2023-12-19 |publisher=National Hockey League |access-date=December 24, 2023 third trio of teammates to reach 40 points in their teams' first 33 games since 1997.<ref>{{cite web |title=Game Notes: Canucks vs. Sharks |url=https://www.nhl.com/canucks/news/game-notes-canucks-vs-sharks-122323 |publisher=National Hockey League |access-date=December 24, 2023 |date=December 23, 2023 |archive-date=December 24, 2023 the [[2024 National Hockey League All-Star Game]] for the second time in his career.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Johnston |first1=Patrick |title=Canucks: Quinn Hughes, NHL's top-scoring defenceman and an Olympic tournament with NHL players.<ref name=\":2\" />\n\n==Player profile==\n{{Quote box|width=31%|align=right|quote=\"The kind of defenceman I love playing with is a good-skating, puck-moving puck to make the best play almost as if he can slow down time.<ref name=\":3\" />\n\nAfter being drafted by the Canucks, general manager [[Jim Benning]] cited his dynamic skating and ability to quickly transition the puck as reasons for drafting him, seeing it as ideal for the team.<ref>{{cite web |last1=MacIntyre |first1=Iain |title=Quinn Hughes believes he can play for Canucks 'right now'
